place name parts - e.g. countries and cities. The Attribute
Values table holds translations of attribute values (e.g.
the value for the attribute Occupation, might be
'Engineer'). The Miscellaneous table holds translations for
everything else - e.g. report titles, headings, labels, sentence
parts, and more.

New
Opens the Edit Translation
Dialog in Create mode, to allow new translations
to be added to the current translation table. If you have a
translation selected when you open this dialog, the new
translations will be inserted immediately after it. If you
want new translations to be appended to the current translation
table, unselect all items before clicking on the New
button.

Move Up

This button is only enabled when 'Unsorted' is ticked, and,
together with the Move Down button, allows you to control the
'unsorted' order of items.

Tip: Move Up and Move Down buttons work with
multiple selection. If you want to move a single item down
below the next 20 items, it may be quicker to select all 20
items below it, and move them up once. Also, if you want a
number of items to be grouped together that currently aren't,
just select each of them using non-contiguous selection
(press-and-hold the Ctrl key while clicking on each item), and
then press either Move Up or Move Down. This will group
them all together with the first or last selected item.

Move Down
See previous.

Add Missing Attribute Values
This button is only available when viewing the Attribute Values
table. It adds all attribute values in the current project,
that aren't already in the Attribute Values table, to that
table. It is up to you to then provide translations for
them.

Add Missing Citation Text
This button is only available when viewing the Miscellaneous
table. It adds all text components of formats used to
generate source citations, to the Miscellaneous table, if they
aren't already there. It is up to you to then provide
translations for them.

title: Latitude & Longitude Dialog
text:
Data Entry Helper Dialogs

Latitude & Longitude Dialog

Latitude and Longitude Dialog

The Latitude & Longitude dialog is a helper dialog, for the
Latitude & Longitude field within Place
and Address records.

Latitude and longitude is sometimes expressed as degrees, minutes and
seconds, sometimes as degrees and minutes, and sometimes just as
degrees. In each case, decimal values can be used in, and only in,
the smallest unit used. So, for example, the following could all
represent the same latitude and longitude:

51°19'26.77"S, 1°55'8.07"W

51°19.446167'S, 1°55.1345'W

51.3241028S, 1.9189083W

-51.3241028, -1.9189083

When only numbers are used (no letters representing North, South, East
and West), negative values are used for south and west.

You can copy and paste any of these values into the Lat./Long. field in
a Place record or Address record (see Property
Box: Main Tab for Place Records and Property
Box: Main Tab for Address Records), and they will be recognised as
the same latitude/longitude.

title: LDS Church Features
text:
LDS Church Features

Family Historian has various special features which are for the use of
members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (the LDS
Church). These features include the ability to record full details
of the following LDS ordinances:

LDS Baptism

LDS Confirmation

LDS Endowment

LDS Initiatory

LDS Seal to Parents

LDS Seal to Spouse

The option to "Enable LDS Support" is available on the General
tab of Preferences, and can be changed at any time. When
enabled, the various LDS ordinances can be added and edited on the Facts
tab of the Property Box, including temple and ordinance
status. Almost all reports can include details of LDS ordinances,
if required, including narrative reports. These options can also be
excluded from reports if required in the main tab of report options for
the report in question (see Report
Options Dialog).

When LDS support is enabled, the FamilySearch
Workspace window has an additional Ordinances
Tab which displays LDS Ordinance information for a selected
person. This ordinance information can be copied back to the
matching record in your Family Historian project. Church members
can click the Reserve Ordinances button on this tab, to open
an appropriate web page in an external web browser for reserving
ordinances and related temple work, for the person in question.
All LDS ordinance information and tasks are only available for LDS
Church members with suitable permission in their FamilySearch account.

title: Log Files Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Log Files Dialog

The Log Files dialog is accessed by clicking on 'Log Files' on the
'Window' menu. It lists all stored log files for the application as a
whole and for the current project, if any. Log files which relate
to the application as a whole have 'System in the second column.
Log files which relate to the current project only have 'Project' in the
second column.

Log files are only generated in exceptional circumstances. A project
may not have any log files. A project log file might be generated if,
for example, you create a new project and import a GEDCOM file into it
which contains errors. One or two log files (usually two) will be
created in this case, which will record all errors that were found in
the GEDCOM file, and all subsequent corrections that were made to fix
the errors.

Buttons

View
View the selected log file

Delete
Delete the selected log file

title: Workspace Windows
text:
Workspace Windows

The main application windows in Family Historian are called
'workspace' windows. There are 10 of them:

The Focus Window
The 'hub' window of the appplication. Shows relationship
information for a chosen 'focus person'.

The Records Window
View and search all the records in your file - not just for
Individuals, but also Families, Sources, Repositories, Media,
Notes, Research Notes, and more. You can also browse Smart Folders in the Records
Window.

The Diagram Window
Diagrams are displayed in the Diagram Window.

The Media Window
Browse and work with your pictures, videos, sound files, and
other media, in the Media Window.

The Report Window
Reports are displayed in the Report Window.

The Book Window
Books are displayed in the Book Window.

The Query Window
Queries are stored instructions for retrieving and displaying
information taken from your family tree file. You can create,
view, edit and run queries in the Query Window. You can also
create, view and edit Smart
Folders in the Query Window.

The Map Window
View events, places and addresses marked on maps.

The Web Search
Window
A Web Browser within a window. It is designed to make it
as easy as possible to transfer data from web pages on the
Internet, to your records

The
FamilySearch Window
FamilySearch is a nonprofit family history organization, based
in Utah, USA, operated by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day
Saints. The FamilySearch workspace window is used to access and
work with these records and the FamilySearch global 'family tree'
which has information about more than 1.7 billion people
worldwide.

If you wish, you can have all of these windows open at the same time.
You can also switch between any or all of them, without having to close
them. Each of these windows, when open, will have an icon representing
it in the Navigation Bar. Simply click
on the relevant icon to switch to that window.

To close any of these windows, except the Focus Window and the Records
Window, click on the little cross in the top right corner of the
application's icon in the Navigation Bar. Alternatively, each of these
windows also has a small close button in the top-right corner of the
window. You can usually see it just below the main application close
button.

With the exception of the Focus Window, the Records Window and the
FamilySearch Window, you can if you wish have multiple instances of all
of these windows, open at the same time. You can configure the extent to
which you want windows to be re-used in the Workspaces
tab of Preferences.

In addition to these workspace windows, there are also five special dialog
boxes (form-like windows) that deserve to be mentioned here. These
are:

The Property Box
The Property Box is your main data entry window. It is designed
to be used alongside, and in conjunction with, workspace
windows. It can be docked at the side of the main
application window, or be allowed to 'float' in front of it.

The Citation
Window

The Citation Window is used for entering and viewing details of
source citations.

The Note Window

The Note Window is the main window for entering notes.

The
Automatic Source Citation Pane
The Automatic Source Citation pane, when open, is always docked
at the top of the main application window. You can use it to
specify source citations to be automatically added to fields and
records that you add or update.

The
Project Window
The application Welcome screen. Select a project to open, or
create a new one.

title: Manage Autotext Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Manage Autotext Dialog

Manage Autotext Dialog

The Manage Autotext Dialog can be accessed by clicking
Manage Autotext on the Tools menu. You can
also access it from the Note Window.
To do that, click Manage Autotext on the dropdown menu that
appears when you click on the menu button on
the Note Window toolbar.

What is Autotext?

Autotext is re-usable text. It is not part of your project data,
but can be inserted into notes, within your project data. To learn
more, see Autotext.

What is Autotext for Plugins?

At the top of the dialog, you can opt to view either Autotext or
Autoext for Plugins. Autotext for Plugins is a
special kind of autotext that is used by (and created by) Data
Entry Assistants, which are a special kind of program extension
called a plugin. Typically this kind of autotext
contains special codes used by the plugin that created it, which will be
replaced with suitable values when the plugin is run. For this
reason, you are not likely to ever want to to insert this kind of
autotext directly into a note in the Note
window. Occasionally, however, you may want to modify some
aspects of the formatting and/or layout of Autotext for Plugins,
to make the text conform to your own style and layout preferences. To
learn more about data entry assistants, see Source-Driven
Data Entry.

Some of the functionality that is available for ordinary autotext, may
not be available for Autotext for Plugins (such as Import and Export).

Research Note Autotext

If you edit standard Research Note autotext (that is, autotext located
under 'Research Note'), we recommend that you should always preserve the
header section within the autotext. If you create your own custom
Research Note autotext, we recommend that you give it a similar header
section too. See Research Note
Header for more details.

How to Safely Combine Standard and Custom Autotext

Autotext is a very useful feature, especially with Text from
Source fields. A number of autotexts are included with
Family Historian (these are called standard autotexts), and
users are encouraged to add your own autotext - especially Text
from Source autotext - and to organise them into folders in
whatever way is convenient and suits you. Autotext you add
yourself is called custom autotext.

There is potential issue however when standard and custom autotext are
combined. Over time, when new versions of Family Historian
are released, we may include more standard autotexts, and may make
changes to existing standard autotext. This new autotext and
changes to existing autotext will be installed when you upgrade to the
new version. When you upgrade, Family Historian will never delete
custom autotexts or custom autotext folders you have created - but
unless you take steps to avoid it, it is possible that autotext files
could be overwritten. Suppose, for example, you had created
autotext called "Census 1901". If by chance, a new standard
autotext was created with the same name, in the same location, it would
overwrite your autotext when you apply the upgrade, and your version
would be lost. We encourage all users to keep backups of all
important data - including autotext. However, you can also take
steps to ensure that your autotext will never be overwritten when you
upgrade. Family Historian's standard text will never be located in
a folder named 'Custom'. So if you create a folder with this name,
you can be sure that it will never be overwritten. You could
create a folder called 'Custom' within the 'Autotext' folder, if you
wish. Or you could create subfolders called 'Custom' within any
existing folder, if you prefer. Either way, you can be sure that
your autotexts will never be overwritten by standard autotexts in the
future. A second solution however, is simply to use an underscore
as the first or last character in the name of your own
autotext. Family Historian will never create any standard
autotext with names that start or end with an underscore. So by
taking this approach, you can also guarantee that your autotext will
never be overwritten by a Family Historian upgrade.

Icons

Autotext 'root' folder

Folder (standard or custom)

Standard autotext

Custom autotext

Buttons

Add
You can add custom autotext files or folders - you will be
prompted to choose which you want to create. The location
for the new file or folder depends on your current
selection. If the current selection is a folder, the new
file or folder will be created within the selected folder.
If the current selection is a file, the new file or folder will be
created in the same folder as that in which the selected file is
located.

Edit
Opens the Note Window in
constrained mode (i.e. not as a floating window), to allow the
selected autotext to be edited.

Clone
Clone - that is, create a copy of - the selected autotext.

Rename
Rename a selected autotext or folder. If you rename a
standard autotext, it will become custom autotext.

Reset
This command works with multiple selection. You can reset
the selected autotexts or folders. Resetting custom
autotexts is allowed, but has no effect. Resetting a folder
which has or had standard autotexts in it (a standard folder in
other words), will reset all the standard autotexts, but will have
no effect on custom autotexts in that folder or elsewhere.
Any deleted standard autotexts for a given folder will be
reinstated when the folder is reset, as will any deleted standard
folders. Resetting a folder also resets all subfolders
located within it (and any subfolders within them, etc). So
reset the root folder to reset all standard autotext.

Delete
This command works with multiple selection but all selected
items must be located within the same folder. You can delete
both files and folders, but deleting folders only works if the
folder is empty. You cannot delete the root folder.
Also, if you delete a standard autotext or standard folder, it may
be reinstated when you next apply an upgrade to Family
Historian. However, you can then delete it again if you wish
to.

Import
Autotext can be shared. Shared autotext is held in
Autotext Collection Files. It may be that someone has
created a collection of Text from Source autotext that relates to
your country, but which is not included as standard with Family
Historian. It might, for example, be available on the Family
Historian User Group website, or elsewhere. Once you have
downloaded this file to your PC, you can import it into Family
Historian. Click on the Import
button. You will be prompted to select the Autotext
Collection File to import it. All Autotext Collection files
store autotext that was originally held within a given folder (see
Export below). When you import, an equivalent new folder
will be created in your environment, and the files (and any
subfolders) will be imported into it. If there is already a
folder with the same name, the Import routine will modify the
imported folder name very slightly to make it unique (e.g. by
adding "(2)" on the end). When you import, no existing files
or folders are ever over-written or deleted.

Export
To export autotext, select the folder that it belongs to, in the
list, and click the Export button.
You will be prompted to specify the location and name of the
exported file.

title: Manage Queries Dialog
text:
Query Window

Manage Queries Dialog

Manage Queries Dialog

The Manage Queries Dialog displays a complete list of installed
queries (standard and custom). It can be accessed in different ways, and
will look slightly different depending on the context of use.

You can open it by clicking "Manage Queries" on the dropdown menu
that appears when you click the Query button on the main application
toolbar.

You can also open it by clicking "Manage Queries" on the dropdown
menu that appears when you click on the cog (menu) button on the query
toolbar, within the Query
Window.

Finally, you can also open it by clicking on the little button with
3 dots
to the right of the box showing the currently selected query, at the
top of the Query Window.

When you access this dialog by either of the first two methods, the
assumption is that you are primarily interested in managing queries
(such as creating new ones, or copying or deleting existing ones) and
the dialog will appear in the form shown above. When you access
this dialog by the third method (the little button with 3 dots), the
assumption is that you are primarily interested in finding a query to
select, to view in the Query Window. In this last case, the dialog
will appear looking slightly different. It will have 3 extra
buttons at the bottom: Select Query,
Close and More
>>. However, even in this case you can still access
all the features that you need to work with queries, by clicking on the
More >> button.

Fields and Buttons

Category
Each query can be assigned up to 3 different categories.
These are assigned in the General
tab of the Query Window. Select a category to filter
on, or choose '<All>' for all categories.

Type
There are 15 query types in total: one for each of the 12 record
types (excluding the header record), and 3 non-record query types:
fact (event or attribute), source citation, or
witness. Select a type to filter on, or choose
'<All>' for all query types.

Filter

Type any text to filter the list, so that it shows only queries
containing the entered text as part of the query name.
Press the Clear button to clear
this filter.

Tip:

use * (asterisk) as a wildcard to match any text.

use ? (question mark) as a wildcard to match any single
character.

use ^ to match the start and/or end of the text.

Custom Only
Tick this checkbox to only view custom queries.

New
Create a new custom query

Run
Run the selected query and view the results in the Result Set tab of the
Query Window.

View
View the selected query in the Query
Window

Rename
Rename the selected query

Clone
Make a copy of the selected query, which can be a standard or
custom query. You will be required to provide a name for the
copy.

Delete
Delete the selected query. Only custom queries can be
deleted.

Import
Import a query from a file.

Export
Export a query to a file. Queries can be shared with
others on the Family Historian User Group
website, and in other ways.

title: Manage Unique Id Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Manage Unique Id Dialog

Manage Unique Id dialog

This dialog box is displayed when you create a new Unique Id or edit an
existing one. Only Individual records can have Unique Ids.
This kind of Id is sometimes called a UID, UUID or GUID. It is a globally
unique id - that is, unique (or intended to be) across the
world. To create a new Unique Id for an Individual record, open
the record in the Property Box, and then click on the 'All' tab.
Right-click on the person's name in the first row, and then, in the menu
that appears, choose "Add Field", then "Add Miscellaneous", and finally
"Add Unique Id". A new Unique Id field will be created, and the
Manage Unique Id dialog will be displayed. Click Generate
to generate the Unique Id. A Unique Id created in this way should
be globally unique. To save your changes, click OK.
The new Unique Id will be displayed in the person's record, and you can
view it at any time in the 'All' tab of the Property Box, when viewing
the person's record.

Most field values can be edited directly in the 'All' tab of the
Property Box. You just click on the value to edit it. This
is not true of Unique Ids. To edit the value, click on it in the
'All' tab of the Property Box, and then open the Manage Unique Id dialog
by clicking on the little button with 3 dots, to the right of the
field. Clicking on the value to enable an edit box, and then
double-clicking on the edit box, will also open the dialog.

Family Historian will allow you to use any value you want as a Unique
Id, but you are recommended to never 'manually' create a Unique Id
yourself. Instead, if you need a new Unique Id, you are
recommended to always get Family Historian to generate one for
you. If you are unsure whether an existing Unique Id conforms
to what Family Historian is expecting for Unique Ids, click Check
(see 'Buttons' below for more on this).

Role of Unique Id in File Merge/Compare

The primary purpose of a Unique Id is to provide a mechanism whereby
you can be confident that a person, referenced in two different
genealogy project files, are in fact the same person - even if the
information stored about the person differs. Imagine, for example,
that you have given a copy of your project data to a relative.
Before giving them the data, you created a Unique Id for each Individual
record in the project. Now let us suppose that your relative
incorporates your research into their research, and makes changes and
additions to it. Later they give you back a copy of what they have
done. At this point, you are likely to want to run Merge/Compare
File (accessible from the File menu), to compare their project data with
yours. At this point, you can choose the option "Check for Individual
record Unique Id matches" to match Individual records which have the
same Unique Id (see the Record
Matching Options dialog). Family Historian will use the
stored value for each Unique Id, whatever it is. However, if you
used the 'Generate' functionality within Family Historian, you can be
confident that it won't be a value that anyone else will, or may, have
used.

How to Assign a Unique Id to All Individual Records in a Project

If you want to assign a Unique Id to every Individual record in your
project, there is a tool for doing this. Click "Record Identifiers"
on the Tools menu to open the Record
Identifiers Dialog. Choose the option "Generate UID (Unique
Id) for Individual records where missing".

Buttons

Generate
Generates a globally unique id. This is done following the
Internationally agreed standard for identifiers of this kind: RFC
4122. To learn more about this standard, search for "RFC
4122" in a web browser.

Check
A value generated by Family Historian (or by another program,
using the RFC 4122 standard) will always look something like the
example value shown in the screenshot above. It consists of
5 groups of characters, with each group separated by a dash
(hyphen). The first group has 8 characters, the last group
has 12, and the other groups have 4 each. Including the
dashes, this comes to a total of 36 characters. The
characters in the 5 groups will always consist of the characters
0-9 or A-F (always upper case). If you click the Check
button, Family Historian will check that the value for the Unique
Id conforms to that description. This is just a minimal
check. If a value passes this check, it does not necessarily
mean that it was in fact generated in accordance with RFC 4122.

Does it matter if a value fails this check? Not
necessarily. If a value does not match the check, this does
not mean that it is not globally unique. It also does not
mean that there is necessarily a problem with it. GUIDs are
often written with curly brackets around them, like this:

{99837229-74066-42FA-A5F5-C683C42D42D0}

A Unique Id that looks like this will fail the 'check', because
Family Historian is not expecting the curly brackets. But it
could nevertheless be used as a Unique Id for this person - see
"Role of Unique Id in File Merge/Compare" above.

Clear
Clears the current value.

title: Map Elements
text:
Map Window

Map Elements

Maps are displayed in the Map Viewer (the area on the right side of the Map Window). Each displayed map may
consist of some combination of the following map elements:

The map layer

Markers

Shapes

These are described in detail below.

The Map Layer

The map layer is the map itself, without any annotations or additions,
zoomed in on a particular location in the world. You can scroll to
view any region of the world.

The map layer displayed by Family Historian is provided by OpenStreetMap
(see https://www.openstreetmap.org).

Markers

A marker is a little coloured icon like this or this
(different shapes and colours are supported) that Family Historian will
place on a map, to mark a place or an address - such as, the place or
address where an event occurred. See the Map
Window for more information about markers and how they are used.

Marker Text

You can optionally display text for any marker. To do this,
right-click on the map and make sure that the option "Display Marker Text"
is ticked. You can change the font and font size used for marker
text in the Preferences
Dialog: Map Window tab. The text displayed is the first
comma-separated part of the Place or Address text (or the whole text if it
does not contain commas).

Shapes

A shape is a kind of annotation that can be added to a map. They are
comparable to shapes that can be added to diagrams (see Diagram
Elements), although there are some important differences.
There are 4 types of map shapes. These are:

Text Boxes (with optional callout lines)

Polylines

Polygons

Circles

Map shapes always appear in front of the map layer, but always appear
behind markers. To learn more about shapes, and all the things you
can do with them, see Add and Edit Shapes.

title: Map Overlays Dialog
text:
Map Window

Map Overlays Dialog

Map Overlays Dialog

An overlay is a saved collection of shapes (text boxes,
polylines, polygons, and circles - as well as groups of any and all of
these) that can be added to a map. You can use overlays to mark the
positions of countries, counties (including historic borders and counties
that no longer exist). You can also use them to mark locations (even
down to the level of houses or grave plots) on maps - and use text boxes
to annotate these locations (with callout lines if required). You
can add overlays to any map. When you save a map that contains
overlays, the overlays are saved as part of the map.

Family Historian provides a number of standard overlays but you can create
your own custom overlays. You can even import overlays, downloaded
from the Internet, in a standard map format (geoJSON).

Any overlays you create or import, can be used with any map in any
project.

Whereas a saved map is saved as part of a particular project (maps can
include markers which are project-specific), a saved overlay is not
associated with any particular project. Overlays are available to be
used with any project. Also, you cannot work on a saved
overlay and save your changes, in the same way that you can with a saved
map. If you want to make changes to a saved overlay, add it to a map
which contains no shapes. Then make whatever changes you want and
save your changes using the "Save Map Overlay..." command on the
right-click menu. You will be required to specify a name for the
overlay. If you specify the name of an existing custom overlay, you
will be asked if you want to replace it.

To learn more about adding and editing the shapes that make up an overlay,
see Add and Edit Shapes.

Buttons

Open

Opens the overlay in the Map Window

Rename

Rename the selected overlay

Description

View or edit the description for the selected overlay. You
can only edit the description for custom overlays.

Simplifiy

Opens the Simplify Map Overlays dialog to allow
overlays to be simplified. Only custom overlays can be
simplified; but if you want to simplify a standard overlay, you
can use the 'Clone' command to make a custom copy of the standard
overlay, and simplify that.

The reason that you might want to simplify an overlay is if it
contains more detail than is needed, and the unneeded detail is
making the overlay slow to load and unresponsive. This is
most likely to happen if you import an overlay from the Internet,
in geoJSON format. Some of these overlays can be very slow
to load, unless you simplify them.

An overlay can be simplified by removing intermediate polygon
nodes which are less than some distance apart (in miles) which you
specify. You can also remove any polygons which have an
overall size that is less than a value (in miles again) that you
specify.

It is usually a good idea to make a copy of the overlay that you
plan to simplify, and try simplifying that. It may take a
few trials before you find a satisfactory balance between detail
and performance.

As well as allowing you to simplify complex overlays, the Simplify
Maps Overlay dialog also has an Overlay
Statistics button which, if pressed, gives statistics
about the number of polygons and nodes in the selected overlay.

Clone

Make a copy of the selected overlay

Delete

Delete the selected overlay(s). Only custom overlays can
be deleted.

Import

Use this option to import overlays. Overlays can be
imported from files which are either in Family Historian Map
Overlay format, or in geoJSON format. The latter is a
standard format, widely available on the Internet.

Export

Use this option to export a selected overlay in Family Historian
Map Overlay format. Exported overlays can be shared with
others (for example, on the Family
Historian User Group website).

title: Map Shape Format Dialog
text:
Map Window

Map Shape Format Dialog

The Map Shape Format dialog allows you to change the options for one or
more selected shapes. For tips on changing the options for
multiple shapes at the same time, see Formatting
Shapes (Single and Multiple) section in Add
and Edit Shapes.

The Map Shape Format dialog shows different information, and different
tabs, depending on what shapes are selected when you open it. The
possible tabs are:

Text Tab

Callout Tab

Shape Tab

title: Map Shape Format Dialog: Callout Tab
text:
Map Shape Format Dialog

Map Shape Format Dialog: Callout Tab

Fields

Enable Callout Line
Tick this box if you wish to display a callout line,
connecting the text box to the text anchor. The
text anchor marks the exact location on the map, that fixes the
position of a text box. When you zoom in and out, the text
box size may change or appear to move (see the discussion of the
Reference Zoom in the Text tab, for the reasons for this), but the
text anchor will always remain at the same latitude and
longitude. When a text box is selected, the text anchor is
displayed as a little yellow circle. You can click-and-drag
on this circle to move it.

If Enable Callout Line is ticked, the callout line will
be displayed whenever the text anchor is moved to a position
outside the text box. If the text anchor is located within
the text box, clicking Enable Callout Line has no effect.

Callout Line Options: End Style
When displaying a callout line, this option allows you to
specify how the line ends. The options are:

None (that is, the line just ends, with no special end
feature)

Arrow thin (the line ends in an arrow head, drawn with
lines only)

Arrow thick (the line ends in an arrow head, drawn as solid
triangle)

Circle (the line ends in a filled circle)

Callout Line Options: End Size
Specifies the size of line end feature if any (see previous).

Fix Text Anchor

The text anchor displays as a yellow circle. If you add a
new text box, the text anchor will be in the top-left corner of
the text box. If you click-and-drag on a text to move it,
the text anchor initially will move with the box. This is
because its position is not yet 'fixed'. You can
click-and-drag on the text anchor itself to reposition it.
Whenever you move the text anchor on its own, in this way, it
becomes 'fixed'. That is to say, thereafter, when you move
the text box, the text anchor will not move and will stay where
you put it. You can still click-and-drag on the text
anchor to move it on its own if you want to.

You can override these default behaviours by explicitly
specifying whether the text anchor should be 'fixed' or
not. That is what the Fix Text Anchor
field is for.

Tip: Regardless of the state of the Fix
Text Anchor check box, text anchors will always move
with the text box if the text box is part of a group of shapes,
and the whole group is moved.

title: Map Shape Format Dialog: ShapeTab
text:
Map Shape Format Dialog

Map Shape Format Dialog: Shape Tab

Fields

Fill Colour
Fill colour of the selected shape(s).

Fill Opacity
Fill opacity of the selected shape(s).

Line Colour
Line colour of the selected shape(s).

Line Opacity
Line opacity of the selected shape(s).

Line Width
Line width of the selected shape(s).

Locked
Tick this option to lock the selected shape or shapes.
Locked shapes are treated as if they are part of the map layer
(see Map Elements), unless the
Access button on the Map
Window Toolbar is pressed). See Locking
Shapes section of Add and
Edit Shapes for more information about locking shapes.

Circle Radius
This field is only displayed if one or more circles are
selected, and no shapes of any other kind. It shows the
approximate radius of the selected circle(s) in whatever
units are used with the map viewer (miles or kilometres).
Map units are specified in Preferences:
Map Window Tab.

Line Length
This read-only field is only displayed if one or more
single-segment lines are selected, and no shapes of any other
kind. It shows the approximate length of the selected
line(s). Again, the unit of distance (miles or kilometres)
is the whatever is used with the map viewer. Map units are
specified in Preferences:
Map Window Tab.

title: Map Shape Format Dialog: Text Tab
text:
Map Shape Format Dialog

Map Shape Format Dialog: Text Tab

Fields

Text
The actual text that will be displayed in the text box

Align
Specifies whether the text should horizontally aligned on the
centre of the text box, or on its left or right sides.

Vertical Align
Specifies whether the text should be vertically aligned on the
middle of the text box, or at the top or bottom.

Font
Choose the font to be used for the text box. You can also
specify the font size in points (subject to the Reference Zoom -
see below), its colour, and (depending on the font), whether it is
bold, oblique, italicized; and also on whether it should be
displayed 'struck out' or underlined.

Inner Margins
Specifies the inner margins around the text, within the text
box.

Reference Zoom

The Map Window can be zoomed in and out. There are 21
levels of zoom, numbered 0 to 20. Think of zoom level 0 as
not zoomed in at all. At this level, you see the whole
world. Every time you zoom in, the zoom level goes up by 1
and the amount of area displayed is a quarter of the previous
level (half the distance vertically and half the distance
horizontally). This means that more and more details
become visible. Level 20 is fully zoomed-in - i.e.
zoomed-in 20 times. At this level you can see street
names, and details of houses.

When you create a text box, you specify the font size you
want. This font size is calculated with respect to a
particular zoom level. For example, if you choose a 10
point font size, with a reference zoom level of 6, this means
that the font will display at 10 point when the zoom level is
6. One consequence of this is that if text boxes behaved
like other shapes do, and zoomed in and out in sync with the map
layer in the normal way, it would follow that text which is
comfortably readable when you are fully zoomed-in, would be so
small that it would disappear completely when you zoom
out. Conversely, text that was easily readable at, say,
zoom level 1, would appear to be too big to fit on the screen,
as you zoom in. If this is not what you want, and it often
isn't, you can prevent it happening, and minimize text zooming,
by enabling the option Minimize Text Zooming on the
Map Window tab of the Preferences
dialog. When this option is ticked, which it is by
default, text boxes will display at the size you created them,
not just when the map is at the reference zoom level of the
text, but even when zoomed in further. So, for example, if a
text box was created at zoom level 12, with a point size 10
font, the text box will remain the same size, and the text
itself, will remain at point size 10, as you zoom in - to zoom
levels 13, 14, 15, etc ... all the way to zoom level 20.

What happens, if you have ticked Minimize Text Zooming,
and you zoom out? The answer depends on another option:
the Text Zoom Margin field. This value (normally
0, 1 or 2) is only used if you have opted to minimize text
zooming. In that case, the text box will display at its original
size until you zoom the map out past a certain point, when it
will start to shrink. The point at which it will start to shrink
is when the current zoom level of the map is less than the
reference zoom level of the text box, minus the Text Box
Margin. The reason for this, when text zooming is
minimized, is to allow a degree of latitude before text boxes
start to get smaller as you zoom out. A value of 2 for
example (the default), means that you can zoom out twice before
a text box will start to get smaller.

If you choose not to minimize text zooming, text boxes will
appear bigger or smaller when you zoom in or out, like any other
map shape.

For more information, see the descriptions for these options in
Preferences dialog
page.

Tip: The current zoom level is displayed at any
given time, in the status bar of the Map Window. It is
also displayed in the text tab of the Map Shape Format dialog,
next to the Reference Zoom field.

title: Map Window Legend
text:
Map Window

Map Window Legend

The following images are displayed next to events and Place records in the
List Pane, and show the status of the geocoding for the place
or address information. Geocoding is the process of determining the
latitude and longitude for a given place or address. See Map
Window for more details about geocoding, maps, and the List Pane.

Family Historian supports both automatic and manual geocoding for places,
but only manual geocoding for addresses. Also, place geocodes can be
marked as 'tentative'. This option is not available for address
geocodes.

Icon
Meaning

Geocoded (i.e. has a latitude and longitude)

Geocoded and marked on the map*

Places only. Geocoded, but flagged as tentative (geocoding
may be wrong and should be checked). By default, all
geocoding which is done automatically is marked as tentative.

Places only. Geocoded, but flagged as tentative, and
marked on the map*

Places only. Automatic geocoding failed. Place was
not found.

Places only. Blocked. Means "do not auto-geocode".

Places only. Automatic geocoding in progress

* 'Marked on the map' does not mean that the marker can necessarily be
seen. It may be scrolled off-screen. Also, if the time
slider is enabled, the marker may be hidden from view by the
time slider. Clicking the View All Markers
button on the Map
toolbar, will zoom the map to show all markers that are not hidden
by the time slider.

To say that an item is 'geocoded' does not necessarily mean that it has
been automatically geocoded. It just means that it has
a latitude and longitude - supplied by whatever means. Any geocode
for a place can be flagged as tentative, whether automatically geocoded
or not. By default, automatic geocoding will always flag a geocode
as tentative. But you can opt to flag all automatic geocodes as
(initially) tentative only if they are deemed to be "partial or
uncertain" if you wish. This is an option in Preferences (Map
Window tab).

Tip: To change the status of a geocoded place (e.g. to mark
it as tentative or not), right-click on the item and, on the popup menu
that appears, choose "Geocoding" and then "Mark as Tentative" or "Unmark
as Tentative". This only works with places. You cannot mark
an address as 'tentative'.

In an Individual & Events marker set (see Map
Window), the icons shown above may be shown both next to events,
and also next to the Individual records that the events are listed
'below' (to see the events for an Individual, you have to click on the
expansion button
at the start of the Individual's row). The icons, when appearing
next to the Individual, have the same meaning as they have when shown
next to their events (i.e. as shown in the table above) except that they
apply collectively to all the events associated with the
Individual. If some but not all of the events for a given
Individual, are marked on the map, an icon showing an intermediary value
( or ) will be
displayed next to the Individual. If an Individual has no events
or facts (or none which have any place information) no icon will be
displayed next to the Individual.

Tip: With Place and Address marker sets you can opt to sort
the whole set by geocode status; so that ungeocoded items, tentative
items, blocked items, and geocoded items are all grouped
together. This makes them much easier to find, and is
particularly useful if, say, you want to check all geocodes flagged as
'Tentative'. To do this, ensure that the relevant Place or Address
marker set is the currently active one in the Marker List Pane, then
click the More button above the list, and
choose "Sort by Geocode Status (ungeocoded first)".

title: The Map Window
text:
Workspace Windows

The Map Window

The Map Window (marked in red)

To open the Map Window click on the Map Window button on the main application
toolbar. A dropdown menu appears with options for displaying maps
in the Map Window. If a Map Window is already open, it
will normally be re-used - unless you have specified in Preferences (Workspaces tab) that
you do not want Map Windows to be re-used, or unless you open a saved
map or overlay, both of which will be displayed in a new instance of the
Map Window.

Terminology: The descriptions below make reference to geocoding
and marker sets. If either of these concepts are
unfamiliar to you, you are recommended to read the Geocoding
and/or Marker Sets sections
below, before reading other sections.

The available menu commands are these:

Map Window
Opens the Map Window. If a new Map Window is opened, the List
Pane (see below) which displays marker sets, will initially show
no marker sets.

Map Individuals & Events...

Creates a marker set for all or selected Individuals. The
marker set will show, for each Individual, all the locations that
they are associated with, if any. Every event can be
associated with a place, an address or both. You will be
able to choose between locating places only, addresses only, or
addresses preferred. If you choose this last option, the
location of the address will be used if known. If not, the
location of the associated place will be used if known.

Map Places...
Creates a marker set for all or selected Place records.
Place records which have been geocoded (assigned a latitude and
longitude) will have a marker on the map. Place records are
normally geocoded automatically. However, if the location of
one or more of the referenced places is not known, you can geocode
it yourself (i.e. assign a latitude and longitude to it) by
dragging-and-dropping from the list on the left-hand side, onto
the appropriate map location, on the right.

Map Addresses...
Creates a marker set for all or selected Address records.
Address records which have been geocoded (assigned a latitude and
longitude) will have a marker on the map. Address records
are not geocoded automatically. If the location of one or
more of the Address records is not known, you can drag-and-drop
the Address text, from the list on the left-hand side, onto its
map location, to geocode it. Alternatively, right-click on the
address in the list and choose "Locate in Map". You will be
asked if you wish to zoom to the location of the Place record
associated with the Address record, or to search the map for the
address name.

Map Overlays

Opens the Map Overlays Dialog.

Saved Maps

Opens the Saved Maps Dialog.

The Map Window has its own menu (Mapping) and
toolbar (Map Toolbar), both of which
are only available when the Map Window is active. The window is
divided vertically into 2 areas, separated by a dividing line. The area on
the left is called the List Pane. The area on
the right is called the Map Viewer. The
partition line between the List Pane and the the Map Viewer can be moved.
Move your cursor over the partition line and click-and-drag to reposition
it.

The List Pane and the Map Viewer will be discussed in more detail below.

See Place Records and Address
Records to learn more about Place and Address records, and how they
are used.

Marker Sets

A marker is a little coloured icon like this or this .
Numerous different icon types are available in different colours.
Family Historian will place markers on a map, to mark either a place or
an address - such as, the place or address where an event
occurred. A marker set is a collection of records and
their associated markers. Each Map Window can have, and can
display, as many marker sets as you want. These are shown in the
marker set list in the top-left of the Map Window. Each
marker set uses a single type of marker only - that is to say, all
markers for any given marker set, look the same. Suppose you want
to mark all places for events associated with your father and his
ancestors using a blue marker, and all places for events associated with
your mother and her ancestors with a red marker. To do this, you
need two marker sets: one marker set for your father and his ancestors,
with a blue marker, and another marker set for your mother and her
ancestors, with a red marker.

Often when you open the Map Window, you will at the same time create a
new marker set. If you are re-using an existing Map Window, this
new marker set will be added to whatever existing marker sets it already
has. You can also add a marker set to a Map Window by clicking on
the Add Set button on the toolbar below the
marker set list.

There are 3 types of marker sets:

Individuals & Events marker sets

Places marker sets

Addresses marker sets

The Individual event marker set type has 3 subtypes: "places only",
"addresses only", or "addresses preferred". The table below
describes the various marker set types and subtypes:

Marker Set Type (and subtype)

"Type" Column of Marker Set List

Description

Individuals & Events (places only)

Events (place)

Shows a 2-level list of individuals and the events (or facts
generally) associated with them that have an associated Place
record (whether geocoded or not). In each case, if the
associated Place record has been geocoded, the place will be
marked on the map.

Note: events which have no specified place will not be listed.

Individuals & Event (addresses only)

Events (address)

Shows a 2-level list of individuals and the events (or facts
generally) associated with them that have an associated Address
record (whether geocoded or not). In each case, if the
associated Address record has been geocoded, the address will be
marked on the map.

Note: events which have no specified address will not be
listed.

Individuals & Events (addresses preferred)

Events (addr/place)

Shows a 2-level list of individuals and the events (or facts
generally) associated with them that have either an associated
Address record or an associated Place record or both (whether
either or both have been geocoded or not). In each case, if
there is an associated Address record and it has been geocoded,
the address will be marked on the map. Failing that, if
there is an associated Place record and it has been geocoded, the
place will be marked on the map.

Note: events which have neither a specified address nor a
specified place will not be listed.

Places

Places

Shows a list of Place records. In each case, if the Place
record has been geocoded, the place will be marked on the map.

Addresses

Addresses

Shows a list of Address records. In each case, if the
Address record has been geocoded, the address will be marked on
the map.

Finding a Marker

As can be seen from the table above, markers are associated with events,
places and addresses. With an Individual event marker set,
you will need to click the little '+' to the left of the Individuals name,
to see their associated events. If an individual has no '+' next to
their name, it means that they have no associated events - or none that
meet the requirements of the marker set subtype. For example, an
event which has no associated address will not be listed in an 'Addresses
only' marker set.

To see the marker associated with a listed event, place or address, click
on the listed item. A Popup Marker Window will be displayed, showing
events associated with the location. If the item has been geocoded
(has a latitude and longitude), and is visible in the Map Viewer, the
Popup Marker Window will be white and will point to the item's exact
location on the map. If the item has been geocoded (has a latitude
and longitude), but is not visible in the Map Viewer because it is
scrolled off-screen (e.g. if the Map Viewer is showing an area of Europe
and the item is in North America), a brown-coloured Popup Marker Window
will be displayed with a Scroll to View
button. If you click on this button, the map will scroll until the
exact location of the item can be shown using a white Popup Marker
Window. If the item has not been geocoded, a brown Popup Marker
Window will be displayed with the text "Not geocoded" in red. There
will also be a Locate button next to
it. Click this button for options to help you locate the item on the
map.

For more on the Popup Marker Window, see Popup
Marker Window below.

Although two Place records can have the exact same latitude and longitude,
the actual place name that they are associated with is guaranteed to be
unique. You cannot give exactly the same place name to two Place
records. So each Place record always gets its own marker. The
same is true of Address records. The same is not true of events
associated with Individuals, however. Any number of events can have
happened at the same place. So within an Individual &
Events marker set, all events that happened at the same place,
will share a single marker.
Geocoding

Before we can mark a Place or Address record on a map, we must first
determine its latitude and longitude. This process is called geocoding.
By default, Family Historian will automatically geocode all Place
records that are either listed, or referred to, in the current marker
set. Automatic geocoding requires an Internet connection, and uses
an Internet geocoding service*. While geocoding is in progress,
you may see a little clock icon next to each place being geocoded.
Address records are not automatically geocoded.

You do not need to use automatic geocoding. You can 'manually'
set the latitude and longitude for both places and addresses if
you wish. There are 3 different ways you can do this:

Open the Place or Address record in the Property Box and enter the
desired latitude and longitude into the Lat./Long.
field. If you have copied a latitude and longitude to the
clipboard, you can paste it in here. A wide variety of formats
for latitude and longitude are recognised and supported. There
is also a Helper dialog for this field, to help you to enter latitude
and longitude information if you wish to (to open it, click on the
little button with 3 dots at the end of the field, or double-click on
the field itself).

If a given Place or Address has already been geocoded and marked on
the map, and you wish to move the marker, click on the Enable
Marker Dragging button on the Map
toolbar. When marker dragging is enabled, you can
click-and-drag on any marker to move it. This updates the
geocoding (the latitude and longitude) in the Place or Address record.

Alternatively, click-and-drag on any place, address or event in the
List Pane, and drag it onto the Map Viewer. If the item you drag
is a place, the Place record's latitude and longitude will be set at
the location where you 'drop' it. If the item you drag is an
address, the Address record's latitude and longitude will be set at
the location where you 'drop' it. If the item you drag is an
event, you might be trying to geocode either the place or the address
associated with the event. In that case, you will be prompted to
specify which of these you are geocoding.

Yet another option is to use a plugin (possibly one downloaded from the
Plugin Store) to geocode some or all Place or Address records.

See the Map
Window Legend for an explanation of the meaning of the icons used
to display geocoding status information in the List Pane.

The List Pane

As stated earlier, the Map Window is divided vertically into 2 areas,
separated by a dividing line, called the List Pane
and the Map Viewer respectively. The
List Pane has a Marker Set List at the top, and below
that, an Item List, which shows the list of items
associated with the currently selected marker set (if any). If the
Marker Set List is empty, or if there is no marker set selected, the
Item List will be blank.

The Marker Set List

The Marker Set List has its own toolbar, at the bottom of the list,
with the following toolbar command options:

Add Set

Click on this option to add additional marker sets to the
list. You will be able to specify the name of the marker
set, its type, marker, and the records associated with the marker
set.

Edit

Edit the selected marker set.

Copy the selected marker set.

Paste the selected marker set.

Delete the selected marker set.

Move the selected marker(s) set up the
list.

Move the selected marker(s) set down the
list.

Shows a dropdown menu with these menu
commands:

Show Marker Set(s) - The selected marker set(s) are made
visible if they had been hidden.

Hide Marker Set(s) - The selected marker set(s) are made
hidden if they had been visible.

When a marker set is hidden, no markers for that set will be
display on the map and the Item List will be blank when the marker
set is selected.

Visible marker sets have a tick in the 'Visible' column of the
Marker Set List. Hidden ones do not.

You can also right-click on any item in the Marker Set List to see a
menu with similar options.

The Item List

The Item List will be blank if no marker set is selected in the Marker
Set List, or if the selected marker set has been hidden. Depending
on the type of the selected marker set, the Item List will display
individuals & events, places or addresses.

Any geocoded items in the list will have a check box on the left side
of the list, which may or may not be ticked. For places, addresses
and events, a check box means that the item has been geocoded (either
manually or automatically) - that is to say, it has a specified latitude
and longitude. If the check box is ticked, the item is marked on
the map with a marker. Depending on which part of the map is being
displayed in the Map Viewer, the map may be scrolled off-screen

In an Individual & Events marker set, individuals may also have
check boxes, and these too may or may not be ticked. If an
individual has a check box, this means that he or she has one or more
events which fit the criteria of the market set, and which have been
geocoded - which is to say, has one or more events which have a check
box (you may have to click the '+' next to the Individual's name, to see
these events). If the individual's check box is ticked, it means that
all of the associated event check boxes are also ticked. If the
individual's check box is not ticked, it means that none of the
associated event check boxes are ticked. If the individual's check
box contains a black square, this is an intermediary state, which means
that one or more, but not all, of the associated event check boxes are
ticked.

At the top of the Item List are the following check boxes and buttons:

Check All

Click on this to check or uncheck all the items in the Item List
that have a check box. This in turn will show or hide all
the related markers (athough, again, markers may be scrolled
off-screen).

Expand All/

Collapse All

Always greyed unless the selected marker is an "Individuals
& Events" marker set type. In that case, it will cause
the tree to be fully expanded, so that all events associated with
the listed individuals (which match the criteria of the marker
set), are displayed. If the tree is already fully expanded,
the text will switch to 'Collapse All' and it will cause all
expanded branches to be closed.

Event Options

Always greyed unless the selected marker is an "Individuals
& Events" marker set type. In that case, it can be used to
specify which event types to show (or hide) markers for. So
if you only want to see markers for death events (say), you would
untick all event types, except 'Death'.

You can also use Event Options to change the subtype of the marker
set - i.e. to determine whether, for each event, to display
places, address or 'address preferred'.

Records
Used to modify the items in the marker set. For an
Individuals & Events marker set, you will be able to select
from a list of Individual records. For a Places marker set,
this will be a list of Place records. And for an Addresses
marker set, this will be a list of Address records.

More
Displays a dropdown menu with the following menu commands:

Check Selection

Uncheck Selection

Show Address Markers for Selected Place(s)

Reverse Display Order

Show Popup on Place or Address Selection

The first 2 menu commands will check or uncheck the rows which are
selected and which have check boxes. If none of the selected
rows have check boxes, these menu commands will be greyed.

The menu command, Show Address Markers for Selected Place(s),
shows all markers for addresses associated with the selected
places - if there are addresses and if they have been
geocoded. You can optionally hide all other markers
first. The addresses will automatically be added to a marker
set for addresses called "Associated Addresses". "Selected
places", in this context, just means the selected items, if the
item list is showing a list of places. If the item list is
showing a list of addresses, it means the places (if any)
associated with the selected addresses. If the item list is
showing a list of individuals and events, and the selection
includes one or more events, "selected places" means the places
(if any) associated with those events. If the selection
includes one or more individuals, it means the places (if any)
associated with the events linked to the selected individuals.

The menu command, Reverse Display Order, is applicable
to Places and Addresses marker sets only. If the place or
address name has comma-separated parts, these will be
reversed. It has no effect on place or addresses which do
not contain commas.

The menu command, Show Popup on Place or Address Selection,
which is ticked by default, will cause the Popup
Marker Window to be displayed, whenever you select a place
or address.

The Map Viewer

The Map Viewer is the name for the area on the right side of the Map
Window, where the map is displayed. It has the following components:

Address Bar and Go To button

If you wish to find a place in the map, enter the place name in
the Address bar (to the right of the 'Location' label) and press
the Go To button
to the right of the list. If matches are found, a dropdown
list of options will be displayed.

Address Bar Menu

This is the menu that appears when you
click on the 'cog' button
to the right of the address bar. The menu choices are:

View in Google Maps (web)

View in Bing Maps (web)

View in Open Street Map (web)

Options

The first 3 menu items allow you to view the current map in an
external web browser, using Google, Bing or Open Street Map.

The last menu item, "Options", takes you to the "Map Window" tab
of Preferences, where you can view and edit Map Window options.

Map

This is the map component itself. There are numerous ways
of zooming in, out, and around the map. The map has its own
on-screen zoom control, and 'rose' in the top-left corner which
can be used to reposition and zoom the map. You can also use
your mouse wheel, and arrow keys to zoom, or move around - but
first click on the map itself to ensure that the mouse wheel
action, and keyboard presses, are directed to the map, and not to
some other component of the Map Window. When you zoom using
the mouse wheel, the map is sensitive to the current position of
the mouse pointer, which is maintained throughout the zoom.

You are recommended to learn how to use the various buttons on the
Map Window toolbar that are
related to zooming and position the map - especially the View
Home Region button , the View All
Markers button ,
and the View World button .

Time Slider

The Time Slider is hidden when you first open the Map
Window. To enable it, click on the Time Slider button
on the toolbar. The Time Slider is used to hide or show
places associated with Individuals and events at given
dates. To use it, you must have at least one marker set of
the Individuals & Places type. The Time Slider
has no useful role with marker sets which just show the location
of (undated) Place records.

When enabled, the Time Slider control is displayed at the bottom
of the Map Viewer, below the map. It causes all dated
markers to be hidden if they do not fall within the start and end
dates of the Time Slider. You can specify in the Map
Window tab of Preferences, whether you wish undated markers
to be hidden or not. Click-and-drag on the Time Slider to
move the date range. You can also separately move the start
and end dates, to extend or shrink the range.

Popup Marker Window

The Map Viewer has a Popup Marker Window which appears
whenever you click on a marker, on the map. It will also be
displayed whenever you select a place or address in the Item List, if the
option Show Popup on Place or Address Selection, is ticked
(which by default it is).

Every marker on the map is associated with either a Place record or an
Address record. If the marker is associated with a Place record, the
Popup Marker Window will show the Place record name at the top - as in
figure 1 below.

Figure 1. Popup Marker Window showing Place Record

In figure 1, the Place record name at the top is "Liverpool
England". This is a link. Click on it to view the Place record
in the Property Box. The list is a
list of all the events associated with the place if it's a Place
Record marker set, or a list of all the selected events
associated with the place if it's an Individual & Events marker
set.

If the marker is associated with an Address record, the Popup
Marker Window will show the Address record name at the top, with the Place
record name that the Address is linked to shown in a grey rectangle below
it. This is illustrated in figure 2 below.

Figure 2. Popup Marker Window showing an Address record

In figure 2, the Address record name at the top is "Bristol Royal
Infirmary". This is a link. Click on it to view the Address
record in the Property Box. Address
records are associated with Place records. The Place record name is
always shown in a grey box, below the Address record name. The Place
record name in this case is not a link.

The list in figure 2 is a list of all the events associated with the
address if it's an Address Record marker set, or a list of all
the selected events associated with the address if it's an Individual
& Events marker set.

The list shows a list of all the events associated with the place if it's
a Place Record marker set, or a list of all the selected
events associated with the place if it's an Individual & Places marker
set (which it is, in this example).

Popup Marker Window Toolbar

The toolbar below the list has 3 buttons:

The Find Event In List button is used with Individual
& Places marker sets only (it is greyed otherwise) and
locates the currently selected event in the current marker set
listing.

The Menu button
displays a small menu (see below).

The Locate In Property Box button locates the currently
selected event in the Property Box.

The menu has the following commands:

Find Place/Address in List

If the current marker set is a Place Record marker
set, this will select the place in the marker set listing on the
left-hand side. If the current marker set is an Address
Record marker set, this will select the address in the
marker set listing on the left-hand side. If the current
marker set is an Individual & Events marker set,
this will select all the events in the current marker set,
associated with this place or address (expanding entries for
Individuals as necessary, if the relevant events are not showing).

Show Place/Address in Property Box
This has the same effect as clicking on the name link at the top
of the Popup Marker Window. It causes the relevant Place or
Address record to be displayed in the Property
Box

Centre Map Here
Moves the map so that the current
marker is in the centre of the window. Use the slider below
the 'rose' in the top-left corner to zoom in and out on this
point, without moving the map at all.

List Selected Events at this Location
This option is only available when the current marker set is an
Individual & Events type. If ticked, only events
associated with the current marker set are listed in the Popup
Marker Window.

List All Events at this Location
If this option is ticked, all events associated with the current
marker set are listed in the Popup Marker Window.

* See Family
Historian Map Search and Geocoding for information about service
providers. All features which use Internet services provided by
third parties (such as automatic geocoding) are subject to the
availability of those services.

Popup Marker Window Variants

As we have seen, whenever you select a place or address in the Item
List, if the option Show Popup on Place or Address Selection,
is ticked (which by default it is) the Popup Marker Window will display
to show the location of the selected place or address. Or rather,
it will do that if the selected place or address is geocoded. If
it is not geocoded, the Popup Marker cannot indicate the position on the
map of the place or address as this is not known. In this case,
the appearance of the Popup Marker Window will be slightly different
from usual. It will have a brown background (by default - this is
configurable) rather than a white background. And it will not have
a little 'tail' pointing to any position on the map, as it usually does
(see images above). Instead it will have a caption bar which
you can click-and-drag on to move the window. And it will appear
in the centre of the window, or wherever you last moved it (in its
variant mode) in the current session. It will have text at the top
of the window that sayscn red. And it will have 2 buttons: Locate... and Set.
The Locate... button has options to help
you search the map, to find the Place or Address. And the Set
button can be used to set the latitude and longitude of the Place or
Address to the map centre (indicated by crosshairs).

Tip: Instead of using the Set
button, you can alternatively click-and-drag the list item onto the map
viewer. When you release the map button, it will prompt you to set
the latitude and longitude to that point on the map. You can also
use this technique to update the latitude and longitude of an item that
has already been geocoded.

The Popup Marker Window will also appear in a variant form if
you click on an item which has been geocoded but where the map location
is not visible in the map viewer at its current position. In that
case, the Popup Marker Window will again have a brown background and a
caption bar; but there will be no text saying "not
geocoded" (because the item is geocoded), and there will also
be no Locate... and Set
buttons (because these are used to help with geocoding, which is not
required in this case). Instead there will be a Scroll
into View button. Click on this button to scroll the map
to bring the item's location into view in the map viewer.

title: Media Records
text:
Record Types

Media Records

Media records are identified by this icon: .
When you add a picture, video, sound file, document file, or OLE object
into a Family Historian project, a Media record is automatically created
to represent that media item within the project. In fact you can treat
any external file (including a GEDCOM file) as a Media item if you wish
to, and when you add it to the project, a Media record will be created
to represent it.

Media records store file links to the media file (the file which holds
the actual picture, video, or whatever it is). The media file can be
kept within the project folder, or it can be located elsewhere. In
general, it is advisable if possible to keep all media files in the
project folder - doing so will make your project much more manageable
and portable.

Media records are created when you use any of the following menu
commands on the Add Menu:

(Add) Document…

(Add) Pictures…

(Add) Picture from Clipboard > Paste Copied Citation

(Add) OLE Object…

(Add) Other Media…

They are also created if you add media items in the
Media tab of the Property Box, or on the Media
Viewer (shows media linked to facts primarily).

If you wish to add links from a picture or some other media item, to
other records, you can do this when viewing the Media record in the Media Window (see, in
particular, the Media Link Tool, which is designed to
help make this as easy as possible), or in the Links tab of the Property
Box when viewing Media records in the Property Box.

Tabs for Media records in the Property Box:

Main
(for Media)

Links

All

title: Media Viewer
text:
Property Box

Media Viewer

The Media Viewer

The Media Viewer is a floating window
that is opened by clicking on the Show Media button on the toolbar of the Facts
tab of the Property Box. It shows all media for the
currently selected fact, or for the currently selected source
citation. For example, it might show all pictures taken at a
wedding or at a christening. If you change the selected fact in
the Facts tab, the dialog will automatically update itself
appropriately.

When showing media for the currently selected source citation (selected
in the Citation List Pane),
additional tick boxes at the top will appear to allow you to choose
between viewing "Source Record Media" and "Citation Media".

Tip: If a fact has media, it will display the media
icon
in the right-hand column of the Fact List in the Facts
tab of the Property Box. A quick way to open the Media
Viewer is to click on this icon.

Buttons

Item
Description

Add Media for Fact

or

Add Media for Source Record / Citation
Displays a dropdown menu with these options:

Insert from File

Link to Existing Media record

Paste Copied Image

In the first and last case, a new Media record is created to
represent the media item being added. In all 3 cases, the
media item in question is linked to the current fact (or Source
record or citation). If you use the Insert from File command,
you can add multiple media items (e.g. multiple pictures) in one
go, and link them all to the current fact.

Edit

Edit the selected media item in the Edit
Media Item Dialog.

Unlink/Delete
Delete or unlink a Media record. You will
be asked which you wish to do.

Move Up/Move Down
Change the ordering of the linked media items.

View
Shows options for displaying the selected media item in an
external player/viewer. You can also opt to view the selected
Media record in the Property Box. Another option allows you
to display all the media items shown in the dialog, in the
(workspace) Media Window.

Include Source Record Media
When displaying Fact media only. If ticked, and if there
are source citations for the current fact, media for all the
associated Source records will also be displayed. Note: The
Move Up/Down buttons are not applicable for these media items.

Include Citation Media
When displaying Fact media only. If ticked, and if there
are source citations for the current fact, media for all the
associated citations will also be displayed. Note: The Move
Up/Down buttons are not applicable for these media items.

Drag-and-Drop

The Media Viewer supports drag-and-drop. This can be a
quick and easy way of adding pictures. See Drag-and-Drop
for more details.

title: The Media Window
text:
Workspace Windows

The Media Window

The Media Window (marked in red)

The Media Window is opened by clicking on the Media button on the main application
toolbar. When you click on this button, a dropdown menu appears
with choices, determined in part by which record or records are
currently selected, as to which media records you wish to display (each
picture, or other media item, is represented by a Media record within
Family Historian). Typically, you may opt to display all media
records, or perhaps just pictures (and other media) that are
pictures of a given person or persons. But you may also
choose to see pictures (and other media) which are instead merely linked
(in various ways that you can choose) to a given person or persons.

The Media Window has its own menu and toolbar, both of which are only
available when the Media Window is active (see Media menu and Media
toolbar). The window is divided vertically into 2 areas,
separated by a vertical dividing line. The area on the left is called
the List Pane. The area on the right is
called the Display Pane. You can choose
to view both (the default), or just the List Pane, or just the Display
Pane (see the Media menu
and Media toolbar). When
displaying both, you can click-and-drag on the dividing line separating
them, to reposition it to suit your needs.

The List Pane

When first installed, the List Pane has one tab only: 'Media
List'. However, when the Media Link Tool is
enabled, it has two - the second tab being 'Media Link Tool'. Each
tab is discussed in turn:

List Pane Tab 1: The Media List

The Media List tab contains a list of Media records. Whichever
Media record is selected in the list, is displayed in the Display Pane
(if in Picture mode), or is shown selected (if in Thumbnail mode).
The Media List supports multiple selection.

Tip: you can add a keyword to any number of Media records
in one go, by selecting them all and then clicking 'Keywords' on the
Media menu. You can also add simple links to any number of Media
records at a time, by selecting them all, and then clicking 'Add Simple
Link' on the Media menu.

Initially the Media List tab displays the list of media records you
chose to view when you opened the Media Window; but you can change the
list displayed at any time, using the following fields (at the top of
the tab):

Media List

Displays 'Selected Media' if you have chosen a specific
selection of Media records. You can also select various
standard collections from the dropdown list. Click the Find button to the right, to display a
menu with extensive further options for selecting Media records,
using search expressions, queries, and other methods.

Keyword Filter

Each Media record can be associated with any number of
keywords. Use the keyword filter to restrict the list to
Media records that match the filter. This can be one
keyword, or several.

List Pane Tab 2: The Media Link Tool

To open the Media Link tool, click on the Media Link Tool button

on the Media toolbar. This button adds or removes a second tab to
the List Pane: the 'Media Link Tool' tab (not shown in the image above).

The Media Link Tool is a powerful tool that makes it very easy to
quickly add links from records of all kinds, to pictures (or other
media). It is, however, particularly useful if you want to add frame
links to pictures. The most common example of a
frame link is a face link - that is a link
from an Individual record to that person's face in a picture.
Frame links can however be used with other record types - and not just
with faces.

To use the Media Link tool, both the List Pane and the Display Pane
must be enabled, and the Display Pane must be in Picture
mode (see below). Choose the type of record you
wish to link to the Media record, using the Selector at the
top of the tab. You can also opt to view Named Lists, if you wish.

Whatever type of record you are listing, as long as it is a kind of
record that can be linked to a Media record, you can add a link from
that record to the picture/media item by selecting the record and
clicking one of the 2 buttons at the bottom of the tab (the Add
Frame Link to ... >> button or the Add
Simple Link to ... >> button). Alternatively, you
can simply click-and-drag on the record, and drop it onto the
picture/media item. When you do so, you will be asked if you wish
to create a simple link or a frame link.

If you are viewing a list of Individual records or Family records, and
you wish to add a link to an event (or other fact) associated with a
particular Individual or Family, you can do this too. Click on the
little box to the left of the record to expand it. You will see
all the fields that belong to that record. Click on the field for
the event (fact) in question, and then either drag-and-drop it onto the
picture/media item, or click the Add Simple Link
to ... >> button, to create a simple link.

When you are viewing a list of Individual records in the
Media Link Tool, an additional panel, called the Close
Relatives Panel, is displayed in the bottom-half of
the tab. You can click-and-drag on the dividing line that
separates the Close Relatives Panel from the list in the top-half of the
tab to increase or decrease the amount of space allocated to this panel.

The Close Relatives Panel shows close relatives of whoever is selected
in the list of Individual records in the top-half of the tab. This
is useful, and can save much searching, because frequently pictures
contain people who are closely related to one another. You can add
links to records in the Close Relatives Panel in exactly the same way
that you add links to records in the top-half of the tab - that is, by
using the Add Frame Link to ... >>
button or the Add Simple Link to ... >>
button, or by using drag-and-drop.

You can use the Close Relatives Panel to find any relative -
not just close relatives. Suppose, for example, that you are
viewing a picture of John Smith and his aunt, Mary Jones, who, let us
say, is the sister of his mother, Ann Jones. First select John
Smith in the list, and add a link to him. At this point, the Close
Relatives Pane will be showing a list of close relatives of John Smith,
which includes his mother. Select Ann Jones and click on the Show
Relatives Of button which is just to the right of
the 'Relatives of' field. This will cause the Close Relatives
Panel to display close relatives of Ann Jones, including her sister Mary
Jones. You can now link Mary Jones to the picture in the usual
way.

Using this technique, to 'navigate' from one relative to another, you
can find any relative of the starting person. You can also 'go
back' to a previous person, whose relatives you have viewed previously,
by selecting them from the dropdown list that appears if you click on
the down arrow, at the right end of the 'Relatives Of' field.

The Display Pane

The Display Pane, on the right side of the Media Window, has two modes:
Thumbnail Mode and Picture Mode.

Thumbnail Mode

In Thumbnail mode, the Display Pane shows one thumbnail image for each
