of the Media records listed in the Media List tab of the List
Pane. Selecting Media records in the Media List will cause their
thumbnail images to be selected in the Display pane. But equally,
selecting thumbnail images in the Display Pane, causes the same Media
records to be selected in the Media List.

Only one picture, or Media record, can be viewed at any one time, in
Picture Mode. To switch to Picture Mode, simply double-click on
any thumbnail, or click on the Toggle Picture/Thumbnail View
button
on the Media toolbar.

Picture Mode

In Picture Mode, the full picture (if the Media Record is a picture) is
displayed. In this mode, the Display Pane is divided into two
parts - and as usual, you can click-and-drag on the dividing line if you
wish. The top part is the Form Panel,
and the bottom part is the Viewer. The
picture is displayed in the Viewer.

The Form Panel has 2 tabs: 'Media Record' and 'Links'. These tabs
are very similar to the information that is displayed when you view a
Media record in the Property Box.

Form Panel Tab 1: Media Record

The Media Record tab is used to enter basic information about
a Media record - its title, date, keywords and a note.

Title

The title of the Media record. This can be whatever you
like.

Date

The date the Media item was created. In the case of
photos, this is the date that the photo was taken. It is a
good idea to provide this if possible, as it may be used later to
calculate other information - such as the ages of the Individuals
in the picture.

Keywords

Every Media record can have as many keywords as you like.
You can type them in to this field as a comma-separated list, or
you can click on the button with 3 dots, to the right side of the
Keywords field (when you move the mouse over the Keywords field or
click on it). When you do this, a Helper dialog appears and
you can choose Keywords from a list.

It is a good idea to associate keywords with Media records as you
can then use these keywords for filtering - see the Filter Pane
section above.

Note
This is a note that applies to the picture as a whole (not to be
confused with 'Link Notes' on the Links tab).

Tip: There are 2 useful links at the bottom of the Media
Record tab, labelled 'File' and 'Location' respectively. Clicking
on the first link opens the media file (the file on your hard disk
containing the media item) in an external viewer, and is the equivalent
of clicking on the Open Editor/Player button on the
toolbar. Clicking on the second link, the Location link, opens
File Explorer to display the media file in its location on your hard
disk. If the media file cannot be found on the hard disk, the
first link will display in red, prefixed by 'File not found - '.
In that case, clicking on the link will open a File Not Found
dialog box, with options for locating the missing media file - which
includes letting Family Historian search for the file for you.

FOrm Panel Tab 2: Links

The second tab of the Form Panel is the Links Tab. This displays
all records that are linked to the current Media record. If a
picture is linked to an event (or fact), the record that the event
belongs to will be listed in the first column, and the event will be
listed in the 'Detail' column.

You can add a note for each link. You can also view more details
about each link in the 'Flags' column. The icons in the Flags
column have the following meanings:

The link is a frame link. If not show, the link
is a simple link. You can convert a simple link to
a frame link by clicking on the 'Add Frame Only' button on the
toolbar (see below).

Exclude from diagrams and the Focus Window.

Exclude from reports, books and web-pages.

Do not let Family Historian generate a caption automatically for
this picture (or other media) when it is displayed in a report or
web-page. Instead use the associated annotation (if any) as the
caption.

The Links tab in the Form Panel is essentially the same as the Links
Tab in the Property Box. See that tab for more details of the
toolbar buttons, and fields.

title: Add Menu
text:
Menus

Add Menu

Parent
Create a new Individual
record, or link an existing Individual record, as a parent of the
currently selected person.

Spouse
Create a new Individual
record, or link an existing Individual record, as a spouse
of the currently selected person.

Child
Create a new Individual
record, or link an existing Individual record, as a child of
the currently selected person.

Unrelated Individual
Create a new Individual
record. You will usually only want to use this command to add a
record for someone who isn't related to anyone else in the current
project.

Into a Diagram ►

New Individual
Create a new unrelated Individual
record and display their box in a diagram in the Diagram
Window (so you can click-and-drag to add more relatives).

New Couple
Create two new unrelated Individual
records and display them as the joint root in a diagram in the Diagram Window (so you can
click-and-drag to add more relatives).

Note Record
Create a new Note record.

Research Note
Create a new Research Note.

Source/Citation ►
Options for creating a new Source
record (or opening an existing Source record) in the Citation
Window, with a view to creating a prepared citation.
This submenu is the same submenu that is displayed when you click
on the Source button on the main application toolbar. To
learn more, see Source-Driven
Data Entry, and also Citation
Window with a Prepared Citation.

Repository
Create a new Repository
record. Usually it is easier to create new Repository records when
supplying details for Source
records.

Document

Create a new Media record
linked to an external document file. You will be asked if you
wish to copy the document into the project folder, and you are
recommended to do so. The new Media record is displayed in the Media Window.

Pictures

Add one or more picture files to the project. A new Media
record will be created for each picture added. You will be asked
if you wish to copy the picture into the project folder, and you
are recommended to do so. The new Media records will be
displayed in the Media Window.

Picture from Clipboard ►

If you have previously copied a picture to the clipboard, you
can use the Paste Copied Citation menu command
to add it to the current project. A new Media
record will be created for the picture which will be displayed
in the Media Window. See Web Clipping to learn more.

OLE Object
Create a new Media record to
store information about an OLE object.

Other Media
Create a new Media record to
store information about a sound or video file, or indeed about any
kind of file. For example, if you wanted to link two family tree
projects together, you could 'add' the GEDCOM
file from one of them into the other as an 'Other Media' object.

title: Book Menu
text:
Menus

Book Menu

This menu is only available when the Book
Window is active.

Rebuild Book

If you have changed the underlying data that a book is based on,
click on this option to force the book to update to reflect the
change.

Go To Page
Use this command to go to a particular page in the current book.

Copy Page ►
Use this command to copy a page of a book in Bitmap or Enhanced
Metafile format. If copying as a bitmap, you can choose to copy it
either at the current zoom level or at the default (100%) zoom
level.

Zoom ►
This submenu provides various zoom options.

Zoom In
Zoom in.

Zoom Out
Zoom out

Whole Page
Zoom so that a whole page is visible (or 2 pages if the Two
Pages check box has been ticked in the panel on the right
hand side of the window).

Page Width
Zoom so that the whole width of a page is visible (or the width
of 2 pages if the Two Pages check box has been ticked
in the panel on the right hand side of the window).

Save Book As ►
Save the current book in the following formats...

PDF File
Save the diagram to PDF file format - see PDF
File Support.

Word-processor Document (RTF)
Rich Text Format is supported by most serious word-processors
(e.g. Microsoft Word). If you save a book in this format, you can
view and edit it in a word-processor.

Edit Book

Opens the Edit Book Dialog to
allow the book to be edited.

title: Diagram Menu
text:
Menus

Diagram Menu

This menu is only available when the Diagram
Window is active. Some of the menu commands apply
exclusively to trees and tree boxes, some apply to
shapes, and some apply to both. To learn more about trees
and shapes, see Diagram Elements.

See also the Diagram
Toolbar.

Save Diagram

Save Changes to Chart

Save Changes to Book Chart

If the current diagram is a saved chart, this command
will be "Save Changes to Chart". In that cases, changes
will be saved back to the saved chart file.

If the current diagram is a book chart (a chart that is part of
a book, and being edited in the Diagram Window) this command
will be "Save Changes to Book Chart". In that case,
changes will be saved back to the book chart.

With saved charts and book charts only, if there
are any unsaved changes, a small orange dot will be displayed in
the top-left of the icon area for the chart, looking like this:

In all other cases, the command will be "Save Diagram".
In that cases you will be prompted to provide a name for a new
saved chart file to save the diagram to.

Saved charts can be viewed later, and opened, by clicking on Saved Charts on the View menu
or on the dropdown menu that appears when you click on the
Charts icon
on the main toolbar.

To learn more about charts, see Working Diagrams and
Charts

Save Diagram As ►
Saves the current diagram as one of the following...

Family Historian Chart
Saves the current diagram as a saved chart. You will
be prompted to provide a name for the saved chart. Saved
charts can be viewed later, and opened, by clicking on Saved
Charts on the View menu.

PDF File
Save the diagram to PDF file format - see PDF
File Support.

Bitmap File (.bmp)
Standard picture format.

JPEG File (.jpg)
Standard picture format.

GIF File (.gif)
Standard picture format.

PNG File (.png)
Standard picture format.

PCX File (.pcx)
Standard picture format.

TIFF File (.tif)
Standard picture format.

Targa TGA File (.tga)
Standard picture format.

Adobe Photoshop File (.psd)
Picture format used by Adobe Photoshop.

Enhanced Metafile (.emf)
Standard picture format.

Custom Diagram Type
When you save a diagram as a custom diagram type, you are
effectively creating a new diagram type - one which will have many
(but not necessarily all) of the characteristics of the current
diagram, and one which you can re-use in the future. To access
custom diagram types, click on the Charts button on the main
application toolbar, and choose from the Custom Diagrams submenu
on the dropdown menu that appears. You can also access the
same submenu via the View menu.

Copy Diagram
Copy the current diagram to the clipboard

Insert Into Diagram ►

This submenu is used for inserting additional diagram
elements into an existing diagram. A diagram element could
be an entire tree (any kind), a fan chart, a picture, a text
box, a line, a rectangle, an arrow, free hand text and more.
There is no limit to the number of trees, or any other kind of
diagram element, that you can have in a diagram.

When you insert a tree, Family Historian will put the new tree
in the centre of the Diagram
Window - even if that means that it overlaps an existing
tree. It will also automatically enable Moving/Resizing, and set
'Tree' moving as the drag-and-move action. This means that you
can immediately click on any box within the tree to move it. See
the Movement Control Box
for more details.

The Shape Toolbar (accessible
from the Diagram toolbar) provides quick access to all of the
above items. See the Shape
Toolbar page for a detailed discussion of all of the
various commands on this submenu.

Find in Diagram
Click Find in Diagram to find the box for a
given individual.

Find Next Box For Individual
It can happen that you get more than one tree box for a given
Individual within a diagram. This feature lets you easily jump
between all duplicate tree boxes for a given Individual. Simply
select any box for the Individual
in question (if they aren't already selected), and then click on Find
Next Box for Individual. The selection will switch to
the next box for the selected Individual. Repeat to loop you
through all of the duplicate boxes.

If a given Individual has no duplicate boxes you will be told
that no other instances were found.

Tip: You can easily see which boxes are duplicates
by enabling Check for Duplicates in the General tab of the Diagram Options
dialog.

Tip: A fast way to search for duplicate boxes for
a given selected Individual is to press the F3 key instead of
using the menu command.

Check For Duplicates

As well as this menu command, there is also a Check
for Duplicates option in the Diagram
Options. If the latter is enabled, Family Historian will
automatically check for duplicate tree boxes for individuals
when you open a new diagram. Depending on the specific options
you use, Family Historian will not only detect duplicate tree
boxes within the diagram, it will also link them using coloured
ribbons and/or will close duplicated branches of the diagram to
keep duplication to a minimum.

If checking for duplicates was not enabled when you opened the
diagram, you can run Check For Duplicates… on the
Diagram menu at any time to enable it, and (depending on your
current diagram options for duplicates) to hide duplicated
branches.

Even if Check for Duplicates is already enabled in
Diagram Options, you may still want to use the menu command to
hide duplicated branches if you have been clicking on branch
expansion buttons to explore trees, and now have a number of
duplicated branches.

Tip: Check For Duplicates… is affected
by front-to-back ordering of trees. If one tree is layered 'in
front of' another (even if it isn't actually positioned in front
of it), Family Historian will close duplicated branches in the
'background' tree in preference to closing branches in the
'foreground' tree. So you can control which tree gets its
branches closed, by right-clicking on any box in one of the
trees, and selecting appropriate commands from the Order
and
Grouping submenu (see below).

Hide/Show Boxes ►

Hide Selected Boxes

All selected tree boxes will be hidden. When you hide a tree
box, the whole branch leading 'outwards' from that box is also
hidden. For example, if you hide an ancestor box the whole
branch of ancestors leading out from that box is hidden.

You cannot hide the root box in a tree, as this would cause
the whole tree to be hidden. If you wish to get rid of an entire
tree you must delete it. To delete a tree, click on any box in
the tree and click on the Delete key. Leave the selection at Delete Selected Diagram Items Only
and press OK. Then confirm that you wish to delete the tree.

Tip: A quick way to hide a box is to click on it
with the right mouse button and select Hide from the
dropdown menu that appears.

Show Hidden Boxes
Check this option to show all hidden boxes. By default these
appear with a purple background. You can then unhide whichever
hidden boxes you wish by selecting them and unticking the Hidden
state on the Box States menu (see below).
To hide hidden boxes again click on Show Hidden Boxes
again, to 'untick' it.

Tip: A quick way to unhide a box when Show Hidden
Box is enabled is to click on it with the right mouse button and
untick Hidden on the dropdown menu that appears.

Expand/Close Branches ►
A common requirement is to be able to close all branches except
one or two. This command allows you to do that. Simply
select the 'tip' box in any branch you wish to leave open
(press-and-hold the Ctrl key while clicking to select more than
one box). Then this command will close all branches except
the ones leading to the boxes you have selected.

Show Expansion Buttons

Hide or show expansion buttons.
These are the little circular buttons on branch lines. They are
crossed if the branch is hidden. Click on expansion buttons to
hide or show tree branches.

Expand Branch (one level)
As an alternative to clicking on expansion buttons, use this
menu command to expand a branch for a selected box. If the branch
has not previously been displayed, only the next level will be
shown (e.g. one generation of ancestors or descendants).

Expand Branch (all level)

Click on this command to fully expand the branch of the
selected box, as far as it will go.

Close Branch

Click on this command to close an expanded branch for a
selected box. You can also click on an expansion button to do
the same thing.

Close Unselected Branches

Click on this command to close all branches of all trees in
the current diagram, except where boxes are selected.

Spouse Display Options ►
'Spouses' refers to spouses of direct relatives of the diagram
root. There are 3 display options for them:

Spouse in Own Box

Each spouse is assigned their own tree box. This is the best
option for displaying information about spouses (and the only
one which allows you to view pictures of spouses), but it
produces larger diagrams than the other 2 options.

By default, Remarriage boxes are not displayed if
spouses are displayed in their own box; however, there is an
option to override this if you wish to. See Spouse
Display Options in the General tab of the Diagram Options
dialog.

This option is not applicable to ancestor boxes.

One Box Per Marriage
Spouses are not displayed in separate boxes; however,
individuals who have more than one spouse, will be allocated an
extra box (a Remarriage box)
for each additional spouse. Standard text schemes make use of this
Remarriage box to display spouse information.

No Spouse Info

Spouses are not displayed in separate boxes, nor are
Remarriage boxes displayed. This option takes up the least
amount of space. Use it when you are not interested in spouse
information.

With standard text schemes, no spouse information is displayed
when this option is chosen. However, in your own custom text
schemes you can show all of a person's spouses if you wish, even
if this option is selected. If you do so, you should be aware
that there will be no visual indication of which spouse is the
parent of which child.

Zoom ►
Zooming only affects how a diagram appears on the screen. It has
no effect on the size of the diagram when printed. If you wish to
change the size of a diagram when printed, you need to adjust Scaling.

Zoom In

Zoom in.

Tip: A quick alternative is to press the + key on
the numeric keypad (or Ctrl+L).

Zoom Out

Zoom out.

Tip: A quick alternative is to press the - key on
the numeric keypad (or Ctrl+K).

Set Zoom to 100%
Revert to 'actual size' (i.e. 100% zoom).

Set Zoom Level
Specify a specific zoom level, as a percentage, to 2 decimal
places. The maximum zoom is 500%.

View Whole Diagram
Adjusts zoom and diagram position so that the whole diagram can
be viewed. If Page Boundaries are being displayed the view will be
extended to include all of each printable page.

Select Area To View
When enabled, you can click-and-drag on the diagram to draw a
stretchy box round the area you wish to zoom to. The zoom will
occur when you release the left mouse button. Press the
right-mouse button, or the Esc key, to cancel.

Centre on Diagram Root
In general terms, this centres the diagram on the diagram root.
However, for Ancestor and Descendant
diagrams, the root may appear near the top or bottom or (depending
on the orientation) side of the Diagram Window, as appropriate.
Does not cause the diagram to zoom in or out.

Layout and Scaling ►
This submenu lets you control various related aspects of layout
and scaling of tree boxes.

Make All Boxes the Same Height (Width)

Depending on the tree orientation, this will make all boxes the
height of the current tallest box (vertically oriented trees),
or make all boxes the width of the current widest box
(horizontally oriented trees).

The Autosize state is
disabled in all boxes (see Box States below).

Make All Boxes in the Same Row (Column) the Same
Height (Width)

Depending on the tree orientation, this will make all boxes in
each row the height of the tallest box in that row (vertically
oriented trees), or make all boxes in each column the width of
the widest box in that column (horizontally oriented trees).

The Autosize state is
disabled in all boxes (see Box States below).

Reset All Box Sizes /Enable Autosize
All menu commands that change the size of boxes disable the Autosize state for those boxes.
This option re-enables Autosize
for all boxes. The effect of this is that all boxes will revert to
their default size. If any pictures have been resized using Scale Pictures to Fit Box Height,
these also will return to their default size. For more on this,
see Box States below.

Make Selected Boxes the Same Height (max)

Makes all selected boxes the height of the tallest selected
box. Only available if at least 2 boxes are selected.

The Autosize state is
disabled in the selected boxes (see Box States below).

Make Selected Boxes the Same Height (min)

Makes all selected boxes the height of the smallest selected
box. Only available if at least 2 boxes are selected.

The Autosize state is
disabled in the selected boxes (see Box States below).

Make Selected Boxes the Same Width (max)

Makes all selected boxes the width of the widest selected box.
Only available if at least 2 boxes are selected.

The Autosize state is
disabled in the selected boxes (see Box States below).

Make Selected Boxes the Same Width (min)

Makes all selected boxes the width of the narrowest selected
box. Only available if at least 2 boxes are selected.

The Autosize state is
disabled in the selected boxes (see Box States below).

Scale Pictures to Fit Box Height

For all selected boxes which have pictures at the side of the
box (left or right), this menu command resizes their pictures to
fit the box height. At the same time, the overall width of each
box is adjusted to maintain the width of the text area of the
box.

If you wish to adjust the height of pictures which are
displayed within the text, you should temporarily
change Diagram Options to move the pictures to the side of the
text, adjust the box size appropriately, use this command to
adjust picture size, and then change Diagram Options to move
pictures back within the text.

The Autosize state is
disabled in the selected boxes (see Box States below).

Make All Rows the Same Height (All Columns the Same
Width)
Depending on the diagram orientation, this will make all rows
the height of the current tallest row, or make all columns the
width of the current widest column.

Reset Row Heights (Widths)
Depending on the diagram orientation, this will either set all
rows back to their default height, or set all columns back to
their default width.

Diagram Scale...

Set any scale for any diagram. The default setting (no
scaling) is 100%, but you can choose values which are either
greater or less than this.

Tip: Diagram scaling can also be adjusted to any
value at any time, by updating the value of the Scaling field in
the General tab of the Diagram
Options Dialog.

Scale Diagram To Fit Exact Number of Rows (Columns)
Per Page
Depending on the diagram orientation, you will be prompted to
specify either how many rows you want to fit vertically onto each
page, or how many columns you want to fit horizontally onto each
page. If rows are not already the same height (or, depending on
orientation, columns the same width) you will be warned that they
will be resized to make them the same size. Then the Diagram scale
will be adjusted to fit the desire number of rows (or columns)
onto each page.
Tip: This function does not automatically align
page boundaries with row or column boundaries. But this can be
done quite easily. To do it, click on 'Show Page Boundaries' -
this will display page boundaries as a grid. Click-and-drag on
any grid intersection to move the grid, and hence page
boundaries. If you press the Ctrl key while doing this, the page
boundary will 'snap' to the nearest row or column boundary.

Reset Diagram Scaling
Resets scaling back to the default value (100%).

Enable Moving and Resizing

Check this option to open the Movement Control Box to enable moving
boxes, branches and trees, and to enable resizing of boxes. When
Moving/Resizing is enabled, selected boxes have little white
boxes in their corners and sides to show that they are selected,
instead of the usual little black boxes. Click-and-drag on any
little white box to resize.

Page Boundaries ►

Show Page Boundaries

Show (or hide) page boundaries. A grid of lines appears. Each
filled and used rectangular area marked out by the grid
corresponds to a printable page - that is, to a physical sheet
of paper that will be printed if you print the whole diagram. A
diagram that extends over multiple grid areas will be printed on
multiple sheets of paper.

The grid rectangle size is determined by the paper size used
by your printer. It will change automatically if you switch to a
different paper size in your printer settings (or switch between
portrait and landscape mode). To change printer settings, click
on Print Setup on the File menu.

To see all printable pages, click on View Whole Diagram
after showing page boundaries.

Tip: Click-and-drag with the left mouse on page
boundary intersections to move page boundaries.

Tip: Usually you will use the Scaling option on
the General
tab of the Diagram Options dialog to set the size of a
diagram when printed, but for convenience you can also adjust
scaling, and resize a diagram when printed, by
clicking-and-dragging with the right mouse on page boundary
intersections (it's usually a good idea to pick one at the
bottom right of the diagram). When you do this, it appears to
adjust the size of pages. But what you are really doing is
adjusting the relative size of pages. If the pages are getting
smaller relatively (bearing in mind that the physical paper you
are printing on does not change) this means really that you are
getting less onto each page - i.e. the diagram as it will appear
when printed, is getting bigger. You can confirm this by looking
at Scaling value. When it is not 100% it is shown in the status
bar.

Tip: If you press the Ctrl key while moving page
boundaries, they will 'snap' to the nearest row/column boundary.
This is especially useful if you have adjusted row/column sizes
so that an exact number will fit within each page (see below).

Avoid Page Boundaries

When checked, Family Historian will layout diagrams so that
boxes do not overlap page boundaries - either at the side or at
the top.

Tip: You can specify how near a box can get to a
page boundary by setting the Avoid boundaries gap in
the More Dimensions dialog, accessible from the Dimensions tab of the Diagram Options
dialog.

Family Connection Mapper...
Opens the Family
Connection Mapper which is used to mark lines connecting
boxes or branches. It can even create a 'route' connecting
any two individuals in a tree. When the How Related tool is
used to show graphically how any two Individuals are related, it
will create a marked route in a diagram - which can be
modified and configured using the Family Connection Mapper.

Order, Grouping & Alignment ►

This submenu has commands relating to the order, grouping,
alignment and size of various diagram elements. Except
where indicated, these commands apply exclusively to shapes
rather than trees or tree boxes (see diagram
elements).

Order

The relevant commands are Bring to Front, Send
to Back, Bring Forward and Send Back.

These commands allow you to control the display order,
front-to-back, of selected diagram
elements. A diagram element is anything that can be
inserted into a diagram - such as a picture, text box, line or
rectangle. Also, each tree counts as a single diagram element.

To select a tree for the purpose of ordering, select any box
within the tree.

Grouping

The relevant commands are Group and Ungroup.

These commands allow you to group diagram elements into grouped
objects, or ungroup them. Only trees cannot be
grouped with other diagram elements.

Alignment

The relevant commands are Align Top, Align Left,
Align Right, and Align Bottom.

These commands allow you to align a number of selected
shapes. Trees cannot be aligned with other diagram
elements using these commands.

To align one or more shapes with each other, you can lock the
position of any one of them (right-click on a shape and choose
"Lock Position" to lock it). Select both the locked shape
and the unlocked shapes and choose the required alignment
command. The unlocked shapes will all align with the
locked shape.

If none of the shapes are locked, the shapes will align with
the leftmost shape if aligning left, the topmost shape if
aligning top, the rightmost shape if aligning right, and the
bottommost shape if aligning bottom.

If more that one shape is locked, any unlocked shapes will
align with (depending on the alignment type required) the
leftmost, rightmost, topmost or bottommost of the locked shapes.

Size

The relevant commands are Make Same Height and Make
Same Width.

These commands allow you to make a number of selected shapes
have the same height or width (preserving aspect ratio).
Trees cannot be resized in this way, and not all shapes can
either. Specifically lines, polylines or grouped shapes
cannot be resized using these commands. All other shapes
can, however.

To make a selection of shapes have the same height or width,
you can lock the position of any one of them (right-click on a
shape and choose "Lock Position" to lock it). Select both
the locked shape and the unlocked shapes and choose the required
alignment command. The unlocked shapes will all be given
the same height or width as the locked shape.

If none of the shapes are locked, the shapes will all be given
the height or width of the largest shape.

If more than one shape is locked, any unlocked shapes will be
given the height or width of the largest of the locked shapes.

Tip: Remember that you can always click 'Undo' on
the 'Edit' menu (or press Ctrl-Z) to undo any
changes to shapes in diagrams. So if you try one of the
above commands and it does not do what you wanted, you can
easily undo the change. You can also 'redo' the change
from the Edit menu (or by clicking Ctrl-Y).

Format

The Format command can be used with all diagram
elements, but it works a little differently depending on
whether you are formatting one or more boxes in a tree or one or
more other kinds of diagram elements (shapes, lines, pictures,
etc).

If you have selected one or more boxes in a tree, the Format
command opens the Override
Box Features dialog, allowing you to override any aspect
of the appearance of the selected boxes. To select
multiple boxes at the same time, see How
to Select Multiple Boxes in Diagrams.

If you have selected one or more other kinds of diagram
elements, you will be able to change their appearance using the
Format dialog, which will have different tabs depending on what
kind of diagram elements you are formatting. See Diagram
Shape Format Dialog to learn more.

You cannot simultaneously format both boxes in trees, and other
kinds of non-tree diagram elements.

Selection & Marks ►

You can mark any tree boxes that you wish to distinguish for
any purpose. Marked boxes have a distinctive background colour
(configurable using Sundry Colours in Diagram
Options).

Tip: An alternative to using Marks is to set
Record Flags for Individuals, and specify conditions for box
features based on these flags. This gives much greater
flexibility than just using Marks. You specify box features in
the Boxes tab
of the Diagram Options dialog.

Tip: You must be displaying boxes to be able to
see which ones are marked. This is controlled from the Boxes tab of the Diagram Options dialog.

Select All Boxes

Selects all tree boxes in the diagram

Select Branch Boxes

If you select one tree box and click this command, the entire
branch of boxes leading off from the first box will be
selected. This can be useful if, for example, you want to
use the Format command to give the entire branch a distinctive
appearance of some kind.

Invert Selection

Causes all selected tree boxes to become unselected, and all
unselected boxes to become selected.

Mark/Unmark Boxes
Sets or clears marks for selected tree boxes.

Set/Clear Marks using Query
Sets or clears marks using a query. Using this technique you
could, for example, mark all of your male ancestors who died of
heart attacks under the age of 50 (say). This is a powerful
feature which can be used in a number of ways for many different
purposes.

Select Marked Boxes
A quick way to select all marked tree boxes.

Clear All Marks
Clears all marks in the current diagram.

Box States ►
This submenu allows you to control the states of selected tree
boxes.

Autosize Box
When enabled (the default) Family Historian will size a tree box
to fit its text. But if you manually resize the box (or use a
command to force a non-default box size - see Page,
Rows/Columns & Boxes above), it will disable
autosizing and use the size you specify instead. Tick this option
to re-enable box autosizing.

Align with Others in Same Row (Column)
When enabled (the default) Family Historian will keep relatives
in the same row (or column - depending on the orientation), in
line with one another. If you move a branch it will disable this
state for the moved boxes. Tick this option to re-enable it, and
force Family Historian to realign a box with the others in its
row.

Box Size Affects Row (Column) Size
When enabled, the row (or column - depending on the orientation)
that the box belongs to will always automatically be kept as big
as, or bigger than, the box height. Moving a box does not disable
this state; but you may wish to set it off, if you have moved a
box away from the row it came from, and the box size is now having
an inappropriate influence on the row size.

Attach to Row (Column)
When you move a box or branch, if 'within row' is ticked in the
Movement Control Box, Family Historian will continue to the treat
the moved boxes as part of the rows (or columns - depending on the
orientation) that they came from and will take these boxes into
account for row/column sizing purposes. If you do not wish Family
Historian to do this, remove this state for the moved boxes.

Keep Near Parents
Enabling this for one box automatically disables it for all
siblings of the selected box. Can be used with box descendant
boxes, and with ancestor boxes in All
Relatives diagrams.

Hidden
This state is ticked for all hidden boxes. See Show Hidden Boxes
above.

Book Layout Compatibility
It is often useful to be able to ensure that the page layout of
a chart matches that of a given book - especially if the chart is
displayed over multiple print pages. You can always add any
chart to a book, but if the page layout is different this may mean
that chart layout looks wrong when you add it to a book. To
ensure that a chart's page layout matches that of a given book,
take the Book Layout Compatibility option and select
the book in question. Books created since version 8 of
Family Historian can be used with this option. If you select
a book created earlier than that, you will be prompted to first
upgrade it to use the latest book format, if that has not already
been done.

Use the Show Page Boundaries option to see the page
boundaries for a chart, given current printer, page settings and
margins.

Although it is useful to be able to specify book compatibility in
advance of adding a chart to a book, it isn't ordinarily necessary
as you can correct any layout issues after adding the chart to a
book if necessary. To do so, select the chart in the list of
book items in the Edit Book dialog
and click the Edit button. You
will be able to edit the chart in the Diagram Window and correct
any layout issues there.

There are special issues relating to book compatibility with
respect to pedigree charts. For more information, see the
discussion of this issue in Pedigree
Chart Dialog.

To learn more about book layout compatibility, see Book
Layout Compatibility for Charts.

Diagram Statistics
Displays a number of statistics about the current diagram.

Options
Opens the Diagram

Options Dialog.

title: Edit Menu
text:
Menus

Edit Menu

Undo
Undo the last change to your data. Changes to diagram
shapes in the Diagram Window, or
map shapes in the Map Window, can
also be undone (or redone).

Redo
Redo the last undo.

Copy
Copy the selected item to the clipboard. Any field can be
copied. Records can be copied too, but only as text (e.g. to paste
into a document or email).

Paste
Paste a previously copied item.

Delete
Delete the selected item(s).

Unlink From ►
Unlink a selected Individual
record from...

Parents
Choose the parent family you wish to unlink
from.

Spouse
Choose the spouse family you wish to unlink from.

Move Up
Re-order the selected item to move it before a previous item of
the same kind. Can be used to re-order fields of any type. It can
be used in different windows. For example it can be used in the Diagram Window to re-order
spouses, siblings or children, or in the
Records Window to re-order any field.

Move Down
Same as 'Move Up' (see previous), but moves item down.

Find...
Opens the Find Dialog to do a
search for an Individual.

Find and Replace

Opens the Find and Replace dialog.

Find in Diagram

If used in the Diagram Window,
it opens a selector dialog where you can select the person you
wish to find. That person will then be selected in the diagram,
and scrolled into view. The same menu command can also be used
when other windows are active. In that case, it will find the
selected Individual in the last-used Diagram Window. If there is
more than one instance of the Individual in that window, press
F3 to switch between them.

Go To Record
Find a selected Individual's record in the Records
Window.

File Root ►
Marking an Individual as a File
Root can be useful. You can choose to see how
other Individuals are related to that Individual, in the Records
Window and elsewhere. Also, when you click the Home
button
on the main application toolbar, the File Root will be displayed
as the focus person in the Focus
Window.

Set as File Root
Makes the selected Individual the File Root.

Clear File Root
Clear the File Root so that the file no longer has a File Root.

Go To File Root
Locate the File Root's record in the Records
Window.

Merge/Compare Records
Compare and merge two selected records in the Merge/Compare
Dialog.

Re-order Events By Date
Will check that all events, attributes, children and spouses,
relating to the selected Individual
are in the correct chronological order. If they aren't, it will
re-order them.

Add to Named List
Add all the selected records (Individual records or any other
kind of record) to a particular named
list. Works with multiple selection. Named lists can
be viewed and managed in the Records
Window.

Record Flags
Opens the Record Flags dialog which shows
which flags are enabled for the currently selected individuals and
allows flags to be set or cleared for these individuals. Works
with multiple selection. See Record
Flags to learn more.

title: FamilySearch Menu
text:
Menus

FamilySearch Menu

This menu is only available in the main application menu bar when the FamilySearch Window
is active as a workspace window. This menu is not available in the
main application menu bar if the FamilySearch Window has been made to
"float" in front of other windows - which is to say that it is not being
used as a workspace window. However, this same menu can always be
accessed at any time by clicking on the Cog menu button in the
top-right corner of the FamilySearch
Window.

Import Tree from FamilySearch

Opens the FamilySearch
Import Dialog which can be used to import Individuals
directly from either the FamilySearch global Family Tree or from a
User Tree.

Upload Current Project to New User Tree in FamilySearch

Create a new User Tree
within FamilySearch and upload the Individuals in your current
project to it.

Auto-Match Unmatched Individuals

Automatically match as many unmatched Individuals as possible in
the current project to the current FamilySearch tree.

Clear All Matches

This will clear all matches. If User
Tree functionality is enabled, you will be able to choose
between clearing all matches for the current FamilySearch tree or
clearing all matches for all trees.

Open FamilySearch Web Page ►

User Tree List

Opens a web browser and displays a FamilySearch page that shows
a list of user trees that you currently have access to.

Current User Tree

Opens a web browser and displays the FamilySearch settings page
for the current user tree. If there is no current user tree,
this option will be greyed.

Matched Person

Opens a web browser and displays the FamilySearch record for the
current person in the FamilySearch window, if that person is
matched to a FamilySearch record. If they are not matched,
this option will be greyed.

FamilySearch Home Page

Opens a web browser and displays the FamilySearch home page.

Colours

Displays a colour-selection window, where you can choose the
colours you wish to use for the FamilySearch
Window.

Options

Opens the Preferences
Dialog: FamilySearch tab where you can specify options that
relate to FamilySearch.

Help on FamilySearch

Opens the Help page for the FamilySearch
Window.

title: File Menu
text:
Menus

File Menu

Project Window
Opens the Project Window,
without closing the current project/file.

Gedcom File Tasks ►
Perform tasks relating to standalone GEDCOM
files (GEDCOM files that are not used to store data for a Family
Historian project).

New Gedcom File
Create a new GEDCOM file

Open Gedcom File
Open a GEDCOM file

Save a Gedcom File Copy
Makes a copy of the current GEDCOM file (can be used to copy the
GEDCOM file which is used to store data in the current project -
if any).

<Up to 9 file names>
For convenience, lists (up to) the last 9 most recently used
GEDCOM files. Click on a filename to re-open it.

Save
Save changes to the current project/file.

Close Project
Closes the current project. The Project
Window will be redisplayed.

Merge/Compare File
Open the Merge/Compare
dialog to compare the current project or GEDCOM file with another
project or GEDCOM file, and optionally merge the other file into
the current file. Can be used either within the context of a
project, or with standalone GEDCOM files.

Split Tree Helper
Open the Split
Tree Helper dialog. The Split Tree Helper dialog provides
means of deleting a large number of records in the current
project/file. It is often used to split a project into two smaller
projects. It can also be used for the situation in which you
have made a copy of your main file (e.g. to send to someone else)
and you wish to delete unwanted records from this copy. However,
it can be used at any time to delete unwanted records. Use with
care!

Validate
Check the current project/file for any internal storage errors,
and optionally fix any errors found. You will be automatically
prompted to validate when opening any GEDCOM file that was not
created by Family Historian.

File Statistics
Show information about the current project.

Page Setup
Configure print options relating to the active window. Is only
available when the Diagram Window is active.

Print
Print the current diagram, report, book, query or map (if you
are viewing one of these). If not, a dialog box will direct
you to the Publishing Tools Finder.

Print Preview
Shows you what the output would look like if you were to print
now. Available when viewing the Diagram Window, the Report Window,
the Book Window, the Query Window or the Map Window.

Print Setup
Configure your current printer.

Import/Export ►

Open submenus to enable you to import or export any of the
following:

GEDCOM file
File containing genealogy data in GEDCOM format. When
importing, the data can be merged (under your full supervision
and control) into the current project. When exporting,
you will be presented with the Export
GEDCOM File Dialog which offers numerous options
relating to the export. You will be able to export all
of your data, or a subset of it. GEDCOM is the most
commonly-used, standard format for genealogy data.
GEDZIP file
File containing genealogy data in GEDZIP format. A
GEDZIP file contains a GEDCOM file, as well as associated
multimedia files (pictures, sound files, videos, etc).
When exporting, you will be presented with the Export
GEDZIP File Dialog which offers numerous options
relating to the export. You will be able to export all
of your data, or a subset of it, and all media files or a
subset.
JSON File
Export only. File containing core genealogy data
(Individuals, Families and Media) in JSON format. Some
third party products may require that the data be supplied in
this format.
Family Historian Project
Import only. When importing, the data will be merged
(under your full supervision and control) into the current
project.
FamilySearch Tree

Import only. When importing, the data will be added
into the current project. By default, selected tree
branches are imported from the main FamilySearch main (global)
tree. However, if support for FamilySearch user trees is
enabled (see Preferences:
FamilySearch Tab), you can optionally also import
branches from a FamilySearch user tree, or even import the
entire tree.

Other Family Tree File (instructions only)
Gives instructions on how to import other kinds of family
tree file into a Family Historian project.
Family Historian Chart File
Chart files contain saved instances of diagrams.
Diagram Type
Diagram types are created when you save a diagram as a
'Custom Diagram Type'.
Diagram Text Scheme
Text schemes store specifications of the text content of
boxes in a diagram.
Diagram Box Preset
Diagram box presets are saved configurations of boxes in
diagrams. They can imported and exported from the
Diagram Box Presets Dialog. To learn more about diagram
box presets and accessing the Diagram Box Presets Dialog, see
the "Presets" section of Diagram
Options Dialog: Boxes Tab.
Diagram Box Icons

Opens the Diagram Box
Icons Dialog where box icons, that can be used in Family
Historian diagrams, can be imported and exported.

Report Type
Report types are created when you save a report as a 'Custom
Report Type'.
Map Overlays

Map overlays are saved collections of map shapes (shapes
that are used in the Map Window).
They can also be imported and exported from the Map
Overlays Dialog. See the Map
Overlays Dialog to learn more about map overlays.

Query
Custom queries can be created on the Query Window.
Smart Folder Set

A smart folder set is a collection of smart
folders. They can also be imported and exported
from the Manage Folder
Sets Dialog.

Property Box Tab
The Property Box can be customized. You can also
import and export customizations created by others.
Accent Set
When you press-and-hold a letter or punctuation key in the
Property Box or other data entry windows, a popup window,
called the Popup Accent Window, appears with a
choice of accent characters for that letter (or alternative
punctuation marks if a punctuation mark). This is fully
configurable in the Configure
Language and Accent Characters Dialog. You can
create your own accent sets, which can be shared (imported or
exported). See Configure
Language and Accent Characters Dialog for more
information about accent sets.
Autotext
Opens the Manage
Autotext Dialog, where autotext can be imported or
exported.
Language Pack
Opens the Language Packs
Dialog, where language packs can be imported or
exported.
Fact Set
Fact sets are collections of fact type definitions.
They can be created on the Fact
Types dialog, accessible from the Tools menu.

Source Template Collection
Source Template Collections are created and managed
on the Source
Template Definitions Dialog. See the help page for
that dialog to learn more.
Colour Scheme
You can change colors in most windows in Family
Historian. If you wish to preserve your colour
preferences (for the whole application) you can export them as
a 'Colour Scheme' file. You can also import colour
schemes created by others. Imported colour schemes can
be selected in the General
tab of Preferences.
User Credentials
The ability to export and import user credentials is
provided for users who wish to access their project files from
more than one computer. In this scenario, it is a good
idea to export your user credentials from one PC, and then
import them into the other PC. That will ensure that
your user credentials are the same on each PC. User
Credentials are primarily used as part of Internet
Data Matching, and sharing user credentials across 2 PCs
ensures that if you confirm or reject a match on one PC, it
will still appear to be confirmed or rejected when viewed from
the other PC. See the "User Credentials" section of Moving Family
Historian to a New PC to learn more).

Plugins
Plugins are 3rd-party extensions to the program. They
can be accessed from, and also imported and exported using,
the Plugins Dialog.

Backup/Restore ►
See Moving Family Historian to
a New PC to learn more about the difference between project
data, settings, and user credentials
(user credentials can be imported and exported using the
Import/Export command above).

Small Backup (Gedcom File
Only)
Create a backup of your current GEDCOM
file. This is the main data file that stores your project
data (see Moving Family Historian
to a New PC to learn more about 'project data'). The
data is backed up to a Family Historian Backup Format file
(.fhbak). Use the Restore command to restore previously backed up
files.

When you do a small backup, you do not backup media
files that are stored in the project folder, or other files
attached to projects, such as saved charts, saved maps and
books. You also do not backup settings. Settings can
be backed up separately (see below).

Medium Backup (Project File and Project Data
SubfolderOnly)
Creates a backup of the core files in your project folder,
including amongst other things, the main data file (the GEDCOM
file), and any media files stored in the project folder. Any
data stored in the Public subfolder within the project
folder are, however, not included. The data is backed up to
a Family Historian Backup Format file (.fhbak). Use the Restore
Backup command to restore previously backed up
files.

When you do a medium backup, you do not backup
media files that are not stored in the project folder,
but you do backup many other files attached to projects, such as
saved charts, saved maps and books. You do not however
backup settings. Settings can be backed up separately (see
below))

Full Backup (Entire Project Folder)
Create a backup of the entire project folder for the current
project, including all data stored in the Public
subfolder. The data is backed up to a Family Historian
Backup Format file (.fhbak). Use the Restore Backup command
to restore previously backed up files.

When you do a full backup, you still do not backup
media files that are not stored in the project
folder. You do however backup many other files attached to
projects, such as saved charts, saved maps and books. You
do not however backup settings. Settings can be backed up
separately (see below))

Restore Backup
Restore a previously backed up file (small, medium or
full). The file can be a Family Historian Backup Format file
(.fhbak) or a legacy Family Historian zip file (.zip).
Earlier versions of Family Historian saved backups to .zip files.

Revert to Snapshot
Opens the Snapshot Manager
which allows snapshots to be managed (and reverted to, if
required).

Backup Options

Displays the Backup
tab in Preferences.

Backup/Restore Settings ►
Settings means preferences, configurations,
customizations, fact type definitions, custom queries, custom
smart folders, custom reports, custom diagrams, custom text
schemes, custom source templates, language packs, custom map
overlays, custom accent files, ... and more. To learn more
about settings, see the "Settings" section of Moving
Family Historian to a New PC.

Backup Settings

Backup settings to a Family Historian Settings File.

Tip: You can also backup settings by opening the Project Window, clicking the More Tasks button and choosing "Backup
Settings" on the "Backup/Restore Settings" submenu.

Restore
Settings (instructions only)

Settings cannot be restored from here. This menu command
opens a Help window with instructions on how to restore settings
(you open the Project Window,
click the More Tasks button and
choose "Restore Settings" on the "Backup/Restore Settings"
submenu).

Exit
Close the program.

title: Help Menu
text:
Menus

Help Menu

Online Tour of Family Historian
Displays an online tour of Family Historian in a web browser.

Quick Start Guide

The Quick Start Guide is the recommended place for all
beginners to start.

Video Tutorials

Open a web browser to view video tutorials for Family
Historian, on the Family Historian website.

Family Historian User Manual
Opens this User Manual in a separate window (sometimes also
known as 'the Help') and display the Contents pane.

Getting Started
Open this User Manual and display a page with advice for anyone
who is getting started with Family Historian.

Help with Current View
Open this User Manual and displays content that is relevant to
the currently active window.

Search the User Manual

Open this User Manual and displays the search panel.

Browse User Manual on the Web

Open this User Manual in a web browser. The search options
are more extensive in this context.

Product Registration

Only available for unregistered products. Used to register your
product. Recommended for all users.

Family Historian Notice Board

The Family Historian Notice Board is a page on the Family
Historian website that displays news about Family Historian, and
other notices that are likely to be of interest to Family
Historian users. The web page is displayed in a web browser.

Technical Support

Open a web browser to view Technical Support options.

User Groups

Open a web browser to view information about Family Historian
User Groups.

Family Historian Website

Open a web browser to view the Family Historian website.

Check for Updates

This command will check whether there is a more recent version
of Family Historian available than the version you have.

Account Settings (<your user name>)

Click this option to login to your Family Historian account on
a web browser. You might wish to do this to renew a
subscription, check licence details, and/or update your registered
email address.

Please bear in mind that logging in to your account within
Family Historian is quite separate from logging in to your
account within a web browser. If you happen to have more
than one Family Historian account (not uncommon), you might be
logged in to one account within Family Historian while being
logged in to a different account within the web
browser. A message will advise you of the user name
that you are using within Family Historian. You can
confirm the username that you are logged in with in the web
browser by looking in the 'Account Details' area. If the
user name does not match the one you are using within Family
Historian, you should logout of the account in the web browser
and log back in with the correct user name. If you have
forgotten your password, click the forgotten password link and a
password reset will be emailed to you.

All users of Family Historian must have a Family
Historian account, and must be logged in to their account.
Your licence to use Family Historian is attached to your
account; so if you wish to install the software on another
computer, you must always login using the same account.

About Family Historian
Provides the version number and other details about your
installation of Family Historian. It also provides more
details about your account and licence.

title: Internet Menu
text:
Menus

Internet Menu

Open Web Search Window
Opens the Web
Search Window

Search the Internet
Opens the Search the
Internet Dialog.

Match with FamilySearch
Opens the FamilySearch
Window. You will be prompted to login to FamilySearch
if you are not already logged-in. You will be able to create
a free FamilySearch account if you don't already have one.

Internet Data Matches
Opens the Internet
Data Matches tab of Preferences.

title: Lists menu
text:
Menus

Lists Menu

This menu is only available when the Records
Window is active.

See also the Records
Window Toolbar.

Named Lists Pane
Hide or show the Named Lists Pane. When visible, this pane
displays on the right side of the Records Window. It contains 3
panels - one above the other. The topmost panel shows all Named
Lists in the current file. The middle panel shows all records
belonging to whichever Named List is selected in the topmost
panel. The bottom panel shows the list note associated with
whichever item is selected in the middle panel - you can edit this
note (or add a new one) by typing directly in this panel.

Configure Record Window Columns/Configure List Columns
This command can be used to open the Configure
Columns dialog to choose and configure the columns to be
displayed in the Records Window or the middle panel of the Named
Lists pane, depending on whichever is active.

Keep Current List Order
The records in a selected Named List are displayed in the middle
panel of the Named Lists Pane. You can easily sort the list by
clicking on any column heading. You can also use the Move Up and
Move Down buttons in the top right corner of the list, to move
items. However, when you do these things, the new list order is
only temporary. If you switch to another list and then switch
back, the list will revert to its previous order. If you re-order
a list and want to preserve the new list order, click on Keep
Current List Order.

Add To Selected Named List

Adds the selected records to the currently selected Named
List. This command only works in the Records Window. If you want
to add records to a Named List when viewing another window,
select the records and click on Add
to Named List on the Edit menu.

To select a Named List, click on its name in the top panel in
the Named Lists Pane.

New Named List
Create a new Named List.

Delete Named List
Deletes the currently selected Named List. This command does not
delete any records in the list.

Empty Named List
Empties the currently selected Named List, but does not delete
it. Again, the records in the list are not deleted.

Delete Named List Records
Deletes all the records in the currently selected Named List.
You will be required to confirm that you definitely want to do
this.

Named List Properties
Opens the List Properties Dialog, to view the properties of the
currently selected Named List.

title: Mapping Menu
text:
Menus

Mapping Menu

This menu is only available when the Map
Window is active.

See also the Map
Toolbar.

Save Changes to Map...
Save the current map details (position, marker sets, markers,
and shapes) in Family Historian Map Format. The map will be
saved within the current project. Saved maps can be accessed
by clicking on the main application Map toolbar icon and choosing
the 'Saved Maps...' menu command.

If you are working on a saved map, this command will save changes
back to that saved map. If you aren't already working on a
saved map you will be prompted to specify a name for the new map
file.

Save Map As ►

Family Historian Map...

Same as 'Save Changes to Map' above, except that you will always
be prompted to provide a name for the map. Saves the current
map details (position, marker sets, markers, and shapes) in Family
Historian Map Format. The map will be saved within the
current project. Saved maps can be accessed by clicking on
the main application Map toolbar icon and choosing the "Saved
Maps..." menu command.

Media Record...

Save the current image in the Map Viewer as a new Media
record. The image will be saved as a file in JPEG format
within the current project. If you want to add a map to a
diagram, report, book or website, it is usually a good option to
save it first as a Media record using this feature.

JPEG File (.jpg)...
Save the current map as an image file in JPEG format.

Saved Maps...

Opens the Saved Maps dialog
where you can view previously saved maps and open, rename, clone
or delete them.

Add Map Overlay...

Adds an overlay to the current map. An overlay is the name
of a saved collection of shapes. See the Map
Overlays Dialog to learn more about overlays.

Save Map Overlay...

Saves all the shapes in the current Map Window as a custom
overlay. An overlay is the name of a saved collection of
shapes. See the Map
Overlays Dialog to learn more about overlays.

Note: All shapes in the current Map Window will be
saved, including both locked and unlocked shapes. See
"Locking Shapes" in Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more about locked shapes.

Manage Map Overlays...

Opens the Map Overlays Dialog
where map overlays can be opened, renamed, described, simplified,
cloned, deleted, imported or exported.

Add Shape ►

Polyline

Add Polyline Shape. Click-and-drag on the Map Viewer (the
part of the Map Window that contains
the actual map) to add a line. Initially the line will be a
straight line between 2 points (i.e. it will have only 2 nodes),
but you can easily add as many nodes as you like, to give the line
whatever shape you want - see Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more.

Polygon

Add Polygon Shape. Click-and-drag on the Map Viewer to
draw a stretchy box. This will give the initial shape of
your polygon - a rectangle with 4 nodes. You can
subsequently add as many nodes as you like to the polygon, to give
it whatever shape you want. See Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more.

Circle (click-and-drag)

Add Circle Shape. Click-and-drag on the Map Viewer to draw
a circle, centred on the point you initially clicked on. You
can later click-and-drag on the perimeter of the circle to resize
it. See Add and Edit Shapes
to learn more.

Circle (with radius)...

An alternative method of adding a circle shape. The circle
is added around the map centre (indicated by cross-hairs on the
map viewer). You will be prompted to specify the radius to
the circle, and this can be specified in miles, yards, kilometres
or metres. Decimal values are accepted in this
context. You can later click-and-drag on the perimeter of
the circle to resize it. You can check the size of a circle
radius (specified in map units - miles or kilometres) at any time,
by right-clicking on it and choosing the 'Format' command
(assuming that the shape is unlocked or otherwise
accessible). See Add and
Edit Shapes to learn more.

Text

Add Text Shape. Click-and-drag on the Map Viewer to draw a
stretchy box. This will give the initial shape of your text
box - a rectangle with 4 nodes and a yellow text anchor. You
can subsequently subsequently resize the text box, and
click-and-drag on the text anchor to move it. See Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more.

Enable Access to Locked Shapes

Locked shapes cannot ordinarily be selected or changed in any
way. Use this menu command, or click on the 'Access'
button
on the Map Window Toolbar, to
enable access to locked shapes. When the 'Access' button is
pressed, locked shapes can be accessed as if they were
unlocked. See "Locking Shapes" in Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more about locked shapes.

Select All Unlocked Text Boxes

Select all text box shapes that are not locked (or are treated
as if they were not locked because the 'Access' button has been
pressed - see previous). See "Locking Shapes" in Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more about locked shapes.

Select All Unlocked Shapes

Select all shapes that are not locked (or are treated as if they
were not locked because the 'Access' button has been pressed - see
previous). See "Locking Shapes" in Add
and Edit Shapes to learn more about locked shapes.

Order & Grouping ►

Bring to Front

Moves the selected shapes forward, in front of all other shapes

Send to Back

Moves the selected shapes back, in front of all other shapes

Bring Forward

Moves the selected shapes forward one step

Send to Back

Moves the selected shapes back one step

Group

Creates a group of all the selected shapes

Ungroup

Removes the grouping of a selected group or groups.

Format...

Open the Map Shape Format
Dialog to format the selected shapes.

Zoom/Region ►

Zoom In

Zoom the map in

Zoom Out

Zoom the map out

View Home Region
Zoom map to show your home region. For example, if you are
American, your home region will be the U.S.A. If you are
Australian, it will be Australia. You can change your home
region to match whatever view the map window is currently showing,
by choosing Use Current Position as 'Home' Region (see
below).

View All Markers

Zoom the map to show all markers

View World
Zoom map to show the whole world.

Select Area to View
Click-and-drag on the map to draw a stretchy box around the area
you wish to zoom the map to.

Use Current Position as 'Home' Region
Change your 'home region' to match whatever view the map window
is currently showing. This option affects, and only affects,
the behaviour of the View Home Region toolbar button and
menu command (see above).

Find Near Map Centre

A dialog box is displayed labelled "Find Near Map Centre".
This search tool will create a new marker set for places or
addresses that are closer than a specified maximum distance from
the map centre (indicated by cross-hairs in the map viewer).
The new marker set can be of any type: Individuals & Events,
Places or Addresses. If you choose an "Individuals &
Events" type marker set, you will also be able to specify if it
should show places only, addresses only, or addresses preferred.

As well as specifying the type of new marker required, you can
also specify the maximum distance from the map centre to
search. This distance can be specified in miles, yards,
kilometres or metres. Decimal values are accepted.

Another option on the dialog box is to specify that the search
region should be shaded. If you take this option, a circle
shape will be created, centred on the map centre, with the
specified radius. This circle will initially be created
locked; so if you want to modify it in any way, or delete it, you
will need to press the 'Access' button to be able to access it
(see above).

A final option is 'Hide All Other Markers', ticked by
default. When you do a search, if this option is ticked,
allmarker sets, other than the new one you are creating, will be
hidden - which means that all of their markers will be hidden.

Reset 'Home' Region
Resets the home region to its installation default.

Display Marker Text

If enabled, every marker will have the first name part of its
place or address (if comma-separated) displayed below the
marker. You can choose the font type and font size to use in
Preferences: Map
Window tab.

Enable Marker Dragging

If a marker is in the wrong position and you wish to move it,
you can drag the marker to the right position - but first you
must enable marker dragging, by clicking this option.

Caution: It can easily happen that you get several
markers on top of one another. Consequently there is a risk that
you might move the wrong one. To prevent this, you are
recommended to always hide all markers except the one you wish
to move, before dragging markers. You can easily hide all
markers in a marker set by unticking the 'Check All' option in
the top-left corner of the Map Window or by right-clicking on a
marker in the Marker Set list window and choosing "Hide Marker
Set".

Sometimes when you want to move a marker, the
destination is not close to the starting position. In that
case, you may find it easier to locate the destination in the
map, and drag the place from the marker list on the left side,
to the desired location in the map. You do not need to
have previously enabled marker dragging to do this.

Time Slider

Enables the time slider control, which appears below the map.
In order to use it, the map must contain one or more marker sets
of the 'Individuals & Events' type. The time slider has no
useful role with marker sets which just show the location of
(undated) Place or Address records.

When the time slider is enabled, you can drag it sideways to
hide or show markers. Only those markers which have dates
that fall within the current range of the time slider, will be
visible. This way, it is easy to watch the movements of
people over time, as locations changed.

By default, markers which have no date associated with them (which
includes markers for Place and Address records, and markers for
undated events) will be hidden when the time slider is
active. However, this is configurable in Preferences:
Map Window tab.

View Map in Web Browser ►

View in Google Maps (web)
View the current map in Google maps, in a web browser.
When you view a map in a web browser, markers and shapes are not
displayed.

View in Bing Maps (web)
View the current map in Bing maps, in a web browser.

View in OpenStreetMap (web)
View the current map in OpenStreetMap maps, in a web browser.

Refresh Map

Refreshes the map images you are currently viewing. Map
images are downloaded from the Internet, and cached locally for
better performance.

Refreshing map images is not related to, and has no effect
upon, geocoding.

Options...
Opens the Map
Window tab in Preferences.

title: Media Menu
text:
Menus

Media Menu

This menu is only available when the Media
Window is active.

See also the Media
Toolbar.

List Pane Only
Only the List Pane is visible (see Media
Window).

List & Display Panes
Both the List Pane and the Display Pane are visible (see Media Window).

Display Pane Only
Only the Display Pane is visible
(see Media Window).

Autosize
If checked, the zoom level will be automatically adjusted to
ensure that large pictures will fit in the available space.
Pictures that are smaller than the available space are displayed
at their normal size (100%).

Play/Open in Default Editor
Opens the given media object in a third party application - the
one specified on your computer as the default application for
viewing or editing files of this type. For a picture, this will
usually mean opening a picture editor to view it. For a sound
file, this is likely to mean opening an application to play it.
For a video, this will usually mean opening a video-player
application to view it. For a document, it will usually mean
opening it for viewing and/or editing in a word-processor. If no
application opens for a given media type, when you click on this
command, you may need to configure your PC to specify a default
application for the file type in question.

Locate on Disk
Opens File Explorer and locates the file for the currently
selected media item.

Enable Media Link Tool
Opens the Media Link Tool, as a second tab in
the List Pane. The Media Link Tool is designed to make it as
quick and easy as possible to add links (frame links and simple
links) to the current media item.

Add Simple Link
Create a link from another record to this Media Object. The link
is to the Media Object as a whole, and not to any specific part of
it.

Keywords
Opens the Keywords dialog to view, edit and add keywords for the
currently selected Media records. Supports multiple
selection, so you can add or edit keywords for any number of Media
records at the same time.

Rename Media File
Rename the media file on the hard disk.

Options
Displays options for Media in Preferences.

Expel Embedded Object (Make Linked)

Only normally available when editing a GEDCOM File in
"standalone mode" (not as part of a Family Historian
project). However, it can be enabled if you wish (not
usually recommended) by clicking Enable
Media GEDCOM Embedding in Project Mode (click on the
Advanced button in the General tab of Preferences).

Converts an embedded Media Object into a linked one, by copying
the Media Object into an external file, and storing a file link
to it.

Absorb Linked Object (Make Embedded)

Only normally available when editing a GEDCOM File in
"standalone mode" (not as part of a Family Historian
project). However, it can be enabled if you wish (not
usually recommended) by clicking Enable
Media GEDCOM Embedding in Project Mode (click on the
Advanced button in the General tab of Preferences).

Converts a linked Media Object into an embedded one, by copying
the external linked file, and storing the copy embedded in the
current GEDCOM file. The external file is not affected by this
action.

Note: it is not usually a good idea to do this as
it will make your data file much bigger and much slower to open.

title: Publish Menu
text:
Menus

Publish Menu

The Publish Menu is the menu that appears when you click on the Publish
button
on the main application toolbar. You can also access this menu, as
a submenu of the View menu.

Publishing Tools Finder

Opens the Publishing Tools Finder, which lists all tools for
creating any form of output - reports, charts, diagrams, books,
booklets, queries, maps, family tree CDs, DVDs, website
generation, etc - under useful categories, making it easy to find
the right tool for any given purpose.

Individual Summary Report
A summary report about Individuals.

Family Group Sheet
A summary report about Families.

Media Report
A report about media records.
Each media record represents a picture, a video, a sound file, or
some other kind of media item.

Narrative Reports ►
Narrative reports provide information about Individuals and
Families in a story format.

Ancestors by Generation
A narrative report about an Individual and his or her ancestors.

Descendants by Generation
A narrative report about an Individual and his or her
descendants.

Individual Narrative
A narrative report about an Individual.

Outline Reports ►
Outline reports show ancestors and descendants using lines and
indentation to show relationships.

Ancestor Outline
An outline report about an Individual and his or her ancestors.

Descendant Outline
An outline report about an Individual and his or her
descendants.

Record Detail Reports ►
Record detail reports are designed to include all information
held in a given record. The emphasis is on clarity and
completeness rather than style of presentation.

Record Detail - Families
A record detail report for Family records.

Record Detail - Individuals
A record detail report for Individual records.

Record Detail - Multimedia
A record detail report for Media records.

Record Detail - Notes
A record detail report for Note records.

Record Detail - Places
A record detail report for Place records.

Record Detail - Repositories
A record detail report for Repository records.

Record Detail - Research Notes
A record detail report for Research Notes.

Record Detail - Source Templates
A record detail report for Source Templates records.

Record Detail - Sources
A record detail report for Source records.

Record Detail - Submission
A record detail report for the Submission record (if there is
one)

Record Detail - Submitters
A record detail report for Submitter records.

Special Data Reports ►
Special Data reports focus on some specific kind of data, and
the occurrence of this data throughout the file.

Data - Addresses
Report about addresses used throughout the file.

Data - Groups, Castes
Report about the kind of data held about groups and/or castes
throughout the file.

Data - Occupations
Report showing the complete list of recorded occupations in the
file.

Data - Origins
Report showing all recorded origins (people's origins) in the
file.

Data - Places
Report showing all recorded places in the file.

Data - Religions
Report showing all recorded religions in the file.

Data - Source Types
Report showing all recorded types of sources. Sources can be of
many different types - e.g. census records, birth certificates,
marriage certificates, death certificates, tombstones, interviews,
books, etc.)

Miscellaneous Reports ►
Sundry different reports that don't fall into any of the other
categories.

Calendar
A report showing a calendar and events that happened on
particular days.

Family Group Sheet (for Web or CD)
All reports can be used as the basis of web pages when creating
a website or a family tree CD. However, the two most commonly-used
candidates are the Internet Summary report and the Family Group
Sheet. This variant of the Family Group Sheet is provided as a
matter of convenience. The idea is that if you wish to use a
Family Group Sheet as a template for your web pages, you can use
this version of the report rather than the normal version. The
default options in this variant of the report have been chosen to
be more suitable for website or family tree CD generation than the
ordinary Family Group Sheet options. Also, this way, if you find
that you wish to change the report options for use in this context
(website or CD creation) you can do so without affecting the
normal Family Group Sheet.

File Statistics
A report showing information about the project as a whole.

How Related
A report detailing how any two Individuals are related, directly
or indirectly.

Individual Census Report
A report detailing Individual census events.

Individual Record Notes
Record notes are notes about a person as a whole (as opposed to
more detailed notes which may cover specific events in a person's
life, or specific attributes of a person). You can also have
record notes that are about a person's family, and their marriage
to another person. These notes are included in Individual Summary
reports and in Family Group Sheets. But it is sometimes convenient
to be able to read such notes on their own - which is what this
report is for.

Individual Summary Report (for Web, CD or DVD)
All reports can be used as the basis of web pages when creating
a website or a family tree CD or DVD. However, the two most
commonly-used candidates are the Internet Summary report and the
Family Group Sheet. This variant of the Individual Summary Report
is provided as a matter of convenience. The idea is that if you
wish to use an Individual Summary Report as a template for your
web pages, you can use this version of the report rather than the
normal version. The default options in this variant of the report
have been chosen to be more suitable for website or family tree
CD/DVD generation than the ordinary Individual Summary Report
options. Also, this way, if you find that you wish to change the
report options for use in this context (website or CD/DVD
creation) you can do so without affecting the normal Individual
Summary Report.

Individual Timeline
A report showing important events in a person's life (comparable
to the information displayed in the Facts
tab of the Property Box).

LDS Ordinances
'LDS' stands for 'Latter Day Saints'. Family Historian uses GEDCOM as its standard
format. GEDCOM is the global standard format for shared
genealogical data. It was created by the Church of Latter Day
Saints, sometimes called the LDS Church. The format includes
special ordinances which are of relevance to the LDS Church. This
report covers these ordinances.

List Report
It is sometimes useful to create Named Lists of records for
various purposes. You can view these lists, and edit them, in the
Records Window. You can also attach notes to any list item. A
typical use of a Named List might be to create a 'To Do' list, of
records that you wish to research when visiting a Record Office.
You might attach specific notes to listed records. This report
allows you to print off the list, and any notes.

Note Records
A report displaying the content of one or more Note
records.

Place Report
A report showing information about
places (Place records).

Research Note
A report displaying the content of one or more Research
Notes.

Source Summary Report
