A summary report about Sources.

Sources and Citations
A report showing Source record
details, and their associated source citations.

Tagged Notes
A report on notes containing a specified hashtag.

Custom Reports ►
Family Historian reports usually have a great many options and
they can be customised in numerous ways. You can save your
customisations as a completely new report type, if you wish. To do
this, click on the Save Report As
button when viewing a report, and choose 'Custom Report Type' from
the menu that appears. Custom reports are accessed from, this
submenu. The same submenu also provides a command to let you
delete custom report types if you wish.

Books & Booklets...
Opens the Book List Dialog
which lists all books and booklets in the current project.
From here you can create new books and booklets or browse or edit
existing books and booklets.

Websites & Family Tree CD/DVDs
Opens the Websites
& Family Tree CD/DVDs Dialog. Here you can family
tree websites, or equivalent website packages, which can be
distributed to friends and family on a CD, DVD, or memory stick.

title: Query Menu
text:
Query Window

Query Menu

This menu can only be accessed by clicking on the Menu button
on the Query Toolbar
which is attached to the Query
Window.

New Custom Query
Create a new custom query

Save As Custom Query
Make a copy of the current query (standard or custom) and save
it as a new custom query.

Manage Queries
Opens the Manage
Queries Dialog where the full list of queries can be viewed,
and queries can be maintained.

Run and Invert Result Set

Run the current query, but instead of displaying all records
or data items that it matches in the Result Set tab,
display all records or data items (of the query type) that are not
matched by the query.

Add Row Records to Named List
Queries based on a given record type
(which is most of them), produce a result set in which each row
shows information about a given record. These are 'row
records'. For queries of this type, this command will add
all these records to a Named List that you specify. So, if there
are 100 rows in the result set, there will be 100 records added to
the specified Named List.

You cannot use this command with queries which are not
record-based. There are 3 non-record query types: facts
(events and attributes), source citations, and witnesses.

Remove Row Records from Named List
Similar to the previous command, but instead of adding the row
records to a given Named List, they are removed from it.

Set Flag on Row Records
Set a record flag that you specify on each 'row record' (see
above) in the result set. Can only be used with
Individual records.

Clear Flag on Row Records
Remove a record flag that you specify from each 'row record'
(see above) in the result set. Can only be used with
Individual records.

Add Selected Cell Records to Named List

Adds every record corresponding to a cell in the current
selection, to a specified Named List.

Save Result Set As

Saves the entire result set as either a PDF file (see PDF
File Support), a Comma-separated CSV File, or as a text
file.

View in Note Window

If a data-linked cell is selected (see
explanation below), and the item of data is a note, or any other
kind of item that can be edited in the Note
Window, this command will cause the item to be displayed
in the Note Window. If the selected item of data is a Note
record or a Research Note, or a link to a Note record or
Research Note, this same command will also cause the note
associated with the Note record or Research Note, to be
displayed in the Note Window.

Tip: If you right-click on a data-linked cell
containing a record or field that is suitable for viewing in the
Note Window, the dropdown menu will show or include a command, View in Note Window, which allows
the appropriate item to be viewed in the Note Window.

Locate in Property Box

If a data-linked cell is selected (see
explanation below), this command will display that data item or
record in the Property Box.

Tip: If you right-click on a data-linked cell
containing a record, the dropdown menu will show or include a
command, Properties, which
allows you to view that record in the Property Box. If you
right-click on a data-linked cell containing a field, the
dropdown menu will have two commands:
Locate in Property Box and Locate
in All Tab.You can also double-click on either kind of
cell as a fast way of viewing the record or field in the
Property Box.

Locate in All Tab

This is similar to the previous command but whereas that command
will pick the most suitable tab to show the data in, this command
will always locate the item in the 'All' tab of the Property Box.

Options
Opens the Query
Window tab of Preferences to set various fonts used for
displaying queries on screen and printing, to set colours and
print margins, and other options relating to the Query Window.

Query Window Help (sub menu)

> The Query Window (overview)
Quick shortcut to the Query
Window Help page.

> Expressions and Contexts of
Use
Quick shortcut to Expressions
and Contexts of Use.

> Functions by Category
Quick shortcut to Functions
By Category.

Data-linked Cells

Some cells in a query result set display calculated values.
Others simply display the value of a particular item of data, taken
directly from records in the current project. The latter kind of
cell is called 'data-linked' and by default it will display in black
where ordinary text will be grey. Data-linked cells can
represent either records or fields. See also the discussion of
data-linked cells on the Result
Set tab.

title: Report Menu
text:
Menus

Report Menu

This menu is only available when the Report
Window is active.

Refresh Report

If you have changed the underlying data that a report is based
on, click on this option to force the report to update to reflect
the change.

Records...
Most reports are based around a record. The Individual Summary
report, for example, shows details about a particular Individual.
When you run the report you must select the record to base the
report on. If you wish, you can, in most cases, base reports on
multiple records. The Records button shows which
records the current report is based on, and allows you to change
them, or re-order them.

Go To Page
Use this command to go to a particular page in the current
report.

Copy Page ►
Use this command to copy a page of a report in Bitmap or
Enhanced Metafile format. If copying as a bitmap, you can choose
to copy it either at the current zoom level or at the default
(100%) zoom level.

Zoom ►
This submenu provides various zoom options.

Zoom In
Zoom in.

Zoom Out
Zoom out

Whole Page
Zoom so that a whole page is visible (or 2 pages if the Two
Pages check box has been ticked in the panel on the right
hand side of the window).

Page Width
Zoom so that the whole width of a page is visible (or the width
of 2 pages if the Two Pages check box has been ticked
in the panel on the right hand side of the window).

Save Report As ►
Save the current report in the following formats...

PDF File
Save the diagram to PDF file format - see PDF
File Support.

Web Page (HTML)
HTML format is the format of the World Wide Web.

Word-processor Document (RTF)
Rich Text Format is supported by most serious word-processors
(e.g. Microsoft Word). If you save a report or book in this
format, you can view and edit it in a word-processor.

Text File
Text format. In this format, all formatting information and
pictures are lost. Only the basic content is retained as text.

Custom Report Type
This is not a file format as such. When you save a report as a
custom report type, you are creating a new type of report, which
you can re-use later. Custom report types can be accessed from the
Custom Reports submenu of the Publish
menu.

Report Options

The options available for reports are extensive and vary between
different report types. This command opens the Report
Options Dialog to let you view and/or alter these options.

title: Tools menu
text:
Menus

Tools Menu

How Related
Opens the How Related
dialog box which shows you up to 9 different ways that two people
are related. If they are not directly related to one another, it
will show you how they are indirectly related through a third
party, if they are.

External File Links
Open the Work
with External File Links dialog to manage links from Media
records to their associated media files (e.g. picture file); and
check for, and fix, any 'broken' links.

Named Lists and Record Flags
Open the Work with Lists and
Record Flags dialog to perform various tasks relating to
named lists and record flags.

Work with Data ►

This submenu allows you to open the Work
with Data Dialog to view and edit values for the following
data types that have been used in the file:

Places

Addresses (Event & Attribute Addresses or Source
& Repository Addresses)

Occupations

Religions

Groups/Castes

National or Tribal Origins

Generic Source Types

If you wish to, you can use the dialog box to update these
values throughout your file. For example, suppose you discover
that you have spelled a given occupation inconsistently in
different contexts. Without having to locate the actual records
(though you can do that too if you wish) you can change values,
and even merge multiple different values together.

The final item on this menu is

Fact/Witness Sentences

This displays a list of 'sentence overrides' in the Results
Window. 'Sentence overrides' are modifications to
the automatically-generated narrative sentences, displayed in
the Sentence field of the Facts
tab of the Property Box, or in the Witnesses
Window. The result set has one row for every
fact sentence in the current project that has been overridden,
as well as one for every instance of a witness to a fact, where
the witness sentence has been overridden. In other words,
you can potentially get multiple rows for the same fact (event
or attribute).

The columns in the result set are explained in the following
table:

Column Heading

Description

Date

Fact date

Fact Id

This is a number assigned arbitrarily for the purposes
of this report only. The reason for including it is
simply that it provides a convenient and easy way of
seeing at a glance when 2 or more rows relate to the same
fact. If they do they will have the same fact id.

Principal

The fact principal. For example, in a Birth or
Baptism event, this would be the person being born or
baptised.

Principal 2

The second fact principal. Individual facts
(like Birth and Baptism) have only one principal, but Family
facts (like Marriage and Divorce) may have two.

Type

"Ind" for Individual facts and "Fam" for Family facts
(see previous).

Fact Name

The fact name (Birth, Marriage, etc).

Fact

A field that represents the fact itself.
Double-click on this field to view the fact in the Facts
tab of the Property Box. A brief summary of the fact
details is displayed in this column.

Value

Facts can be events or attributes. Attributes,
like 'Religion' or 'Occupation', have values.
Events do not. For example, the attributes
'Religion' and 'Occupation' might have values like
'Catholic' or 'Farmer'.

For attributes, their associated value will be displayed
in this column. For events, the column will be
blank.

Witness

Remember that each row can represent a fact sentence
that has been overridden or a witness sentence that has
been overridden. For fact sentences, this column
will be blank. For witness sentences, this column
will show the name of the witness.

Role

For fact sentences, this column will be blank. For
witness sentences, this column will show the role of the
witness. A witness role might be 'Bridesmaid' or
'Best man' for a Marriage event, or perhaps 'Beneficiary'
for a Will event.

Sentence (display)

This column shows how the fact or witness sentence would
look in a report.

Sentence (raw)

Overridden sentences can include Sentence Template Codes, which are
used to generate the sentence that appears in
reports. This column displays the 'raw' content,
including sentence template codes.

Record Identifiers
Open the Work with Record
Identifiers dialog. This dialog allows you to renumber
record identifiers (although this is not recommended) and to
perform various other tasks relating to record identifiers.

Manage Autotext
Open the Manage Autotext
Dialog.

Language Packs
Open the Language Packs
Dialog.

Fact Types
Open the Fact Types Dialog to work with
fact definitions and fact sets.

Source Template Definitions
Open the Source
Template Definitions Dialog.

Automatic Source Citations

Open the Automatic
Source Citation pane which you can use to define, and
enable, an automatic source citation. When you have enabled an
automatic source citation, new and updated data will
automatically be given the defined citation. You can also copy
and paste an automatic source citation, if you wish to apply it
to existing data that you are not changing.

When automatic source citations are enabled, the text
'Auto-Citation Enabled' will show in the last pane of the status
bar, in the bottom right corner of the main application window.

Re-order Out-of-Sequence Data
Opens the Re-order
Out-of-Sequence Data Dialog to check whether any data is in
the wrong order (such as events, attributes, children, marriages,
and spouses) and to re-order them, if necessary.

Uncategorised Data ►
'Uncategorised Data Fields' (also known as UDFs) are fields
which Family Historian has created to store data that it does not
recognise. This can occur when a GEDCOM
file that was created by another application is opened or
imported, if the file contains fields which are invalid in some
way, or which are the other application's extensions to GEDCOM.
UDFs can also be created when you import a GEDCOM file into a new
project, if you previously chose the option Store
Uncategorised for handling other applications'
extensions to GEDCOM, in the File Load/Save tab
of Preferences. Family Historian treats
UDF data as text.

The submenu allows you to either Find Uncategorised Data
or Recover Uncategorised Data. If
you choose the latter option, Family Historian will use the latest
information it has to identify and process UDFs, to convert them
into fields which can be fully incorporated into your
project. Details of which fields were 'recovered' in this
way, if any, are written to a log file. Log files can be
accessed from the Windows menu.

Windows Snipping Tool

The Windows Snipping Tool allows you to click-and-drag anywhere
on the screen to select an area that you wish to copy as an
image to the clipboard. For example, you could use this
technique to copy a section of a diagram or map. You can
then insert the copied image into the program as a Media
record, by clicking on the 'Add' menu, and choosing
"Picture from Clipboard" and "Paste Copied Picture". You
will be prompted to specify a file name for the pasted image,
and optionally a location if not the default.

Another option is to simply click 'Paste' on the Edit
menu. In most contexts, this is just another way of doing
the same thing. You will be asked if you want to insert the
clipboard image as a new Media record. However, if you
click 'Paste' when viewing the Diagram
Window (or if you right-click on the background of the
Diagram Window and choose 'Paste' from the dropdown menu that
appears), you will be offered a choice. You can either
paste the copied image into the current diagram, or you can
insert the copied image into the current project as a new Media
record.

If you have copied an image, and want to insert it into the
program as a picture of a particular person (that is, inserting
it, and linking it to a given person in a single step), you can
do this too. In that case, click the Add
Media button on the Media
tab of the Property Box, when viewing the record of the
person in question. Then choose "Paste Copied Image" from
the menu that appears.

See also Web Clipping.

<some plugins may be listed here>

If you have installed or written any plugins (see next item),
you can opt for them to be added to the Tools menu. If so,
they will appear at this position on the Tools menu.

Plugins
Opens the Plugins Dialog which
shows a list of installed plugins. You can use the Plugins
Dialog to install more plugins, and to access the Family Historian
Plugin Store to download free plugins. You can also create
your own plugins if you wish using tools and documentation
provided. Everything you need to do this is available via
the Plugins Dialog.

Preferences
Open the Preferences Dialog
to set your preferences for various aspects of the program.

title: View Menu
text:
Menus

View Menu

Go To ►
This submenu provides commands for going back and forward (only
supported in the context of the Focus
Window), going to a record (in the Records
Window) and showing the file root as focus person in the
Focus Window (equivalent to pressing the Home button on the main application
toolbar).

Display in Focus Window
Displays the selected person as focus person in the Focus
Window.

More Workspace Windows ►
Displays an option to open each of the other workspace
windows.

Research Notes
Displays all Research Notes
in the Records Window.

Other Record Lists ►

Activates the Records Window
and displays the appropriate tab for records of the following
types:

Individuals

Families

Notes

Sources

Repositories

Media

Places

Addresses

Source Templates

Special Records ►
Each Family Historian project has only one Header
record, and should normally have at most one Submitter
and one Submission record.
This submenu has commands to open the Property
Box and display these records. If there is no submitter or
submission record you will be asked if you want to create one.

Named Lists ►
Provides quick access to any Named
List. Named Lists are viewed in the Named Lists pane
which is displayed, when enabled, on the right side of the Records
Window. See also the Records Window's Lists
menu.

Charts ►
Displays a menu with a choice of options for displaying charts
and diagrams in the Diagram Window,
including saved charts and custom diagram types that you have
created yourself. This is essentially the same menu that is
displayed when you click on the Charts button on the main
application toolbar.

Publish ►
Displays a menu with a choice of options for displaying reports
in the Report Window. The same
menu also has three other menu commands:

Publishing Tools Finder - a tool for finding any
report, book, diagram, chart, query, smart folder, website or
other listing of any kind

Books & Booklets - lets you select books to
view and/or create a new book (see also the
Book Window)

Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks - opens the Websites
& Family Tree USB Sticks Dialog.

This is the same menu that is displayed when you click on the
Publish button
on the main application toolbar.

Queries/Smart Folders ►
Displays a dropdown menu with a choice of options for displaying
queries in the Query Window.
There is also a "Smart Folders" menu command which allows smart
folders to be viewed and edited in the Query Window (Smart Folder
pane). And there is a "Manage Folder Sets" menu command
which opens the Manage Folder
Sets Dialog. This is the same menu that is displayed
when you click on the Query button on the main
application toolbar.

Maps ►
Displays a dropdown menu with a choice of options for displaying
Map information in the Map Window:

Map Window
Opens the Map Window without creating any new marker sets.
Individuals & Events

You will be prompted to select one or more Individual
records. If any Individual records are already selected
in the current workspace window, they will be automatically
added to the selection list. Events and addresses can be
associated with places and addresses, both of which can have a
latitude and longitude. You will be asked if you want to
mark event places or addresses (or addresses "for
preference"). Then the Map Window will be displayed with
a marker set showing an expandable 2-level view. This
view shows the Individuals you selected and all the places
that they are associated with, and a map marker for each one,
if the place's latitude/longitude is known or can be
determined automatically (that is, geocoded).
Places
You will be prompted to select one or more Place
records. If any a Place records are already selected in
the current workspace window, they will be automatically added
to the selection list. Then the Map Window will be
displayed with a marker set showing a map marker for each
place, if the place's latitude/longitude is known or can
be determined automatically (that is, geocoded).
Addresses
You will be prompted to select one or more Address
records. If any Address records are already selected in
the current workspace window, they will be automatically added
to the selection list. Then the Map Window will be
displayed with a marker set showing a map marker for each
address, if the address's latitude/longitude is known
(addresses are not automatically geocoded).
Map Overlays
Opens the Map Overlays
Dialog.

Saved Maps
Opens the Saved Maps Dialog.

This is the same menu that is displayed when you click on the
Map button
on the main application toolbar.

If you already have an open Map Window and your
preference is to re-use the open Map Window (which is the
default), a new marker set will be added to any existing marker
sets that may already be showing in the open Map Window.
You can easily switch between marker sets, or hide/show all
markers, or delete or re-arrange them, using the buttons,
options and Marker Set list, in the top-left of the Map
Window. However, if you prefer to open a new Map Window
each time, set the 'Re-use of Open Windows Permitted' setting to
'No' for the Map Window in the Workspaces
tab of Preferences (accessible from the Tools menu).

Navigation Bar
Shows or hides the Navigation Bar

Citations to Source Record
Shows a table detailing all citations to the selected Source
record, in the Results
Window. If no Source record is selected, you will be
prompted to select one.

Prepared Citation
Shows the current prepared citation (if there is one)
in the Citation Window.
See also Citation
Window with a Prepared Citation.

Record Links
Shows all records that have links to the selected record. You
can also 'go to' those records (view them in the Property
Box).

Properties

Opens the Property Box to view
the selected record.

Tip: A quick way to open the Property Box for a
selected individual is to press ALT+Enter. Also, in many
contexts, if you right-click on a record, there will be a
'Properties' option.

title: Window Menu
text:
Menus

Window Menu

Refresh

Refreshes the current displays of the underlying data.

Close All Nonessential Windows

Closes all workspace windows except the startup window - e.g.
all diagram, report, book, query, media, map or web search
windows. By default, the Focus
Window is the startup window. Also by default, the Records Window always has an
icon in the Navigation Bar, even if closed. However, this
is configurable in Preferences.

Lock Window (prevent re-use)

Depending on the settings in the Workspaces
tab in Preferences, some workspace windows can be
re-used. When a workspace is re-used, the existing
contents are normally replaced. The exception to this is
the Map Window. When you open the Map Window, you normally
specify a set of places or events to mark on the map. A
new marker set is created with markers for each such place or
event. The Map Window can display multiple marker
sets. If it is re-used, an additional marker set will be
added. The existing marker sets will not be replaced.

If you allow the Diagram Window
to be re-used and if you are currently viewing a diagram in a
Diagram Window, and you choose an option to open another
diagram, Family Historian will re-use the existing Diagram
Window to show the new diagram, replacing the current contents
of the Diagram Window. If you wish to make quite sure that
a Diagram Window will not be re-used in this way, do not allow
re-use of the Diagram Window (this is specified in the Workspaces
tab in Preferences). If you want to allow re-use of
the Diagram Window usually, but want to prevent it in a
particular case, tick Lock Window when the relevant
window is active. Locking a window only prevents the window
being re-used. It does not prevent it being edited or closed, or
anything else.

The Diagram Window can never be re-used if it is displaying a saved
chart - that is, a diagram that has been saved as a
saved chart, in Family Historian chart format. In this
case, the Lock Window option will not be available.

The Lock Window command is applicable to all workspace windows
where re-use is permitted. There is no limit to the
number of workspace windows that you can have open at any one
time.

Workspace windows can only be re-used if re-use is enabled for
the relevant workspace type, in the Workspaces
tab in Preferences - and even in that case, you can
prevent re-use for any particular window, by clicking on Lock
Window . If re-use is not enabled in Preferences
for a given workspace type, locking windows of that type will
have no effect.

Please note incidentally that a Diagram Window can only be
re-used to display a diagram, a Report Window can only be
re-used to display a report, and so on. If you choose a menu
command to open a report (say) and there is no available Report Window which can be re-used, a new Report Window will be
opened.

The Focus Window and Records Window can never be re-used so
this option is not available for those windows.

Cascade
Organise all workspace windows
into a tidy overlapping arrangement.

Tile Horizontally
Organise all workspace windows
into a horizontally tiled arrangement.

Tile Vertically

Organise all workspace windows
into a vertically tiled arrangement.

Arrange Icons
Rarely used. If you have minimized workspace windows within the
frame of the main application window, each workspace window will
have an icon to represent it - usually displayed in the bottom
left corner of the main application window. This command will
arrange these icons tidily.

Log Files
Opens the Log
File Dialog to display all log files in the current project
(if any). The Log File Dialog is only available in the context of
a project.

<Window List>

List of currently open workspace windows. Click on any of
these windows to activate it (bring it to the front).

title: Menus
text:
Menus

This section describes the main menus. Some menu commands require that
one or more items be selected. If nothing is selected, these menu
commands may be greyed.

The main menus are:

File

Edit

View

Add

Tools

Lists (only
available when Records Window is active)

Diagram (only
available when Diagram Window is active)

Media (only
available when Media Window is active)

Report (only
available when Report Window is active)

Book (only available
when Book Window is active)

Mapping (only available
when Map Window is active

Internet

Window

Help

Many of the commands listed in these menus are also available from toolbars.

In addition to these menus, many items have context menus.
These are menus which appear when you right-click on an item. They allow
you to perform tasks and activities which are relevant to the item you
clicked on.

Some windows and some dialogs have additional menus which can be
accessed by clicking a Menu button
on the window or dialog's toolbar. See the specific window Help
pages for more details.

title: Merge/Compare Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Merge/Compare Dialog

Merge/Compare Dialog (File Merge)

Family Historian supports 3 types of merging:

Basic Record Merging

Branch Merging

File Merging (also known as Project Merging)

Corresponding to each of these there are also 3 types of comparing:

Basic Record Comparing

Branch Comparing

File Comparing (or Project Comparing)

The Merge/Compare Dialog is used for all three types of
merging/comparing. The documentation emphasizes merging more than
comparing, because in practice the ability to compare records or files
is often important primarily as a way of helping you get the merge
right. However that is not always the case. Sometimes it is just the
ability to compare files or records that you need. See File Merging and Comparing for an example of how
you can use File Comparing to help you keep an audit trail of
changes made to your file.

The differences between the different types of merging are explained
in Introduction
to Merging - the Three Types.

For more detailed information about the different types, see Basic Record Merging and Branch Merging and File Merging and Comparing.

To find out more about the Merge/Compare Dialog, see Features of the Merge/Compare Dialog.

Tip: It is always a good idea to make a backup of your
file or project before making any significant changes to it, in case you
make a mistake and want to �rollback� your changes. Merging (any type of
merging) is a relatively complex task, and you would be well-advised -
especially if you are not already familiar and comfortable with the
merge process - to make a backup of your file before you start.
See Backups for more information.

title: More Diagram Dimensions
text:
Diagram Options
Dialog: Dimensions Tab

More Dimensions

Family Historian dimensions are given in your preferred units. You can
choose between inches, centimetres, or millimetres. These are set in Preferences
(accessible from the Tools menu).

Diagram Orientation Issue

All diagrams can be displayed in all orientations - that is, top-down,
bottom-up, left-right or right- left. The dimension settings are
applicable to all orientations. But for convenience all descriptions and
labels are given as for top-down orientation.

Vertical Dimensions

Family Historian uses the Min proximity gap below boxes
value to determine how close one box is allowed to get to another. It is
the minimum gap that must be left below each box.

The Ancestor connector offset is only used in All
Relatives trees where the Style is 'Flat'. It specifies the
distance between the horizontal crossing line that connects
an ancestor box to their parents' child bar, and the child bar
itself. The 'child bar' is the horizontal line below a set of
parents that all their children are connected to. The 'crossing
line' is only used in All Relatives diagrams. It is usually
dotted, but you can make it solid if you wish (see the Lines tab of
Diagram Options). If the Ancestor connector offset value is 0, the
crossing lines will overlap child bars, which is not recommended
as this can result in a diagram which is confusing and hard to follow.

Other vertical dimensions are not described here as it is easier to
see what they are used for by looking at the images on the right hand
side of the More Dimensions dialog.

Other Dimensions

Relationship description gap
If you are showing relationship descriptions, this value
specifies how big a gap there should be between the relationship
descriptions and the rest of the diagram.

Stretchy line zigzag width and height
Stretchy lines are only used to connect remarriage boxes (see
Spouse Display Options
in the General tab
of the Diagram Options Dialog). You can use these settings to
control the shape of these stretchy lines, if you use them.

Avoid boundaries gap
You can choose to prevent boxes overlaying page boundaries by
clicking on the Avoid Page Boundaries button on the Diagram Window toolbar. The gap
specified here determines how close boxes are allowed to get to a
page boundary in that case.

Gap between trees
These settings are used to control how trees are spaced out when
you generate an Everyone diagram.

Icon size
Use this setting to specify the size (height and width) of the
space that you wish to allocate for each icon displayed below each
box (if any). The display of icons is controlled on the Boxes
tab of Diagram Options.

Note: This setting is used with vector format icons only.
Pre-installed icons use a vector format. Custom icons
usually are not. Icon Size is ignored when
displaying custom or legacy bitmap icons (if any) - that is, icons
in bitmap file format.

Gap between icons
This setting specifies the horizontal gap between icons, and the
vertical gap between rows of icons.

title: More Layout Options Dialog
text:
Diagram Options Dialog:
General Tab

More Layout Options Dialog

Fields

Limit overhang
You can use this feature to specify that a given box must not be
overhung except by direct ancestors, for a given number of
generations back. This may sometimes help to make complex diagrams
clearer. But it will spread boxes out and make diagrams larger.
The bigger the number of generations specified, the larger the
diagram is likely to be.

Place solitary ancestors close to their parents

Only applicable to All Relatives trees. If this
option is checked, Family Historian will automatically set the Keep
Near Parents box state flag for any 'solitary' ancestors
(that is, ancestors which either have no recorded spouse, or
their spouse, if also an ancestor, has no recorded parents).
This can improve the layout in some cases.

For more on Box States in general, and the Keep Near
Parents box state in particular, see the Diagram menu.

Centre diagram root between parents

Only applicable to the Ancestors and Descendants
tree, and the
All Relatives tree. Check this option if you want the
root always to be centred between his or her parents. If not
set, the root's parents will be positioned, by default, roughly
in the mid-point between all of the root's siblings.

Centre ancestor-to- parents connecting line between the parents

Only applicable to the All Relatives tree. Check this
option if you want parents of ancestor boxes to appear
immediately above the ancestor. If this option is not set a
given ancestor's parents will be positioned, by default, roughly
in the mid-point between all of the ancestor's siblings. If the
ancestor has no siblings (or none showing) this option will make
little difference.

You can override this option and set the Keep Near
Parents box state flag on any ancestor or its siblings to
position the parents immediately above the box in question - see
the Diagram Window for more on the Keep Near Parents
box state flag.

Straighten descendant branch lines where possible
If this box is checked, spouse boxes will be taken into account
when centring children below their parents. This may mean that the
line connecting parents to their child has a kink in it. But
descendant branches as a whole will be much straighter -
especially when displaying a single line of descendants over
several generations.

Disable Box Autosizing

Disables the autosize box feature for the current diagram.

Ordinarily boxes will automatically adjust their size to fit
the text that they contain, subject to the minimum values set in
the Dimensions tab. If the text changes, or if the font
changes, each box will adjust its size accordingly. You
can disable this autosize feature for individual boxes if you
wish (see the 'Box States' submenu on the Diagram menu).
If you manually resize a box, or if you resize it by using one
of the 'Layout & Scaling' submenu commands, the affected
boxes will have autosize disabled. By choosing the
'Disable Box Autosizing' option here, however, you are
effectively overriding the individual Autosize Box
states and disabling box autosizing for the whole diagram.
This can be useful if you have added lines and other items which
are aligned with boxes in trees and you don't wish the boxes to
move.

Tip: Font sizes are determined in part by your
current printer. If you change printer, the text may get
slightly bigger or smaller. If autosize boxes is enabled,
this may cause the whole tree (or trees) to change layout
perceptibly, and non-tree items (lines, pictures, etc) which
previously were aligned with boxes may cease to be correctly
aligned. You can prevent this misalignment happening by
disabling box autosizing. However, it is possible, if you
do this, that the resized text may no longer fit in the
boxes. If this is the case, you should consider making
font sizes smaller accordingly. Font sizes can be adjusted
in the Text tab of Diagram options.

Keep First Child Near Parent
If this option is checked, the 'Keep Near Parent' flag
will be automatically set for each descendant's first child, in a
descendant diagram. This is most often used with left-to-right
descendant diagrams, as the descendants are displayed in a
convenient 'waterfall' layout.

title: Movement Control Box
text:
Diagram Window

Movement Control Box (Diagram Window)

The Movement Control Box allows you to perform a range of tasks, such
as move boxes and branches, switch the positions of spouses and siblings
for display purposes (if you don't wish to change them permanently),
move entire trees to different positions (diagrams can contain any
number of trees - see Diagram Elements),
and even adjust the position of an entire diagram on the printed page or
across multiple printed pages. You can also use it to adjust diagram scaling
- that is, the size that the diagram has when printed. Diagrams can be
printed at any scale.

The Movement Control Box is opened (or closed) by clicking on Enable
Moving/Resizing on the Diagram
Menu, or on the equivalent button on the Diagram
toolbar. When Moving/Resizing is enabled, you can resize any box
by clicking on it to select it, and then clicking-and-dragging on any of
the little white squares that appear in the corners of selected boxes
(they are only white when Moving/Resizing is enabled). The only
limitation to this is when the Everything drag-action is
selected (see note on this below).

Please note that although all diagrams can have any orientation, for
convenience the descriptions below assume a top-down orientation.

Movable Bar Types

There are 4 movable bar types. These are:

Child
bar

Used in all trees except ancestor
trees. Where a person or a couple's children are displayed
below them, these are normally attached to a horizontal bar called
a child bar. These bars are coloured yellow when
Box & Bar moving is enabled (see image left). Child bars
can be moved out (away from the parents) and sideways.

Parent bar

Used in all trees except descendant trees. Where a person's
parents are displayed above them (as in an Ancestor tree), these
are normally attached to a horizontal bar called a parent bar.
These bars are coloured green when Box & Bar moving is enabled
(see image left). Parent bars can be moved out (away from
the children) and sideways.

Ancestor offset bar

Used in All Relative trees only. These vertical
bars can be used to offset ancestor branches vertically, if
required, in All Relatives trees. These bars are coloured
blue when Box & Bar moving is enabled (see image left).
By default, they are barely visible as blue dots. They
become bars when you click-and-drag on them to stretch them.
They extend in one direction only - outwards.

Ancestor sibling bar

Used in All Relative trees only. All ancestor
siblings are attached to these horizontal bars in All Relatives
trees. These bars are coloured white when Box & Bar moving is
enabled (see image left). An ancestor that has no siblings
with have a minimal sibling bar, consisting of a single white dot,
but this can be stretched if you click-and-drag on it.
Sibling bars can be moved out and sideways. Although you can
move a sibling bar both outwards and sideways, the branch boxes
attached to a sibling bar can not be moved below the top of the
ancestor offset bar, to bring them down on the 'wrong' side of the
ancestor offset bar. If the bar is attached to a left-side
ancestor, the 'wrong' side would be the right-side, and vice
versa.

Please note: in some cases these bars may overlap.

Fields and Buttons

Box & Bar

When enabled, you can click and drag on any box to move that
box, and its branch, 'outwards'. For example, if you
clicked-and-dragged on an ancestor box in an ancestor diagram
you could move that box, and its entire ancestral branch
outwards (or back).

When the drag-action is box and bar you can either click on a
box or on a bar (see Movable Bar Types above for
details of supported bar moves).

Because Family Historian trees are smart trees, the diagram
will automatically adjust to accommodate the new branch
positions, and to make best use of space.

The ...within row check box changes the behaviour of
Box & Bar moves. If ticked, when you drag a box (or boxes)
or bar, instead of the boxes and branches being moved out of the
row that they belong to, the whole row will be widened to
include the box in its new position. This could be useful if,
for example, you want to position a number of boxes in staggered
pattern (alternately higher or lower in the row) to save space.

If the orientation of the diagram is left-right or right-left,
rather than top-down or bottom-up, the option still works, but
controls movement within columns instead of rows.

Fixed Point

Fixed Point dragging is used if you want to move 2 spouses or
siblings further apart (or bring them back closer together). But
you can also use it to move entire branches of a tree further
apart or closer together. For example, to move a brother away
from this sister, make the sister a fixed point by selecting her
box and then clicking on the Set
button. Then click-and-drag on the brother's box.

To drag 2 entire branches apart (or bring them back together)
make any one box, in either branch, a fixed point; and
click-and-drag on any box in the other branch (this only works
if the boxes belong to the same tree).

You can use fixed point dragging to create a space within a
diagram to put a picture into (say). Suppose in a descendant
diagram, you clicked on a descendant box and moved his or her
entire branch outwards. His or her siblings (and their branches)
would move inwards to fill up the space. To move them back to
where they had been, make one of the siblings a fixed point and
click-and-drag to move the others.

Tip: When moving/resizing is enabled, a quick way
to set a fixed point is to press the Alt key
while clicking on a box. Pressing Alt while
clicking elsewhere clears the fixed point and switches you back
to Box and Bar.

Tree
When enabled, you can move an entire tree around by
clicking-and-dragging on any box within the tree. You can also
move multiple trees around by selecting boxes from different trees
and clicking- and-dragging on any one of them. You do not have to
select all boxes within each tree. If the selection includes one
or more boxes from a given tree, that entire tree will will be
moved, along with the other trees, when you click-and-drag on any
selected box.
Usually when you open a diagram there is only one tree in it
(the exceptions are the All Relatives + Indirect Relatives
and the Everyone diagrams which typically contains
numerous trees, even when first opened). You can add more trees
using commands on the Diagram menu.

Everything (position on page)

Use this option when you wish to change the position of an
entire diagram on the printed page. If you choose this option,
the display of page boundaries will be automatically enabled if
they weren't already, so that you can see what you are doing.
Then, to move the diagram, simply click-and-drag anywhere on the
diagram.

Note:

Tip: There is also another way of changing a
diagram's position on the printed page. Instead of the approach
just described, you can, if you prefer, click-and-drag on any
intersection of the grid lines that appear, when page boundaries
are displayed. By doing so, you move the grid. When you move the
grid, you are effectively changing the position of the diagram
relative to the printed page. You can do this whenever page
boundaries are displayed, whether or not moving/resizing has
been enabled.

Note: Ordinarily, when moving/resizing is enabled
you can still click on any box to select it, you can click on
any expansion button to expand a branch, and you can
click-and-drag on any of the little white squares that appear in
the corners of selected boxes, to resize the box. All of these
actions become temporarily unavailable when select Everything
(position on page) as your chosen Drag-and-Move action.

Shift Box: Spouse
Use the Shift Spouse buttons (
and ) to
change the displayed order of spouse boxes within a diagram. This
does not affect the order of spouses in your records. A
'spouse box' (that is, a box of that type) is a box that
represents a spouse of a descendant or cousin of the root.
Boxes that represent ancestors of the tree root, for example, are
not spouse boxes as such as. See Box
Types to learn more about the various types of boxes in
diagrams.

Tip: If you wish to change the order of spouses in
your records use the
Move Up and
Move Down commands instead of the Shift Spouse buttons.

Shift Box: Sibling
Use the Shift Sibling buttons (
and ) to
change the displayed order of sibling boxes within a diagram. This
does not affect the order of sibling in your records.
Sibling boxes are boxes of type 'descendant', representing
siblings in the diagram. See Box
Types to learn more about the various types of boxes in
diagrams.

Tip: If you wish to change the order of siblings
in your records use the Move Up and Move Down commands instead of the Shift
Sibling buttons.

Scale

The scale of a diagram determines the size it will have
when printed. Do not confuse this with zooming which is
display-only, and doesn't affect the diagram's size when
printed. You can adjust the diagram scale, either by typing the
required scale into the Scale box, or by dragging the
slider up and down. When you drag the slider, the percentage
scale will be adjusted in increments of 2.5%, and the largest
scale is 100%. If you want to adjust scaling more precisely, or
if you wish the scale to exceed 100%, simply type the desired
scale as a percentage into the Scale box, and press the
tab key.

Tip: You should normally show page boundaries when
you adjust the scale of a diagram, so that you can see what
effect the change is having.

Tip: In an earlier tip, we saw an alternative way
of moving a diagram on the printed page, by
clicking-and-dragging (using the left mouse button) on
the intersection of the grid which displays page boundaries.
There is also an alternative way of scaling a diagram, which is
to click-and-drag on the same grid intersection (when
displayed), but using the right mouse button. When you
do this, the entire grid is resized becoming larger or smaller,
depending on which way you drag. When you resize the grid, you
are effectively changing the size of the diagram relative to the
printed page (remember that the physical paper doesn't change
size and still equates to each rectangle in the grid).
Consequently, the real meaning of this action is effectively to
resize the diagram relative to the printed page. You can do this
whenever page boundaries are displayed, whether or not
moving/resizing has been enabled.

Tip: If you wish to move a branch of a tree to a position
in your diagram that you cannot reach using any of the supported
drag-and-move action types, you can achieve the same effect by inserting
another tree into the diagram showing the same information as the branch
you wished to move. You can then hide the branch in the first tree
(using expansion buttons, or by using the Hide Selected Boxes command).
Finally, you can insert into the diagram as many lines as you wish to
link the newly inserted tree back to the first tree.

title: Moving Family Historian to a New PC
breadcrumb: Moving Family Historian to a New PC
text:
Moving Family Historian to a New PC

If you have installed and used Family Historian on one PC, and you later
buy a new PC and want to move Family Historian to it, you may want to
transfer some or all of the following:

The software itself

Some or all of your project data

Your settings (this includes all customizations)

Your user credentials (see below)

These are discussed in turn.

The Software

You cannot exactly transfer the software, as such. Instead you just
install it on the new PC. To do that, open a web browser and go to https://www.family-historian.co.uk/install8.
Click on the button to download and install Family Historian 8. When
you run the program after installation, you must login with the same
account (username and password) you used for your original install. It has
to be the same account because your licence is attached to this
account. Your licence will specify the number of devices that you
are permitted to install on. If you try to install on more devices
than your licence allows (normally 2), you will be prompted to select a
computer to deactivate. Just pick one you do not want to use any more. If
you want to install on more computers than your licence allows you will
need to purchase another licence.

Project Data

One way to transfer your project data is simply to copy the entire Family
Historian Projects folder to the new computer. By default, this will
be a folder called "Family Historian Projects", located in your
'Documents' folder. You can use a memory stick or writable CD or DVD
if the PCs are not linked to one another. Ordinarily, either a folder
copy, is all you need do. If you have pictures in your projects, these
should appear correctly when you look at the copied project on the new
computer. This is because the default option, when you add pictures to
Family Historian, is to copy the pictures into the project folder. That
way, the pictures become part of the project and are easily copied, or
backed-up, with it. However, some users prefer to keep pictures
separately, elsewhere on their PC. If you opted to do this, with some or
all of your pictures, you will need to locate those pictures and copy them
separately to the new PC. The tool, "External File Links" on the Tools
menu, can be used both on the old PC, to locate pictures that were
not copied to the project folder, and again on the new PC, to resolve any
problems with links to pictures, once you have copied them over.

Settings

"Settings" in this context means preferences, configurations,
customizations, fact type definitions, custom queries, custom smart
folders, custom reports, custom diagrams, custom text schemes, custom
source templates, language packs, custom map overlays, custom accent
files, custom record flags, custom autotext, custom diagram presets,
plugins, custom spellcheck files, custom colour schemes ... and
more. They can all be transferred in one go. To do that, open
the Project Window on your old PC, and
click on the More Tasks button, and choose Backup/Restore Settings and finally Backup
Settings. This will backup all your settings to a settings
file. Copy this file to your new PC. Now run Family Historian
on your new PC and open the Project Window.
Click on the More Tasks button, and choose Backup/Restore Settings. then Restore
Settings and select the settings file you backed up. This
will restore your settings to the new PC.

Settings can also be backed up from the Backup/Restore submenu on the File menu.

User Credentials

User credentials are generated for you automatically when you use Internet
Data Matching. Sharing user credentials across 2 PCs ensures
that if you confirm or reject a match on one PC, it will still appear to
be confirmed or rejected when viewed from the other PC. To transfer your
user credentials to your new PC, you should first export them as a file by
clicking on the File menu, and then
choosing Import/Export, Export
and finally User Credentials.
This will save your settings to a file. Copy the file to the new PC,
and then, on the new PC, run Family Historian and on the File
menu, choose Import/Export, Import,
User Credentials and select the file you
previously exported, and press OK.

To learn more, see Import/Export and Backup/Restore on the
File menu.

title: Name Formats
text:
General Topics

Name Formats

Fields

Surname
Surname

First
First name

Given
The
given name is the always first name, unless a 'name used' value has been
provided, in which case that is the given name, or unless the first name is the surname, in which case the
given name is the first non-surname word in the name.

Given All
All given names - ie. everything except the surname.

Middle
All middle names - i.e. everything except the first name

and the surname.

Full
Full name

Surname First
Full name, with the surname first, separated from the rest

of the name by a comma.

Preferred
Given name and surname (see also description for 'given

name').

Adorned
Given name and surname, preceded by name prefix, if any, and followed by name suffix, if any.

Prefixed
Given name and surname, preceded by name prefix, if any.

Suffixed
Given name and surname, followed by name suffix, if any.

Adorned (full)
Full name preceded by name prefix, if any, and followed

by name suffix, if any.

Prefixed (full)
Full name preceded by name prefix, if any.

Suffixed (full)
Full name followed by name suffix, if any.

Stored
Displays name exactly as it is stored in your records
- e.g. "John /Smith/" will display as "John /Smith/".

Soundex
Soundex is a system designed to encode surnames so that names that sound alike have the same code. By
sorting on a name's soundex you should find that like- sounding names are grouped together.

title: The Navigation Bar
text:
The Navigation Bar

The Navigation Bar is a bar that displays down the left-side of
the main application window. It displays one icon for each
open Workspace Window*.
There is no limit to the number of Workspace Windows you can
have open at any one time. It is possible, using options
on the Windows menu, to see more than one Workspace Window at a
time, but normally you can only see one because any other open
Workspace Windows are hidden behind it.

The Navigation Bar makes it easy to see which Workspace Windows
you have open at any one time. In the example on the left,
there are 4 workspace windows open - the Focus Window (with a
magnifying glass icon), the Records Window (with a database
icon), the Map Window (with a red pin icon) and the Diagram
Window (with a small diagram icon).

The current workspace window in this case, is the
Map Window, marked in orange.

As well as making it easy to see which Workspace Windows you
currently have open, the Navigation Bar also makes it easy to
switch between them. Just click on the Workspace window
you require to bring it to the front.

To close a Workspace Window, click on the little 'X' in the
top-right corner of the window's box - except that, usually, you
cannot close the Focus Window or the Records Window.

You can also right-click on the icons on the Navigation Bar,
and choose options from the Dropdown menus that appear, to
either close the window or lock it (prevent it being re-used).

With saved charts, book charts and saved
maps (all items that can be worked on, and changed over
time) a small orange dot
will display in the top-left corner of the icon space for the item
in question if there are any unsaved changes. If you close
any one of these when there are unsaved changes, you will be
prompted to save them.

See also Workspace Windows.

* The Records Window is a small exception because by default, for
reasons of convenience, it always has an icon in the Navigation Bar,
even if it is not actually open. However, this is ignored for the
present discussion.

title: New Folder Set Dialog
text:
Smart Folders

New Folder Set Dialog

The New Folder Set Dialog can be accessed by clicking the New button in the Manage Folder Sets Dialog. You
can also access it by clicking "New Custom Folder Set..." on the dropdown
menu that appears when you click on the cog (menu) button on the smart
folder toolbar, within the Query
Window. It is used for creating a new custom folder set from
scratch. That isn't the only option. You can also create a new
folder set by copying an existing folder set. To do that, select the
folder set you wish to copy and click the Clone
button on the Manage
Folder Sets Dialog.

Unlike queries, smart folders do not have to be 'run' as such.
Indeed they can't be. They can however be viewed - either in the
Records Window, in record selector dialogs, or in the Query Window.

The first thing you have to decide when creating a new custom folder set
from scratch, is what type you want it to be. Every
folder set has a type, just as every query does. And the possible
types are exactly the same in each case - see New Query Dialog for a discussion of
query types.

Fields

Set Type

Choose the type of folder set required. There is one for
each record type (apart from the Header record), as well as 3
other non-record types. These non-record folder set types
are fact (facts are events and attributes), source
citation and witness.

Tip: Probably the most potentially confusing
type is witness. Remember that 'witness' in
this context, just means 'non-principal participant'. What
does a witness folder set show information about? The
answer is that a witness folder set will show information about
each occurrence of a person in a non-principal role with respect
to an event or (more rarely) attribute. So, for example,
this will include all cases in which someone is recorded as,
say, a bridesmaid in a marriage, or as a beneficiary in a
will. A person can be recorded as a witness to an event in
which they are also the principal. Subject to filtering,
they would be listed for each occurrence of their role as a
witness, but not for their role as principal. A person can
also be recorded more than once as a witness to the same
event. They would be listed once for each occurrence of
their role as witness, even if some of these occurrences were
for the same event. For example, a person might have a
role as executor for a will, while also having a role
as beneficiary.

Set Name

Choose a unique name for your new custom folder set.

title: New Language Pack: Step 1
text:
Language Packs Dialog

New Language Pack: Step 1

Language packs are created in two steps. In Step 1, select the
language pack you require and supply the field values as described
below. When you have completed this, click Next
to proceed to Step 2.

Fields

Language
The language of the language pack

Name
The English name of the language. This is usually
determined by the Language selection, but you can optionally
modify it if you want to.

Internal Name
Also called 'Endonym', this is the language name as it would be
in the language itself. For example, the internal name, or
endonym, for French is Français. As with the Name field
above, this is usually determined by the Language selection, but
you can modify it if you want to.

3-Letter Code
This is the 3-letter ISO code for the language. More
specifically it is the 639-2/T code. You do not have to
enter this code - indeed you can't. The code is determined
by your selection in the Language field above.

ISO stands for 'International Organization for Standardization'.

Variant
Every language pack has a unique "Language Id", which is used to
identify it. Typically this will consist simply of the
3-letter code for the language. So, for example, you might
have a language pack for french, with language id "FRA". If
you want to have more than one language pack for french, you
must add a value to the Variant field to allow the variant to be
distinguished. A single letter or number would
suffice. If a variant is supplied, the language id
will consist of the 3-letter code followed by the variant value,
with a space separating the two parts. So, for example, if
the Variant value for a second french language pack was '2', the
language id would be 'FRA 2'.

If you are creating a language pack which is used for translation
from one language into another, where neither language is English,
you are recommended to use the Variant field to indicate
this. For example, if you want to create a language pack for
translating from Polish to Russian, the 3-letter code will be
'RUS' because you are translating into Russian. But you
should set the Variant to "[project=POL]" (or similar) to indicate
that the language pack expects the project language to be Polish.

Description
Describes what the language pack does. If this is your
language pack, it is a good idea to use this field to describe the
purpose of the language pack. For example, if it supports
both same-language rendering (e.g. French-to-French), you can say
this. If it also supports other-language translation (e.g.
English-to-French) you can mention this too.

title: New Language Pack: Step 2
text:
Language Packs Dialog

New Language Pack: Step 2

The actual initial creation of a new language pack is just the first
step in the process of building a language pack (see How
to Create a Language Pack). Once it has been created, there
are various tasks that need to be done, to make it function properly and
well. However, Family Historian will make the job simpler by
creating a skeleton version of the translation tables and other items
you will need in your language pack, to get you started. As part
of this process, Family Historian will create language variants of all
the standard text schemes for diagrams. That does not mean that
diagrams are automatically translated. Dates, for example, are
displayed in text schemes, but are translated as part of a separate
process. So creating language variants for text schemes does not,
on its own, mean that dates will be translated when displayed in
diagrams using your new language pack. Nevertheless, creating
language variants of text schemes is a process that can be automated,
and is consequently worth doing at this stage, as it significantly
reduces the amount of work that needs to be done. Bear in mind
that you will be able to modify these language variants, at a later
stage, if you want to and need to - in exactly the same way you can
modify ordinary text schemes now (in the Text
tab of Diagram Options).

In order for Family Historian to be able to create the language
variants of text schemes, it needs you to do a little translating
first. The tasks are described in the section below.

When you have finished translating all the items in the list (and have
decided what to do about Place Prepositions), click the Create
Language Pack button to finish. You have now
created a skeleton, initial version of a language pack. There is much
more that needs to be done, however, before your language pack will be
complete. See How to
Create a Language Pack for details.

Place Preposition

In various text schemes, in English, Text will be output that describes
each person's birth, marriage, death, and other details.
Frequently these descriptions specify both the date and place of the
event. In English, the place is usually preceded by a preposition,
like this:

Born: 12 June 1980 in Manchester, England

The preposition is the word 'in', which separates the date from the
place information (it doesn't appear at all if there is only a place and
no date).

If you were creating a German language pack, you might decide to
specify the same word 'in' as the place preposition. This is
because it just so happens that the same word is used in German, in much
the same way that it is used in English.

In French it is more problematic. Depending on the place, you
might want to use 'à', 'en', 'au', or even 'aux'. French uses
different prepositions for different places. For this reason, we
would recommend that you don't use a preposition at all for
French. If you leave it blank, Family Historian will simply use a
comma to separate a date from a place in diagrams (more complex
solutions are possible, and may be needed, in reports - but that is
handled separately).

So, depending on the language of your language pack, you may wish to
provide a place preposition or not. If in doubt, we recommend that
you leave it blank.

Translation List

As well as the place preposition, you are encouraged to provide
translations for the listed text items. Some of these items of
text will be used as labels. Do not assume that you necessarily
need to interpret them literally. For example, how should you
translate the word 'Born'? This will be used as a label in diagram
text schemes. We have already seen an example that uses it:

Born: 12 June 1980 in Manchester, England

If you were translating this into French, you might think that the word
to use would be 'Né'. And that is a possibility. But is it
the most appropriate word to use in equivalent circumstances in
French? For one thing, 'Né' is the masculine form. For
women, the equivalent would be ''Née'. Perhaps a better solution
would be to use 'Naissance', even though strictly-speaking, that is the
translation of the noun 'Birth' rather than the past-participle 'Born'.
Whatever strategy you adopt, try to be consistent.

To translate the items in the list, select each item in turn and fill
in the appropriate value in the Translation field at the bottom.
To make life easier, you can use the Next
button to step quickly forwards through the list (or press the Previous
button to move back). Easier still is to press F3 after each
translation, to move on to the next.

title: New Project Wizard
text:
Project Window

New Project Wizard

The New Project Wizard is used for creating new projects in the
current default project location. Choose from the available
options in each step and click Next to
proceed to the next step. The steps vary depending on what type of
import you choose. The steps, in order, are:

Choose
Import Type (first step and common to all imports)

Legacy Import Options
(Legacy imports only)

RootsMagic Import
Options (RootsMagic imports only)

TMG Import Options (TMG
imports only)

Starting Person (if no
import)

Project Name (final step in
all cases)

See also Transferring
Data into Family Historian.

title: New Project Wizard - Choose Import Type
breadcrumb: New Project Wizard - Choose Import Type
text:
Project Window

New Project Wizard - Choose Import Type

New Project Wizard - Choose Import Type

The New Project Wizard is opened by clicking New
Project on the Project
Window. Choose the kind of import you wish to do (if any)
and then click Next to proceed to the
next step.

The five options in this first step are:

Start a new project (no import)

Choose this option if you want to start a new project from
scratch.

Import directly from genealogy software data file

Family Historian can import directly from the following family
tree files:

Family Historian project files

Genbox data files

Legacy database files

RootsMagic database files

The Master Genealogist database files

When you choose this option you will be prompted to select a
file. Click the Browse button
and select the family tree file you wish to import. If Family
Historian does not recognise the format of the file you have
specified you will need to use the original genealogy
application to export the data you need in GEDCOM format, and
then import that GEDCOM file (see previous option).

Family tree files in all of the above-mentioned formats may
contain links to media files on your hard disk. If there
are any, you can optionally copy these files into the folder
that will be created for your new project, and you are usually
recommended to do so. If you opt not to copy them,
however, Family Historian will still be able to access these
files at their current locations on your computer's hard disk.

If there are links to media files, but some or all of them are
invalid (the media files don't exist where they are supposed to
be), Family Historian will be unable to locate the media files,
but the import will not be otherwise affected.

Family Historian does not provide a direct import from Family
Tree Maker. This is because Family Tree Maker prevents
other applications from accessing its data. If you have a
copy of Family Tree Maker, or any other program that Family
Historian does not import from directly, you will need to export
your data from that program in the form of a GEDCOM file or
GEDZIP file. You can import from that file into a new
Family Historian project.

Import a GEDCOM file

Choose this option if you have a GEDCOM file that you wish to
import into the new project you are creating. When you click
on the check box, other boxes appear below. Click the Browse button and select the GEDCOM file
you wish to import. GEDCOM files may contain links to media
files (pictures, videos, sound files, etc) on your hard
disk. If there are any, you can optionally copy these files
into the folder that will be created for your new project, and you
are usually recommended to do so. If you opt not to copy
them, however, Family Historian will still be able to access these
files at their current locations on your computer's hard disk.

If there are links to media files, but some or all of them are
invalid (the media files don't exist where they are supposed to
be), Family Historian will be unable to locate the media files,
but the import will not be otherwise affected.

Import a GEDZIP file

Choose this option if you have a GEDZIP file that you wish to
import into the new project you are creating. A GEDZIP file
contains data in GEDCOM file format, together with any media files
that may be associated with the GEDCOM file. This is the
advantage of GEDZIP files. They contain all associated
media.

Import from FamilySearch

Choose this option if you wish to import directly from
FamilySearch. You can import either from the FamilySearch
global family tree, or, if you have FamilySearch
User Tree functionality enabled (see the FamilySearch
tab of Preferences), you can import directly from any user
trees that you have permission to access. When you take this
option, Family Historian will initially create a new, empty
project and then provide you with instructions on importing into
it directly from FamilySearch.

title: New Project Wizard - Legacy Import Options
breadcrumb: New Project Wizard - Legacy Import Options
text:
Project Window

New Project Wizard - Legacy Import Options

You will only see this page if you opted to import a Legacy file into
your new project.

Fields

Default Media Folder
Legacy specifies a default media folder. It is important
to specify this folder location, so that Family Historian can find
media files. In recent versions of Legacy, you can confirm
the location of this folder by clicking 'Customize' on the Legacy
'Options' menu. On tab "6. Locations", the field is labelled
"6.2 Default location of media files (ff)".

Set the 'Rejected' fact flag on all 'alt' events
In Legacy, you can record 'alternative' versions of some facts
using fact names that are prefixed with 'Alt' (e.g. 'Alt
Birth'). The implication is that this is not what you
believe to be the correct information, but you want to keep it
anyway, partly in case you later discover that it was right after
all, and partly so that you can record the fact that you have
considered and discarded this possibility. The recommended
way to do this in Family Historian is to record the information
using the standard fact type (e.g. 'Birth'), but set the Rejected
fact flag for this fact (you can record as many instances of each
standard fact type, including 'Birth', as you want). That
way, this 'fact' will be excluded from all reports etc, by
default. You can always unset the flag at any time if you
want to.

Another option in Legacy is to record a fact with a 'Disproven '
prefix (e.g. "Disproven Birth"). Again, with this import
option checked, such 'facts' will be recorded as a standard fact
type ("Birth"), and with the Rejected fact flag set.

Import Christening/Baptism Events as
Baptisms
In Family Historian, Christening
and Baptism are separate event types. In
Legacy, there is only one event type for both. Events of
this type are labelled in Legacy as either 'Christening' or
'Baptism' (this is a Legacy customization option).

If you tick this import option, all such events will be imported
into Family Historian as baptisms. If unticked, they will be
imported as christenings.

Import Sentence Overrides
Both Family Historian and Legacy allow you to override the
generated sentence for narrative reports, for facts and shared
events. Tick this option if you want these sentence
overrides to be imported into Family Historian.

Convert Codes in Sentence Overrides

Sentence overrides in Legacy may contain special Legacy codes
such as [Name], [Desc], [inPlace], etc. Tick this option
if you want Family Historian to convert these codes to Family
Historian equivalents. This is an experimental
feature. You are advised to check the results after
import.

Tip: See Sentence
Template Codes for advice about Family Historian sentence
template codes.

Tip: To view a complete list of Sentence Overrides,
after the import has completed, click the Tools menu, and then
click Work with Data, and then Fact/Witness
Sentences.

title: New Project Wizard - Starting Person
breadcrumb: New Project Wizard - Starting Person (if no import)
text:
Project Window

New Project Wizard - Enter Details of Starting Person

You will only see this page if you opted to create a new project from
scratch, without importing any data. Enter the name of a person who
will be the starting point for your project. Most people start with
themselves - and if in doubt, this is what we recommend you do. But
the starting person can be anyone. It doesn't have to be you.

Starting Person

Enter the full name of the starting person here.
When entering the names of women, you are recommended to use their
maiden name as their surname, rather than their married name.

Sex
Please choose the sex of the starting person. If you don't
know it, choose 'Unknown'.

Father
If you know the starting person's father's name, enter it
here. If you don't know the father's name, leave this box
blank.

Mother
If you know the starting person's mother's name, enter it
here. Again, you are recommended to use her maiden name as
her surname, if you know it, rather than their married name.
If you don't know the mother's name, leave this box blank.

title: New Project Wizard - RootsMagic Import Options
breadcrumb: New Project Wizard - RootsMagic Import Options
text:
Project Window

New Project Wizard - RootsMagic Import Options

You will only see this page if you opted to import a RootsMagic file
(version 7 or greater) into your new project.

Fields

Fact Types to Import & Convert
The options are

All fact types

Custom & unrecognised fact types only

Both Family Historian and RootsMagic support a long list of
standard fact types. Both also allow you to create your own
custom fact types. If the "All fact types" option is
selected, Family Historian will create fact definitions for all
the different types of recorded facts in the imported file.
In doing so it will convert the RootsMagic sentence templates for
the facts (including sentence templates for roles associated with
the fact) into the equivalent sentence templates in Family
Historian, replacing RootsMagic template codes with the equivalent
Family Historian codes. If 'Custom & Unrecognised fact
types only' is chosen, it will only do this for custom and
unrecognised fact types.

Location for Fact Type Definitions
All Family Historian fact definitions are held in fact sets.
When importing and converting RootsMagic fact definitions, Family
Historian will store all these fact definitions in a fact set
called "RootsMagic Import". This fact set can be project-level
or system-level. If a fact set is
project-level, that means that the fact set can only be seen, and
is only available for use, within that project. If a fact
set is system-level, that means that the fact set can be used with
any project.

The project-level option has the advantage that if you choose this
option, the import will not affect any other projects. For
that reason, this is a good option to choose unless you are
planning to make repeated imports. After you have imported a
data file, you may want to make changes to the fact
definitions. For example, you might need to rework a
sentence template that uses a RootsMagic expression which is not
available in Family Historian. If you make these changes at
the system-level, you will only need do this once.
Thereafter, if you repeat the import, you won't need to repeat
your changes. If you choose the system-level option, fact
definitions will not be added (or updated) at the system-level, if
they already exist in the system-level "RootsMagic Import" fact
set. If you chose the project-level option, however, you would
need to repeat your changes.

If you want to import from several different RootsMagic databases,
it is usually recommended to import each one using a project-level
fact set.

Another consideration though is that if you choose to import to a
project-level fact set, after the import you will be easily able
to see exactly which file definitions have been created, because
they will be the file definitions in the project-level "RootsMagic
Import" fact set.

This is not a critical decision because you can switch a fact set
from project-level to system-level or vice versa, at any time (see
the Fact
Sets Dialog, accessible from the Fact
Types Dialog).

Alternate Names
In Family Historian, each person can have any number of
names. In RootsMagic, each person has one primary name, and
other names are recorded as 'alternate name' facts about
the person. When importing alternate names into Family
Historian, you have a choice. You can either record them as
additional names for the person, or you can record them as
additional facts about the person ('alternate name' facts), or you
can do both. The various names for a person are displayed in
the Names/Titles Dialog
for that person. The various facts about a person are
displayed in the Facts
tab of the Property Box, for that person.

If in doubt, you are recommended to import names as both names and
facts. This can result in a minor duplication of data; but
if need be, you can easily delete unwanted data at a later
stage. Using a query, you could easily delete all alternate
name facts, or all additional names, within a project - if you
later wished to do so.

Import FamilySearch Matches
Tick this option to import details of FamilySearch
matches. For more information about FamilySearch, see The
FamilySearch Window.

title: New Project Wizard - TMG Import Options
breadcrumb: New Project Wizard - TMG Import Options
text:
Project Window

New Project Wizard - TMG Import Options

You will only see this page if you opted to import a TMG file into your
new project.

Note on TMG versions: Creation of fact definitions
equivalent to tag type definitions, can only be done if you have TMG
8.05 or later. You can import earlier versions of TMG, but the
creation of equivalent fact definitions will not occur in that case (see
Creating Fact Definitions During Import below
for more on this). For best results, we recommend users of
earlier versions of TMG, to upgrade to version 9 if possible, before
doing the import. If you are not sure how to do that, seek
advice from other TMG users. For example, if you ask for advice
on the Family Historian User Group (www.fhug.org.uk),
there are ex-TMG users there who may be able to help you.

You can leave most options as the default values, if you just want to
try out a sample import. An exception is 'Languages'. You
are advised to check this carefully and make sure you choose the most
appropriate setting - even for a trial import.

Bear in mind that you can repeat the import as many times as you like,
and experiment with different settings. Every time you do an
import, a new Family Historian project will be created. These can
easily be renamed or deleted if required. Do not be afraid to
experiment. Try an import, and look carefully at the
results. For advice on locating imported items after import, and
for pre- and post-import tips, see the article Importing
from The Master Genealogist on the Family Historian website.

Fields
