pedigree chart options. If this means that the number of pages
needs to change, that will happen. Pedigree charts which have been
added to a book directly as a pedigree chart, are listed as 'Pedigree
Chart' in the book items list, in the Edit
Book Dialog. If you choose to edit this item, you will be
able to view and modify the options in the Pedigree Chart dialog.
Pedigree charts which have been added to book indirectly via the saved
chart route, are just listed as 'Chart' in the book items list. If
you choose the edit option for this item, you will be offered the choice
of editing the chart in the Diagram Window, or selecting chart
pages. But you will not be able to view or edit the original
pedigree chart options in the Pedigree Chart dialog.

For this reason, you are normally recommeded to always add a pedigree
chart to a book 'directly', and only use the indirect saved chart
approach if you have a particular reason to do so.

What to Do if the Text is Too Small

If the text seems too small, you may want to untick Fit Chart on
Page option (if available) and click the Fonts
button to choose a font of the size you require. This will solve
the text size problem, but it may also mean that the chart no longer
fits comfortably onto a single sheet of paper when you print it.
If this is an issue, you should probably tick Fit Chart on Page again
and find another way of adjusting the text size. The first thing
to try is to reduce the number of generations. If there is plenty
of spare space at the top and bottom, but not much at the sides, this
suggests that the chart is too wide to make best use of the available
space on each page. By reducing the Box Width you should
be able to change the overall shape of the chart, until it approximates
to that of your printed page size. This will allow Family
Historian to make best use of the available space. Another
possibility to consider is reducing the first line indent. This
will have the effect of making the root box in each chart (the leftmost
box), jut out less far to the left; which may mean again that Family
Historian can make better use of the available space.

If Fit Chart on Page is ticked, Family Historian will
re-size the chart to fit on a page - if the chart is too
big. However it won't increase the size of the chart if it is
smaller than it needs be. Increasing the font size will be of no
benefit if Fit Chart on Page is ticked, and Family Historian
has to shrink the size of each chart. But if Fit Chart on
Page has no effect because the chart is small enough already,
then consider increasing the font size to make the chart bigger.

Tips on Customization

Pedigree Charts are created using diagram shapes. When viewing a
pedigree chart in the Diagram Window, you can right-click on a chart and
click Format to change aspects. You can select any
chart and click Ctrl-C to copy it to the clipboard,
and Ctrl-V to paste it - into the same diagram or any
other diagram. You can even choose the 'root' person for each
chart (right-click on a chart, and choose 'Format' from the menu that
appears; then select the 'Base Person' on the Data tab).

Each chart is a group object composed of multiple component
objects. This means that if you want to you can ungroup them
(right-click and select Grouping and then Ungroup)
and manipulate the component parts independently. Some
component parts are themselves also group objects which can be further ungrouped.

FIELDS

Root Person
The person whose ancestors will be shown. Always required
unless you opt to display a blank diagram (see Contents below).

Chart Shape
Choose the shape of the chart - wide or narrow.

Fonts
Choose the fonts, style and sizes to use in the chart.

Generations per Chart
The number of generations to display
in each chart.

Continuation Charts
If your root person has more generations of ancestors that can
fit onto a single chart, you can optionally display extra
ancestors on additional continuation charts.
Suppose, for example, that you have chosen to display 3
generations in each chart. This means that parents and
grandparents of the root person will be shown. But what happens if
you also have a record for the person's great grandmother? If Continuation
Charts are set to 1 level or higher, Family Historian will
create a second chart showing the ancestors of the great
grandmother. And what if the great grandmother herself has one or
more recorded great grand parents? In that case, if Continuation
Charts are set to 2 levels or higher, Family Historian will create
additional charts for each of these great grandparents. And so on.

If you don't want any continuation charts, just set this value to
'none'.

Max Generations
This shows the maximum number of generations that could be
displayed, for any given root. You cannot edit this value -
it is provided for information only, and is determined by the
number of generations per chart you have chosen and the number of
continuation chart levels. If the value seems unintuitive,
bear in mind that the root box of every continuation chart is a
repeat of a box from an earlier chart; so continuation charts add
one fewer additional possible generations than can be displayed on
the first chart.

Contents
Choose the contents of the boxes in charts. Choose Custom
if you wish to customize the contents yourself.
Choose Blank to display a blank chart. This can
be useful if you want to give other people blank sheets, for them
to fill in, recording their ancestors' details.

Ahnentafel Numbers
If ticked, Family Historian will display the appropriate
ahnentafel number for each person in the chart.

Chart Titles
If ticked, a title will appear above each chart.

Always Label
If ticked, the labels 'b.', 'm.', and 'd.' (for 'birth',
'marriage' and 'death') will always appear, even in empty boxes
and on otherwise blank lines. This option is only available if
appropriate Contents are selected.

Record Ids
If ticked, names will be displayed with record ids in both the
title and boxes (unless boxes are blank or have custom contents).

Continuation Arrows
If continuation charts are enabled, Family Historian will show
the linking chart number in a little arrow, to the right of the
box for each person with ancestors that are displayed in a
separate continuation chart.

Box Width
The width of each box

First Line Indent
The amount of the indent from the left box edge of the root box,
to the vertical line going up to the parents.

Normal Line Indent
Same as First Line Indent, but for all other boxes.

Horizontal Line Length
Most lines connecting a box to a parent's box have only 2 parts
- a vertical part and a horizontal part. This value is the
length of the horizontal part of these lines.

Vertical Gap
The vertical gap between boxes

Chart Margins
This is the size of the gaps that Family Historian leaves around
each chart.

Fit Chart on page
If ticked, and if each generated chart is larger than the
current default printer page size (allowing for Chart Margins),
Family Historian will automatically re-size the chart to fit it
within a page. This option is ticked and not editable if you
are adding a pedigree chart directly to a new or existing book.

More options
Click on this link if you wish to override diagram options for
this chart. Some print options will not be available if you adding
a pedigree chart to a new or existing book, or if you have
specified 'Book Compatibility' (see below).

Book Compatibility
This option is not available if you are adding a pedigree chart
to an existing book, or editing a pedigree chart in an existing
book. Even if available, it can normally be left blank,
unless you plan to add a pedigree chart to a book, via the
'indirect' saved chart route, described in the section A
Third Way of Displaying Pedigree Charts in Books
above.

'Book Compatibility' (also known as 'Book Layout Compatibility')
is an option on the Diagram menu,
which allows existing diagrams to use the same printer details and
page layout, as a given book. Normally this can be done
after a diagram has been created. However, with pedigree
charts, the page layout significantly affects the layout of the
chart itself, and therefore has to be known in advance. If
you are adding a pedigree chart to an existing book, the page
layout details are known. If you are creating a
new pedigree chart as a booklet, default printer and page layout
settings, suitable for a booklet, will be used, unless you
explicitly opt for compatibility with an existing book. So
in these cases, book compatibility is either not needed or is
inessential. However, when creating a pedigree chart as a
saved chart that you later plan to add to a book, it is important
to known in advance, the printer and page layout details of the
book to which you intend to add it.

Books created since version 8 of Family Historian can be used with
the book compatibility option. If you select a book created
earlier than that, you will be prompted to first upgrade it to use
the latest book format, if that has not already been done.

title: Place Formats
text:
General Topics

Place Formats

Genealogists sometimes have their own systems for separating elements
of a place name with commas. Those who take this approach may wish to
use extra commas to mark unknown elements of a place name - e.g.
�Rothbury,, Northumberland� might be used if you do not yet know the
parish of Rothbury. Family Historian supports this approach by
automatically removing these extra commas when you display place names,
in all formats except Full.

Fields

Short
Places are displayed in shortened format. Only text up to the
first comma (if any) is displayed.

Medium
Places are displayed in a slightly shortened format. Text up to
the second comma only (if there are two) is displayed.

Tidy
The full place details are displayed, but extra commas are
removed.

Full
The full place details are displayed (this is the default).

title: Place Records
text:
Record Types

Place Records

Place records are identified by this icon: .
Whenever you enter details of the place that an event occurred (such as
where someone was born), Family Historian will automatically create a
Place record to represent this place, if it doesn't already exist.
The Place record is used to store any pictures you may wish to record
about the place, as well as notes, and the latitude and longitude of the
place, if known.

Every Place record can optionally be associated with one or more Address
records which can be used to provide more details about the exact
location of an event. For tips and advice on how to use Address
records and Place records together, see the Address
records page.

(for Places)

title: Plugins Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Plugins Dialog

Plugins Dialog (in expanded mode)

To open the Plugins Dialog, click on Plugins on the Tools
menu. The Plugins Dialog lists all the plugins
you have installed (if any). A plugin is an extension to the main
program which adds capabilities and features. The features added
could be almost anything - a new report, a new diagram, a new way of
entering or importing data, a new way of exporting data, a new mapping
or timeline tool, a new website generator .... anything at all.
Before you can run a plugin, you have to install it.

To find and install a plugin, click on the Plugin
Store button. This will open your web-browser and take
you to the Plugin
Store page on the Family Historian website. The Plugin
Store contains numerous free plugins, with more being added all the
time. Browse the available plugins until you find one or more you
wish to install. Within the details page for each plugin is
a Download Now button. Click this
button to download and install the plugin file. When you click on
this button, your web-browser may ask you if you wish to 'open' or 'run'
the file. If you do either, this will install the plugin.
Alternatively, you can download the plugin file to your hard disk and
run it there (e.g. if you download it to your desktop you can
double-click on it to run it). This is another way of installing
it. It doesn't matter whether or not Family Historian itself is
running when you install a plugin.

The Plugin Store is only one possible source of plugins. Anyone
can write a plugin, and can make them available wherever they
want. See the Plugin Store home page for other possible sources of
plugins.

Plugins can be run from the Plugins Dialog by selecting it and clicking
the Run button. If you find that a
plugin is particularly useful and you wish to be able to access it more
easily, make sure it is selected and tick Add To Tools Menu,
to add it to the Tools menu (you may need to click the More
>> button to see this tick box). Thereafter you
will be able to run the plugin by simply clicking the new command on the
Tools menu.

Any plugins obtained from external sources should
be treated with care as they could potentially contain errors or even
malicious code. If you are using plugins obtained from other people you
should treat them with no less caution than you would treat any other
computer program. You should not import or run a plugin unless you
know and trust the source of the plugin, and you know what it does.

How to Write Your Own Plugins

Family Historian provides everything you need to write your own
plugins, and it isn't hard to do - especially for anyone who has prior
experience of writing scripts, macros, plugins or computer programs of
any kind. Family Historian plugins are written in a language
called Lua, which is used in a similar way in many commercial
applications such as Adobe Lightroom and also in games software.
Its emphasis is on ease-of-use for non-programmers. But it is also
powerful, fast and lightweight.

To create your own plugin, simply click the New
button. This will open the Family Historian Editor/Debugger
for a new plugin. All the documentation and information you need
for writing a plugin, is provided in the Family
Historian Plugin Help, which is accessible from the Family
Historian Editor (see the Editor's own Help menu or just click F1 when
viewing the editor), or can be accessed by clicking on the How
To Write Plugins button in this dialog (see below). The
Plugin Help documentation includes (or provides links to) everything you
need to know about Lua, about how to access your data from within a
plugin, and about the Editor/Debugger.

Buttons

New*
Opens the Plugin Editor to create a new plugin.

Edit*
Edit a plugin in the Plugin Editor.

Rename*
Rename a plugin.

Import*
Import a plugin.

Export*
Export a plugin.

Delete*
Delete a plugin.

How to Write Plugins*
Access the Plugin Help to learn how to write plugins.

Add To Tools Menu*
Select a plugin and tick this option if you want the plugin to
be added as a command to the Tools menu. You can remove it
from the Tools menu at any time, by selecting the plugin and
unticking this option.

Run
Run a plugin.

Plugin Store
Access the Plugin Store (see above).

More >>

(<< Less)

Show or hide the buttons on the right hand side.

* If there buttons are not visible, click the More
>> button to show them.

title: Advanced Preferences
text:
Preferences Dialog: General
Tab

Advanced Preferences

Fields

PC Performance
Family Historian contains optimizations to take advantage of
today’s powerful processors, and to give better-looking results
when displaying diagrams. If you have an old PC, however, these
optimizations may have an adverse affect on the performance of
your PC. You are usually strongly recommended to let Family
Historian automatically detect what your PC is capable of (i.e.
this setting should normally be left at the default,
'Auto-Detect’). However, exceptionally, you can experiment with
alternative settings if you wish.

Diagram/Report Image DPI (max)
By default, images within diagram boxes, and within reports or
books, are displayed at a maximum of 300 dots per inch. You are
not usually recommended to increase this figure. The minimum
allowed value is 75 dpi which will give less good image quality.

You can also choose 'no max' in which case no maximum dpi value
will be used. The advantage of this option is that pictures
may load more quickly; however, more memory will be used.
This could mean, if a diagram or report has many pictures, that
some pictures will not load.

In general, the larger the figure, the better the image quality
(most noticeably when printing); but there is a point beyond which
it will make no difference. A larger figure will however
mean that more memory is used, so do not make the figure larger
than you need. The figure you specify will in any case cease
to have any effect when printing if it is larger than the printer
dpi setting.

Includes printing
If this option is ticked (the default) the Diagram/Report Image
DPI (max) figure applies when printing a report or book, or when
generating a PDF for a report or book. Unticking this option could
result in errors when printing large reports

or books, and is consequently not recommended.

Legacy Charts (pre-v8)

When loading a chart that was created using a version of Family
Historian earlier than version 8, you can choose between the
following options:

Prioritize text quality

Prioritize position accuracy

Prioritize shape positions

Choosing the first option will ensure that priority is given to
the appearance of text. Choosing the second option will
ensure instead that accurate positioning of items within the
chart is the priority. The third option (the default),
ensures that accurate positioning of items within the chart is
the priority if the chart contains shapes (because positional
movements are likely to be most noticeable if a chart contains
shapes); but with charts that don't contain shapes, the
appearance of text is the priority.

Even if you choose not to prioritize text quality,
you are unlikely to notice any difference most of the time. The
only context in which it may be noticeable is when saving a
chart to PDF, and even in that case, the difference, if any, may
be quite small.

Report/Book Image Caching
There are 3 options for images used
in reports and books:

Cache on load

Cache on view

Don't cache

'Cache on load' is the default. It means that images will be
cached when a report or book is loaded (memory permitting).

'Cache on view' means that images are cached only when you first
view them (again, memory permitting). Reports and books may
open faster if you take this option, but you may find that
scrolling through a report is (initially at least) slower and less
smooth than with 'Cache on load'.

'Don't cache' means that images are not cached at all. You
probably only want to choose this option if you are getting errors
with either of the other two options.

Maximum Recently Used Items
Some dropdown record lists show recently-used records. The
maximum number of recently-used records that are displayed, is
determined by this figure.

Thumbnail Images
'Auto-cache' means that thumbnail images for pictures in each
project are automatically cached within the project. If you open a
GEDCOM file that is not part of a project, the thumbnail images
are not cached, but instead are loaded automatically when the
GEDCOM file is opened. 'Load When Opening Project' means that
thumbnail images for each project or GEDCOM file are loaded
automatically whenever the project or file is opened. 'Load When
Needed' means that thumbnail images are only loaded when they are
needed. You are normally recommended to leave this setting at the
default, which is 'Auto-cache', unless you have a particular
reason not to.

Auto. Snapshot Cycles (fast/slow)

If Automatic Snapshot Management is enabled (the default),
Family Historian will automatically take and keep a snapshot of
your project's data file periodically. At most one snapshot is
taken per day, but only for data stored in projects, and only
when changes are saved. So if no saves occur, no snapshot will
be taken. And no snapshots are ever taken for standalone GEDCOM
files. Snapshots provide an additional layer of security, in
case of mistakes. You can revert to recent snapshots using the Snapshot Manager.
But snapshots should not be viewed as a substitute for regular
backups.

To ensure that snapshots do not take up an excessive amount of
disk space, they are not kept indefinitely. Two settings
are used to determined which snapshots are kept. The first
of these is called the 'Fast Cycle' setting, and the second is
the 'Slow Cycle' setting. To understand how these work,
let us first imagine that the Slow Cycle setting is set to 0
(zero), and the Fast Cycle setting is set to 5. In that
case, Family Historian would keep a maximum of 5 snapshots for
each project. Once you'd reached that maximum, if you used
Family Historian every day and made changes to your project
every day, you would always have one snapshot for the last 5
days. If you used Family Historian once a week and made
changes to your project each time you did so, you would always
have one snapshot for the last 5 weeks.

Now imagine that we leave the Fast Cycle setting at 5 and set
the Slow Cycle setting to 3. If the Slow Cycle setting is
greater than zero, each time Family Historian starts a new cycle
on the Fast Cycle (i.e. every 5 times, in this case), instead of
simply deleting an old snapshot and replacing it with a new one,
it will retain one old snapshot from the Fast Cycle - the first
in the cycle. These retained snapshots are kept in a
second cycle - the Slow Cycle. If the setting for the Slow
Cycle was 3, Family Historian would keep a maximum of 3
snapshots in the Slow Cycle. That means that eventually
when you have reached your maximum number of saved snapshots on
both cycles, you would, at any given time, always have 8 saved
snapshots. Of these, 5 would be snapshots of the last 5
times (if on different days) that you made changes to the
project. The remaining 3 snapshots would be more
spaced-out snapshots, each representing one of a previous group
of 5 snapshots.

Automatic snapshots can be disabled, if required, on the File
Load/Save tab of Preferences.

Automatically Calculate Relationships
Family Historian can display relationship information in a
variety of contexts - in the Records Window, in diagrams, in
reports, in queries, in web pages, and so on. For example, you can
have a column showing how each individual listed in the Records
Window is related to the File Root (if there is one). Or you could
have a line in boxes in a diagram showing how each person shown in
the diagram is related to the File Root (or to the Diagram Root).
Ordinarily Family Historian will do all calculations of
relationships automatically - i.e. this option is enabled by
default. The extra processing involved in such calculations is
normally undetectable. However, if you have a low spec PC and
you believe that calculating relationship information is
adversely affecting the performance of your PC, you can if you
wish switch this off.

If you do switch off this feature, relationship information is
not automatically updated whenever you simply add or delete
relationships between people. Consequently, if you do this, the
displayed relationship information can become out-of-date and
wrong. However, even in this case, relationship information will
still be automatically re-calculated whenever you open a file,
and in some other circumstances – such as when you run a query
that involves relationship information, or when you delete
records.

Tip: If you have disabled automatic calculation of
relationships, you can always force relationship information to
be updated whenever you want, by clicking on Refresh on the
Windows menu.

Tip: If you believe that the time taken to
calculate relationship information is significantly slowing down
the time it takes to open a file, try using the Configure
Columns Dialog (right-click on any column heading) to configure
columns for the Records Window, and remove any columns that show
relationship information. Then re-open the same file and see
whether performance has improved.

Auto-rotate Images
Phone cameras and digital cameras often record the orientation
of the phone or camera when the photo was taken, in 'EXIF'
metadata embedded within the image file. If Auto-rotate
Images is enabled, Family Historian will use this EXIF
metadata, if it exists, to ensure that images are rotated
correctly.

Cache Printer Settings
Occasionally poorly-performing printer drivers can cause
problems with the display of diagrams (e.g. making them appear
sluggish). If so, enabling this option may solve the problem. If
the option is enabled, however, and you are having problems
displaying diagrams, try disabling it. With most users it is
likely to have no effect, if enabled or disabled. But it is
enabled by default.

Enhanced PDF Diagram Support
This feature only affects the way that Family Historian
calculates the exact dimensions of a diagram, when trying to fit
the diagram onto a single page of a PDF file. You are usually
recommended to leave this option enabled.

Refresh Internet Services
This option is always displayed as unticked. There is normally
no need to use it. However, if an Internet service used by Family
Historian does not appear to be functioning correctly, try ticking
this option. If ticked, Family Historian will perform checks on
the currently available services when you press the OK button.

Emulator Compatibility Mode
This option should only be used if you are running Family
Historian under a Windows emulator, on some other operating
system, and reports do not display correctly on-screen. In that
case, ticking this option may fix the problem. Ordinary users,
running Family Historian under Windows should never tick this
option.

Auto-cleanup Unused Family Records
If checked (the default), Family Historian will automatically
delete family records when you delete (or unlink) all the members
of the family. You are recommended to leave this checked.

Enable Auto-complete

Enable Auto-complete and Enable Auto-list (see next) are both
features that make data entry quicker and easier.

Auto-complete operates in the same context as auto-list, but
they are independent of one another. You can enable either
or neither or both. By default, both are enabled.

If auto-complete is enabled, Family Historian will
auto-complete the values for certain fields, using previously
entered values for the same field type. For example, if you type
“I” as a place, and had previously used “Ireland” as a place,
Family Historian might auto-complete the field as “Ireland”.
When Family Historian auto-completes a field, the 'guessed’
portion (in the example this would be “reland”) is shown
selected. So, if the ‘guess’ is wrong, you should simply keep
typing and ignore the auto- completion. If you have finished
typing the value you want, and Family Historian is still trying
to auto-complete it, press the Delete or Backspace key to cancel
the ‘guessed’ portion.

To accept an auto-completion at any time, press the Tab key or
click elsewhere.

Family Historian supports auto-completion for the following
field types:

Place

Address

Occupation

Religion

National or Tribal Origin

Group/Caste Membership

Generic Source Types

Temple (if LDS Support is enabled - see LDS
Church Features)

With all fields that support auto-completion, you can
double-click on the field, or click on the little button with 3
dots to the right of it, to see a list of values previously
entered for that field type. This will work even if
auto-completion is not enabled.

See also Enable Auto-list (see next).

Enable Auto-list

Enable Auto-list and Enable Auto-complete (see previous) are
both features that make data entry quicker and easier.

Auto-list operates in the same context as auto-complete, but
they are independent of one another. You can enable either
or neither or both. By default, both are enabled.

If auto-list is enabled, when you start typing a value into
certain fields, Family Historian will automatically drop a list
of all the existing values for those fields, in the current
project, that match the text you have typed so far. For example,
if you type “I” into a place field, Family Historian will drop a
list below the place field, of all the places in the
current project that start with an "I". If you keep typing
and ignore the list, the list will adjust itself to reflect the
letters you have typed. So, for example, if following the
"I" you type an "r", Family Historian will list all the places
that begin with "Ir". If at any point no items begin with the
letters you have typed so far, there will be no dropped
list.

If you wish to pick one of the listed items, you can click on
it with the mouse. Alternatively, press the down arrow to
move the selection down to the listed item you want. When
you reach that item, press Enter or Space to select it.

Family Historian supports auto-list for the same field types
that it supports auto-complete for - namely:

Place

Address

Occupation

Religion

National or Tribal Origin

Group/Caste Membership

Generic Source Types

Temple (if LDS Support is enabled - see LDS
Church Features)

With all fields that support auto-list, you can double-click
on the field, or click on the little button with 3 dots to the
right of it, to see a list of values previously entered for that
field type. This will work even if auto-list is not enabled.

See also Enable Auto-complete (see
previous).

Prefer Full Row Selection

If checked (the default), you will be able to click on any text
in any column to select a row in multi-column lists.

Enable Automatic Ordering of Events/ Attributes by Date
If this option is checked (the default) Family Historian will
ensure that all events and attributes are kept in chronological
order if you enter and edit them using the Property Box (or if you
copy and paste them). The only exception to this is that if you
wish to add or edit events using ‘low-level editing’ in the ‘All’
tab of the Property Box or in the Records Window, events and
attributes will not automatically be kept in chronological order.
But even in this case, you can still easily keep them in order by
selecting the record and clicking on Re-order
Events by Date on the Edit menu.
Tip If you want to be sure that all events and
attributes in your file are in chronological order, use the Re-order Out of Sequence Data
command on the Tools menu.

Tip Pressing F9 when a record is selected is a
quick of activating the Re-order Events by Date command.

Suppress deprecated fields

'Deprecated' fields are fields which are supported by Family
Historian but which users are discouraged from using. For
example, for historical reasons, it is possible to store a copy
of a person's surname in a separate Surname subfield of a Name
field. This is permitted but discouraged. Family Historian
expects you to include a person's surname in the main Name
field, and it adds no value to store an extra copy of it
separately. With most fields, if you right-click on them in the
'All' tab of the Property Box, you will normally be able to add
any permitted subfields from the dropdown menu that appears.
Deprecated subfields are excluded from these dropdown menus,
unless this option to suppress them is unticked (it is ticked by
default). If a particular deprecated field happens to have a
value, however, for whatever reason, Family Historian will
display the field and its value in the 'All' tab of the Property
Box, for the record in question, whether or not deprecated
fields are being suppressed.

Reset Web Search Window Browser on Next Startup
Resetting the Web Search window web browser will clear all
cookies stored for that browser, which can sometimes be
useful. To do a reset, tick this option, save changes, and
close and restart Family Historian. The actual reset occurs
when Family Historian is next started. You will see a
message telling you if the reset was successful. The
reset will not be attempted if more than one instance of Family
Historian is running, so be sure to close all instances before
restarting the program. If the browser reset is not
successful, consider restarting your PC before trying again.

This option is automatically cleared when a reset is attempted,
whether successful or not.

title: Preferences Dialog: Backup
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Backup

Fields

Default Backup Folder
If you usually backup to the same folder, specify that folder
here, so that it is always the default when you do a backup.

Generate Backup File Name using Date in Year-Month- Day Order

When you do a backup, Family Historian will always
automatically generate a default name for the backup file, using
the current date and time. If this option is checked, Family
Historian will format the date with year first, then month, then
day. The advantage of doing it this way is that if you sort the
folder containing the backup files, by name, the files will be
in the correct chronological order.

If this option is not checked, Family Historian will format the
date with day first, then month, then year.

Filename Prefixes for Backup Types

As well as adding the current date and time to the end of the
name for the backup file, when you do a backup, Family Historian
will also add a prefix to the backup file name which indicates
what type of backup was done. There are 3 types of backups -
Full, Medium and Small. You can override the default and specify
your own prefix (or get rid of them altogether) if you wish.

To learn more about the 3 backup types, see Backups.

Prompt for Backup on Exit (if changes)
If 'Prompt for Backup on Exit (if changes)' is checked, Family
Historian will prompt you to do a backup at the end of every
session - if you have made any changes to the records in your
project (including additions or deletions) during that session. At
that point, you will be presented with a dialog box with 3 buttons
on it: Backup, Skip or Cancel. The 'Backup Button Action' option
determines what will happen if you click the Backup button. You
can choose the kind of backup that you prefer to do at the end of
each session. If you want to be given a choice each time, choose
'Let Me Choose Backup Type' (the default).

title: Preferences Dialog: Diagrams
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Diagrams

‘Dynamic’ Diagram Options

In some programs that generate diagrams, you start by specifying your
options and the program builds a diagram using those options. If you
then decide that you want to change an option, you can’t change it for
that diagram. You have to create another one. This process does not fit
well with the way human beings work. A better process is this:

Build the diagram with the current default options

Look at it and decide if you like it.

Make changes and/or modify diagram options and see what the effect
is

Repeat this process until you are happy with the results

That is what Family Historian lets you do. In most cases, if you
change a diagram option (e.g. from the Diagram Options dialog), Family
Historian will simply update the existing diagram to reflect the change.
If you have expanded branches, resized or moved boxes, or made other
changes, it doesn’t matter. The diagram will be kept the same (or as
near the same as is consistent with the options you have chosen) and
will be dynamically updated to reflect the new options.

This makes it easy for you to experiment and try things out until you
are happy with the results.

There are, however, a small number of diagram options (normally
coloured red in the Diagram Options dialog - see ‘Fields’ below) which
cannot be handled in this way. With these options (called 'rebuild
options'), if you change them, the tree part of the diagram will have to
be rebuilt. When this happens all existing trees within the diagram will
be discarded, and a single new tree will be re-created; and if you have
made changes to the tree part of a diagram since it was first built -
e.g. resized or moved boxes, inserted additional trees, or expanded or
closed branches, etc - these changes will not be retained. Even in this
case, however, all diagram elements other than trees (that is,
additional pictures, lines, rectangles, or text boxes) will be retained
and not discarded when the tree part of the diagram is rebuilt.

Policy on Rebuild and Close Warnings

Family Historian diagrams are classed as either Working
Diagrams or Charts.
The latter are also known as Saved Diagrams or Saved
Charts. These are diagrams that have been saved in the
Family Historian Chart format. See Working Diagrams and Charts for more on the
differences between them the two kinds of diagram.

With charts you will always be warned and given the chance to cancel,
if you make a change to diagram options that would require a ‘rebuild’.
Also if you close a chart (or take some other action would force the
chart to be closed), you will always be given the chance to save any
unsaved changes you have made to the chart.

With working diagrams, you can choose how much warning you wish to be
given in both scenarios. See fields below.

Fields

Rebuild warning
This option applies to working diagrams only (see definitions
above). The tree part of a diagram is 'rebuilt' if, and only if,
you change a diagram option which requires it to be rebuilt
(coloured red in the Diagram Options dialog). Before this happens
to a working diagram you can opt to be warned. There are 3
options:

Always warn

If diagram has been changed

If any change other than just branch open/close

Option 3 is the default.

See ‘Dynamic Diagram Options’ above for more
information about rebuilding the tree part of a diagram. See Working
Diagrams and Charts for an explanation of these terms.

Close warning
This option applies to working diagrams only (see definitions
above). A diagram is closed when the Diagram Window is closed for
any reason. A working diagram is also closed if it is replaced in
the Diagram Window with another working diagram (which can happen
if the option to re- use the last-used diagram window if unlocked,
is enabled - see below).
There are 3 options regarding when you get warnings of closure
of working diagrams:

If diagram has been changed

If any change other than just branch open/close

Never warn

Option 2 is the default.

See Policy on Warning of Changes above for more
information. See Working
Diagrams and Charts for an explanation of these terms.

Colour tree rebuild options
By default, options which, if they are changed, will require the
tree part of a diagram to be rebuilt, are coloured in red in the
Diagram Options dialog, so that they are easy to see. If you
prefer another colour, you can select it here. If you do not wish
‘rebuild options’ to be coloured distinctively, you can opt for no
colouring. For more information, see Dynamic Diagram Options
above.

Relationship text for diagram root row
When you display 'relationship text' to the left or right (or
both) of the diagram in the Diagram Window, the text shown here is
used for the row containing the diagram root. If you change this
value, you will have to rebuild any open diagrams if you wish them
to use the new value. The default text is 'root & siblings'.

Disable glow effect below zoom level
The glow effect can be set in the Boxes tab of Diagram Options.
It can significantly slow down the time it takes to display boxes.
This is not usually noticeable at normal zoom levels, but can
become significant with very large diagrams if zoomed out so that
the whole diagram is visible. At the same time, the glow effect
may be barely discernible at these zoom levels. For this reason,
it makes sense to disable it below a certain zoom level (on-screen
only - this option does not affect printed output).

Silhouettes...
Click on this button to view the default silhouette images that
will be used in diagrams if you request silhouettes to be
displayed (for Individuals with no picture, perhaps, or instead of
a picture). You can change the default silhouette images if you
wish.

Saved Options...
When you open a diagram using one of the diagram buttons on the
main toolbar, Family Historian will re-use whatever options you
used last time (provided the 'Save Options' checkbox in the
bottom-left corner of the Diagram Options dialog was ticked when
you last changed the options). You can check these saved options,
and modify them if you wish, by clicking on this button.

title: Preferences Dialog: Estimates
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Estimates

Some of the settings on this page are used for validation on data
entry. They are all also used for estimating dates of birth and death.
For example, if you select "Life Dates (Est.)" as an item to be
displayed in the Records Window for Individuals, Family Historian will
display its estimate of the earliest date at which each person might
have been born (if this information is not recorded) and the latest date
at which the person might have died (again if this information is not
recorded).

The values specified here do not have to be strictly accurate. It does
not matter if you specify, for example, that the maximum lifespan is 100
years and it turns out that someone in your file lived over 100 years.
The values just have to be good enough approximations for purposes of
estimation.

Other Fields

Estimate Future Death Dates
By default, Family Historian will return no value if its
estimated death date is set in the future. However, if you wish it
to estimate future death dates, tick this box.

Default Date Range
In Family Historian, dates can be specified imprecisely. For example, you can say that an event occurred
after or before a specified date. If you have specified that an event occurred before 1900, say, should
Family Historian show the event if events are being filtered by date, and only events that occurred between 1820 and 1850
are being displayed (e.g. using the time slider in the Map window)? Family Historian will decide this question by
using the value specified for the Default Date Range. If the value of field is 10, for example, Family Historian will
filter by treating the event specified as 'before 1900' as falling in the 10 years leading up to 1900 (i.e. 1890-1900).

title: Preferences Dialog: FamilySearch
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: FamilySearch

FamilySearch is a nonprofit family history organization, based in Utah,
USA, operated by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. It
maintains a collection of records, resources and services designed to
help people learn more about their family history. To learn more,
please see the FamilySearch Window

Fields

Enable FamilySearch User Trees
FamilySearch have recently added an exciting new feature which
allows anyone to upload user
trees that are completely separate from the global family
tree. These family trees can be kept hidden from ordinary
users of FamilySearch, or you can allow access to everyone on a
read-only basis, or you can allow access only to individuals that
you specify. You can give these individuals read-only
access, if preferred, but you can also optionally allow these
individuals to contribute to the shared tree, and edit and
maintain it. Family Historian allows you to add, edit and
maintain records in user trees in the same way that you can add,
edit and maintain records in the FamilySearch global family
tree. See FamilySearch
User Trees to learn more.

Prompt to unmatch FamilySearch records if flagged as 'deleted'
If you match a Family Historian record to a FamilySearch record,
what should happen if someone somewhere deletes the FamilySearch
record? If you want to be asked if you wish to unmatch your
Family Historian record from the deleted FamilySearch record, tick
this option (the default). Otherwise, the Family Historian
record will effectively be unmatched automatically.

Warn of change to FamilySearch Id following a merge of
duplicates

It is a common occurrence that more than one record can be
created for the same person on FamilySearch. Anyone who
spots this happening can merge them - either within Family
Historian or on the FamilySearch website. When 2
FamilySearch records are merged, one of the 2 records is deleted
(after any missing details have been copied to the other
record). If you have matched a Family Historian record to a
FamilySearch record which has since been merged and then deleted,
Family Historian will automatically detect this situation when you
come to view the record, and update the stored FamilySearch record
id to the new record id. If you want to be warned when this
happens, tick this option (it is ticked by default).

Treat standardized place values as 'normalized'

Within every Family Historian Place
record, there is a field called 'Standardized' which can
optionally be used to store the place name in a standardized
format. For example, if you are a Texan, you might have a
Place record where the name of the place is given simply as
"Paris" - referring to the city of that name in Texas. There
is no requirement to provide a standardized version of this place
name but you can if you want to. If you were to do so, you
might provide the standardized version of the place name as
"Paris, Texas, United States".

When data is copied to FamilySearch, this may include place
details. FamilySearch permits place details to be provided
in two ways: in what it calls the 'original' form, and also in
what it calls the 'normalized' form. Family Historian will
always provide the standard place details to FamilySearch as the
'original' version. Additionally, if there is a
'Standardized' version of the place details and if the option Treat
standardized place values as 'normalized' is
ticked, Family Historian will also provide this standardized
version as the 'normalized' form.

Regardless of how place details are provided to FamilySearch, it
will attempt to match up the place details with its own conception
of what the normalized form should be. Often the 'original'
form of the place details, if detailed enough, will suffice on its
own for FamilySearch to feel confident that it can match these
place details to a normalized version. So it isn't always
necessary to provide a standardized version of place names.
However, if you do provide a version of the place name in the
standardized field, even if the version you supply does not
perfectly match the FamilySearch normalized version, this is
likely to be helpful, and provide useful clues which may
significantly increase the likelihood that FamilySearch will find
a version of the place details in normalized form, that it is
satisfied with.

If FamilySearch is unable to identify the normalized form of
a place to its own satisfaction, it won't reject the information
provided, but you may see highlighted messages to the effect that
FamilySearch has been unable to identify the normalized version of
the place details, if you view the record details on the
FamilySearch web site.

See also Property Box:
Main Tab for Place Records.

Whenever you see a place field in the Property
Box, you can access the Place record by either double-clicking
on the field or by moving your mouse over the field, and
clicking on the little button with 3 dots, to the right of
it. Doing either will open the Place List window with the
Place record selected. If you right-click on the selected
record and click 'Edit' you will be able to view and edit
details of the Place record, including the 'Standardized
Version' of the place name. Another approach is to view
and edit the Place record in the Property Box.

Rows per page (searches)
You can do searches of FamilySearch
trees on the Matches tab of the FamilySearch
Window. You can specify here how many rows per page
you want to see.

FamilySearch Window Colours
View and optionally change the colours used in the FamilySearch
window.

title: Preferences Dialog: File Load/Save
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: File Load/Save

Fields

Other Applications' Gedcom Extensions

There are 3 options:

Load Where Possible (the default)

Store Uncategorised

Exclude

You are strongly recommended to use the Load Where
Possible option (the default), unless you
have a good reason not to. The GEDCOM specification
permits applications to extend it, and add their own custom
fields. If you choose Load Where Possible,
when you import a GEDCOM file into a new Family Historian
project, Family Historian will load and incorporate into your
project, all data stored in GEDCOM extensions used by other
programs, that it recognises. Any GEDCOM extensions that Family
Historian does not recognise will still be loaded, but will be
saved as 'Unrecognised Data Fields' (UDFs).

If you choose, Store Uncategorised,
Family Historian will load all GEDCOM extensions, and will save
all of them as UDFs.

If you choose Exclude, all GEDCOM
extensions created by other applications will be excluded.

All three options are applicable not just to import, but also
whenever you simply open a GEDCOM file. In this case,
however, the Load Where Possible and
Store Uncategorised options
have the same effect - that is, to load GEDCOM extensions as
UDFs.

To view details of exactly how GEDCOM extensions are
incorporated into your project, if you choose Load
Where Possible, see the appropriate log file
(log files can be accessed from the Windows menu).

Exclude fields that are not valid for GEDCOM 5.5.1
By default, Family Historian will load as much data from a
GEDCOM file as it can. It can even load GEDCOM tags which are not
valid for GEDCOM 5.5.1. If you wish it to ignore invalid GEDCOM
tags, check this option.

Move invalid data into note fields where possible
Family Historian does not put invalid data into fields; but
other applications may do. If this option is enabled, and a field
is encountered which contains data that is not valid for that
field, the data will be moved into a note 'subfield', if that is
possible. If it isn't, a special 'Uncategorised Data Field' (UDF)
will be created as a subfield to hold the data. If this option is
not enabled, UDFs will always be used in these cases.

Accept Dates in Numeric Format
Some applications sometimes specify dates in GEDCOM using a
numeric format - e.g. 3/12/1998. This is not valid GEDCOM. In the
U.S.A. this date would probably be the 12th March, 1998. In the
U.K. it would be December 3rd, 1998. If you want Family Historian
to interpret these numeric dates as dates, choose one of the
choices which tell Family Historian how to interpret numeric
dates. For example, if you choose dd/mm/yyyy, Family Historian
will interpret 3/12/1998 as 3rd December, 1998. If you choose
mm/dd/yyyy, Family Historian will interpret it as 12th March,
1998. Choose 'No' if you do not want Family Historian to accept
numeric dates.

Check date order of spouses, children & facts on import
If checked, when you import data into a new project, Family
Historian will automatically ensure that all spouses, children and
facts are in the correct date order.

Output Family records before Individual records
In GEDCOM, all records apart from the header and trailer, can be
saved in any order. However, some applications expect Individual
records to be saved before Family records, and some may expect the
reverse. Family Historian outputs Individual records before Family
records by default, but you can output them in the reverse order
if you wish. In general, you are recommended to leave this option
unchecked unless you have a good reason to do otherwise.

Re-output the Current File’s Header Record (this session only)
In general when Family Historian saves a GEDCOM file, it writes
its own details in the header record. However, if you wish to use
Family Historian to edit data belonging to another application, it
may occasionally be advantageous to preserve the original header
record. This option is deliberately not saved persistently, and
consequently will always revert to the default (unchecked) at the
start of each new session.

Prompt save changes to current chart or map, if previously saved
If this option is enabled, when you hit the Save button on the
main toolbar, if the currently active window is the Diagram Window
and you are editing a saved chart, or if the currently active
window is the Map Window and you are editing a saved map, you will
be prompted to save changes to the chart or map, if there are any
unsaved changes. The prompt will allow you to choose 'Yes',
'No' or 'Cancel'. If you choose 'Yes', the current chart or
map details will be saved, and the current project details will
also be saved. If you choose 'No', the current chart or map
details will not be saved, but the current project details will be
saved. If you choose 'Cancel', the save will be cancelled.

If you untick this option, hitting the 'Save' button on the main
toolbar will always just result in a save to the current project.

Automatic snapshot management
If enabled, Family Historian will automatically take periodic
snapshots of your main project data file (that is, GEDCOM file).
This provides an extra layer of protection against some possible
problems that can occur, but should not be seen as a substitute
for taking regular backups. Snapshots can be managed, and
accessed, in the Snapshot
Manager.

Save using UTF-16 file format
If checked, GEDCOM files will be saved in UTF-16 format.
Otherwise, they will be saved in UTF-8 format (the default).
UTF-16 files are larger than UTF-8 files (normally about twice as
large), but opening and saving UTF-16 files may nevertheless be a
little faster. UTF-8 is much more widely supported than UTF-16.
Some third party applications - including companion products for
Family Historian - may support UTF-8 only, which is why it is
usually recommended. There is no difference between UTF-8 and
UTF-16 in terms of the actual content of data saved. Family
Historian can read both UTF-16 and UTF-8 files and will
automatically detect which format has been used when the file is
opened.

Enable Autosave
If you enable this option, Family Historian will automatically
save any changes you make, every few minutes - you specify how
many. Also, if 'Autosave on close' is checked, Family
Historian will automatically save any changes when you close a
project or exit (if the latter option is not checked, you will be
prompted to save changes).

title: Preferences Dialog: Focus Window
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Focus Window

Fields

Max Pictures of Focus Person at Top of Window
You can display up to 9 pictures of the Focus Person at the top of the Focus
Window.

Parent Pictures
Display pictures of the parents in the Spouses
& Children tab and the Parents
& Siblings tab.

Child Pictures
Display pictures of the children in the Spouses
& Children tab and the Parents
& Siblings tab.

Max. Ancestor Generations (space permitting)
Specify the maximum number of generations (up to 5) that you
wish to see displayed in the Ancestors
tab.

Descendant Generations (default)
Specify the default number of generations (up to 99) that you
wish to see displayed in the Descendants
tab. This is only the default. You will be able to expand
branches further by clicking on expansion buttons, if you wish.

Marriage Status
Display the status of marriages in the Marriage box. The default
status (blank) is married.

Children's Relationship to Parents
Display the nature of each child's relationship to its parents,
in a column labelled 'Rel.' The column displays a code
letter corresponding to the child's relationship to its parents.
For example, the letter. 'a' means that the child is adopted, 's'
means that it is a step child, and so on.

If the column is blank, this means that the status is 'birth' (the
default). Right-click on any child box to edit this relationship
field, and to see what the codes mean.

Ancestors Dates
Show each ancestor's life dates, in the Ancestors tab.

Descendants Dates
Show each descendant's life dates, in the Descendants tab.

Descendants Spouses
Show spouses of each descendant. Also, if there is any ambiguity
about who were the parents of any given descendant, modify the
descendant line to show which spouse they were a child of.

Descendants Spouses Dates
If showing descendant spouses, this option allows you to choose
whether or not to also display their life dates.

Record Ids
Display each person's record id.

Ages
Display age information in the Spouses & Children tab, and
the Parents & Siblings tab. Each person's age at the time of
their death, marriage or divorce is displayed, if this is is
applicable, and is known or can be calculated. Each person's age
now is displayed if the person is or may be alive.

Child Places
If enabled, place details will be included for child events.

Notes
If enabled, the first line or so of their record notes will be
displayed in the parents' boxes in the Spouses & Children,
and Parents & Siblings tabs.

Custom Text
Click on the Edit
button to specify custom expressions for up to 2 additional lines
of text for parent and grandparent boxes, and to to specify 1
additional column of information for children. To display
the text, the Custom Text check box must also be ticked.
Leave fields blank if not required. Any blank fields will be
ignored. For example, if the Child Text field is blank, you
will not get an additional column for children (the Child Text
Heading is ignored in this case).

Show Customize Link
Display a link, "customize", at the top right of the Focus
Window, to allow quick access for options for the Focus Window.

'More Ancestors' Lines
If this option is enabled, a line will extend to the right of
the box for any ancestors in the last generation displayed, who
have one or more recorded parents.

FamilySearch Match Icon

If enabled, a blue FamilySearch icon will be
displayed in the 'Spouses & Children' tab, or the 'Parents
& Sibling' tab, in the box for each person who is
matched to a FamilySearch record. This icon is a link.
Click on it to show the matching records in the FamilySearch
workspace window. There are more options relating to
FamilySearch on the FamilySearch
tab of Preferences, and there are options relating to
FamilySearch hints on the Internet Data Matches
tab of Preferences. To learn more about FamilySearch and
matching records, see the FamilySearch
workspace window.

Double Click Action
If you choose Make Focus Person,
double-clicking on any box in the Focus Window will make that
person the Focus Person for the window. If you press the Alt
key while double-clicking, however, the alternative action will
occur - i.e. the person will be displayed in the Property Box
(which will be opened, if not already opened). If you choose View in Property Box, the reverse
occurs. Now double-clicking on a box shows that person in the
Property Box, but pressing the Alt
key while double-clicking causes the person to become the Focus
Person.

Bear in mind that when the Property Box is open
with Sync with
Workspace Selection enabled, it will automatically sync
with the current selection whenever you change it - either by a
single click or a double click. The Double Click
Action setting will not change that.

Click on the Fonts button to
change the Focus Window fonts. Click on the Colours
button to change its colours. Click on the Restore
Defaults button to reset all settings back to their
installation defaults.

title: Preferences Dialog: General
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: General

Fields and Buttons

Warn of Possible Errors on Data Entry

If checked (the default), when you enter data in a field and
press the Tab key to exit the field, or simply click elsewhere,
Family Historian will validate the data entered and warn you if
it appears to be invalid, or looks unlikely for whatever reason.
Also, if you press F5, Family Historian will warn you if the
data may be incorrect. You are recommended to leave this
checked.

Display Surnames in Uppercase
If checked, Family Historian will use upper case when displaying
surnames in the Records Window, in lists, in diagrams, and in
reports.

Insert likely surname when adding children or fathers
If checked, Family Historian will automatically insert the
surname of the father when adding children and will automatically
inserting the child's surname when adding a father. This applies
to relationships created from the main 'Add' menu, or added on the
Focus Window, the Property Box, or the Diagram Window (using
Diagram-based Editing). It does not apply to relationships created
using low-level editing in the Records Window.

Use 'Circa' for Approximate Dates
If enabled, Family Historian will indicate that a date is
approximate by prefixing it with 'circa' or 'c.'. If not enabled,
Family Historian will indicate that a date is approximate by
appending '(approx.)' or '(app)' or '?' after the date. See Date Formats for more details.

Use Quarter Date Display Format
A quarter date is a date like "Q1 1978". It means the first 3
months of 1978. "Q2 1978" is the next 3 months (April to June
1978) and so on. You can always enter dates as quarter dates if
you wish to. This option determines whether Family Historian will
display them in the same format, or use a Date Range instead. If
using a Date Range it would display "Q2 1978" as "Between April
1978 and June 1978".

Enable LDS Support

Enables functionality relating to The Church of Jesus Christ of
Latter-Day Saints. See LDS
Church Features to learn more.

Preferred Standard Date Format
Choose dd mmm yyyy if you prefer dates to normally
appear day first (e.g. "23 Dec 1987"). Choose mmm dd, yyyy
if you prefer dates to appear month first (e.g. "Dec 23, 1987").
This choice only affects date formats where the month is written
as a word, such as 'December' or 'Dec'. In some contexts you may
want the date to be abbreviated to all-numeric form. See Preferred
Short Date Format next for options for this scenario. See Date Formats to
learn more about the many ways in which dates can be presented in
different contexts.

Preferred Short Date Format
In some contexts (diagrams, reports or elsewhere) you may wish
to see dates abbreviated to all-numeric form (or 'short date'
form). The Preferred Short Date Format option allows
you to choose how you wish dates to appear in such contexts.
For example, the option mm/dd/yyyy would mean
that the 23rd of December, 1987, would be abbreviated in
all-numeric form as "12/23/1987" - that is, month first, and using
a slash character, '/', to separate the month, day and year.
See Date Formats
to learn more about the many ways in which dates can be presented
in different contexts.

Changeover to Gregorian Calendar

Pope Gregory introduced the Gregorian calendar in 1582. England
and the American colonies did not switch to using the Gregorian
calendar until 1752. This setting will affect how Family
Historian calculates days-of-the-week and leap years between
1582 and 1752. It will have no effect on these calculations for
years before or after these dates. It does not in any way affect
how data is stored in your file.

See The
Gregorian Calendar for a brief description of the
Gregorian calendar, and the complexities involved in its
introduction.

Measurement Units
Specify whether you prefer to work in Inches, Centimetres or
Millimetres.

To Enter Accents When Typing

The default option is Press-and-hold key. If
this option is taken when you press-and-hold a letter key, a
small accent popup window will appear, offering you a choice of
variations of that letter, with accent characters - making it
very easy to select accents. When the popup widow is open, you
can select an accent character by clicking on it, by pressing
the number associated with it, or by using the arrow keys to
select it, and then pressing Enter. Pressing Escape will
close the popup window without selecting anything. The
list of accents displayed for any given letter is configurable
via the Configure
Language & Accents Dialog (accessible both from the
Popup window, or from the toolbar menu at the top of the
Property Box). You can choose any combination of accent
characters associated with a number of languages, or create your
own list of required accents.

Even if Press-and-hold key is the chosen
option, you can still temporarily switch off the
accent-selection behaviour, by pressing-and-holding the Insert
key before you press-and-hold a letter key. If you do this, the
default Windows behaviour will be used instead, which is to
cause the letter to auto-repeat.

The Press-and-hold key option may not work
properly with all keyboards. If problems are experienced,
the alternative option is Press Insert and letter key.
When this option is chosen, you can open the accent popup window
by pressing-and-holding the Insert key and then pressing a
letter key.

Finally, you can the Disable option will
disable this functionality altogether.

To learn more about the accent popup window, and
accent-handling, see the Configure
Language & Accents Dialog.

Latitude & Longitude Format
Specify your preferred display format for latitude &
longitude information.

Colour Scheme
The colour scheme specified here is your default colour
scheme for the program. You can override these colours if
you wish. To revert to the default settings for the colour
scheme, change the colour scheme, press Apply,
and then change it back again, and press Apply
again. You can also create your own colour schemes if you
wish. To do this, set all the colours, everywhere in the
program, to the colours you want for your scheme. Then use
the File > Import/Export > Export > Current
Colour Scheme command to export the colour scheme as a
file. Then re-import the colour scheme file (use File
> Import/Export > Import > Colour Scheme) to
create a new colour scheme.

Maximum Undoable Actions
The default number of undoable actions (edits, inserts, deletes,
etc) is 999, but you can increase this if you wish.

Timeline Facts
Opens the Select
Timeline Facts Dialog.

Advanced
Opens the Advanced
Preferences Dialog.

title: Preferences Dialog: International
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: International

Fields

Display Language (menus, labels, etc)

The language options currently supported by Family Historian
for the menus, labels, messages, etc, within the program, are

English - United Kingdom

English - United States

How to Display Language Names
Do you want a German language pack to be listed as 'German' or
as 'Deutsch'? If your prefer 'German', choose
'Default'. If you prefer 'Deutsch', choose 'Untranslated'.

Current Project Language
Read only. Shows the current project language. The
project language is the language used for the project
content. This is specified in the Header record for the
project, using the 'Language' field. To access the header
record, click on 'Special Records' on the View menu, and choose
'Header Record'.

Default Output Language
This is the default language to be used for reports, diagrams,
etc. It is also the language that will be displayed in the
'Sentence' fields, in the Facts tab of the Property Box, and on
the Witnesses Window. If you choose 'Default', this means
that the default position is that output will not be
translated. Regardless of what you choose as the default
output language, you will always be able to override this for any
given report or diagram. So if a given diagram is not
producing the language output were expecting, check the 'Language'
tab within the options for that report or diagram.

If there are no options available in the list, apart from
'Default', this means that you have no installed language
packs. To install a language pack, click on 'Language Packs'
on the Tools menu, and then choose 'Import'. You can import
language packs directly from the Family Historian plugin store
(which holds language packs as well as plugins). If
there are language packs listed, but not the one you want, again
you should check the Family Historian plugin store. If you
still cannot find the language pack you want, consider writing it
yourself! All the tools you need are built into Family
Historian. Advice is available, if needed, from other Family
Historian users (see the Community section of the Family Historian
website for pointers).

Status Bar Language Pane
Read only. Shows how information about the current project
language and the default output language, will be displayed in the
status bar language pane, with most workspace windows. When
the active workspace is a Diagram Window, a Report Window or a
Book Window however, the status bar pane will not necessarily
match the values shown here. This is because with those
workspace windows, it is possible to override the default output
language, and specify a different output language.

title: Preferences Dialog: Internet Data Matches
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Internet Data Matches

Hints in the Focus Window (circled in red)

Internet Data Matching (and Hints)

If Internet Data Matching is enabled for any supported data providers
(that is, FamilySearch, Findmypast, or MyHeritage) Family Historian will
check whether records in the current project match data records stored
in the relevant provider's databases on the Internet. Only records
you view in the first two tabs of the Focus Window are checked - that
is, the Spouses & Children and Parents & Siblings
tabs - and only, in each case, if their Private flag is not set.
These checks are done automatically with no special action on your
part. If matches are found, a hint showing the number of
matches found, will be displayed in a green and white circle in the
bottom right corner of the relevant person's box, in the Focus Window
(see examples of hints, circled in red, in image above). Click on
the hint to view details of the match. If you 'hover' the mouse
over the hint, a popup will display more information about the matches
found.

When you click on a hint for Findmypast or MyHeritage, to view the
matches found, a web-page is displayed where you can click on buttons to
'Confirm' or 'Accept' a match, or to reject it if it is an incorrect
match. If you confirm a match, you are recommended to copy any new
data you have found into your Family Historian record for the person in
question. The data is not copied automatically.

Tip: When updating your records from data
provider web pages, we recommend that you use 'drag-and-drop' in the Web
Search window, to copy the data into the Property Box. This way
you can update your records without having to do any typing.
Before you do so, however, we recommend that you first use the Automatic
Source Citations pane to specify the source for your data - which
you should be able to do, again, without having to type any text.
When automatic source citations are enabled, all the new or updated data
will be automatically given the source citation you specify. So
don't forget to disable automatic source citations as soon as you have
finished inputting the data.

MyHeritage provides two kinds of matching: 'Record matches' which are
matches against historical data records, and 'Smart matches' which are
matches against family trees that other genealogists have created.

FamilySearch matches work a little differently.
FamilySearch hosts a large, unified database of connected genealogy
information called Family Tree, which anyone
can access and anyone can edit and add to (see https://www.familysearch.org/tree/overview).
You can match Family Historian records with Family Tree records.
You can optionally receive hints about possible matches. You will
only receive these hints for Family Historian records which are not
already matched to FamilySearch Family Tree records. You can also
receive hints about possible duplicates. This arises when
FamilySearch thinks that it may have more than one record for the same
person. You will only receive hints of this kind for Family
Historian records which are already matched to FamilySearch
records. Finally, FamilySearch also provides hints about
historical records which appear to mention a person that you have a
record for. Again, you will only receive this kind of hint for
Family Historian records which are already matched to FamilySearch
records.

When you click on a hint for a FamilySearch hint, you will be taken to
the Matches tab of the FamilySearch Window, if it is a 'possible match'
hint or a 'possible duplicate' hint. If the hint is a FamilySearch
historical record hint, a web page will be displayed showing the
relevant information. You will then be able to choose whether or
not you wish to attach this historical record as a source for the
FamilySearch record. If you do so, you will then be able to see
this information displayed as a source for that FamilySearch record, in
the Sources tab of the FamilySearch Window - and optionally copy the
same information as a Source record, into the matching Family Historian
record.

To learn more about Automatic Internet Data Matching, including privacy
policies of data providers, discounts for Family Historian users, and
the current status of providers' Internet services, please see www.family-historian.co.uk/aidm.

Manually Refreshing Hints

When you confirm a match or reject a Findmypast or MyHeritage hint
(which you do within the data provider web-page that you are taken to,
when you click on a hint), Family Historian will normally detect that
the match has been confirmed or rejected and update hints
accordingly. However, it can sometimes happen for technical
reasons, that Family Historian hints get out of sync with the data
provider, with regard to the status of matches (this is more likely to
happen if you use an external web browser to display record matches,
than if you use the Web Search Window). Similar things can happen
with FamilySearch hints. If Family Historian does get out of sync,
you can manually refresh any hint to correct it. You can do this
by right-clicking on the box for the person in question, and choosing
'Refresh Internet Matches' from the dropdown menu that appears.
Alternatively, if you let the mouse hover over the hint, so that
the the popup window mentioned above opens, you can click on the
button in the top-right corner of the popup window. This will also
refresh the match.

Discounts for Family Historian Users

FamilySearch records (historical records or Family Tree records) can be
freely accessed. In most cases (there are a few exceptions), you
will need a paid-for account to view details of Findmypast or MyHeritage
records. When you click on any link, for either Findmypast or
MyHeritage, you will be told if a paid-for account is required, if you
don't already have one. Look
out for significant discounts for Family Historian users with
MyHeritage accounts. There is normally a discount for
Family Historian users when you open a MyHeritage account in this
manner. These will be advertised, if available, on the web page
you see when you click on a link. Note: these discounts will
normally only be available if you take out a new data subscription with
MyHeritage on the web page you are taken to, when you click on a hint
within Family Historian. To learn more about discounts for Family
Historian users, please see www.family-historian.co.uk/aidm.

Fields

Hint Click Action
By default, when you click on a hint in the Focus Window, you
will be taken to the match results page - which is normally a web
page, but can also, in the case of some FamilySearch hints, be the
Matches tab of the FamilySearch
Window. However, you can alternatively specify that
clicking on the hint causes a popup to be displayed instead
(the same popup that is always displayed if you 'hover' the mouse
over the hint, and which also contains a clickable link to the
match results page).

Location to Display Matches

You can choose whether you want to display the match results
page in an external web browser, or in the Web Search window.

Tip: Although you should always be able to
drag-and-drop text from the Web Search window into the Property
Box, you may not be able to do this with an external web
browser. It depends on what web browser you use, and on
its current settings. Consequently, if you wish to use
drag-and-drop, you may prefer to use the Web Search window to
display match results.

Display Match Progress Indicators
If this option is enabled, a small grey clock will be displayed
in the bottom right corner of a person's box when a new search for
a match is in progress for that person. Also, if match data
is later updated (perhaps as a result of changed information), the
hint will briefly flash (for less than one second), to show that
an update has occurred.

Findmypast Settings

Automatic Matching

Options are 'Enable', 'Disable' or 'Disable for this project
only'

Filter
By default, Findmypast will only show matches that are 'new' -
that is, matches that you have neither accepted nor
rejected. However, you can opt to see accepted or rejected
matches instead if you wish.

MyHeritage Settings

Automatic Matching

Options are 'Enable', 'Disable' or 'Disable for this project
only'

Match Types Required

Options are 'Record Matches (historical records)' 'Smart
Matches (family trees)' or 'All Matches'

Filter
By default, MyHeritage will only show matches that are 'pending'
- that is, matches that you have neither confirmed nor
rejected. However, you can opt to see confirmed and/or
rejected matches also if you wish.

Minimum Confidence Level

MyHeritage gives each match a score that indicates the level of
confidence of the match. You can override the default, to
specify the level of confidence you require.

Exclude email list from Smart Matches
If you have an account with MyHeritage, you may have uploaded
your own family tree to the MyHeritage website. If you wish
to exclude matches against your own family tree, enter the email
address associated with your MyHeritage account, here. You
can exclude multiple family trees if you wish, by entering a list
of email addresses, separated by one or more spaces.

Show 'Value Added' (if available)
Tick this option if you want hints to include a sentence about
the 'value added' by MyHeritage records in any given case. For
example, a hint might mention that MyHeritage records include
birth date or place for an Individual, if that information is not
already stored in the Individual's record.

FamilySearch Settings

Automatic Matching

Options are 'Enable', 'Disable' or 'Disable for this project
only'

Matches to Family Tree (unmatched only)
These hints are only available for Family Historian Individual
records which are not already matched to records in FamilySearch
Family Tree. They show possible matches. Clicking on
one of these hints will cause the possible matches to be displayed
in the Matches tab of the
Family Search Window.

Possible Duplicates in FamilySearch (matched only)
These hints are only available for Family Historian Individual
records which are already matched to records in
FamilySearch. They show possible duplicates for whichever
FamilySearch record the Family Historian record is matched
to. Clicking on one of these hints will cause the possible
duplicates to be displayed in the Matches tab of the
Family Search Window.

Historical Record Hints (matched only)
These hints are also only available for Family Historian
Individual records which are already matched to records in
FamilySearch Family Tree. They show historical records which
appear to mention the person in question. Clicking on one of
these hints will cause a relevant web page on the FamilySearch
website, to be displayed in a web browser. It will then be
possible to attach the historical record as a source for the
FamilySearch record in question. If you do so, you will then
be able to see this information displayed as a source for that
FamilySearch record, in the Sources tab of the FamilySearch Window
- and optionally copy the same information as a Source record,
into the matching Family Historian record.
