To learn more about FamilySearch and its Family Tree database, see the FamilySearch Window, or see FamilySearch
Family Tree.

title: Preferences Dialog: Map Window
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Map Window

Fields

Enable Auto-Geocoding
If enabled, whenever a place is displayed in the Map
Window, Family Historian will attempt to automatically
determine its latitude and longitude, if this information is not
already held for the Place record in question.
Automatic geocoding requires an Internet connection, and uses an
Internet geocoding service.*

Mark Auto-geocodes as Tentative

By default, automatic geocoding will always flag a geocode as
tentative. But you can opt to only flag automatic geocodes
as (intially) tentative if it is deemed to be partial or
uncertain. See also Map
Window Legend.

Enable Zoom Animation
By default, zooms in the Map Window are animated. Untick
this option to disable animation if required.

Minimize Text Zooming

Maps can be viewed at up to 19 different zoom levels, numbered
0-18, where 0 is not zoomed-in at all (i.e. whole world view)
and 18 is fully zoomed-in (maximum close-up). All text boxes are
defined relative to a particular zoom level (normally the zoom
level that was current when the text box was created). This is
called their 'Reference Zoom' level, and you can view this
value, and change it if you want to, in the Map
Shape Format dialog, for each text box. If you opt to
minimize text zooming, text boxes will display at the size you
created them when displayed at their reference zoom level, or
when zoomed in further. They will, however, start to shrink as
you zoom out, subject to the Text Zoom Margin setting
(see next).

If you choose not to minimize text zooming, text boxes will
appear bigger or smaller when you zoom in or out, like any other
map shape.

For more information, see the description for the Reference
Zoom field in the help page for the Text tab of the Map Shape Format
dialog.

The current zoom level, at any given time, is
displayed in the status bar of the Map Window. It is also
displayed, next to the Reference Zoom field, in the Text tab of
the Map Shape Format
dialog.

Text Zoom Margin
This value (normally 0, 1 or 2) is only used if you have opted
to minimize text zooming. In that case, the text box will mainly
display at its original size unless you zoom the map out past a
certain past. The point at which it will start to shrink is when
the current zoom level of the map is less than the reference zoom
level of the text box, minus the 'Text Box Margin'. The reason for
this, when text zooming is minimized, is to allow a degree of
latitude before text boxes start to get smaller as you zoom out. A
value of 2, for example, means that you can zoom out twice before
a newly-created text box will start to get smaller.

Display Marker Text

If this option is ticked (the default), the first part of the
relevant address or place text will display as a short textual
description below each marker displayed in the Map Viewer.
Click the Fonts button (see below) to
configure the font used for this text. Click the Colours
button (see below) to configure the colour of the text, and also
the colour of the 'glow' that surrounds the text (the glow is
designed to make the marker text stand out from other map text).

Tip: A quick way to hide or show marker text in the
Map Viewer, is to right-click on the Map Viewer itself and tick
or untick "Display Marker Text" on the context menu that
appears.

Block Refresh for Non-tentative Geocodes
You can force an automatic refresh of geocoding for any selected
places, using the Refresh Geocoding menu
command, which is accessible both on the Geocoding submenu of the
Map menu, within the Map Window, and by right-click on items in
the List pane. Enable this option to prevent a place that
already has a latitude and longitude from being refreshed in this
way, unless it is marked as tentative.

Hide no-date markers when time slider is active
When the Time Slider is enabled (see discussion of the Time
Slider in the Map Window) markers
for places associated with dated events are only displayed if they
fall within the range specified by the Time Slider. Use this
option to specify whether, when the Time Slider is enabled, you
wish to hide markers for places which have no date, or not.

Preferred Map Type
The Map Window currently only supports one map type:
'OpenStreetMap'.

Units
Miles or kilometres. These values are displayed in the Map
Window. If you right-click on a circle or on a
single-segment line, and choose the 'Format' command, the radius
or the circle, or the length of the line will be displayed, using
the units chosen here (see Map
Shape Format Dialog: Shape Tab).

Override Default Country Code
Normally this field should be left blank. It is only relevant to
auto-geocoding, and only then when trying to determine the
latitude and longitude of a specified place, if the place details
do not include any recognisable country specifier, and there is a
need to guess what the most likely country might be. If this
happens, ordinarily the 'Home Location' country held by Windows
(as specified in the 'Region' settings in the Control Panel) is
used as the default country. However, it may be that you are using
a PC in one country to work on a project for people who lived
predominantly in another country. Or the Region settings on your
PC may be wrong. Either way, you can if you wish override the
default country, by specifying the ISO code of the country that
you wish to be the default. The code must be 2 letters. See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1
for a list of possible 2-character country codes.

If you enter a country code and later wish to revert to the
default, just clear the code you entered.

Changes to this field are not applied immediately. They only
have an effect as from the next time you start Family Historian.

Fonts
Specify fonts for the Map Window.

Colours
Specify colours for the Map Window.

* All features which use Internet services provided by third parties
(such as Automatic Geocoding) are subject to the availability of those
services.

title: Preferences Dialog: Media
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Media

When media items are added to a project, a new Media record is created
for each one, to represent the media item within the project.

Fields

Autogenerate Keywords
New Media records will be automatically given one of the
following keywords, as appropriate:

Document

Picture

OLE Object

Audio

Video

Copy Image Tag Values to the Media Record
Some image files contain data, sometimes called 'tags' or
metadata, which store information about the image. If this
option is enabled, when a media item is added to a project, the
following image tag values will be automatically copied to the new
Media record field:

'Title' to the Title field

'Comment' to the Note field

'Date' to the Date field

'Keywords' to the Keywords field (merged with auto-generated
keywords)

Media Window Thumbnail Size
Specify the preferred size of Media Window thumbnail images.

Colours
Choose the colours which are applicable to the Media Window and,
in some cases, the Media tab of the Property Box.

title: Preferences Dialog: Named Lists
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Named Lists

Fields

Auto-Create Named Lists
Named Lists are discussed in the section for the Records Window, and are managed and
maintained in the Records Window. Although Named Lists are stored
with your other data in your data file, there are some lists which
you may always wish to use in all files, and you may wish them to
be created automatically if they don�t exist in a given file. You
may wish to always have a Bookmarks list, for example, even if it
has to be created as an empty list. You can have up to 6 of these
�Auto-Create� Named Lists.

Named Lists Columns
You can configure the columns displayed for named lists. Each
named list can have a different set of columns.

title: Preferences Dialog: Display
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Display

Fields

Screen Font Scaling

If the size of text in Family Historian is too small, rather
than changing the size of particular fonts used in the various
different components of the program, a better and easier option
is just to adjust screen font scaling. This will change
the displayed size of screen fonts used throughout the
program. "Screen fonts" means fonts that are used, and
only used, within the program, to display information on your
screen - as opposed to fonts which are used in reports, books,
charts, diagrams or websites. Fonts used for any kind of
program output are of course configurable, but are not affected
by changes to screen font scaling.

Many open windows will automatically adjust themselves
appropriately if you change the value of Screen Font Scaling,
but some won't, and some will only partially adjust. If
there are any windows open that will not fully automatically
adjust when you change font scaling, a message will be displayed
warning you that you will need to close and reopen these
windows, to force them to update themselves. An easy
alternative to closing and reopening these windows is to simply
close and reopen Family Historian itself.

These are screen fonts affected by Screen Font Scaling:

The Default Font, set on this tab of
Preference. This font is used in record and place
listings.

The Focus Window fonts, set on the Focus Window tab of
Preferences.

The Property Box fonts, set on the Property Box tab of
Preferences. The Property Box text font is used not just
by the Property Box, but also by all satellite windows of the
Property Box, and the Citation Window. The Property Box
text font is also used as the default font (the 'automatic'
font) for the Note Window, and is also the font used in most
ordinary dialogs, and in fields and buttons on many workspace
windows.

The Query Window Results font, set in the Query Window tab
of Preferences.

Changing screen font scaling will not affect the recorded point
size of any of these fonts. So, for example, if your
Property Box font (set on the Property Box tab of Preferences)
is Tahoma, 10 pt, you will still see "Tahoma 10 pt" as the value
for this font on that tab, even if you change Screen Font
Scaling to 150%. However the actual font that will be
displayed in the Property Box in that case will be 15pt (10 pt
scaled 150%).

Tip: You may notice that when you increase Screen
Font Scaling, the size of fonts previously selected by you in
the Note Window may appear to get bigger. You may be
wondering if this will not affect output, if these notes are
subsequently included within a report, say. The answer is
that output will not be affected. This is because Family
Historian maintains all font sizes in notes as relative sizes
- that is, the size of the font relative to (bigger than, or
smaller than) a given default.

Reset Screen Font Sizes

This option will be greyed if all screen fonts already have
their default sizes.

One good reason to use Screen Font Scaling (the
previous command discussed above) is that it is a very easy way
to change a number of screen font sizes, while keeping them all
in proportion relative to one another. But what if they
are not already in the correct proportions before you change the
scale? This can easily happen if you change some screen
font sizes but not others, or give them non-proportionate
sizes. One quick and easy way to ensure that all screen
fonts are in the correct size proportions, is to use Reset
Screen Font Sizes, to reset them all to their
installation default sizes. Resetting screen font sizes
sets their sizes as recorded in Preferences - that is, before
any scaling is applied. It doesn't change or reset the
Screen Font Scaling value.

Reset Screen Font Sizes, as the name suggests, only
affects the recorded font sizes. Other aspects
of a font (such as the name of the font, and whether it is bold
or not) are not reset.

Main Window Toolbar Size

Choose your preferred size for main window toolbars -
that is, toolbars attached to the main application window.

Main Window Toolbar Text

Choose your preferred option for text on main window toolbars :

Minimal: text appears to the right of the
items on the first section of the main window toolbar only (5
items)

Standard: text appears to the right of the
items on the first two sections of the main application
toolbar only

Below Button: (the default) text appears
below all items on all main window toolbars

Include Key Diagrams on Main Window Toolbar

If ticked (the default), buttons for the 4 main diagrams will
each have a button on the main application toolbar. If not
ticked, these become the first 4 items in the dropdown menu that
appears when you click on the Chart button.

Other Window Toolbar Size

Choose your preferred size for window toolbars attached to any
window that is not the main application window. This
setting applies, for example, to the Property
Box, the Citation
Window, and all toolbars attached to workspace windows,
among others.

Always Show Records Window Icon in Navigation Bar

If this option is ticked (the default), an icon for the Records Window will always be
displayed in the Navigation
Bar, even if the Records Window is closed. This is to
provide faster, easier access to the Records Window.

This option has no effect if the Records Window is the
'Startup' window (see Startup
tab) as the Startup window's icon is always the first icon
in the Navigation Bar.

Navigation Bar Text
Text can be displayed next to the icon for windows in the
Navigation Bar (except for the icons for the Focus Window and
Records Window, which never have text next to them). Use this
option to specify your preferred length for the text (long, medium
or short). Set the option to 'None' if you do not wish any text to
be displayed in the Navigation Bar.

Navigation Bar Size
Choose your preferred size for the Navigation Bar.

Default Font
The default font is used in most record lists, and elsewhere.

Automatic Source Citation Colours
The colours used in the Automatic
Source Citation pane can be configured here.

title: Preferences Dialog: Notes
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Notes

Fields

Enable Spellcheck

Tick this option to enable spellcheck in the Notes Window.

Dictionary
Choose your preferred dictionary for
spellchecking.

Custom Dictionary
You can flag words to be ignored, so that the spellcheck does
not flag them as misspelled. All such words are stored in
the Custom Dictionary. By default there is only one: Custom.

Advanced
When you click on a word in the Notes Window, using the right
mouse button, Family Historian will offer you the opportunity to
look up the work in a web-based dictionary or thesaurus. The
lookups can be configured using the Advanced dialog.

Default Font
Unless you override it, the font in the Notes Window for any
given text, is shown as 'automatic'. This means that it is
shown using the default font. You can change the default
font here. The font used in the Notes Window is the same
font that is used in the Property Box, so changing it in either
context will affect both.

Force Property Box to float when displaying linked records
(other Note Window options)
If you click on a record link in the Note Window, the record
will be displayed in the Property Box. By default, if the
Property is docked it will remain docked (but will flash
slightly), and if it is floating it will remain floating but will
come to the front. This option, if ticked, will cause the
Property Box to be forced to float (and come to the front),
whenever you click on a record link in the Note Window.

title: Preferences Dialog: Property Box
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Property Box

Names and Surnames

When you enter a person's name that consists of more than one word,
Family Historian will always assume that the last name is the surname,
unless you explicitly indicate otherwise by using slash characters to
mark the surname. Suppose, for example, that Elizabeth Powell Smith's
surname is 'Powell Smith'. If you entered her name simply as "Elizabeth
Powell Smith", Family Historian would assume that 'Smith' was the
surname. To mark her surname correctly you would need to put slashes
round 'Powell Smith' like this: "Elizabeth /Powell Smith/". If the name
had been hyphenated however (as 'Powell-Smith') there would have been no
need for slashes as Family Historian would have treated the hyphenated
name 'Powell-Smith' as the last name, and hence the surname.

In some languages, the surname may not necessarily appear at the end of
the name. For example, "Mao Tse-Tung" should be entered as "/Mao/
Tse-Tung" because 'Mao' is the surname. If you only enter only one word
as the name (e.g. 'Jane') Family Historian will, by default, assume that
it is not the surname and will automatically add two slash
characters on the end of the name to reflect this ("Jane //"). If
actually 'Jane' was the surname, and that's the only name you had, you
would need to enter it as "/Jane/" to make this clear. Of course,
the alternative is to use a question mark or something similar, to mark
the unknown name part - for example, "Jane ?" or "? Jane".

Why does Family Historian need to know which part of the name is the
surname? It needs to know this so that it can provide a number of
different services, such as automatic capitalization of surnames,
surname-first ordering, and search-by-surname.

When viewing names in Name fields, for editing purposes, Family
Historian can, if you wish, always put slashes round the
surname, to make it clear which part of the name is the surname.
However, for aesthetic reasons, Family Historian by default keeps the
use of slashes to a minimum, and only puts slashes round the surname
when this is needed for clarity - that is, if the surname is not the
last name, or if there is only one word in the name. See Show
Surnames Between Slashes below for options relating to this.

Fields

Show Surnames Between Slashes

See the discussion of "Names and Surnames" above. Choose
Always if you want Family Historian to always
mark the surname by slashes in Name fields when names are being
edited in the Property Box. If you choose Only
When Necessary, Family Historian will only mark the
surname by slashes if the surname is not the last word in the
name, or if the recorded name consists of one word only.

Whatever option is chosen here only affects Name fields in the
Property Box. It has no effect on how names
appear in reports, books, charts, diagrams, web-pages, or on how
they appear elsewhere in the program. It also makes no
difference to how you enter names into Name fields.

Fonts

Choose the fonts you wish to use (including size and style) for
the Property Box. The 'Title' font is only used when the
Property Box is docked (see next).

Preferred Position for Citation List Pane When Property Box is
Docked or Floating

To display or hide the Citation List Pane for the Property Box,
click on the yellow scroll button on the Property Box
toolbar. The Citation List Pane shows source citations for the
data in the Property Box. When you click on an item in the
Property Box, the Citation List Pane updates automatically to
show you the source citations for that item of data.

The Citation List Pane can appear either below the main body
of the Property Box, or to the right of it. By default, it will
appear below the main body of the Property. If space is
limited, you can also opt to show the Citation List pane in its
own window (this is the Open in New Window
option).

Thumbnail Size
Configure the size of thumbnails in the Media tab.

Colours
Configure colours for the Property Box

Captions
Configure how captions are displayed in the Property Box. See Property Box
Captions.

Open New Notes in the Note Window
Tick this option if you want new notes to be automatically
opened in the Note Window.

Show Field Helper Buttons When Mouse Over
Some fields in the Property Box - such as date fields - have a
Helper dialog that can be used as an aid, to make it easier to
enter complex information (such as complex date information). To
access this Helper dialog, you can either double-click on the
field, or click on the little button with 3 dots at the right end
of the field. Only fields which have a Helper dialog associated
with them, have this button, and it only appears when you click on
the field or when you move your mouse over the field. If you do
not wish the button to appear when you move the mouse over the
field, uncheck this option (enabled by default).

Enable 'Add Citation' Menu
Tick this option if you want a dropdown menu to appear when you
click the Add Citation button on the
Citation List pane.
If enabled, the menu items will be:

Cite Existing Source

Add New Generic Source

Add New Free Form Source

Add New Templated Source

If the menu is not enabled, clicking on the Add
Citation button will behave as "Cite Existing Source"
had been clicked - that is, the Source record selector will be
displayed to allow you to select an existing Source record for
the new citation. However this record selector has a New... button. Clicking on that
button allows a new Source record to be created - either
templated, generic, or free form.

In other words, the same functionality is available, one way or
another, whether you choose to display a menu or not.
Users who usually create new sources, may prefer the menu
approach. User who usually don't create new sources, may
prefer the alternative.

title: Preferences Dialog: Query Window
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Query Window

Fields

Print Margins
Specify the size of margins when printing

Smart Folder Printing

If you need to print the output of a smart folder in the Query
Window, this is where you can specify the Title, Subtitle,
Orientation and Multi-page Handling.

Title

This will appear as a title line, at the top of each page, when
the query is printed. You can use special codes if you wish the
current date or time to be included as part of the title. See Special
Codes in Query Titles and Subtitles.

Subtitle

Choose one of a list of pre-defined subtitles. The
subtitle appears beneath the title line, at the top of each page,
when the query is printed. If you wish to create your own custom
subtitle, choose 'Custom' and enter the subtitle in the box that
appears to the right of the dropdown list. You can use
special codes in your subtitle if you want the current date or
time to be included as part of the subtitle. See Special Codes in Query Titles and Subtitles.

Orientation

Format of page when printed - Landscape or Portrait. Can also be
changed in Print Setup (accessible from the File menu).

Multi-page Handling

Indicates what you wish to happen if the query, when printed,
is more than a single page in width (given the current
orientation). The choices are:

Down then across
Print all pages for the leftmost columns, before printing
any pages for columns to the right.
Across then down
Print all pages for the topmost rows, before printing any
pages for subsequent rows.
Max. one page across
Ignore all columns which cannot fit onto a single page

Always sort null values last
If checked, null (i.e. blank) values will always be listed after
non-null values when you sort a column (ascending or
descending). The exceptions are columns which display flags
and named list membership, which are not affected by this option.

If this option is not checked, null values will normally display
before non-null values when you sort a column in ascending order,
and will display after them if you sort a column in descending
order.

Fonts
Specify fonts to be used for printing, and also for the Result
Set tab of the Query Window.

Colours
Choose the colours for text in the Result
Set tab of the Query Window. The colour "Data-Linked
Text" is used for cells which represent actual fields or
records. "Ordinary Text" is used for cells which do not
represent actual fields or records - for example, calculated text
values. It is useful to be able to distinguish between them
visually, because you can double-click on any data-linked cell to
jump straight to that value in the Property Box (if you
right-click on the field of a data-linked cell, you can even
choose to view that field in the All
tab of the Property Box if you prefer). For more
details, see the Result
Set tab of the Query Window.

title: Record Window Options Dialog: Display Tab
text:
Preferences Dialog

Record Window Advanced Options

Fields

When displaying an Individual's Spouse Family

See "Viewing Linked Records" below.

When displaying an Individual's Parents' Family

See "Viewing Linked Records" below.

When displaying a Family's Husband/Wife Details

See "Viewing Linked Records" below.

When displaying a Family's Child Details

See "Viewing Linked Records" below.

Indicate where children are adopted,
fostered, etc

If checked, an adopted child (John
Smith) will be listed as "John Smith (adopted)" in his family
record. See How
to Flag a Child as Adopted, Illegitimate, etc.

Double-click on record in Record List does default record action

If checked, double-clicking on a record in the main record area
of the Record Window will perform the default action for records
of that type. For all record types except Research Notes and
Note records, this means displaying the record in the Property
Box. For Research Notes and Note records, this means showing the
research note or note in the Note Window. Double-clicking on
the record when the Alt key is pressed will expand the record's
branches. If not checked, double-clicking on a record will expand
the record's branches. In that case, double-clicking on the record
when the Alt key is pressed will do the default record action.

Double-click on record in Named List means 'Go To Record'

If checked, double-clicking on a record in a Named List within
the Record Window (when the Named List Pane is visible) will
open the Property Box to view the record. Double-clicking on the
record when the Alt key is pressed will expand the record's
branches. If not checked, double-clicking on a record will expand
the record's branches. In that case, double-clicking on the record
when the Alt key is pressed will open the Property Box to view the
record.

Lock first column when scrolling horizontally

If checked, the first column will be locked in position when you
scroll horizontally.

If the first column is locked and fills the whole window, or
nearly does, when you scroll horizontally, this feature will be
temporarily switched off (if it weren't, nothing would appear to
happen when you scrolled horizontally). In this situation,
you can re-enable first column locking, by resizing the first
column so that it is smaller than the window width, and moving the
scroll bar to the leftmost position.

Viewing Linked Records

When viewing a record in the Records Window, you can expand any linked
record to view the linked record as if it were part of the first record.
For example, to see an Individuals spouse and children, you can expand
the Spouse Family link. When you do this, you are actually viewing a
Family record which stores links to all the Individual records for the
members of the family.

If you are viewing a person's spouse family record, as a linked
record, do you wish to see them listed as a spouse in the Family record
that is then displayed? If you are viewing a person's parents' family
record as a linked record, do you wish to see them listed as a child?

The same issues apply when viewing an Individual record, as a linked
record, from the point-of-view of a Family record.

If you want a strictly accurate viewing of the linked record, you
should uncheck all of the "When Displaying..." options. Most users
prefer the installation default settings which are:

Don't show the individual as one of the spouses

Only show if family has more than one child

Only show if individual has multiple spouses

Only show if child has multiple sets of parents

title: Preferences Dialog: Records Window
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Records Window

Record Window Options are used not just in the Records
Window itself, but also in other contexts, such as record selector
dialogs.

Always sort null values last
If checked, null (i.e. blank) values will always be listed after
non-null values when you sort a column (ascending or
descending). The exceptions are columns which display flags
and named list membership, which are not affected by this option.

If this option is not checked, null values will normally display
before non-null values when you sort a column in ascending order,
and will display after them if you sort a column in descending
order.

Display individuals surname first in main list
If checked, John Smith will be displayed as "Smith, John" in the
list. If unchecked he will be displayed as "John SMITH".

Use Short Title for Source record names if available
If enabled, Source records will be listed under their Short
Titles, if they have one, and their Titles if not. If not enabled,
Source records will always be listed under their Titles only.

Show record Ids for all linked Records…
Records frequently contain links to other records. If this
option is checked, the record Id of the linked record is
displayed, in square brackets, at the end of the record name.

…except Family Records
This option qualifies the previous option (if checked) by
excluding Family records. It is not normally useful to see the
record Ids when viewing linked Family records, and there is a risk
that they may be confused with Individual records Ids.
Consequently, by default, this option is checked.

Record Type Display Options
Each record type, if not hidden, is assigned its own tab in the
Records Window. You can specify for each record type whether you
want it always to be shown, always hidden, or only shown if not
empty. The Individuals record type is an exception - it is always
shown.

Columns
Configure the Columns in the Records Window. See Configure Columns Dialog

Colours
Configure colours for the Records Window.

Advanced
Configure advanced features of the Records Window. See Records Window Advanced Options.

A quick way to access these options is to right-click on
any row in the Records Window, and select Records Window Options from
the context menu that appears.

title: Preferences Dialog: Sources
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Sources

Fields

'Book' Style
'Book' style options are only applicable
to those parts of footnotes and bibliography entries which, in
their design, have been designated as books, using the
'BOOK' style qualifier (see 'Style Qualifiers' below).
This designation is intended to be used for book titles, or
similar.

If you wish to change which field values these named styles are
applied to, in a given footnote or bibliography entry, you need to
modify its design (see 'Style Qualifiers' below).

'Title' Style
'Title' style options are only applicable to those parts of
footnotes and bibliography entries which, in their design, have
been designated as titles, using the 'TITLE' style
qualifier (see 'Style Qualifiers' below). This designation
is intended to be used for non-book titles, such as newspaper,
magazine or article titles, or similar.

If you wish to change which field values these named styles are
applied to, in a given footnote or bibliography entry, you need to
modify its design (see 'Style Qualifiers' below).

Source Templates
Opens the Source
Template Definitions Dialog.

Generic Source Formats
Opens the Generic
Source Formats Dialog.

Style Qualifiers

The contents of footnotes and bibliography entries are specified by formats.
A 'format' can be either a source template format or a generic
format. You never need to specify or modify these formats,
but you can if you want to. Formats use expressions to reference
field values in Source records and citations. When referencing any
field value, you can optionally use a style qualifier ('BOOK' or
'TITLE'). A single format may have any number of references to
field values, each of which can optionally have either the 'BOOK' style
qualifier or the 'TITLE' style qualifier.

For information about formats and style qualifiers, seen Source
Template Formats, and Style
Qualifiers.

title: Preferences Dialog: Startup
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Startup

Fields

Default Startup File
Use this field to specify a data file that should be loaded by
default, when Family Historian starts up.

Startup Actions: Display the Last-Used
Focus Person in the Focus Window
If enabled, when a project is opened,
will set the focus person within the Focus Window root to be the
person who was the focus person when the project was last
accessed. Has no effect if Family Historian is used to open a
GEDCOM file in standalone mode. Is not applicable, and is greyed,
if the Records Window is used as the startup window, instead of
the Focus Window (see next).

Startup Actions: Display the Records Window, instead of the
Focus Window
Self-explanatory

Startup Actions: Check for Updates Automatically
Get Family Historian to periodically check for new updates.

title: Preferences Dialog: Web Search Window
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Web Search Window

Fields

Default Start Page
The default start page to display when the Web Search Window is
opened. Changing this option does not affect any Web Search
Windows that are already open.

Default Zoom
The default zoom level for the Web Search Window. Changing
this option does not affect any Web Search Windows that are
already open.

title: Preferences Dialog: Workspaces
text:
Preferences Dialog

Preferences Dialog: Workspaces

Workspace windows are the main windows within Family Historian (see Workspace Windows). They are designed to
serve a variety of different roles and to facilitate a variety of
different tasks. The Property Box is not itself a workspace window; but
is designed to be used in conjunction with workspace windows.

You can have any number of Workspace Windows open at the same time,
although usually one is in front of the others so that you can only see
one at a time. You can switch between them using the Navigation
Bar.

Fields & Buttons

Re-use of Open Windows Permitted

If you click on a button to open a diagram, what should happen
if you already have one or more Diagram Windows open? Would you
like one of these windows to be re-used, or would you prefer to
keep the existing Diagram Windows and open a new one? You can
have as many diagrams open at any given time as you want. But if
you are using working diagrams (new diagrams that you create
as-needed, and which have never been saved) to browse and
explore your family tree data, it may be inconvenient if Family
Historian always opens a new Diagram Window for each new working
diagram. You may end up with a great many Diagram Windows open.

You can choose whether or not to allow re-use, with respect to
all types of workspace window, except the Focus Window, the
Records Window and the FamilySearch Window, which are always
re-used, as you can never have more than one of them. Even if
you permit re-use of a given workspace window, it does not mean
that it necessarily will be re-used. Existing windows will never
be re-used if they have been 'locked' to prevent re-use (you
can't lock the Focus Window or Records Window). Also, special
rules apply to the Diagram Window.

If you have opted to allow re-use of Diagram Windows, Family
Historian will re-use the most recently-used Diagram Window when
you open a new working diagram if it contains an unlocked
working diagram. Depending on the Close Warning options you
selected (see Diagrams tab in Preferences), you may get warned
if significant changes have been made to the diagram that is to
be replaced (e.g. if boxes have been moved or resized, or if
diagram elements have been added). The Re-use option has no
effect on Diagram Windows if you are opening a chart (a saved
diagram), or if the last-used diagram window contains a chart.
In either case, a new Diagram Window will always be opened.

Note: Locking a given workspace window has no effect if re-use
is not permitted for the workspace window in question.

Tip: A quick way to lock a window is to right-click
on the windows icon in the Navigation Pane and select the
command from there.

Preferred Position for Property Box

The Property Box can be used in conjunction with all workspace
windows. Depending on the window, and the size of your monitor,
you may prefer the Property Box to be docked or floating. When
the Property Box is docked it is fixed to the right side of the
workspace window and is the same height as the workspace window.
When docked, there is a gripper bar on the left edge of the
Property Box and you can click-and-drag here to increase or
decrease its share of the available space.

When the Property Box is floating, it can be moved or resized
quite independently of the workspace window, and if it overlaps
the workspace window, it will always be in front of it.

If you have no preference, choose 'None'.

Default Property Box Action When Workspace is Opened

As well as choosing, for different workspace windows, whether
you prefer the Property Box to be docked or floating (or have no
preference), you can also specify what you wish to happen when a
new instance of a workspace window is opened. The options have
the following meaning:

None
No action is taken. If open, the Property Box is left as it
is.
Open It
The Property Box will be opened in its preferred position,
if not already open. If it is already open, it will be
switched to its preferred position if any (docked or
floating).
Close it
The Property Box will be closed, unless the 'Pin' button has
been pressed so that it is now 'unpinned'. In that case, the
Property Box will not be closed but it will be switched to its
preferred position.
Move it
No action is taken if the Property Box is not already open.
However if it is open, it will be switched to its preferred
position if any (docked or floating).

Open Workspace Windows Remember Property Box State

If enabled (the default), when you switch to a workspace window
(e.g. by clicking on its icon in the Navigation Bar) the
Property Box will be returned to the state it was in when that
particular workspace was last activated - i.e. opened or closed,
and docked or floating.

If this option is not enabled, the Default Property
Box Action When Workspace is Opened settings (see
previous) will be used to determine what should be done with the
Property Box.

Disable Property Box Management
Click on this button to change all of the above settings, so
that the Property Box is always left where it is, and is not
automatically opened or closed, docked or made to float.
Disabling Property Box management does not affect the question of
whether workspace windows are re-used or not.

title: Prepared Citation
text:
Prepared Citation

The term 'prepared citation' has not always been used within Family
Historian, but there has been an implicit concept of a prepared citation
since automatic source
citations were first introduced. This is because the
prepared citation details are the details used for automatic source
citations - they are the same thing (although the prepared citation is
no longer just used for automatic source citations - it is also used by
Data Entry Assistant tools, for example). At any given time, there
is only ever at most one prepared citation. There may be
none. At a minimum, a citation (any citation) consists of a link
to a Source record. However, all kinds of details (field values)
can be attached to such links, even including notes and media. And
this is true of both actual and prepared citations.

You can view the prepared citation (if any) in the Citation Window (see
Citation Window
with a Prepared Citation) or in the Automatic
Source Citation Pane, or in both at the same time.To view the
prepared citation in the Citation Window, click on the Source
button
on the main application toolbar and choose View Prepared Citation
from the menu that appears. This menu command will be greyed if
there is no prepared citation. To view the prepared citation in
the Automatic Source Citation Pane, just click the Automatic Source
Citation button
on the main application toolbar. If there is no prepared citation,
the Source field will display a search icon and the View
button will be disabled and greyed, as in figure 1 below.

Figure 1 - Automatic Source Citation Pane with No Prepared Citation

If there is a prepared citation, the Source field will
display a Source record icon
and the View button will be enabled (not
grey). If automatic source citations are not enabled, it will look
something like figure 2 below.

Figure 2 - Automatic Source Citation with a Prepared Citation

Finally, if there is a prepared citation and automatic source citations
are enabled, the large button on the left will be blue and
show the word 'Enabled', and the Automatic Source Citation pane will
look something like figure 3 below.

Figure 3 - Automatic Source Citation with a Prepared Citation, with
Automatic Source Citations Enabled

In practice, most of the time it will be easier to view and work with
prepared citations in the Citation Window (see Citation
Window with a Prepared Citation) - not only because it is a larger
window, with a more convenient layout, but also because you can also
view full details of the Source record at the same time, which you can't
with the Automatic Source Citation Pane. Also, most importantly,
in the Citation Window you have access to Data
Entry Assistants, which you don't in the Automatic Source Citation
pane. Furthermore, in the Citation Window side panel, you can see
a preview of how footnotes and bibliography entries will appear in
reports and books, and again you can't do that in the Automatic Source
Citation Pane. But you can copy a prepared citation in either
context. In the Citation Window you click the Copy
Citation button to do this. In the Automatic Source
Citation Pane, you have to click on the menu button and then choose Copy
Prepared Citation from the menu that appears.

We saw above that If you want to view an existing prepared citation in
the Citation Window, one way is to click on the Source button on the
main application toolbar and choose View Prepared Citation
from the menu that appears. However, this menu command will be
greyed if there is no prepared citation. The other way is to click
on the Automatic Source Citation button on the main
application toolbar, and then click the View
button when the pane appears. This button will again be greyed if
there is no prepared citation. You can create a new prepared
citation by clicking on any of the first three menu commands on the menu
that appears when you click on the Source button on the main application
toolbar. Or you can create a prepared citation by simply selecting
a Source record in the Automatic Source Citation Pane. By the same
token, if you want to clear the prepared citation, you just need to
clear the selection in the Automatic Source Citation Pane (by, for
example, clicking the Clear button to the right of the Source
field).

Prepared citation details are stored persistently in the Family
Historian header record, so if you create a prepared citation in one
session, it will still be there, and you can still use it, in the next.

title: More Dialog Boxes
text:
Using Family Historian

More Dialog Boxes

Many dialog boxes have already been described. 'Dialog
boxes' (sometimes also just called 'dialogs') are form-like
windows. Any dialog boxes (such as Diagram
Options or Report Options)
which are closely linked to a particular workspace window, are described
in the context of the Help pages for that window. Some dialog
boxes are satellite windows of the Property
Box (closely-linked to it). These are described in the
context of the Help pages for the Property Box. This section
describes more important dialog boxes.

title: More Dialog Boxes...
text:
Dialog Boxes

More Dialog Boxes

This section describes other dialog boxes used in Family Historian.

title: Print Preview Toolbar
text:
Print Preview

Print Preview Toolbar

The print preview toolbar offers you the following options:

Print
Bring up the Print Dialog.

Next Page
Preview the next page.

Prev Page
Preview the previous page.

One Page/Two Page

Preview one or two pages at a time.

Zoom In
Take a closer look at the page.

Zoom Out
Take a larger look at the page.

Close
Return from Print Preview.

title: Private Notes
text:
General Topics

Private Notes

If you want any text within a note to be treated as private, you
should include it in square brackets, like this: [[secret text]]. This
is called private text or a private note. You can
include the entire contents of a note within the doubled square
brackets, or any part of it. It may be just a word or phrase that you
wish to treat as private (e.g. "he limped as a result of a
[[self-inflicted]] war wound"). Ordinarily, private notes are excluded
from reports and books, or from pages in websites or family tree CDs and
DVDs, when these are based on reports. But they can be included if you
wish. The relevant option is usually to be found on the main page of
options for the report or book in question. If you choose to include
private notes, you can also choose whether or not to include the double
square brackets around them.

Private notes can be entered into any Note field, and within any note
field you can have as many private notes as you like. A 'note field' for
these purposes means any field labelled 'Note' (it doesn't include Named
List notes though - see below). You can however also include private
notes in a small number of other fields, which are not labelled 'Note' -
such as "Address" fields, or the "Text from Source" field on Source
Citations and Source records. Only fields which allow multiple lines of
text to be entered into them, support private notes. If you double-click
on a field that supports multiple lines of text, the Note
Window opens. This is a floating window which you can use to
view or edit any text field. You cannot enter multiple lines of text
into Name fields, Date fields, Age fields etc, so none of these support
private notes. Another example of a field which does not allow multiple
lines of text is the "Where within Source" field on Source Citations.
Although superficially similar to the "Text From Source" field, you can
enter multiple lines of text into the latter, but not into the former.
Nothing will prevent you entering text enclosed in doubled square
brackets in the "Where Within Source" field; but if you do so, it will
not be treated as a private note and will be displayed as entered in
reports and books, regardless of options chosen.

Private notes can also be entered using the Insert Hashtag
button on the Note Window.
Private notes entered in this way will normally have a distinctive
background colour and a hash tag (such as '#Research') making them easy
to spot and easy to search for.

Private notes can be used in conjunction with word-processing features,
such as tables. If an entire table is included within a private
note and you opt to exclude private notes, the entire table will be
excluded. If however, the private section just covers text within
a cell or straddles one or more cells within a table, or covers an area
that includes part of a table only, and if private notes are excluded,
all the cells (rows and columns) of the table will be left intact - but
the actual text within the private notes will be excluded.

Private notes are not used with Named Lists. You can enter a note for
a Named List and/or for each item in a Named List. And there is nothing
to stop you entering text in doubled square brackets in these notes; but
the text will not be treated as a private note.

If you wish to delete all private notes from a GEDCOM
file, the Split Tree
Helper tool (accessible from the File menu)
can be used to do that.

If you export a GEDCOM file, private notes are excluded by default -
but you can choose to include them if you wish (see the Export
Gedcom File Options dialog).

Note: as well as marking text within a note as private, you can
also mark an entire fact as private, by setting the 'Private' flag on
the fact, in the Facts tab of
the Property Box.

title: Product Support
text:
Product Support

To find out about free services, including product support options,
available to Family Historian users (such as user forums, user group
website, newsletters and other support options) visit www.family-historian.co.uk/support.

Before seeking product support, however, you should first check the
following sources of information for a solution to your problem or
query:

The User Manual (a.k.a. the help)

The User Manual is what you are looking at now. It is also sometimes
referred to as the 'Help'. To search it you can do the following:

Browse the Contents pane of the Help (this is normally shown on the
left side, but if it is hidden, click on the 'Show' button on the
toolbar above to show it).

Click on the Index tab of the Contents pane, to view an Index for
the Help.

Click on the Search tab of the Contents pane to do a search within
the Help

When using Family Historian, if you are viewing a dialog box (form
window) that has a Help button, press this
button to display help information that is relevant to that dialog box.
If there is no Help button pressing the F1 key will
often take you to Help that is relevant to the window or dialog that you
are looking at. For example, you can get Help for any workspace window
by simply pressing F1 when using the respective window or dialog.

The Readme File

The Readme file was installed on your machine when Family
Historian was installed. It contains information relevant to installing
and uninstalling the program.

You can access the Readme file from the Family Historian submenu of
the Windows' Start menu.

If you still have a problem or query...

Visit Family Historian on the web at www.family-historian.co.uk/support for up-to-date
support options.

Also, if you bought Family Historian from a specialist genealogy
supplier, they may provide telephone or email support or both.

title: Project Window
text:
Dialog Boxes

Project Window

Project Window

The Project Window is the first window you see when you run the program
for the first time. From here you can create a new family tree project,
or view a list of projects you have already created. You can select a
project in the list, and open it. If the Project Window is closed, you
can always open it by clicking Project
Window on the File menu.

New and upgrading users are recommended to read Tips for New & Upgrading Users. Otherwise,
see Features of
the Project Window.

title: Features of the Project Window
text:
Project Window

Features of the Project Window

The Project Window appears each time you start Family Historian,
unless you have specified that a particular project is to be your
default project - in which case, Family Historian will automatically
open that project for you and the Project Window will not be displayed.

The Project Window will also be opened whenever you close the current
project that you are working on (click on Close
Project on the File menu).
Or you can open it without closing the current project or file, by
clicking on Project Window on the File menu.

Fields

Current Project

You can view the Project Window, even if you already have a
project open. The name of the current open project, if any, will
be shown here. If you have a standalone GEDCOM file open (not
part of a project) its name will be shown here.

Autosave

The current autosave settings are shown in the top-right of the
Project Window. Click on the text as a link to open the Autosave
Options dialog to change the settings.

Alternatively, you can also change Autosave settings by
clicking on the More Tasks...
button, and then clicking on Autosave
Options on the menu that appears.

Family Historian Projects

The list shows all Family Historian projects in the folder
specified by the Location field (see next). Each project has its
own folder. Usually the project name is the same as the name of
the project folder. In this case, the folder name is not
mentioned. However, if the name of the project folder is
different from the name of the project itself, which it can be,
the name of the folder will be given in brackets after the name
of the project, preceded by "Folder: " - e.g. "My Project
(Folder=Temp)".

When Family Historian is first installed, this will show only
one project - "Family Historian Sample Project", which is a
sample project, used to illustrate some of the things you can do
with the program. Do not enter your family data into this
project - create your own one, by clicking on the New
Project button.

To open a listed project, double-click on it; or select it and
click on Open Project.

Location

Shows the folder in which all the listed Family Historian
projects are located. By default, this folder will be "Family
Historian Projects" in the default Windows location for user
documents. However, you can change this location to whatever you
want. To do so, click on the location text as a link. A menu
appears with two options: Choose
Location and Reset Location
to Installation Default.

Alternatively, you can also change the location by clicking on
the More Tasks... button, and then
clicking on Choose Location for
Projects on the Project
List submenu that appears.

New Project

Click on this button to create a new project. The New
Project Wizard will appear to take you through the steps.
You can import directly from a Family Historian project file,
from other genealogy programs' data files, from a GEDCOM file or
GEDZIP file, or directly from FamilySearch. Or you
can create a new project from scratch.

Open Project

Select a project in the list of Family Historian projects and
click on this button to open it - or just double-click on the
project name.

More Tasks

When you click on this button a drop down menu appears - see 'More Tasks' menu below.

Exit Application

Close the application.

Tips for New & Upgrading Users

Click on this text link to view Tips
for New & Upgrading Users.

More Tasks Menu

This is the menu that appears when you click on the More
Tasks button.

Search for Projects, Backups & Gedcom Files

This menu command is used for searching your hard disk(s) for
Family Historian projects and backups, and for GEDCOM
files. The File
Search Options dialog is displayed where you can specify
the search options required. The results of the search are
displayed in the Search Results Window.

View Last Search Results

You can view the results of the last search you did (if any),
at any time, by selecting this option. The results of the
search are displayed in the Search Results Window.

Browse for Projects, Backups & Gedcom Files >

Browse for Project

You don't have to keep Family Historian projects in the same
folder. You can keep them anywhere. If you wish to open a
project that is not in the current location, it won't be listed.
In that case, you can either change the location, or, if you
wish to open the project without changing your current location
setting, you can use the Browse for
Project command. When you click on this command, a file
selector dialog will appear. Choose the project file for the
project you wish to open, and click Open.

Restore Backup

Choose this option to restore a saved backup

Browse for Gedcom File

Family Historian can open standalone Gedcom files using this
option.

In general, editing Gedcom files is not recommended
except as a temporary expedient. If you plan to use the
data from a Gedcom file to any significant extent, you should
create a new Family Historian project (using the New
Project Wizard) and import the Gedcom file into that.

Recent Gedcom Files

Select a Gedcom file from a list of recently-accessed Gedcom
files.

Project List >

Choose Location for Projects

See the discussion of the Location field above.

Reset Location to Installation Default

If you have changed the location, use this command to reset the
location to the installation default.

Refresh Project List

Refresh the list of Family Historian projects.

Current List Selection >

Set as Default Project

This command makes the currently selected project the default
project. When Family Historian is opened, it will
automatically load the default project if there is one. If not,
it will display the Project Window. You can make any project the
default project.

View Public Subfolder

You can use Family Historian to create output of many
different kinds - websites, family tree CDs, pictures of
diagrams, reports saved as PDF files, and so on. By default, for
convenience, Family Historian will save these output files in a
special subfolder of your project, called 'public'. This command
will open the Public subfolder for the currently selected
project to allow you to view, copy or delete the output files
contained in it.

Copy Project

Make a copy of the entire project folder for the currently
selected project,

Delete Project

Delete the entire project folder for the currently selected
project, including all the files contained in it. Use
with caution! You will be required to confirm the full
list of files that you wish to be deleted.

Rename Project

Rename the currently selected project.

Manage Snapshots

Opens the Snapshot Manager
dialog.

Backup Project (full)

Do a full back up of the selected project.

Backup/Restore Settings >

Backup Settings

"Settings" in this context means preferences, configurations,
customizations, fact type definitions, custom queries, custom
smart folders, custom reports, custom diagrams, custom text
schemes, custom source templates, language packs, custom map
overlays, custom accent files, ... and more. They can all
be backed up to a Family Historian settings file.
This can be very useful if you want to install Family Historian
on a new PC and want to transfer your settings to that PC.
You create a settings file, copy it to the new PC, and then
restore it in the new context.

For more information, see Backup/Restore
Settings.

This same backup option is also
accessible via Backup/Restore
on the File menu.

Restore Settings

Use this command to restore previously backed-up settings from
a Family Historian Settings file.

For more information, see Backup/Restore
Settings.

Help on Backup/Restore Settings

Opens the Backup/Restore
Settings Help page.

Autosave Options

See the discussion of the Autosave field above.

Sample Project >

Reset Sample Project

Resets the Family Historian sample project to its initial state
- that is, as it was when Family Historian was installed.

Tip: You can also access the full set of options in the
"Current List Selection" submenu by right-clicking on any project in the
list.

title: Tips for New & Upgrading Users
text:
Project Window

Tips for New & Upgrading Users

Quick Start Guide

All new users are strongly recommended to read the Quick
Start Guide which is accessible from the Help menu, or viewed
in the Quick Start Guide web page. It is a short,
visual guide to the basics of using the program.

Getting Started with Your First Project

If you have just started using Family Historian, then you are probably
at the Project Window. If the window
you are looking at says "Project Window" in the caption, then that's
what it is.

When Family Historian is first installed, you will see only one
project in the Projects list. This is Family

Historian Sample Project. You can open and browse the sample
project if you wish. You can also use it to experiment and to try
things out and it's a good idea to do so; but do not use it to store
your own family tree information. For that you should create your own
project.

If you do browse the sample project, you will need to know how to get
back to the Project Window. To do that, simply close the sample project
- which you do by clicking Close Project
on the File menu. Whenever you close
the current project, the Project Window will be re-displayed. You can
also view the Project Window at any time, without closing the current
project, by clicking on Project Window
on the File menu.

To create your own project, click on the New
Project button on the Projects Window, and follow the
instructions. If you make your project the default project, you will
find that the next time you run Family Historian, it will automatically
load that project, and effectively skip past the Projects Window. That
means that any information you enter will be added to that project.
That's fine. You can use one project to store all the genealogy data
that you accumulate. But if you ever need to create any more projects
(or to have another look at the sample project) remember that you can
always get back to the Project Window by closing the current project, or
by clicking Project Window on the File menu.

To open an existing project from the Projects Window, simply
double-click on any listed project, or select it and click on the Open Project button.

When you have created your first project, if you need more help, click
on Getting Started on the Help
menu.

Upgrading from an Earlier Version of Family Historian?

Users upgrading from an earlier version of Family Historian are
recommended to read Notes
on Upgrading to Version 8.

title: Property Box
text:
Property Box

The Property Box (marked in red) - docked
and floating

The Property Box is the primary window for data entry and
for viewing details of stored records. It is used with records of
all types:

Individuals

Families

Notes

Sources

Repositories

Media

Places

Addresses

Research Notes

Source
Templates

Submitters

Submission

Header

It displays different tabs depending on the record type. See the
various record types for more details.

You can open the Property Box to view and edit a record by selecting
the record (in whatever window you are viewing it), and clicking on the
Property Box button
on the main application toolbar. Another way of accessing the
Property Box, which works in the Focus Window and in other contexts, is
to right-click on the record, and select 'Properties' from the dropdown
menu that appears.

The Property Box can be docked at the side of a window, or it
can float like an ordinary dialog box. Click on the Dock
button to dock it when it is
floating. Click on the Float button to float it when it is docked.

It can be resized in various ways. Click-and-drag on gripper bars
to reposition boundaries between panes and other areas of the Property
Box. There can be up to 4 of them visible at any one time, depending on
which tab you are looking at (some Property Box tabs have an extra
gripper bar just below the tab toolbar). Gripper bars can be horizontal
or vertical. Horizontal gripper bars look like this:

When the Property Box is resized, fields within the Property Box will
be resized and repositioned. If there isn't room for one or more
fields, vertical or horizontal scrollbars will appear as needed, to
allow hidden fields to be accessed. The Property Box can also be
customized to show more fields (or different fields), and even more tabs
if you wish - see Customize
Property Box.

The Property Box has its own toolbar (at the top). The toolbar buttons
are described below:

Item
Description

Go Back to previous record.

Go Forward to next record (after having clicked 'Go Back').

Individual records only. Go to parent record (father if
there is one, or mother if not). If you press the Alt
key while clicking on this button, it behaves
differently. In that case, it opens the Parents
Window to display the parents for the current Individual.

Individual records only. View the current Individual in
the Focus Window.

Go to this record's entry in the Records
Window.

Show or hide the Property Box Citation List Pane.

Individual records only. Show or
hide the Parents Window.

Enable or disable Sync with Workspace Selection. When
enabled, the Property Box always displays the record details for
the currently selected record (that is the record currently
selected in the active workspace
window). When disabled, the Property Box will not
automatically change contents when you change selection in the
active workspace window; but you can still 'manually' force the
Property Box to update itself by, for example, selecting a record
and clicking on the Property Box button
on the main application toolbar.

Displays a dropdown menu with commands that are relevant to the
Property Box. The commands are:

Text Size
Set the font size (and even the actual font) to be used in
the Property Box. The same font will also be used in
other windows, such as the Note Window (default font),
Witnesses Window and Parent Window.
Configure Language & Accent Characters
Opens the Configure
Language and Accents Character Dialog.

Open Character Map
Opens the Character Map program. This is a Windows
accessory program. It is useful for investigating and
researching font options.
Show Source Record's Citations in Result Window
Visible with Source records only. Shows a table of
source citations linked to the current Source record, in the Results tab of the
Query Window.

Sort Family & Events in Date Order

Individual and Family records only. Sorts spouse
families by marriage date (if an Individual family is
selected), and sorts events by date (both Individual and
Family events).

Tip: The purpose of this menu command is
sometimes misunderstood. It sorts fields within
records. It does not sort the listed fact rows in the
Facts tab of the Property Box. This is because the
Facts tab is not displayed in field order. The events
shown on the Facts tab of the Property Box frequently come
from numerous different records, and are displayed, by
default, in date order (although you may need to refresh the
ordering if you change dates). See the Facts
tab for more details.

Open Parent Window
Individual records only. Opens the Parents
Window.

How to Delete Records & Change Relationships

Opens the Help, to display the page How
to Delete Records and Change Relationships.

Customize Property Box

Opens the Customize
Property Box Dialog.

Options

Opens the Property
Box tab of Preferences.

Recent
Displays a menu with a list of records that were recently
displayed in the Property Box. Click on any of them to
switch to showing that record in the Property Box.

Causes the Property Box to 'float' in front of the main
application window (only available when the Property Box is
'docked' at the side of the window). See Floating
Windows to learn more.

Causes the Property Box to 'dock' at the side of the window
(only available when the Property Box is 'floating').

Closes the Property Box. Only applies when the Property Box is
docked. When floating, you get the ordinary window close button on
the caption bar.

Satellite Windows of the Property Box

The Property Box has satellite windows. These are floating
windows that are work in conjunction with the Property Box, and
provide additional information about the record currently showing in the
Property Box, or about the currently-selected fact in the Facts
tab of the Property Box. In each case, they update
themselves to reflect changes in the Property Box and are only ever open
when it is open. Effectively they extend the functionality of the
Property Box. The satellite windows are:

Names & Titles Dialog

Witnesses Window

Parents Window

Media Viewer

The Citation List pane is
not usually a separate window but it too can be if you choose the
appropriate option in the Property
tab of Preferences.

The Citation Window (not to be confused
with the Citation List pane) is not a satellite of the Property Box, and
nor is the Note Window. Both of these
are independent floating windows, which can be opened from the Property
Box, but are separate from it.
Drag-and-Drop

The Property Box supports drag-and-drop, which can be a quick
and easy way of adding text and pictures. See Drag-and-Drop
to learn more.

title: Property Box: Addresses Tab
text:
Property Box

Property Box: Addresses Tab

The Addresses tab (not to be confused with the Main
Tab for Address Records) is only used with Place
records. It shows a list of addresses associated with the current Place
record, and allows these to be edited, and even merged.

Click-and-drag on a horizontal gripper bar below the toolbar, to resize the list and increase or
decrease the space available for address notes.

The Toolbar

The toolbar buttons have the following functions:

Item
Description

Add a new address for the current Place record.

If you want to edit the text for an address, you can do this when
view the Address record for this address, in the Property
Box. See the last toolbar button below.

Merge two or more addresses. To select multiple addresses,
press-and-hold the Ctrl key to add to a
selection, without unselecting previously selected addresses.

When you merge addresses, you will be prompted to choose a final
form for the merged address. This final form will be one of
the addresses that you are merging. This change will affect
any event that references the merged addresses. They will
all be updated automatically to reflect the change.

Tip: If you make a mistake when merging addresses,
you can always undo the change by clicking 'Undo' on the Edit
menu.

Shows a list of records that reference the selected address
(including the actual Address record). You will be able to
click a Go To button to view any of
these record in the Property Box.

Shows where a selected address record is used. This is not
just a list of records (see previous). Details of each event
that references this address, including the date, and other
contextual details, are displayed in the Result
Set tab of the Query Window.
If you double-click on a cell in the Date, Place or Address
columns, the particular event will be displayed in the Property
Box.

If you click on this button, a dropdown menu will offer you a
choice of displaying the selected address in the Map Window or in
an Online Map. You can select multiple addresses and display
them all in the Map Window if you wish. If you do that, a
new marker set called "Selected Addresses" will be created and
displayed in the Map Window. The addresses do not have to be
geocoded.

The option to display an address in an Online Map requires a
single selection. It is not available if you have multiple
addresses selected. If the selected address is geocoded,
it's exact location will be displayed using Google Maps, in a web
browser. If the selected address is not geocoded, Google
Maps will still be displayed and will be searched using the
address text.

Allows the Address record for the selected address to be viewed
in the Property Box. After doing this, you can return to
where you had been by clicking the Go Back button on the main Property Box toolbar.

title: Property Box: All Tab
text:
Property Box

Property Box: All Tab

The All Tab is used with all
records. It shows you a complete listing of all the data that you have
for the current record, in a hierarchical layout. This is exactly the
same layout that is used in the Records Window. It also shows the
record id, and the last updated date.

You can if you wish edit almost any aspect of a record in the All
tab. The technique is the same as that used when editing
records in the Records Window. Right-click on a field name (left column)
to bring up a context menu with 'Add' commands for each of the
sub-fields which you can validly add to that field. Alternatively, to
delete a field, select it and press the Delete key.
If you want to edit the value of a field, click on its current value in
the right-column.

To change the order a field with respect to its sibling fields where
this is permitted (which it isn't always), select the field and click
the Move Up or
Move Down
arrow buttons, in the top-right corner of the listing.

View Linked Records

Where a record contains links to other records, the name of the linked
record is shown in the right column with a little white check box to the left of the record icon.
Check this check box if you want to see details of the linked
record. If that record in turn links to other records, you can
follow their links in the same way. And so on, indefinitely.

title: Property Box Captions
text:
Preferences Dialog:
Property Box Tab

Property Box Captions

This dialog box is reached by clicking on the Property
Box Captions button of the Property Box tab, of the Preferences
dialog. It is used for configuring the captions in the Property Box. The
Property Box is used to display information about all 13 record types
supported by Family Historian. You can tailor the caption it displays
appropriately for each record type.

For example, suppose you want each individual�s Custom Id to be
displayed in the caption when viewing an Individual record. Position the
cursor where you want the Custom Id to appear within the caption labeled
�Individual� and click on the �<< Insert Data Ref� button
immediately to the right of this caption. A new dialog box �Expression
Entry Assistant� appears. In the listing in this dialog box are a number
of items: �Name�, �Sex�, and so on. Locate �Miscellaneous� and click on
its small expansion button to expand it. Locate �Custom Id� in the
expanded area (you may have to scroll) and select it. Click OK.
The Expression Entry Assistant dialog box closes and the text
�%INDI.REFN[1]%� is inserted into the caption for Individuals, at the
current cursor position.

Use care when doing this. Expressions that start and end with a �%�
character are data references (see Understanding Data References). Do not insert
your data reference into the middle of another data reference. That will
result in an expression which Family Historian will not recognise.

By default, the caption for an Individual looks like this:

Individual: %INDI% [=RecordId()]

'%INDI%' is a data reference that refers to the Individual record as a
whole. The caption also contains another expression however:
'=RecordId()' is a function which returns the Record Id that
Family Historian keeps for each record (for more about functions, see Understanding
Functions). If you want to see the Custom Id instead of the Record
Id, you could simply substitute the two expressions - i.e..:

Individual: %INDI% [%INDI.REFN[1]%]

If you want to see them both (separated by a slash character let us
say) you could use the following:

Individual: %INDI%
[=RecordId()/%INDI.REFN[1]%]

You don�t have to use a slash character. Nor do you need the square
brackets. These are only there to make the caption easier to read. If
you prefer some other arrangement you can change these. You can shorten
the label �Individual:� or remove it altogether if you like.

You can make similar changes to the captions for other record types if
you wish.

There is no harm in experimenting. The worst that can happen is that
you will not get the results you want. You can return to the default
settings for all captions at any time, by pressing the Restore
Defaults button.

title: The Citation List Pane
text:
Property Box

The Citation List Pane

Citation List Pane (marked in red) positioned at the bottom of the
Property Box

You open or close the Property Box's Citation List pane by
clicking on the Show Sources button on the Property Box toolbar. By default, the
Citation List pane has a yellow background, to make it easily
distinguishable from the rest of the Property Box. It is normally
displayed at the bottom of the Property Box, but this is
configurable. If you do not have a large screen, you can also
specify that you want the Citation List pane to open as a separate
window, if you prefer (see the Property
Box tab of Preferences).

If the Citation List pane is too small, click-and-drag on Gripper
Bars, in the area separating the Citation List pane from the rest
of the Property Box, to re-size it. Gripper bars can be horizontal or
vertical. The horizontal ones look like this: .

The Citation List pane has one field ('Sources for') and a list of
Source Citations:

Sources For
This lists all the fields in the record which contain data, and
for which a source can be cited. Some subfields cannot be given
separate source citations. For example, a single source citation
is used for both the place and date of birth. If the source
citation only applies to one of these, this fact should be noted
in the Note field.

Citation List
This list is a list of source citations associated with the
currently selected item in the Sources
For field above. The list has 2 columns: Citation,
and Source Rec. By default, the Citation column
displays the Footnote text for the citation, but this is
configurable (see below). The kind of text used is displayed
after the word 'Citation' in the column heading. The record id of
the Source record associated with the citation, is shown in the Source
Rec column.

Below the Citation List is the Citation List toolbar, which has the
following toolbar commands:

Add Citation

Add source citation. By default, clicking on this button
will result in a menu being displayed with these options:

Cite Existing Source

Add New Generic Source

Add New Free Form Source

Add New Templated Source

However, it is also possible to configure the toolbar to not
display a menu, and instead to always execute the first
option: Cite Existing Source. This is because the
Source Selector Dialog, which is displayed when you take
that option, has a New button, which
can be used to add a new generic, free form, or templated source.
The option is called Enable 'Add Citation' Menu (ticked
by default) on the Property
Box tab of Preferences.

When a new Source is created, or an existing source is cited, full
details of both the Source record and the citation link to it, are
displayed in the Citation Window.

To learn about the difference between generic, free form and
templated Source records, see Sources
and Source Templates.

Edit Source Citation

Displays the selected source citation in the Citation
Window. Double-clicking on a source citation does the
same thing.

Note: Once you have double-clicked on a source citation, the
Citation Window will not only open to display that source
citation, but the window will become pinned, meaning
that it will stay in sync with the selection in the Citation List
pane. As the selection changes, the Citation Window will
update itself appropriately.

Copy Citation

Requires a selection in the Citation
List. Copies the citation to the source clipboard.
The source clipboard is a separate clipboard, different from the
usual Windows clipboard, managed internally by Family
Historian. This means that if you copy something else
(something other than a citation), to the usual Windows clipboard,
the copy will not affect the source clipboard, so you will still
be able to paste a previously copied citation.

Paste Citation

Requires that a citation should previously have been copied to
the Source clipboard. Pastes the citation into the Citation
List.

Delete Citation

Deletes a selected citation.

Show Media

Shows media linked to the source citation in the Media tab of
the Citation Window.

Show Media

Displays a menu with the following menu commands:

View Media in Workspace Media Window
If the selected source citation has associated media, this
will cause them to be displayed in the Media
Window.
Open Media in Editor/Player
If the selected source citation has associated media, a menu
will be displayed with each item listed. Selecting one
of the media items causes it to be displayed in an external
application - an editor or player.
Display Citation As...
Affects how citations are displayed in the first column of
the Citation List. The options are Footnote, Short
