Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

title: Property Box: Media Tab
text:
Property Box

Property Box: Media Tab

This tab is used for Individual,
Family, Source,
Place and Address
records. It shows all pictures and other media items (sounds, videos,
etc) associated with the current record. Or rather, it shows such items
if they are linked to the current record as a whole. It does not
show pictures and other media items which are associated with events and
attributes belonging to an Individual or Family record, for
example. To view these, you need to switch to the Facts
tab (there is a toolbar button on that tab for viewing media for
each event or attribute).

Pictures and other media items are stored in Family Historian as Media
records. So the list of media items that you can see in the top part of
the Media tab is a list of linked Media records. The list shows the
format of each item, its date (if supplied) and, if the Property Box is
showing details for an Individual record, the Individual's age at that
date. This is most interesting when the media item is a picture. You can
sort the list by clicking on the column headers.

The list also shows the preference order for the linked media objects.
Preference values are used to determine which pictures appear in
diagrams. Typically, the picture with highest preference (preference
value = 1) is used in diagrams and reports and other contexts. There are
toolbar buttons and to raise or lower the
preference values.

The final column is the 'Flags' column. This can display the following
icons:

Excluded from diagrams and the Focus
Window.

Excluded from reports, books, web-pages and pages for family
tree CDs/DVDs.

Use the associated note (if any) as the caption for this
picture.

Beneath the list of media items is a toolbar. The toolbar buttons have
the following functions:

Item
Description

Add a picture or other media item - or link to an existing Media
record. There is no limit to the number of pictures or other media
items that a person can have.

If you have copied an image to the clipboard, you can also add it
using the Paste Copied Image command.

Media items that are added to the project in this way, are
automatically linked to the current record.

Opens the Edit
Media Item dialog. Using this dialog you can edit details
relating to the picture or other type of media item. In the case
of pictures, you can also link a person to their face in the
picture. See How to Link Individuals to Their Faces in
Pictures.

Delete or unlink a Media record. You will be asked which you
wish to do.

Give this media item a higher preference for the current record.
See the discussion of preferences above.

Give this media item a lower preference for the current record.
See the discussion of preferences above.

Switch between showing thumbnails or one picture at a
time. Image alternates appropriately.

Switch between showing whole pictures or close-ups of the
current person's face - if there is a link to a face (or other
area) within the picture.

Opens the given media item in a 3rd party application - the one
specified on your computer as the default application for viewing
or editing files of this type. For a picture, this will usually
mean opening a picture editor to view it. For a sound file, this
is likely to mean opening an application to play it. For a video,
this will usually mean opening a video-player application to view
it. For a document, it will usually mean opening it for viewing
and/or editing in a word-processor. If no application opens for a
given media type, when you click on this command, you may need to
configure your PC to specify a default application for the file
type in question.

Displays a dropdown menu with the following options:

display pictures (or other media) of the current Individual
(or other record type) in the Media Window

display pictures (or other media) linked to
the current Individual (or other record type) in the Media
Window

If you choose the latter option you will be prompted to choose
the type of pictures (or other media) to include. Options,
for an Individual record, include pictures (and other media)
linked to

The record itself

Associated Events/Facts

Associated Places

Associated Sources & Source Citations

With Individual records you can additionally choose to apply
all of the above options not just to the Individual record
itself, but also to all spouse Family records associated with
the Individual record.

Display the Media record's details in the Property Box. You can
subsequently click on the Go Back
button on the Property
Box main toolbar, to go back to the previous record.

Click-and-drag on a horizontal gripper bar below the toolbar, to resize the list and increase or
decrease the space available for pictures.

title: Names & Titles Dialog
text:
Property Box

Names & Titles Dialog

Names & Titles Dialog

The Names & Titles Dialog is a floating
window and satellite of the Property Box. That is
to say, it stays in sync with the current record in the Property Box and
closes when the Property Box closes, or if the Property Box displays a
record which is not an Individual record.

To open the Names & Titles dialog, click on the 'more...'
link to the right of the Name field, in the Main
tab of the Property Box, when viewing an Individual record.

The Names & Titles Dialog allows additional names and titles to be
entered for an Individual. Each name can be associated with a name
prefix, suffix, nickname and/or "Given Name Used". Don't confuse a
title with a name prefix. "Dr" would count in this context as a name
prefix. "Lord Beaconsfield" would count as a title.

You can't add names in the Facts
tab of the Property Box, but you can add (or edit or delete)
titles there. If you add a title here in the Names & Titles Dialog,
it will show up in the Facts tab, and vice versa. If you want to
associate a title with dates and/or other details, such as a note, you
can only do this in the Facts tab.

Names and Surnames

When you enter a person's name that consists of more than one word,
Family Historian will always assume that the last name is the surname,
unless you explicitly indicate otherwise by using slash characters to
mark the surname. Suppose, for example, that Elizabeth Powell Smith's
surname is 'Powell Smith'. If you entered her name simply as "Elizabeth
Powell Smith", Family Historian would assume that 'Smith' was the
surname. To mark her surname correctly you would need to put slashes
round 'Powell Smith' like this: "Elizabeth /Powell Smith/". If the name
had been hyphenated however (as 'Powell-Smith') there would have been no
need for slashes as Family Historian would have treated the hyphenated
name 'Powell-Smith' as the last name, and hence the surname.

In some languages, the surname may not necessarily appear at the end of
the name. For example, "Mao Tse-Tung" should be entered as "/Mao/
Tse-Tung" because 'Mao' is the surname. If you only enter only one word
as the name (e.g. 'Jane') Family Historian will, by default, assume that
it is not the surname and will automatically add two slash
characters on the end of the name to reflect this ("Jane //"). If
actually 'Jane' was the surname, and that's the only name you had, you
would need to enter it as "/Jane/" to make this clear. Of course,
the alternative is to use a question mark or something similar, to mark
the unknown name part - for example, "Jane ?" or "? Jane".

Why does Family Historian need to know which part of the name is the
surname? It needs to know this so that it can provide a number of
different services, such as automatic capitalization of surnames,
surname-first ordering, search-by-surname, and more.

When viewing names in Name fields, for editing purposes, Family
Historian can, if you wish, always put slashes round the surname, to
make it clear which part of the name is the surname. However, for
aesthetic reasons, users may prefer it if Family Historian keeps the use
of slashes to a minimum, and only puts slashes round the surname when
this is needed for clarity - that is, if the surname is not the last
name, or if there is only one word in the name. See the Show
Surnames Between Slashes option in Preferences: Property Box
tab for options relating to this.

Source Citations

You can add, edit or delete source citations for names and titles, in
the Property Box Citation
List Pane, just as you would for any field displayed in the
Property Box. If the Citation List Pane is open, it will always
display source citations for the current name or title field in the
Names & Titles Dialog.

Fields

The fields in the Names & Titles Dialog are:

Primary Name
Your preferred name for the person. Put slashes round the
surname - as in "John /Smith/". If you don't know the surname, put
slashes at the end - as in "John //". If you only know the
surname, put slashes round that - as in "/Smith/".

Name Prefix
e.g. 'Dr'

Name Suffix

e.g. 'Jr."

Nickname
The person's nickname.

Given Name Used

The Given Name Used field is for cases where the name
a person was known by was one of their names, but not the first.
For example, even before she was baptised, her parents may
always have intended that Jean Clare Smith should be called
“Clare” say - or perhaps even “Jean Clare”. In the first case
you would enter "Clare" as the given name used. In the second,
you would enter "Jean Clare". If she was always known as "Jean"
there is no need to enter this in the Given Name Used
field, and we recommend that you don't. If no name is specified
as the given name used, Family Historian will assume that it is
the first given name.

Add

Add an alternate name or a title.

Edit
Edit the name or title.

Delete
Delete an alternate name or title. You can blank the contents of
the Primary Name, but you can't delete it.

Move Up/Down
You can change the order of names with respect to other names.
You can also change the order of titles with respect to other
titles. But you cannot change the order of names with respect to
titles, or vice versa.

Make Primary
This command can only be used with names. Makes the name the
primary name. The existing primary name is not deleted. It is
merely demoted to the status of alternate name.

title: Property Box: Notes Tab
text:
Property Box

Property Box: Notes Tab

This tab is used for Individual,
Family, Source,
Repository, Media
and Place records.

The top part of the tab shows a list of all the notes associated with
the current record. There are 5 different types of note, all of which
except fact notes, can be added by clicking on the Add Note
button on the toolbar.
When you add a note, the note is created immediately as an empty
note. You can then type in the details. By default, new
notes are displayed in the Note Window
(this is an option in Preferences).
If you change your mind after creating a new note, and want to
remove it, click Undo on the Edit menu.

The 5 types of note that can be displayed in the Notes tab are these:

'Local notes' that apply to the current record only
The most common kind of note. These are normally labelled
as "Note about..." followed by the record name.

Shared Note for a Couple
Only applicable when the current
record is an Individual. If you want to add a note for a given
Individual, but the note applies equally to his or her spouse, you
should add it as a Shared Note
for a Couple. The note will appear in the notes list for
both spouses.

Shared Note Record
If you want to add a note that is applicable to more than one
record (and not just to two spouses), you should add a link to a
Note record. This can be to an
existing Note record, or to a new one (click the New
button in the Select Note Record dialog, to create a new
one). Any number of records, of different types, can all be linked
to the same Note record.

Shared Research Note
A Research Note is a note that is separate from all other
notes. It is a note you make for your own research purposes
only (see Research Note
for more details). Research notes are stored as
records. You can link to them from any number of other
records, of different types. This can be a link to an
existing Research Note record, or to a new one (click the New
button in the Select Research Note Record dialog, to create a new
one).

Fact Note
Fact notes are notes associated with facts (see the Facts
tab). Unlike all the other notes listed above, Fact notes
cannot be added by clicking on the Add Note
button. They can only be added on the Facts
tab of the Property Box (and are only applicable to
Individual and Family records). But although they cannot be
added on the Notes tab, they can nevertheless optionally be viewed
in the Notes tab.

Click-and-drag on a horizontal gripper bar below the toolbar, to resize the list and increase or
decrease the space available for notes.

Each note can be viewed and edited in the edit box in the bottom half
of the Notes tab. You can also double-click on the edit box, or
click the long thin vertical button to the right of the edit box, to
open the note in the Note Window, if you
wish.

The Toolbar

The toolbar buttons have the following functions:

Item
Description

Add a note. A dropdown menu offers you a choice of the
kind of note to create (see above).

Delete the selected note (if a local note, fact
note, or Shared Note for a Couple). If the
note is a Shared Note Record or a Shared Research Note, only the
link from this record to the shared note will be deleted. If
you want to delete the actual Note record or Research Note, you
can do so in the Records Window.

These buttons are used for re-ordering notes. Not all
notes can be re-ordered.

Enable or disable the display of fact notes - that
is, notes attached to facts which are associated with the current
record. These notes can also be viewed in the Facts tab of
the Property Box.

If the currently selected note is a Shared Note Record or a
Shared Research Note, this Go To button will
cause the linked record to be viewed in the Property Box. If
the note is a Shared Note for a Couple, clicking this button will
switch to viewing the note in the context of the other
spouse. If the note is a fact note, clicking this
button will switch to the Facts tab, to select and view the fact
in question.

After clicking the Go To button, you can return to
where you had been by clicking the Go Back button on the
main Property Box toolbar.

title: Select Relationship Type Dialog
breadcrumb: Property Box: Main Tab for Individual Records
text:
Property Box: Main Tab
for Individual Records

Select Relationship Type

Select Relationship Type

This dialog allows you to specify the relationship between a child and
his or her parents. Although you can if you wish specify explicitly that
a child's relationship to his or her parents is 'birth', we do not
recommend that you do so ordinarily as this will add considerable work
for little benefit. Instead, we recommend that you leave the
relationship field blank for all children if they are birth children. If
the relationship type is not specified, it will be taken to be birth by
default in any case. You should only specify explicitly that a child's
relationship is 'birth' if you have some specific reason to do so - e.g.
to emphasize the nature of the relationship, in circumstances in which
it might otherwise be doubted.

Where possible, you are recommended to not use the option Specify
relationship to each parent separately unless you need
to. Note that two values ('Ilegitimate' and 'LDS Sealing') can only be
used in relation to both parents jointly, not separately.

The possible values and their meanings are:

Adopted
Child was adopted

Birth
Birth child (rarely used - see note above).

De Facto

Use De Facto as a catch-all if none of the other
options apply. It is useful if, for example, a child has been
accepted by the world as a person's son or daughter, even if in
fact they aren't that person's genetic offspring. For example,
through your research you may be satisfied that a given boy is
not the birth child of a given man X. But X, and everyone else -
even possibly including the child's mother - may all wrongly
believe that the boy was X's son, and the child may have been
brought up as X's son, and lived and died believing that he was
X's son. None of the other options apply. The child is not
adopted, fostered, step or birth; nor is he X's illegitimate
son. So what is their relationship? De Facto covers it
best.

Foster
Child was fostered

Illegitimate

It is recommended that this relationship type is only used
with respect to individuals who lived at a time when the concept
of 'illegitimacy' was used, viewed as important, and carried a
social stigma; and where the fact that they were viewed as
'illegitimate' had significance for the lives of the individuals
in question. It is not intended for use with modern-day children
who happen to be born out of wedlock.

This relationship type can only be applied with respect to
both parents.

LDS Sealing

This relationship type is specific to the LDS Church (Church
of Latter Day Saints) who originally devised the GEDCOM
format.

This relationship type can only be applied with respect to
both parents.

Step
A step-child.

title: Property Box: Text from Source Tab
text:
Property Box

Property Box: Text from Source Tab

The Text tab is only used with Source
records. It allows you to add and edit the text of Text from Source
for a Source record. If you want to edit the text in the Note
Window, double-click on the text, or click on the grey bar just
just to the right of the vertical scrollbar.

When you click on the Add Text from Source
button on the toolbar,you will be given the opportunity to select from a
number of Text from Source autotexts, that will form the
first draft of the new field. See Autotext
to learn more.

title: The Query Window
text:
Workspace Windows

The Query Window

The Query Window (marked in red)

the Purpose of the Query Window

The Query Window is used for two purposes:

for running and maintaining queries

for viewing and maintaining smart
folders

These roles overlap to an extent because smart folders contain, or can
contain, queries. So maintaining smart folders may also involve
maintaining the queries contained within them.

Smart Folders

Whereas the output of a query can only be viewed in the Query Window,
the same is not true of most smart folders. Smart folders can also
be viewed in the Records Window, or in
record selector dialogs. However, there are some smart folders
(smart folders that are related to non-record data items like source
citations, facts, or witnesses) which can
only be viewed in the Query Window.

Click on the Smart Folder icon on the Query
Window toolbar to open the Smart Folder Pane.

The rest of this page, and the pages it links to, describe the primary
use of the Query Window, which is for running and maintaining queries.
See Smart Folders to learn more
about smart folders generally. To learn about using the Query
Window to view and maintain smart folders, see Smart
Folders in the Query Window.

Queries

A query is a reusable set of
instructions for extracting information from a Family Historian project.
The information returned by a query is called a result
set, and it is laid out in tabular form, in a grid of
rows and columns. There are 15 types of query - one for each of the 12
record types (excluding the header record), one for facts (events or
attributes), one for source citations, and one for witnesses (shared
events). If the query is an Individual
query, each row returned, and displayed in the result set, will
correspond to an Individual record. If it is a Source
query, each row will correspond to a Source record. With fact
queries, each row corresponds to a fact. With source citation
queries, each row corresponds to a source citation. And with
witness queries, each row corresponds to an instance of a person having
a role as a witness (non-principal participant) in an event.
An example might be a person being a best man at a wedding, or a person
being the beneficiary of a will.

To open the Query Window, click on the Query
button on the main
application toolbar and select the query you want to run from the
dropdown menu that appears. You can also open the Query Window
without running a query by choosing the Query Window command
(the first item on the dropdown menu). You can run any query from
within the Query Window itself if you want to. To do this, make
sure that your required query is selected in the query toolbar at the top of the Query Window, and
click the Run button to run
it. When you run a query, you may be required to make choices and
selections. Some queries prompt you to supply information or make
choices when you run them. Some do not. Either way, the
results will be displayed in The
Result Set Tab.

If you want to create a new query, click on the Query
button on the main
application toolbar and choose New Custom Query.
If the Query Window is already open, you can also create a new query by
clicking on the Menu button on the query toolbar and choosing New Custom Query
from the dropdown menu that appears.

When Family Historian is installed, it comes with a set of queries
ready for use. These are called standard
queries. You cannot delete or alter standard queries
significantly. If you want to modify an existing standard query (which
is the best way to start learning how to work with queries), you must
copy them as custom queries, and then
modify the copy. One way to copy a query is to use the Save
As Custom Query command, which is available from the Menu
button
on the query toolbar.
Another way is to use the Clone button in
the Manage Queries window. A custom query is any query that
you create yourself. You can have any number of custom queries, and you
can change or delete them, as you like. All queries, custom or
standard, are available to be used with all Family Historian projects.
Queries are not stored in Family Historian projects - they are managed
separately.

As we have already seen, the Query Window has its own Query Toolbar. There is also a small Query Menu, which is available from the Menu
button
on the toolbar.

When constructing or modifying a query, here are some of the decisions
you will need to make, and where to go to make them:

Decision
Where Specified

What records do I want?
The
Filters Tab

What information do I want to display about each record?
The
Columns Tab

In what order do I want the rows to be displayed?
The
Columns Tab

What order do I want the columns to
appear in?
The
Columns Tab

What headings do I want for each column?
The
Columns Tab

How wide do I want each column to be?
The
Result Set Tab

If you want to print a query as a report, you also have to decide:

Decision
Where Specified

What title(s) do I want for the printed report?
The
General Tab

Do I want the report to appear in
Portrait or Landscape mode?
The
General Tab

If the report is too wide to fit across a single page width,
what do I want to happen about the overflowing columns?
The
General Tab

The Query Window has 4 tabs:

The
General Tab
For specifying general features about the query, such as the
query type, a description, print details, and so on.

The
Columns Tab
Allows you to select the columns you wish to appear in the
'Result Set'. Can also specify column headings and sort order.

The
Filters Tab
Allows you to specify which rows you
wish to appear in the Result Set by creating a set of filters.

The
Result Set Tab
A 'Result Set' is the table of data that is displayed as a
result of running a query. The Result Set tab displays the result
set.

title: Query Window: Columns Tab
text:
Query Window

Query Window: Columns Tab

Query Window: Columns Tab

This tab allows you to specify the columns that you wish to see
displayed in the result set. Columns typically display the value of a
field (like Birth Date say); but they can also display the value
returned by a function (more on this later). The list of
possible fields (given the type of the Query) are displayed in the list
on the left-hand side. When creating or editing a custom query, select
one of the fields listed here, and click the Add
Column > button (or just double-click on it) to add the
field to the Columns List (on the right-hand side). See below for more
information.

Components of the Columns Tab - the Left-Hand Side

Fields Etc

This panel displays all the possible fields that can be added,
given the type of the query. Click on the expansion button
(boxes with a '+' or '-' in them) to show or hide field
‘branches’ (subfields). Some fields are grouped into
categories,represented by folder icons.

When creating or editing a custom query, select a field in the
Fields Etc list and click on the button to the right of it Add Column > to add it to the Columns
List.

As well as being able to add fields as columns, it is also
possible to add values of other kinds, such as calculated values
(hence the 'etc' in "Fields Etc"). The most useful
examples of this are grouped in the same listing under ''Common
Functions'. Select any item in that branch and click Add Column > to add it to the Columns
List. Within that area, calculated values giving the
number of items in various categories, are grouped under
'Counts'.

In all cases, the items available will vary depending on the
query type.

The Information Panel
This panel, which appears immediately below the Fields Etc list,
displays information about the item selected in the list.

Displays the Fields Etc Dropdown Menu - see below.

The Fields Etc Dropdown Menu

Show Linked Records in List
Show (or hide) linked records. For example, if viewing
fields for an Individual record and you expand the 'Family as
Child' field to view its subfields, do you want to see Family
record fields listed here too?

Show Qualifiers in List
Show (or hide) field qualifiers.
For example, when you expand a date field, do you want to see a
list of qualifiers (:DAY, :DAY_OF_WEEK, :MONTH_NUMBER, etc) which
can be used with dates?

Show Description in Box
Do you wish to see a description of the currently selected list
item, in the box below the Fields Etc list?

Show Expression in Box
... or would you rather see the expression that can be used to
reference the data?

Show Both in Box
... or would you like to see both?

Components of the Columns Tab - the Right-Hand Side

The Columns List

The Columns List lists the columns that will appear in your
result set when you run the query (except that you can have
hidden columns - these are described in more detail below).

The Columns List itself has four columns. These are:

Heading

Sort

Type

Align

You can re-size columns in the Column List by clicking on the
line between the column headings, and dragging left or right.

You can also add 'Expression' as an additional column, if you
wish, by clicking "Show Expressions" on the dropdown menu that
appears when you click on the 'cog' icon in the toolbar below
the Columns listing.

Deletes the currently selected row(s) in the Columns List above.

For re-ordering rows in the column list. Moves the selected row
up one.

For re-ordering rows in the column list. Moves the selected row
down one.

'Cog' menu. Click this button to display a menu with one
or more of the following commands:

Enable Column

Disable Column

Add Default Columns

Show Expressions

The menu commands do the following:

Enable Column: Only available when a disabled
column is selected. Re-enables the column.

Disable Column: Only available when an enabled
column is selected. Disables the column

Add Default Columns: When you create a new
query you can add default columns. They can also be added
at any time using this menu command. You will be asked if
you want the default columns to replace the existing
columns. If you choose 'No', the new columns will be
appended. It is a good idea to check that you haven't
accidentally added an duplicates if you choose the 'append'
option. If you find any, you can of course just delete
them. To learn more about default columns, see the discussion
in New
Query Dialog.

Show Expressions: Tick this menu command if
you want expressions to display as an addition column in the
Columns list.

Tip: You can see the same menu at any time by
right-clicking on any item in the Columns list, or by
right-clicking on the background of the Columns list.

Heading
This is the text that will appear as a column heading in the
result set when you run the query, or in your printed report, if
you print it. If you add an entry to the list by inserting it from
the Fields Etc list on the left-hand side of the window, a default
heading will be supplied, as well as an expression. You
will usually want to change the default heading, to make it more
meaningful. You may also want to edit the expression.

Expression

The expression represents the data that you wish to
appear in the result set column. There are two kinds of
expressions that can be used:

Data References - which
identify fields.

Functions - which compute
values

When you create or edit a custom query, you can write your own
data references if you want to, but it's easier to let Family
Historian do it for you. To do that, simply select the field you
want from the Fields Etc list on the left- hand side of the
window, and click Add Column >
to insert it as a column. Advanced and technically-minded users
may wish to look at Understanding Data References for more
information on data references.

Various examples of expressions that use functions, can be
found listed under 'Common Functions' (or under 'Counts' within
that) in the Fields Etc list. To find out what each one
does, select it, and view the description for it in the box
below the list.

The easiest way to add function expressions is from the 'Common
Functions' branch. Another approach is to find a sample
query that uses the function you want, and copy the relevant
expression from that query. There are many more
functions that can be used, however. And many functions
can be configured to behave differently depending on supplied
parameters. Advanced and technically-minded users who wish
to understand more about how to use functions, should see Understanding Functions for more
information.

Tip: A quick way to access all the available
documentation on functions, is to click on the 'cog' menu, in
the query
toolbar, and then click "Query Window Help", and finally
"Functions by Category".

Tip: A quick way to copy text is to select it and
press Ctrl-C. Ctrl-V can
then be used to paste it where you want it. These
key-combinations work in the vast majority of windows and dialog
boxes in Windows.

Sort
You can sort on as many columns as you wish - either ascending
or descending. See next paragraph for information about how to
control the order in which sorts are applied.

Type
The possible column types are:

Normal

Hidden

Buddy

Group By

Hidden columns do not appear in the result set, or in
printed reports. You rarely need to make columns hidden, but it
is occasionally useful, as a way of getting the exact kind of
sort you want. Family Historian will always apply sorts in
column order precedence, from left-to-right. If you need to
create a query in which the order of precedence of sorts, does
not match the display order of the result set columns, you can
do it by making all the sort columns hidden, and ordering them
however you like. Then add all the visible columns you need, in
the display order you want, including duplicate columns (i.e.
duplicates of a hidden column) where necessary.

Buddy columns are also hidden and also do not appear
in the Result Set, or in printed reports. They are used as
a means to associate a cell with a data item (to make it
'data-linked') so that if the user double-clicks on the cell, or
right-clicks on it to view a context menu, he or she will be
able to view the underlying data item in the Property
Box.or, in some cases, in the Note
Window. Buddy columns provide the data-linking for
the immediately preceding column in the query. In order
for a buddy column to have any effect, it must contain a
data-reference or an expression which returns a reference to a
data item. It must have an immediately preceding column,
and that column must not itself be hidden or a buddy column, and
it must not contain a data-reference or an expression which
returns a reference to a data item. See the "Individual
Timeline" query for an example of a query that uses a buddy
column.

Within an ordinary query group by columns are
permitted but discouraged. In the context of an ordinary
query, they behave exactly like hidden columns.
Although they add no benefit to an ordinary query, because they
don't do anything that you can't do with a hidden column, 'group
by' columns, have an essential role to play within
query-type smart
folders. The use of 'group by' columns within
this type of smart folder is described in the 'Grouping' section
within Create
and Edit Folder Sets in Design Mode.

A Normal column is any column that isn't either a
hidden or buddy column, or a 'group by' column.

Align
The Align field is only available for columns where the type is
'Normal' (that is, for columns which are not hidden). It can be
used to specify that a column should be left-aligned (the
default), centred, or right-aligned.

Add Column

Click on this button to add a new entry to the list (i.e. to
add a new column to the result set), using the values supplied.
The new entry will be added to the bottom of the list, but you
can re-order the list if you wish to using the arrow buttons. If
the data in the Expression field is not a valid
expression (i.e. a data reference or a function), the add will
fail and an error message will be displayed.

Notice that there are two Add Column
buttons: this one, for adding a new column from the values
entered in the form, and the Add Column
> button to the right of the Fields Etc list, which
is used for adding columns directly from that list.

Tip: You can use the Add
Column button effectively as a way of duplicating an
existing column. Just select the column in the Columns
list and then click the Add Column
button to add a second instance. Of course, usually, you
will want to modify it in some way, or there wouldn't be much
point in having it.

Apply Changes
When you select a column in the Columns list, the various values
for that column will be displayed in the fields below the Columns
list. If you make any changes to these values, the Apply
Changes and Discard Changes
buttons will become ungreyed. Click the Apply
Changes button to apply your changes to the currently
selected column in the Columns list. If the data in the Expression
field is not a valid expression (i.e. a data reference or a
function), the update will fail.

Discard Changes
As just noted, when you select a column in the Columns list, the
various values for that column will be displayed in the fields
below the Columns list. If you make any changes to these
values, the Apply Changes and Discard Changes buttons will become
ungreyed. Click the Discard
Changes button to discard your changes and revert to the
values currently stored with the selected item in the Columns
list.

Disabling and Re-Enabling Columns

As discussed above, you can disable any column in a custom query by
right-clicking on it, and selecting Disable Column from the
dropdown menu that appears. The line will then display with greyed
text, to show that it is disabled. To re-enable it, right-click on
it again, and select Enable Column from the dropdown menu
that appears. You can also disable or enable columns using the cog
menu on the toolbar below the columns list.

title: Query Window: Filters Tab
text:
Query Window

Query Window: Filters Tab

Query Window: Filters Tab

The Filters tab displays a list of filters used in the current query
(if any). If the query is a custom query and not read-only,
filters can be added, edited or deleted on this tab.

All queries have a domain. This is the complete set of records or
data items, that the query applies to. For example, if the query
is a Media record query, the domain is the set of all Media records in
the current project. If the query is a source citation query, the
domain is the set of all source citations in the current project.

Filters are used to specify which records or data items should appear
in rows in the result set. The records or data items that do
appear are 'filtered-in'. The ones that do not appear are
'filtered-out'.

Filters can be positive or negative. For example, you could use a
'Relationships' filter to find (that is, filter in) anyone who is an
ancestor of given person, or to find anyone who is not an
ancestor of the given person.

Filters can be combined in any way you like. For example, if you
have 3 filters, you can combine them by specifying that a record or data
item must match all of the filters to be filtered-in.
Alternatively, you could instead specify that a record or data item only
has to match any of the filters (i.e. one or more) to be
filtered-in. You might want to combine filters in much more
complicated ways. We will see shortly how you can do that.

Please note: In this documentation, the terms 'group' and
'subgroup' (as applied to filters) are interchangeable. The term
subgroup is typically used in reference to 'group', to emphasize that
the subgroup itself belongs to a higher-level group or subgroup. But any
group is also a subgroup and vice versa.

After filtering has been performed, the filtered-in records or data
items are displayed in the Result
Set tab of the Query Window. If there are no filters, all
records or data items in the domain will be displayed in the Result Set tab.

Filter Types

There are 4 types of filter, each of which has its own the tab at the
bottom of the Filters tab window. These are...

General
filters (General Filter tab)

General filters use an expression - that is,
either a data reference (see Understanding Data References) or a function (see
Understanding
Functions) - and compare its value against a value specified in
the filter. Expressions can be as complex as you like. If
you want to create complex and/or conditions, for example, you can do
this with expressions. However there is usually no need to do this
because all such groupings can also be achieved by combing filters into
groups - and that is usually a clearer and easier approach.

Queries of all types support general
filters.

Relationships filters (Relationships Filter
tab)

Relationship filters are used to check
relationship conditions - such as whether a given Individual is a
relative of a specified type of anyone who is already in the result set.

Relationship filters are only supported for
Individual queries. This tab will only be present with Individual
queries.

List
filters (List Filter tab)

List filters are a convenient way of
checking membership of Named Lists (see How to Use Named Lists).

List filters are only supported for
record-type queries. This tab will not display if the query is a
non-record type (facts, source citations or witnesses).

Subgroup
filters (Subgroup Filter tab)

Subgroup filters are a convenient way of
grouping other filters together.

Queries of all types support subgroup
filters.

All editing of filters can only be done with custom queries and only if
they are not marked as read-only. Filters can be added using the Add Filter button in the bottom right corner of
the Query Window. When you add a filter, you will be prompted to choose
how the new filter should be combined with existing filters (see Combining
Top-Level Filters, and Complex Combinations of Filters
below). Filters can be deleted by clicking on the the Delete
button ,
or re-ordered by clicking on the Move Up and Move Down
buttons , at the bottom-left corner of the filter
list. When you select a filter, the filter details will be
displayed in the tabs and fields below the filter list. If you
make any changes, the Apply Changes and Discard Changes buttons will become
activated. Click the Apply Changes
button to apply your changes to the currently selected filter. Click the
Discard Changes button to set values to
revert back to the values of the selected item.

Disabling and Re-Enabling Row Filters

Sometimes, if filters do not produce the results you expected, it can
be helpful to try disabling one or more lines, to see what effect this
has. You can disable any row filter in a custom query by
right-clicking on it, and selecting Disable Filter from the
dropdown menu that appears. The line will then display with greyed
text, to show that it is disabled. To re-enable it, right-click on
it again, and select Enable Filter from the dropdown menu
that appears.

If you disable a subgroup filter, the entire branch will be disabled.

Combining Top-Level Filters

If the list of filters does not contain any subgroups, all of the
filters are top-level filters - as in the example
above. The list of top-level filters itself constitutes a
group. The filters in any group, including the top-level group,
can be combined in two ways. You can specify that the group as a
whole matches if and only if all filters in the group
match. Or you can specify that the group as a whole matches if and
only if any (that is, one or more) filters in the group
match. Users who are used to logical syntax should see the former as
combining filters using 'AND', and should see the latter as combining
filters using 'OR'. To specify the former, right-click on the
background of the filters list and click on "Top-level group is matched
if all members match ('AND')". To specify the latter, right-click
on the background of the filters list and click on "Top-Level group is
matched if any members match ('OR')". The same options can
also be accessed from the cog menu, on the toolbar below the filter
list.

If you choose "Top-level group is matched if all members match
('AND')", all top-level filters will be displayed in blue
text, linked with the word 'AND' in the filter list. If
you choose "Top-level group is matched if any members match ('OR')", all
top-level filters will be displayed in green
text, linked with the word 'OR' in the filter list.

Complex Combinations of Filters

Users who are familiar with propositional calculus will be used to the
idea that propositions can be combined using brackets and 'AND' or 'OR'
clauses. Exactly the same thing can be done by using combinations
of groups and subgroups, each of which can be an 'AND' group or an 'OR'
group. The best way to understand this is through an
example. The "Same Sex Relationships (Individuals)" query finds
everyone who has one or more recorded same sex relationships. It
assumes that no-one in the domain has had more than 4
relationships. Figure 2 below shows what the filters list looks
like in the Filters tab, for this query.

Figure 2. Filters list in Same Sex Relationships (Individuals)
Query

Using brackets instead of tree branches and subgroups, one could write
this as follows:

((person is male AND (spouse 1 is male
OR spouse 2 is male OR spouse 3 is male OR spouse 4 is male)) OR
((person is female AND (spouse 1 is female OR spouse 2 is female OR
spouse 3 is female OR spouse 4 is female))

Again, the green text are filters that belong to an 'OR' group, and the
blue text are filters that belong to an 'AND' group. As this
example illustrates, you can have groups of different types, nested
inside one another.

Tip: Branches in the filters list can be hidden or
expanded, by clicking on the little white boxes at the start of each
branching line. Clicking these boxes has no effect on the action of
filters but it can be convenient to hide branches from time to time, to
help get a better understanding of what the filters do. By
temporarily hiding some of the detail, you can get a simplified view
which may make the overall purpose of the filters easier to understand.

Filter MENU OPTIONS

The following filter menu options can be accessed by clicking on the
cog menu, on the toolbar below the filters list. The options that
are available will depend on whether a filter is selected, and if so, on
the type of the filter selected. The same menu options can also be
accessed by right-clicking on the background of the filter list, or by
right-clicking on any filter in the list.

With the sole exception of the "Always Show Expressions" menu command,
all of the menu commands will always be greyed unless, at a minimum, the
current query is a custom query. So to explore and try out the
menu commands, you should create a custom query and select that as the
current query. One good option is to make a copy of an existing
query (e.g. use the Clone button on the
Manage Queries window).

Menu
Description

Clone Filter

Makes a copy of the selected filter.

Clone Filter Branch
Makes a copy of the entire branch of the selected subgroup
filter (i.e. entire subgroup, and all contained subgroups).

Disable Filter

Disables the selected filter. Disabled filters are
displayed in grey text, prefixed with "*** DISABLED:".

Disable Subgroup

Disables a selected subgroup filter. Disables the entire
branch. Disabled subgroups are displayed in grey text,
prefixed with "*** DISABLED:", and all filters belonging to that
branch are displayed in grey text.

Enable Filter

Re-enables a selected disabled filter.

Enable Subgroup

Re-enables a selected subgroup filter. This re-enables the
entire branch.

Delete Filter

Deletes the selected filter

Subgroup options

Options are

Matches if all members match ('AND')

If ticked, all members must match for the subgroup as a whole
to be deemed to match. The text of filters in the
subgroup will display in blue,
and all filters will be linked with 'AND'.

Matches if any members match ('OR')

If ticked, subgroup as a whole to be deemed to match if any
members of the subgroup match. The text of filters in
the subgroup will display in green,
and all filters will be linked with 'OR'.

Move Up

Moves the selected filter (including subgroup files) up.
When you move a subgroup filter, the entire branch moves.
See also drag-and-drop below.

Move Down

Moves the selected filter (including subgroup files) down.
When you move a subgroup filter, the entire branch moves.
See also drag-and-drop below.

Move into New Group

Creates a new subgroup and moves the selected filter into this
group. You will be prompted to choose the required subgroup
option ('AND' or 'OR').

Move into Group Above

Moves the selected filter into the next subgroup above the
filter in the filter list. See also drag-and-drop
below.

Move Out of Group

Moves a filter in subgroup out of that subgroup. See also
drag-and-drop below.

Top-level group is matched if all members match ('AND')

If ticked, the top-level group is deemed to be matched if all
members of the top-group match. Top-level filters will
display in blue,
and will be linked with 'AND'.

Top-level group is matched if any members match ('OR')
If ticked, the top-level group is deemed to be matched if any
members of the top-group match. Top-level filters will display in
green,
and will be linked with 'OR'.

Always show expressions

This option only affects 'General' filters (created on the
'General' filter tab). All such filters have an optional
description which will display if available. If "Always show
expressions" is ticked, the expression used in General
filters will always display, even if the filter has a description.

Drag-and-Drop

The filters list supports drag-and-drop (custom queries only).
Click-and-drag on any filter to move it to a different position within
the same subgroup, or to move it out of the subgroup or into another
subgroup. If you click-and-drag on a subgroup filter, the entire
branch is moved. If you press the Ctrl key
while dragging-and-dropping, the filter or filter branch is copied
instead of moved.

In some cases, there may be a number of different horizontal positions
that you can drag a filter to, depending on exactly which group you wish
it to belong to. In all cases, a blue horizontal bar will show you
where you are dragging to.

Filtering Changes Since Version 7

Users of queries dating back to version 7 of Family Historian or
earlier, may notice that there has been a significant change in this
area. In version 7 area, what is now the 'Filters' tab, was
previously called the 'Rows' tab. And filtering was achieved using
conditions that were combined using 4 condition types: "Add If", "Add
Unless", "Exclude If", and "Exclude Unless". These conditions have
been removed and replaced by the filters described here. There
were a number of reasons for that. First, the previous system was
less flexible and did not support all possible ways of combining
filters, as the current system does (previously, the only way of
supporting all possible combinations was by using complex function
operators which most people would find difficult to use). Second,
many users found the previous system difficult to understand. The
current system for using and combining filters should hopefully be much
more familiar in what it sets out to achieve, and hopefully also more
intuitive to use and easier to 'read'. All queries that were
designed for the previous system are automatically converted to the new
style; so the new style is, in that sense, fully backwardly-compatible
with all previous queries.

One key difference between the old style of filters and the new style,
is that old style filters were applied sequentially in order, whereas,
in general, new style filters are not - or at least, do not have to be,
as the order of filters within a group does not in general affect their
behaviour. There is an exception to this however. Relationship
filters (that is, filters created using the 'Relationship' tab)
are effectively applied sequentially. Any filter in the
relationship tab can reference all the people matched by earlier filters
in the same group. The example, in the screenshot above,
illustrates this. The second filter applies to everyone who
matches the first filter, and the third filter applies to everyone who
matches the second. This is a useful feature of relationship
filters. But notice, to repeat, that the ordering only applies to
filters within the same group. The phrase used by these
filters is "....any of the above". This phrase must always be
interpreted as applying to, and only to, filters in the same
group. Filters in a group are applied sequentially if the group
contains one or more relationship filters.

Another difference between old style filters and the new style is that
with the old style, the result set was initially assumed to be empty if
the first filter as one of the 'Add' type, and to be full (i.e. to
include the entire domain) if the first filter was a 'Remove'
type. Filters had the effect of adding or removing items from the
result set. There is no equivalent of this with new style
filters. They are simply applied to items in the domain.

title: Query Window: General Tab
text:
Query Window

Query Window: General Tab

Query Window: General Tab

Query Type
The record type of the Query. You can create a query for any
type of record supported by Family Historian, except for Header
records. You can also create a query to range over facts (events
or attributes), source citations, and witnesses (this
last covers the roles that some Individuals may have
within shared events - such as the bridesmaids at a
wedding).

Read-only
Check this if you want to protect a query against changes or
accidental deletion. Only available with custom queries (standard
queries are always read-only).

Description
This is a comment field. Standard queries always have a
description. It is a good idea to provide a description for
each of your custom queries, to remind yourself of the purpose it
was intended to serve (and to inform others, if you export your
query and give others a copy of it).

Title
This will appear as a title line, at the top of each page, when
the query is printed. You can use special codes if you wish the
current date or time to be included as part of the title. See Special
Codes in Query Titles and Subtitles.

Subtitle
Choose one of a list of pre-defined subtitles. The
subtitle appears beneath the title line, at the top of each page,
when the query is printed. If you wish to create your own custom
subtitle, choose 'Custom' and enter the subtitle in the box that
appears to the right of the dropdown list. You can use
special codes in your subtitle if you want the current date or
time to be included as part of the subtitle. See Special Codes in Query Titles and Subtitles.

Orientation
Format of page when printed - Landscape or Portrait. Can also be
changed in Print Setup (accessible from the File menu).

Multi-page Handling
Indicates what you wish to happen if the query, when printed,
is more than a single page in width (given the current
orientation). The choices are:

Down then across
Print all pages for the leftmost columns, before printing
any pages for columns to the right.
Across then down
Print all pages for the topmost rows, before printing any
pages for subsequent rows.
Max. one page across
Ignore all columns which cannot fit onto a single page

Category 1/2/3
When you click on the Query button on the main
application toolbar, a dropdown menu shows queries broken down
into different categories (submenus) - such as "Ages and
Birthdays". This makes queries easier to find.
You are recommended to assign all custom queries to one or more
appropriate categories. If an appropriate category does not
already exist, you can create your own. To do this, click on
one of the Category fields and choose <Add New...>
from the list. If you wish, you can add queries not just to
categories, but to subcategories within categories (nested to any
level), and the menu structure will reflect this. To learn
more see Add Query Category
Dialog.

The same categories can also be used for filtering in the Manage Queries Dialog.

It is possible to change the categories for standard queries as
well as custom queries. Be aware if you do this, however,
that any changes may be lost (and therefore may need to be
re-applied) when you next apply an upgrade to Family Historian.

title: Query Window Options Dialog
text:
Query Window

Query Window Options Dialog

The Query Window Options Dialog is available from the Options
command on the Query Menu.
It allows you

The Query Options dialog allows you to specify font details for query
reports (every query can be printed as a report). Use Print Preview
on the Query toolbar to preview the
results of font changes on a sample result set. You can also
change the font used to display a result set in the Query Result Set tab.

The

title: Query Window: Result Set Tab
text:
Query Window

Query Window: Result Set Tab

Query Window: Result Set Tab (also known as the Results Window)

The Result Set tab of the Query Window is sometimes known as the
Results Window, for short. This is where
the results of a query are displayed. You can sort the results by
clicking on any column heading. Click it again to reverse the sort.
A result set can be copied to the clipboard, saved to a file, or printed
as a report (click on Print on the File menu). See the Query Toolbar and Query
menu for options.

Press Ctrl+A when the keyboard focus is within the
result set, to select all cells in the result set. To select some other
group of cells, click the top-left cell and, keeping the mouse pressed
down, drag down to the bottom right cell.

If the group is large, an easier technique is to click in the top-left
cell. Then (without keeping the mouse pressed down) scroll down till the
bottom right cell is in view. Now press-and-hold the Shift
key and click on the bottom right cell. This will select all cells in
between. You can use the same technique to select all cells in a
column.

Data-Linked Cells

Some cells in a result cell are displayed in black text, and some are
displayed in grey (or at least, these are the default colours).
Black text means that the cell is data-linked. That is
to say, it represents (is linked to) an actual field or record in your
project. Double-click on any such cell to locate that data item in
the Property Box. Where a cell has
grey text, this means that the cell displays calculated values, which do
not directly represent (are not directly linked to) any particular field
or record, so double-clicking on these cells does nothing.

If you right-click on a cell with black text, a dropdown menu will be
displayed with options to:

Locate in Property Box

Locate in All Tab

The first is the same as double-clicking. The second will locate
the data item in the All tab of
the Property Box.

If you right-click on a field with grey text, the menu items will be
greyed.

Other Uses for the Results Window

The Result Set tab of the Query Window is often referred to as the
Results Window, in other parts of the program. It is used
not just with queries but also for other purposes. For example, if
you use the Find Dialog to search your
project, there is a button Display Results in
Results Window, which you can press, to display results
here. If you click Citations to Source Record on the View
menu, to view all citations for a given Source record, the
resulting table will also be displayed in the Results Window.
Plugins too can display their output in the Results Window.

When the Results Window is used in this way, there is no query that is
associated with it at that point, and the Query field will be
blank.

title: The Smart Folder Pane
text:
Query Window

The Smart Folder Pane

See Smart Folders in the
Query Window.

title: Record Matching Options Dialog
text:
Merge/Compare Dialog

Record Matching Options Dialog

Record Matching Options dialog

The Record Matching Options Dialog is displayed when you do a File
Merge/Compare, after selecting the Family Historian project or GEDCOM
file that you wish to compare (and optionally merge) with the current
project or GEDCOM file.

Fields

Record Matching Options
This option allows you to specify if you want Family Historian
to suggest possible record matches, between the two files being
compared. Family Historian will compare records of all
types.

Check for Individual record Unique Id matches
Every Individual record can optionally have one or more Unique
Ids. Unique Ids, sometimes knowns as UIDS or GUIDS, are
identifiers that are intended to be globally unique.
"Globally unique" means that, if used correctly, the identifier
should be completely unique across the world, so that no two
persons, anywhere in the world, share that same identifier
(although any given person may have more than one).
Correctly-used Unique Identifiers might look something like this:

94ED392F-E3FA-46B1-9B3C-76026C14D583

Unique Ids like this should never be generated 'by hand'. To
ensure uniqueness, they should only ever be generated by a tool
such as Family Historian that is designed to generate them.

If you tick the option to check for Unique Id matches for
Individual records, Family Historian will treat two Individual
records as matched if they share one or more Unique Ids, provided
only that they are the same sex. If two Individual records
do not match in virtue of their Unique Ids (they either don't have
them, or they do and they don't match), Family Historian will not
assume that they are not records for the same person. In
that case it will use its normal techniques for comparing records,
to determine if the records are the same or not. If it finds
a possible match, it will assign a 'score' to this match, to help
you determine how much trust you should place in the suggested
match.

Individual records which are matched in virtue of their Unique Ids
will display '(guid)' in the 'Score' column, in the Merge/Compare
Dialog.

title: The Records Window
text:
Workspace Windows

The Records Window

The Records Window (marked in red)

What is the Records Window?

The Records Window is home to records of all types in the current
Family Historian file. There are 13 record types and the Records Window
has one tab for each of them, although by default several of these tabs
are hidden when Family Historian is installed (see the Record
Window tab in Preferences).

Unexpanded rows in the Records Window represent records. If you 'open'
a record by clicking on the little box to its left, the record will
expand to display the fields within it. If these fields contain
sub-fields, they too can be further expanded, and so on. To see an
entire record, press the ALT key while double-clicking on the record
name - that is, the 'left most' row in the left column (assuming you
haven't changed the default double-click action in Preferences).

Smart Folders

The Records Window supports smart
folders, which allow records to be automatically organised into
whatever groups and categories are most useful, interesting and
important. Click on the Smart Folder icon (top-left) to open the Smart
Folder pane. Smart folders can be customized to show information
in any way desired. See Smart Folders
to learn more about smart folders generally. See Smart
Folders in the Records Window to learn about specific features of
their use in the Records Window.

List Filtering

When viewing lists of records of most record types, filtering options
are provided at the top of the window. For example, if you are
viewing a list of Individual records, you can filter on last name, first
name and life dates - or any combination of these. Use *
(asterisk) as a wildcard to match any text. Use ? (question mark)
as a wildcard to match any single character. Use ^ to match the
start and/or end of the text. Click on the Clear
button to clear the current record filter. Click on the Options
button to view record filtering options.

Search By Partial Name

A quick way to find the first record with a name that matches a given
text, is to click on any name in the list (not in the filter
boxes at the top) and then type the first few letters of the name your
are searching for. As long as you type the letters without
pausing, the first record with a name that matches the letters you
typed, will be selected. For example, if you type 'SMI', the first
record with a name starting 'SMI' will be selected'. If you type
'S' and pause, and then 'M' and pause, and then 'I' and pause, 3
different records will be selected in turn - beginning with the letters
'S', 'M' and 'I' respectively.

Record Id

If you want to find a record quickly and know its record id, you can
type this into the 'Go To' Record Id box at the top of the Window.
If a record exists with the record Id, it will be instantly selected
and, if necessary, scrolled into view.

Configuring Columns

The columns in the Records Window are highly configurable. Right-click
on any column heading, or anywhere in the main body of the Records
Window, and choose Configure Columns...
from the menu that appears to open a Configure
Columns dialog. These default columns will be re-used in
most record selector dialogs. They will also appear as the default
columns that you can optionally include when you create a new custom
query for records of this type. See New
Query Dialog.

Editing Records

Double click on any record name to open the Property Box to edit that
record (unless you have changed the default double-click action in
Preferences)

Browsing & Low-level Editing

Most users will typically use the Property Box for editing records.
But they may sometimes prefer to use the Records Window (or the All tab
of the Property Box, which has the same layout) as a quick way of
browsing records, and seeing all the information stored about a subject.
Almost any kind of editing can
be done in the Record Window, and some kinds of advanced editing can
only be done in the Records Window. Editing in the Records Window (or in
the 'All' tab of the Property Box) is called low-level
editing.

To add a new field to a record using low-level editing, right-click on
the record name (the text in the left column) to bring up a context menu
with an 'Add Field' submenu, with commands for each of the fields or
sub-fields which you can validly add. You can also, similarly, add
subfields to existing fields by right-clicking on the field name, to
bring up a context menu with 'Add' commands for each of the subfields
you can validly add. Alternatively, to delete a field, select it
and press the Delete key. If you want to edit the value of a field or
subfield, click on its current value in the right-column.

Where a record contains links to other records, the name of the linked
record is shown in the right column with a little white check box to the left of the record icon.
Click on this check box if you want to see details of the linked record.

Some features of the Records Window can be configured in the Record
Window tab in Preferences.

Menu and Toolbar

The Records Window has its own menu and toolbar, both of which are
only available when the Records Window is active. The Records Window
menu is the Lists menu.
This is used for maintaining Named Lists.
Named Lists are used for a variety of purposes. You can use them in
whatever way you wish. You might, for example, use a Named List as a
list of bookmarks, or as a 'To Do' list, or as a convenient way of
selecting items for a report. You can print the contents of a list (and
associated notes) using the List Report. There is no limit to the number
of Named Lists you can have. Every Named List can contain all types of
records - not just Individual records. You can re-order the items in a
Named List, and preserve the new order.

title: Re-order Out-of-Sequence Data Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Re-order Out-of-Sequence Data Dialog

The Re-order Out-of-Sequence Data dialog is available from the Re-order
Out-of-Sequence Data command on the Tools menu.

By default, Family Historian will keep spouses, children, events &
attributes, and LDS ordinances, in date order. But you are not forced to
use date order and you can override this.

If you have a file which contains spouses, children, events &
attributes and/or LDS ordinances which are not in date order, you can
use this dialog to re-order them all in date order.

If you only want a particular type of item to be re-ordered, you can
uncheck other items in the Items to Check
list.

If Prompt For Confirmation Before Each
Update is checked, Family Historian will display each record
before doing any updates, and show you which type of fields need to be
re-ordered (that is spouse, children, events & attributes, LDS
ordinances, or any combination of all of these). You can then decide
whether to let Family Historian reorder the record or to skip that
record and continue to the next.

If Prompt For Confirmation Before Each
Update is unchecked, Family Historian will automatically
re-order all the fields for you. A progress dialog will however be
displayed showing progress, and giving you the opportunity to cancel, if
you wish to do so.

If you wish it to do so, Family Historian will keep a list of records
that have been updated.

title: Report Options Dialog
text:
Report Window

Report Options Dialog

Report Options Dialog (aspects will vary considerably depending on the
report)

The Report Options Dialog is used to configure the options for the
report currently displayed in the Report Window. The Report Options
Dialog has several tabs, but the tabs actually available vary depending
on the report type. The options available within the tabs also vary
depending on the report.

In most cases, you can open the Report Options Dialog either before or
after opening a report. When you select most reports, you will
normally be prompted to specify a few key requirements (such as who the
report is about). In most cases, there is a link on this dialog,
"more options...". Click on this link to open the Report Options
Dialog. Alternatively, wait until the report is open and then
click on the Options button on the panel on
the right side. If you take the latter approach, when you make
changes to a report, you can click the Apply
button to view the affect of the changes immediately.

title: Report Options Dialog: Contents Tab (Family)
text:
Report Options Dialog

Report Options Dialog: Contents Tab (Family)

Although listed here as a tab used in the Report Options Dialog, this
tab can also be used in the Item
Settings Dialog. This Help page covers both contexts of
use.

Fields

Sections
The summary can consist of up to 5 different sections. Check all
of the ones that you wish to appear in the report.

Family Events/ Attributes (Family Summary)

Family events/attributes ((e.g. 'Marriage', 'Divorce' etc)) are
listed in the Family Summary section, if this section is
included in the Report (see Sections above). You can choose
whether you wish to see all of the family events/attributes, or
just a specific list; or you can see all of them except an
excluded list. Double-click on the list itself, or click on Edit List to change the contents of the
list. Note that you can specify custom events/attributes as well
as standard events/attributes.

Family Member Main Items (in order)

In a family report, each family member has a section of their
own. Use this list to specify which items should appear for each
family member. Use the Move Up/Move Down buttons near the
top-right corner of the list, to change the order of the items,
if you wish to do so. Double-click on any item (or select it and
click Edit) to open the Edit
Item Details dialog, to view or change the
settings for that item. Most items will only appear in a report
for a given Individual if that Individual has a value for that
item. But for some items you can select "Show Even if Empty". In
this case, a line will appear showing the label for that item,
even if the record has no value for it.

If you wish not to see a particular item, whether or not there
is a value for it, you should select 'Hide' in the Edit
Item Details dialog for that item.

The ability to add items to this list, is a powerful feature
which lets you customise reports in a very flexible way. For
example, if you wished to see an Individual's grandfather shown
in a report, you could click on the Add
button, specify an appropriate label, and add the following as
the expression:

%INDI.~FATH[1]>~FATH[1]>%

If you wanted to see the grandfather's life dates, you would
use this instead:

%INDI.~FATH[1]>~FATH[1]>%
(=LifeDates2(%INDI.~FATH[1]>~FATH[1]>%))

This should be added all on one line. Once you have added it
this item, you can change its position in the list using the
Move Up/Move Down buttons.

Ordinarily you would use the <<
Insert Data Ref button to help you generate the
required expression.

Note: the 'Spouses' item is ignored when displaying items for
the parents of the family. The 'Parents' items are ignored when
displaying items for the children of the family.

Family Member Events/ Attributes
As well as the items listed in the previous paragraph, you can
also specify which events and attributes you wish to be included
for each family member. You can choose whether you wish to see all
of the person's events/ attributes, or just a specific list; or
you can see all of them except an excluded list. Double-click on
the list itself, or click on Edit List
to change the contents of the list. Note that you can specify
custom events/attributes as well as standard events/attributes.

Additional Info for Events/Attributes
The date and place for each event or attribute are displayed
automatically, if known. You can also opt to display
additional information such as addresses or notes associated with
the event or attribute. Depending on the 'Display' setting,
this extra information can be displayed on the line immediately
below the event or attribute it relates to, or all such
'additional info' can be displayed separately, grouped together in
its own section (entitled "Additional Info"). If you choose
the latter option you should tick 'Instances' to ensure that the
instance for a given event or attribute, is shown in brackets
after its label, if there is more than one (e.g. "Occupation
(2)"). If you don't do this and you have multiple events or
attributes of the same type, there might be no way of knowing
which particular event or attribute an address or note related
to. There is no need to tick 'Instances' of course if you
display notes and addresses immediately below the event or
attribute they relate to.

Note that the 'Instances' option is not applicable to the
"Additional Info" section itself, as these will always show the
instance for events and attributes that occur more than once.

Dates with Names
Show each person's life dates in brackets after their name. If
birth and death dates are not known, baptism, christening and/or
burial dates may be shown instead.

Inc. [[private]] Notes
You can include private text in notes by enclosing it in double
square brackets, like this: [[secret text]]. Ordinarily, private
text does not print in reports, but if you want it to be included,
check this option. See Private
Notes for more details.

Remove [[ and ]]
Only applicable if Inc. [[private]] Notes has been checked. If
set, the double square brackets around private text is not
displayed, even if the private text is displayed.

Inc Witnessed Events
Witnessed events (or witnessed
attributes, if any) will be included in the report.

Ages with events, if recorded
If you have explicitly recorded a family member's age at the
time of an event or attribute, that age will be displayed.

or calculated
Only applicable if Ages with events, if recorded is checked. If
you haven't explicitly recorded a family member's age at the time
of an event or attribute, but it is possible to calculate it, the
calculated age will be displayed.

Additional Info for Events/Attributes

title: Report Options Dialog: Contents Tab (Source)
text:
Report Options Dialog

Report Options Dialog: Contents Tab (Source)

Although listed here as a tab used in the Report Options Dialog, this
tab can also be used in the Item
Settings Dialog. This Help page covers both contexts of

Fields

Inc. [[private]] Notes

Main Section Items (in order)

Lists the items that should appear in the Main section of the
report (if that is being displayed - see Sections above). Use
the Move Up/Move Down buttons near the top-right corner of the
list, to change the order of the items, if you wish to do so.
Double-click on any item (or select it and click Edit')
to change the settings for that item. Most items will only
