text:
FamilySearch Window

Family Historian Upload Terms and Conditions

Important information About Uploading Your Family Tree Data

By uploading your family tree data from Family Historian to
FamilySearch, you acknowledge and agree to the following terms and
conditions:

Your Responsibility

When you choose to upload your family tree data to FamilySearch, you
are doing so entirely at your own discretion and risk. You are solely
responsible for:

Deciding what information to upload

Ensuring you have the right to share the information you upload

Understanding and accepting FamilySearch’s own terms of service and
privacy policies

Being aware that your uploaded data may become visible to other
FamilySearch users worldwide

Any consequences that may result from your decision to upload data

Calico Pie’s Position

Calico Pie Limited, the developer of Family Historian, acts solely as
a software provider that facilitates the technical process of uploading
data to FamilySearch.

Calico Pie Limited accepts no responsibility or liability whatsoever
for:

Any consequences arising from your upload of data to FamilySearch

How FamilySearch stores, displays, or uses your uploaded data

Who may access or view your uploaded data on FamilySearch

Any disputes, claims, or issues that may arise from your uploaded
data

Any loss, damage, or harm of any kind resulting from your decision
to upload data

Any errors, defects, or malfunctions in the Family Historian
software that may affect the upload process or the data uploaded,
whether or not Calico Pie Limited was aware or should have been aware
of such errors

This exclusion of liability applies in all circumstances and without
exception, including but not limited to cases involving software errors,
bugs, or technical issues.

Before You Upload

We strongly recommend that you:

Carefully review FamilySearch’s terms of service and privacy policy

Consider the privacy implications of making family information
publicly accessible

Obtain appropriate consent from living individuals whose
information you plan to upload

Review your data to ensure it is accurate and appropriate for
sharing

Understand the privacy settings and controls available within
FamilySearch

Back up your data before uploading

Agreement

By proceeding with the upload, you confirm that you have read,
understood, and accept these terms and conditions in full.

title: Using Family Historian
text:
Using Family Historian

This section explains how to perform some common tasks in Family
Historian.

title: Validate Dialog
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Validate Dialog

The Validate Dialog is used to run a series of checks on your current
project, or standalone GEDCOM file, to ensure that it is in a valid
state. It will report in detail on any errors found. If
required it can optionally fix errors found.

As well as checking for errors, the Validate Dialog can also be used to
check for issues which are not errors, as such, but which you might want
to know about anyway. See the option "Report inoperative record
links in text fields" in the table below, for an example of this.

Fields

Correct general data errors if found

If this option is ticked, Family Historian will not only report
on any data errors it finds, but will correct them where possible,
in order to leave your project or file in a valid state. If
you want to find out about errors without making any changes to
the project or file, you should untick this option and the next.

Correct legacy media issues if found

Historically, the GEDCOM has allowed 2 ways of storing media
items in a GEDCOM file. The first, and most common, is to
hold all the details about the media item in a Media record.
The second way is to store the media item details in fields that
are sometimes called "local media objects". The latter is a
method of associating media items (such as pictures) to your data
without creating a media record to represent the media
item within your project. One might conjecture that this
option was designed for the benefit of genealogy programs that
were not capable of maintaining and managing Media records.
As part of its commitment to full support for GEDCOM, Family
Historian supports this legacy option, and will import local media
objects from GEDCOM files if found. But it is not
recommended. The recommended approach (which Family
Historian will automatically use by default whenever you add a
media item to a project) is the first method - which is to have a
Media record for each media item. There are numerous
advantages to doing that. It means, for example, that media
items can be easily shared between other records, which is
frequently very useful. If you have a photo with several
people in it, each person in the picture can be linked to their
own face. This would not be possible if the media item could
not be shared. Using a Media record to represent a media
item also has considerable advantages in other ways. It
makes is much simpler to find media items and browse them in the
Media Window, and to use filtering, keywords, queries, smart
folders and other tools, to work with your media items, and keep
track of their usage. If the option ''Correct legacy media issues
if found" is ticked (which is recommended), Family Historian will
check for local media objects and, if any are found, will
automatically convert them to Media records. There is no
loss of functionality in this.

Report inoperative record links in note fields

A 'note' field is any field which stores, or can store, multiple
lines of text. A note field may be labelled 'Note', but
doesn't have to be. A 'Text from Source' field, within a
Source record, would be an example of a note field.

If this option is ticked, the report will list all inoperative
record links found in the current file or project. An
inoperative record link is a hyperlink that does nothing when you
click on it. You can tell that it is inoperative by looking
at it, because instead of a solid underline (which ordinary
hyperlinks have), it will have a 'broken' underline. An
inoperative record link is not - or not necessarily - an
indication of an error as such. They will occur whenever you
have a hyperlink, in a note field, that links to a record, and you
later decide to delete that record. This will cause all
hyperlinks that reference the deleted record to become
inoperative. This is by design. However, even if
inoperative record links are not an indication of a problem, you
may nevertheless wish to find them. This option causes them
to be listed in the validation report.

title: Web Clipping
text:
Workspace Windows

Web Clipping

A design goal for Family Historian was to make it as easy possible to
extract text and images from any website that a user may visit, while
also making it as easy as possible to provide appropriate source
citations. There should be no need to have to re-type any text. The
designers of Family Historian considered creating a special tool to
support web clipping, but concluded that a better job could be done by
creating or enhancing a number of different components or features that
can be used for web clipping, but not just for web clipping. The
components and features that are relevant here are:

The Web Search Window

Drag-and-Drop

Copy-and-Paste Images and the Windows Snipping Tool (see below)

The Automatic Source
Citation Pane

Floating Windows

Source-Driven Data Entry

Click on the links above to learn more.

Copy-and-Paste Images and the Windows Snipping Tool

Frequently, if you are viewing a web page in a web browser (either an
external web browser or in the Web
Search Window) you can copy an image by simply right-clicking on
it, and choosing 'Copy' from the dropdown menu that appears. If
this doesn't work, or if the image you want is not displayed in a web
page, you can use the Windows snipping tool to copy any image you are
viewing on the screen. To use the Windows Snipping Tool, click
"Windows Snipping Tool" on the Tools menu.

The Windows Snipping Tool allows you to click-and-drag anywhere on the
screen to select an area that you wish to copy as an image to the
clipboard. For example, you could use this technique to copy a
section of a diagram or map.

When you have copied an image by any technique, you can then insert the
copied image into the program as a Media
record, by clicking on the Add menu,
and choosing "Picture from Clipboard" and "Paste Copied Picture".
You will be prompted to specify a file name for the pasted image, and
optionally a location, if you don't want to save it to the default
location.

Another option is to simply click 'Paste' on the Edit menu. In
most contexts, this is just another way of doing the same thing. You
will be asked if you want to insert the clipboard image as a new Media
record. However, if you click 'Paste' when viewing the Diagram
Window (or if you right-click on the background of the Diagram
Window and choose 'Paste' from the dropdown menu that appears), you will
be offered a choice. You can either paste the copied image into
the current diagram, or you can insert the copied image into the current
project as a new Media record.

If you have copied an image, and want to insert it into the program as
a picture of a particular person (that is, inserting it, and linking it
to a given person in a single step), you can do this too. In that
case, click the Add Media button on the Media tab of the Property Box,
when viewing the record of the person in question. Then choose
"Paste Copied Image" from the menu that appears.

title: The Web Search Window
text:
Workspace Windows

The Web Search Window

Web Search Window (marked in red) with Property Box docked to the right

The Web Search Window is opened by clicking on the Web Search Window
button
on the main application toolbar. When you click on this button, a
dropdown menu appears. The first menu item is 'Web Search
Window'. Click on this to open a new Web Search Window. You
can also open a Web Search Window by clicking on Open Web Search
Window on the Internet menu.
By default, the Web Search Window is also opened or updated if you click
on any Internet Data Matching hints on the Focus
Window, or if you do a search in the Search the Internet dialog.

The Web Search Window displays a web browser and an address
toolbar. It is used primarily, as the name suggests, for searching
the Internet for genealogy records. See the Web
Search Toolbar for details about the Web Search Window toolbar.

If you wish, you can always choose to use an external Web Browser
instead of the Web Search Window (this is an option in the Internet Data
Matches tab of Preferences, and also an option on the Search the
Internet dialog). Although you are never required to use the Web
Search Window to view web pages, there are a number of benefits of doing
so:

If you want to drag-and-drop text and pictures from a web page into
the Property Box,
and/or into the Automatic
Source Citation Pane, this is much more likely to work if you
are viewing the web page in the Web Search window, than if you are
using an external browser (note: if drag-and-drop does not work, you
may still be able to copy and paste either text or pictures).

By using the Web Search window you can arrange the layout of the
Property Box and the Automatic Source Citation, so that they are
conveniently docked at the side, and at the top of the window,
respectively. You cannot dock either of these windows next to an
external web browser.

You can save bookmarks with other recorded genealogy sites in the
Search the Internet Dialog.

Web Clipping

A
design goal for version 6 was to make it as easy possible to extract
text and images from any website that a user may visit, while also
making it as easy as possible to provide appropriate source citations.
There should be no need to have to re-type any text. We considered
creating a special tool to support web clipping, but concluded that we
could do a much better job by creating or enhancing a number of
different components that can be used for web clipping, but not just for
web clipping. The components and enhancements (all mentioned elsewhere
on this page) are:

The New Web Search window

The New Automatic Source Citation
Pane

Easier, Faster Data Entry

Drag-and-Drop Everywhere

Copy-and-Paste Images

More 'Modeless' Windows

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
text:
Websites & Family
Tree USB Sticks

Website and USB Stick Wizard

Websites and USB Stick Wizard (Step 1)

The Website and USB Stick Wizard is accessed from the Websites
and Family Tree USB Sticks Dialog.

The first step in creating a website or Family Tree USB Stick (or
Family Tree CD/DVD) is to generate the contents (the package) that you
want for your website or Family Tree USB Stick/CD/DVD. At this
point, you don't have to decide your eventual goal. In fact, if
you want, you can later use the same package to generate either a
website or a Family Tree USB Stick/CD/DVD or all of them. The Website
and USB Stick Wizard creates the package contents for you.
These packages can only be created in the context of a Family Historian
project. That is, you cannot use this wizard if you are using Family
Historian to view or edit a standalone GEDCOM file. If you have a
standalone GEDCOM file and you wish to use it as the basis for creating
a website or Family Tree USB Stick/CD/DVD, you must first create a new
project and import the GEDCOM file into that project. You can do this by
clicking on the New button in the Project Window.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 1
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 1
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 1

Start by deciding on a policy for privacy. Especially when creating a
website, it is usually advisable to hide all information, except
possibly for basic details, about people who are still alive. When
creating a USB Stick (or a CD/DVD), you may be able to afford to be less
careful if, say, you are planning to only distribute the USB Stick, or
CD/DVD, to close members of your family.

Fields

Omit all references to Individuals with record flag ‘Private’
All mention of individuals with the ‘Private’ record flag will
be excluded altogether.

Show basic details only for Individuals where this flag is set

Individuals with the specified record flag are not excluded,
but all details about them apart from their name, and their
relationship to others, are excluded. No pictures will be
displayed for them in contexts which would be identifying (such
as in a section about them). If you want to ensure that no
pictures of them are displayed at all, in any context, you
should also tick the "Hide all pictures..." option (see next).

Hide all pictures linked to private or 'basic-details-only'
Individuals

This option has no effect unless at least one of the previous
2 options is ticked. It has the effect that any pictures which
have any links to flagged individuals (that is, flagged
according to either or both of the two prior options), will not
be used anywhere in the website.

This option is sometimes misunderstood. If you have ticked the
"Show basic details only..." option above, no pictures will be
displayed next to 'basic-details-only ' individuals (e.g. in the
person's web-page). That will be the case whether this option is
ticked or not. The effect of this option is to ensure that any
picture that contains (i.e. is linked to) a private or
basic-details-only individual or both (depending on the other
options you picked) will not be used anywhere else in the
website either.

Tip: Another privacy feature, not configured here, is the
ability to include or exclude private sections within a note. If you put
doubled square brackets around a section of a note (e.g. “Paul died in
1983. [[He committed suicide.]]”) the section within the doubled square
brackets is marked as a private section. In any web page which includes
notes, you can specify whether or not you wish private sections to be
included; and, if they are to be included, whether you want the doubled
square brackets to be removed, or not. Individual web pages can be
configured in Steps 3 and 4 of the Wizard.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 2
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 2
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 2

Select all the Individuals who you wish to feature in your website or
family tree USB stick or CD/DVD. If you elected to omit all references
to �Private� individuals, these will be automatically filtered out, even
if you clicked on Add All, or
selected them using Select� You
will always be warned if Individuals are filtered out in this way.

Each person selected will get their own page - either a page for them
alone or a page shared with a spouse, depending on your choices in Step
3.

If you do not select a person at this stage it does not follow that
they will not be mentioned in the website, family tree USB stick or
CD/DVD. It just means that they won�t get their own page. If you wish to
be sure that a person is not mentioned at all, you should set that
person�s �Private� record flag and tick the privacy flag option in step
1.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 3
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 3
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 3

Now choose the report to use as a template for the pages that will be
generated for each of the featured individuals (that is, the individuals
you selected in step 2). If you want each featured individual to have a
page all to themselves, you should use an Individual report as the Primary
Page Type. In that case, there is no need to specify a Secondary
Page Type.

You may prefer to use a family report. This means couples will share a
web page. If a person married more than once, there will be additional
pages for each marriage, and these will be linked together. If you use a
family report as the Primary Page Type, you must specify an Individual
report as a Secondary Page Type. This will be used for those individuals
who never married.

Family Group Sheet (for Web, CD or DVD) and Individual
Summary Report (for Web, CD or DVD) are intended for use with generating
websites, or family tree USB sticks, CDs or DVDs. You do not have to use
these reports as page templates. You can use any listed report. But the
advantage of using a report type that you only use for generating
websites, USB sticks, CDs or DVDs is that you can modify options in
these reports as needed, without affecting printed reports - which may
need subtly different settings. If you wish to use different settings
when making a USB stick or CD/DVD from those you use when generating a
website, you could use the “Save Report As...” button in the Report
Window to create a custom report type to be used only in that context.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 4
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 4
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 4

The home page of your website (or family tree USB stick, CD or DVD)
will have a Table of Contents. In this step you choose what items will
be in the table of contents. There is no limit to the number of items
you can have. You should not attempt to add a link to each of the pages
for the featured individuals. There is no need for that. An index page
will be created automatically which will provide these links. Each
page on your website will have a link to the index in the menu bar.
However, you are recommended to add links to key individuals (yourself
perhaps, for one).

You are also recommended to add some interesting reports, to get your
visitors started. If, for example, you wish to highlight a few key
individuals, you could add reports showing all their ancestors or
descendants. As well as page links and reports, you can also add
pictures and downloadable files. The pictures could include diagrams,
perhaps in JPG format. The downloadable files could include your GEDCOM
file.

The different types of item that can be added are:

Link to page
Link to a page for one of the featured individuals

Report
This is not a link to a page. When you add an item as a report,
a new page is created for that report. The report can be any of
the ones listed under ‘Available Items’ (for a full list, untick
Show most commonly- used reports only).

Image

You are normally recommended to use pictures in .jpg (or
.jpeg), .gif or .png format for this purpose. You should also
check that the picture size is what you want, and resize it if
necessary.

You can save diagrams in .jpg or .png format using the “Save
Diagram As…” command. So diagrams can be included in the website
using this technique.

Download
If you wish to give your visitors/users a copy of your GEDCOM
file (or any other file) you can include it (or them) here as a
download file.

Link to website
Add a link to other websites if you wish.

Index
There is no need to add a link to the Index in the Table of
Contexts as there will be a link in the menu bar at the top of
each page, in any case. However you can if you want to.

By default, only the most commonly-used reports (that is,
commonly-used for website, family tree USB stick, CD or DVD generation)
are listed as ‘Available Items’. To see a complete list of reports that
you can use, untick the option Show most commonly-used reports only.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 5
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 5
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 5

As we saw in the previous step, the home page of your website (or
family tree USB stick, CD or DVD) will have a Table of Contents. In this
step you choose the other items that will appear on the home page -
above the Table of Contents.

Home Page Title
The main title for your home page, and probably the first thing
your visitor/user will read when they arrive at your site, or
start the family tree USB stick or CD/DVD. Leave this blank if you
do not want a title.

Home Page Picture
You can optionally display a picture on your home page, just
below the title. As usual, .jpg (.jpeg), .png or .gif formats are
recommended.

Caption for Picture
If you are displaying a picture, you can optionally also give it
a caption.

Picture Size
'Default' means that a suitable size for the picture will be
chosen automatically. 'Original' means that the original
size of the picture will be used, whatever that is.
Alternatively, you can choose your own preferred size.

Welcome Text
An optional welcome message. This can be long if you wish, over
multiple paragraphs.

Make Welcome Text Centre Aligned
If your welcome text is short, it may look better if you tick Make Welcome Text Centre Aligned
to make it display in the middle of the page.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 6
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 6
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 6

You can optionally have a Contact Page and/or Statistics page if you
wish.

Name and Address
If you want to have a Contact page, enter details here that you
wish to make available to anyone who wishes to contact you.

Email Address
You can optionally enter a contact email address here.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 7
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 7
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 7

This step is concerned with presentation. Your website (or family tree
USB stick, CD or DVD) will look much better if you have a logo and a
header line at the top of each page, to give the site a strong identity.
You can use the default logo if you wish (a tree) or your own custom
logo.

Logo
The default logo is a picture of a tree. You can use any picture
of your own as a logo if you wish. As usual the .jpg (.jpeg),
.gif, or .png formats are recommended. You are recommended to use
a small picture, about one inch, or 96 pixels, high.

Header Text
Header text is optional. If supplied, it will appear at the top
of each page.

Action When a User Clicks on a Picture

There is no difference between the "Display Full Picture..."
options and the equivalent "Display Same Picture..." options,
for a given image in your website, if the website is already
showing the full picture (at whatever size). In some cases,
however, an image may be showing only part of a picture - a
person's face for example. In these cases, the "Same Picture"
options will cause the same image (e.g. the face) to be
displayed enlarged when the image is clicked on. The "Full
Picture" options however will cause the full picture to be
displayed.

Choosing one of the 'popup' options will mean that the
displayed image (full or not) is displayed as a 'popup',
overlaying the existing page which appears darkened in the
background. The user clicks a 'Close' button on the popup, or
clicks anywhere outside the popup image, to close it. If you
choose one of the "Own Page" options, the displayed image will
be displayed in a separate page and the user will need to click
a 'Go Back' button on their browser to return to where they
were. In general, popups are recommended. These use JavaScript
which may cause a warning message to be displayed on some
web-browsers, depending on how they are configured, when a user
visits the website.

The option chosen here affects all pictures in all pages of the
website, except any picture pages which may be created in Step 4
of the wizard. Picture pages are created by adding Picture items
to the Table of Contents in Step 4. Any such pictures are
excluded because it is assumed that as they each have a web-page
of their own already, they are presumably already complete and
need no further enlargement.

Maximum Size of Full/Enlarged Picture
Specify the maximum size for the Full/Enlarged Picture (see
previous paragraph).

Animate Popups
If this option is enabled, the display of popups is animated for
stylistic effect.

Colours
Click on this button to change colours.

Tip: Most presentation details are set in Report options.
The report options for the Primary Page Type (set in step 3) are
used as the default settings. So, for example, to change the font type
or size for the caption to the picture on the home page, click on
Options… next to the Primary PageType setting in Step 3 and edit the
Caption font in the Format tab.

title: Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 8
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 8
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard

Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 8

Fields & Buttons

Home page file name
This option is only available when generating a website. You
should use the name ‘index’ unless you have good reason to do
otherwise.

Advanced
Advanced users, familiar with HTML (the format of the World Wide
Web) can add additional HMTL to different parts of each page,
using this option - see also Advanced
Customizations.

The Next Step

When you have completed step 8, the files for your website (or family
tree USB stick, CD or DVD) will be created. At this stage, you have done
all the creative work; but there is still one more thing to do. If you
are creating a website, you need now to put your website up on the
Internet. If you are making a family tree USB stick, you will need to
copy the files to the USB stick. If you are creating a family tree
CD/DVD, you now need to burn CDs or DVDs using the content that you have
created. See How
to Create a Website or Family Tree USB Stick for more on this.

title: Advanced Customizations
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
Website and USB Stick Wizard - Step 8
text:
Website and USB Stick Wizard -
Step 8

Advanced Customizations

The topics in this section are for advanced and
technically-minded users only. Ordinary users do not need to be aware of
the issues discussed here.

The Website and USB Stick Wizard provides numerous options for
customizing and configuring your package (a website or family
tree USB stick, or CD/DVD). And you can go further by configuring
the report templates in step 3. But for technically-sophisticated
users who are familiar with HTML (the programming language used by web
pages), there are even more ways that configure websites to suit your
own needs and requirements, by inserting your own low-level instructions
(in HTML) into sections of the generated code. To do this,
click on the Advanced button in step 8 of
the wizard. In some cases, you may also want to reference your own
files. This page explains how to do this.

When you generate a package, Family Historian will store the files in a
sub-folder with the package name, within a folder called 'Packages',
which is itself a sub-folder of the main data folder of your project
(data folders use the project name but have a ".fh_data" suffix).
Within your package folder, there is a sub-folder called "data
files". If you wish to store any custom files of your own, you
should put them in a sub-folder of the "data files" folder. You
are recommended to use a name that begins with an underscore (e.g. "_my
custom files") to ensure that there is no risk of conflict with folder
names used by Family Historian. Family Historian will never use
sub-folder names in this context, that begin with an underscore.
By putting your files here, you can ensure that they are copied and
exported when the package is copied or exported, and that they are not
deleted when the package is rebuilt. However, be aware that if you
delete the package, these files will also be deleted.

title: Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
text:
How to...

Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks

This section looks at how to create a website, and also how to create a
complete family tree on a USB stick, that anyone can view and explore
using any web browser. If you want to create a copy of a website
on a CD or DVD, you can also do that.

See How to Create
a Website for Family Tree USB Stick.

title: Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks
breadcrumb: Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks
text:
More Dialog Boxes...

Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks

Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks Dialog

To open the Websites & Family Tree USB Sticks Dialog, a floating
window, click on Websites and Family Tree USB Sticks on
the Publish menu. The dialog
shows a list of packages that you have created in the current
project for websites or for Family Tree USB Sticks (or, more rarely, for
writable CDs or DVDs). There is no limit to the number of packages
you can create in any project. To learn more about packages and their
role in creating a website or a Family Tree USB Stick, or a CD/DVD, see
How to Create a
Website or Family Tree USB Stick.

Fields

New
Create a new package. Opens the Website
and Family Tree USB Stick Wizard.

Edit
Opens the selected package in the Website
and Family Tree USB Stick Wizard, to allow settings to be
edited and to rebuild the contents.

Rebuild
Rebuild the selected package using the current settings

Rename
Rename the selected package

Copy
Create a copy of the selected package

Delete
Delete the selected package

Preview
View the contents of the selected package in a web browser.

Export
Generated package files are stored in the project folder.
Click the Export option to copy them to another location on your
PC. You will need to specify whether you want the files for
the purpose of creating a website, or to create a Family Tree USB
Stick or CD/DVD.

title: What's New in Family Historian 8?
text:
What's New in Family Historian 8?

Features And Enhancements in Version 8

Headline Features

Smart Folders - an important innovation for
the genealogy world

FamilySearch - full support, including the
new user trees

Maps - innovative mapping tools that let you do so
much more

Queries - redesigned, more powerful, and easier
to use

New All Relative Narrative report -
includes all relatives of subject person

Sources & Citations - extensive enhancements
including free form
sources, customization, & more

Addresses - can now have map locations,
pictures and notes

Diagrams - numerous improvements including a
major graphics update

Books - extensive enhancements, including support
for scrapbooks and photo books

64 bit - Family Historian can now handle much
larger projects

Support for Non-Family Relationships

Full LDS Church support

Other New Features and Enhancements

Enhancements to reports

Improved Expression Entry Assistant
tool

Improved options for export of source and
citation information

Improvements to source templates

Customizations for the Focus Window and other
improvements

Improvements to the Records Window and
record selector dialogs

New search tool: for searches for projects, backup
files and GEDCOM files

Smart Folders - an Important innovation
for the Genealogy World

Smart folders are a major Family Historian innovation and, we
believe, a genealogy world first. We are not aware of any comparable
feature anywhere else. Smart folders allow all of your data to
be automatically organised into structured folders, which allow you to
explore and browse your data, so that you can instantly and easily
view all the interesting and important information that it contains.

Every record listing - that is, every tab in the Record Window, and
every record selector dialog - now has an optional pane for displaying
smart folders, which can be enabled by clicking this icon: .

Smart folders can also be displayed in the Query Window. All
query types are supported as folder set types (and there are now 15
query types, including 3 non-record query types).

Family Historian comes with a number of standard folder sets,
covering all record types and more.

Smart folders are grouped within 'folder sets'. Users can
create their own custom folder sets, to display information in smart
folders in whatever way they wish.

Smart folders offer valuable insights and perspectives with records
of all types, and in other contexts, but are especially valuable when
used with sources and citations - see Sources
& Citations - extensive enhancements including free form
sources, customization & more.

To learn more, see Smart Folders.

FamilySearch - full support, including the
new User trees

FamilySearch is a nonprofit organization and website,
offering free global resources for all genealogists everywhere.
It has more than 1.7 billion individual records in its main (global)
tree. It is now fully supported within Family Historian.
Users have to sign up for a free FamilySearch account to make use of
the functionality. To learn more about FamilySearch, see the FamilySearch
Wikipedia page.

FamilySearch has recently introduced the ability to have shared
user trees. You can create your own trees,
public or private, and share them in a controlled way with whoever you
wish. This feature is also supported within Family Historian.

Family Historian has a new FamilySearch
window. The FamilySearch window is unique in that as well
as functioning as a workspace window, it can also be made to float in
front of other workspace windows. This is so that you can use it
either as a primary workspace in its own right, or as a satellite
window, when working on other workspace windows. It can be
synced with selection, so for example, if you want to see details of
each person in a diagram, select each in turn and view the information
held about them in FamilySearch, in the floating FamilySearch window.

Individuals in your Family Historian project can be matched with
individuals in a FamilySearch tree (either the global tree or a user
tree). When you match a record in FamilySearch, you do not share
any information with FamilySearch, or anyone else. Effectively
all that happens is that Family Historian will store the FamilySearch
Id for the matching record.

When you have matched a record to FamilySearch, you can move
information from FamilySearch to Family Historian or vice versa.
A colour-coding system makes it easy to see and compare the different
records, side-by-side.

You can also receive FamilySearch hints about historical records for
the matched Individuals. It is also possible to receive hints
about possible duplication, and/or hints about unmatched Individuals
who may have a match in the FamilySearch tree. You can make
changes to a shared family tree in FamilySearch (again, either the
global tree or a user tree) if you wish to. Or you can use the
FamilySearch functionality entirely as a means of searching for
information, and for improving your own Family Historian project data,
without contributing in any way, to any FamilySearch trees at
all. It is entirely up to you, and under your full control.

To learn more, see the Query Window.

Maps - innovative mapping tools that let you do so
much more

Maps now allow addresses to be mapped and geocoded
(assigned a latitude and longitude); but unlike places which are
automatically geocoded, addresses have to be manually
geocoded. Events can be mapped by address or place or
either ('address preferred'). For more on this, see Addresses
- can now have map locations, pictures and notes.

The Marker Set pane has been redesigned to make it easier to view
and manage multiple marker sets simultaneously. There are new
options allowing marker sets to be copied and pasted. You can
also now easily hide or show entire marker sets. And there is a
new marker set type for Address records.

Maps now support shapes, which are similar to, but
different from, shapes in the Diagram Window.

Map shapes can be polylines (that is, lines with multiple
segments), polygons, circle or text. When you zoom in and out
on the map, shapes zoom in and out exactly like any other map
feature - except that special-handling is supported for text (see
below).

You control the opacity of shapes (especially important with
polygons and circles), so that areas and regions can be highlighted,
without obscuring the underlying details.

Shapes can be formatted, grouped, and/or ordered with respect to
one another.

Multiple shapes can be selected and edited jointly. They can
also be copied and pasted between different map windows (or within
the same map window).

Text shapes are anchored to particular points on the map, and can
optionally have callouts, which are lines connecting the text box to
their anchor point.

Text shapes have a 'reference' zoom, which allows you to control
how text is zoomed so that it appears in an appropriate form in all
contexts. See Map
Shape Format Dialog: Text Tab for more information.

You have full undo-redo for all changes to map shapes.

Shapes can be 'locked' in position, which means that they can be
clicked on without selecting or moving them, so that they can
effectively be treated as if they are part of the underlying
map. A new 'Access' button on the map toolbar, allows 'locked' shapes
to be accessed, so that they can be selected, edited, moved and
deleted.

Maps now support overlays. An 'overlay' is a way of
annotating and marking distinctive features on maps. Version 8
includes a number of standard overlays, such as the historic counties
of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, as well as overlays
which mark the boundaries of the former soviet union, or the
boundaries of the Roman Empire, or the U.S. at the start of civil
war. Users can easily create their own custom overlays.

A new tool is provided for managing overlays. They can be
cloned, renamed, deleted, simplified (more on this below) and shared
(i.e. imported and exported). You can also provide descriptions
for overlays, which can be read in the Overlays tool window.

As well as Family Historian's own format for overlays, you can also
import overlays in 'geoJSON' format, which means that geoJSON files,
widely available on the Internet, can be imported as Family Historian
map overlays. Sometimes imported overlays may have far more
detail than is needed for Family Historian purposes, and this can
affect performance and responsiveness. A new 'simplify' tool
allows imported overlays to be easily simplified to remove unneeded
detail, and ensure good performance and responsiveness.

Overlaps are built-up using map shapes (especially polygons and
text). All shape setups can be saved as overlays. Overlays
typically lock shapes in position (although, as mentioned above, these
can be 'unlocked' using the Access button in the
Map toolbar). To view overlays (standard or custom), click on
the "Map Overlays" command on the menu that appears when you click on
the 'Map' button on the main application toolbar.

Maps can be saved and re-used. To view a saved map, click on
the new "Saved Maps" command on the menu that appears when you click
on the 'Map' button on the main application toolbar.

Maps can be saved directly as Media records and/or as images, in
JPEG format, making it much easier to incorporate them in reports,
books, websites, etc. To do this, right-click anywhere on the
background of a map, and choose from the "Save Map As" submenu.

The same context menu also allows you to temporarily unlock shapes,
select all unlocked shapes, and select all unlocked text boxes, as
well as do many of the other tasks listed above.

Markers can now optionally show the place or address name (shortened
version) below the marker. A right-click menu option (on the map
itself) allows this 'marker text' to be shown or hidden.

New tools make it easy to work with markers and to make more of map
data in a number of ways - such as finding all markers that fall
within a specified distance from a given point, shading the search
area, and copying marker events to the Results Window for further
exploration and analysis.

To learn more, see the Map Window.

Queries - redesigned, more powerful, and easier
to use

Queries have been redesigned and have a new file format.
Old-style queries are automatically converted to the new file format
on import or upgrade. Old style queries have a .fhq file
suffix. New style queries have a .fhqx suffix.

The Query Window now has a dual role in managing queries and smart
folders. There is a new hide-able pane on the left-hand side for
viewing, and managing smart folders. The Query Window now has
its own toolbar at the level of the main window, with a single button,
for hiding or showing the Smart Folder pane. There are options
in the Query Window
tab of the Preferences dialog, for specifying titles when
printing the contents of smart folders (see Smart
Folders - an important innovation for the genealogy world).

The 'Rows' tab of the Query Window has been renamed as the 'Filters'
tab.

Various changes (mainly detailed below) have been made to make
queries easier to understand, and to hide unnecessary
complexity. So, for example, the expressions used in
columns and filters are now less prominent, and there is less need for
users to understand expressions, in order to achieve the results they
need.

Some users complained that the condition-handling of old-style
row-filters, using "Add if…", "Add unless…", "Remove if…" and "Remove
unless…", was confusing and hard to use. It also did not
allow for all the possible 'AND'/'OR' combinations that users
sometimes required. The old conditions have been now been
completely removed. Instead filters can be grouped using the
familiar 'AND' and 'OR' style, which is easier to understand and
easier to use. All possible 'AND'/'OR' combinations are catered
for because filters can now be placed within subgroups,
nested to any level. Each group or subgroup can be either an
'AND' subgroup or an 'OR' subgroup. Filters are laid out in a
tree-structure, so that each subgroup has its own branch, which makes
the groupings easy to read. A useful visual clue is that 'AND'
subgroups are coloured blue and 'OR' subgroups are coloured
green. Individual filters, or entire branches, can be moved and
copied within this tree structure, using drag-and-drop.
Old-style queries which used the old-style conditions are
automatically converted to use the new-style 'AND's and 'OR's.

When you add a filter, you will be prompted to specify in what way
it should be combined with existing filters (using 'AND' or 'OR), and
filters will be automatically grouped, as needed, to achieve this.

The Filters tab of the Query Window also has a new tab on the pane
at the bottom, labelled 'Subgroup', which is used for adding and
managing subgroups.

The same pane has a new 'Description' field on the General
tab. It is now possible to add optional descriptions to make
filters more readable. Standard filters all have
descriptions. A cog menu option allows you to switch between
viewing descriptions or expressions in the filter list above.

The expression field has a new 'Insert' button which allows
column-expressions to be added, or to open the new Expression Entry
Assistant tool (see section below).

The appearance of the Query Window has been improved in various
minor ways ("parameter" has been renamed "Prompt" in various
contexts). Buttons have been renamed for greater clarity.
The various toolbars now support different sizes. The filter
list toolbar now has a 'Cog' menu button with numerous options to help
with managing filters.

The Columns tab of the Query Window has had similar cosmetic
improvements to the Filters tab and the 'Columns' list toolbar also
has a new cog menu button. By default column expressions are no
longer displayed in the Columns list, but you can add them back to the
display if required (cog menu option).

You can use drag-and-drop to move or copy columns or filters (press
the Ctrl key while dragging to copy). If you move or copy a
filter branch, the entire branch will be copied or moved. On the
Columns tab, click-and-drag from the left-hand side list of fields to
the right-hand side list of columns, to add new columns.

There is a new tool for managing queries which lists all
queries, and displays the description associated with the selected
query. The tool allows filtering queries by category or by type
and you can opt to view custom queries only. It also allows for
textual filtering (type some text to find matching queries). The
tool list has columns for query name, type, custom and
last-updated. Click on a column header to toggle sorting.
It allows custom queries to be renamed, cloned or deleted, as well as
run, viewed, imported or exported. The tool can be accessed by
clicking "Manage Queries" on the dropdown menu that appears if you
click on the Query button on the main application toolbar, or on the
cog menu of the Query toolbar. There is also a button with 3
dots to the right of the Query name at the top of the Query
Window. Clicking this button opens a variant of the Manage
Queries tool, allowing for fast selection of queries.

When you create a new custom query, there is now a check box which
allows default columns to be inserted. This is ticked by
default.

There are 3 new query types: one for Address records, one for
source citations and one for witnesses.

There are several new standard queries

There are several new operators available to be used in the Filters
tab of the Query Window (allowing all possible negations).

There is a new column type, "Group By", set on the Columns tab of
the Query Window, for use with smart folders.

The Query Window dropdown menu (which appears when you click
on the Query button on the main application toolbar) is now much
faster to display.

The Data Reference Assistant dialog has been renamed the
"Expression Entry Assistant" dialog, as it now supports both data
references and built-in functions (see Improved Expression Entry Assistant
tool)

The column tab has been simplified and improved. The Fields
list has been renamed the "Fields Etc" list because it now includes
commonly-used functions. The Columns list does not display
expressions by default, but these can be displayed if required.

You can now view record links for any Individual, or any other
record type, by selecting "Record Links" on the context menu that
appears when you right-click on their record in the Query
Window: Result Set Tab.

You can now quickly access the "Expressions and Contexts of Use"
help page, and also the "Functions by Category" help page, by clicking
on the cog menu on the Query toolbar, and choosing "Query Window
Help".

To learn more, see the Query Window.

New All Relative Narrative report -
includes all relatives of subject person

A major new report - the All Relatives Narrative report -
includes all relatives of a subject person, in narrative format,
organised by generation, with the youngest generation first.

The new report optionally includes a section showing ancestors and
descendants of the subject person, for easy reference.

Numerous options, including the ability to see how each person is
related to the subject person.

Sources & Citations - extensive
enhancements, including free form
sources, customization, & more

Smart folders offer great benefits in all contexts, but are
particularly useful for sources and citations, and when used in these
contexts they effectively bridge the divide between splitters and lumpers
as they allow each group to get all the benefits of each other's
approaches with no need for structural data changes (or any other kind
of data change). Previously genealogists had been forced to
adopt organisational solutions (in the way data is structured) to
achieve presentational goals. Thanks to smart folders, that is
no longer necessary. The same - or better - presentational goals
can now be achieved without compromising on optimal data organisation,
and allowing data entry to be kept as simple as possible.

The standard smart folders for sources and citations automatically
update to reflect changes to source templates.

A new "Source & Citation wizard" also allows custom smart
folders to be generated based on existing source templates, including
custom source templates. For more details about smart folders,
and their use with respect to sources and citations, see Smart
Folders - an important innovation for the genealogy world.

In version 7 there were two types of Source record: generic
and templated. There is now a 3rd type: free
form. Free form sources can be fully customized in the Citation
Window, using bold, italics and underline.

All source citations can now be fully customized in the Citation
Window. Click on the new 'Customize' link in the side panel, on
the right-hand side of the Citation Window. Using the Customize
window, you can now customize a citation either by simply modifying
the finished output (using bold, italics and underline, as
required). You can also customize the "Citation Format", which
is the template used to specify the contents of the citation.
This allows you to make use of template codes if you wish to.
Finally you can even customize the "Source Format" in a similar
way. Text at the top of the Customize Window explains that
customizations of the 'Citation' or 'Citation Format' will affect the
current citation only, but customizations of the 'Source Format' will
affect all citations to that particular source record.
Customizations can be at the 'Footnote', 'Short Footnote' or
'Bibliography' level . You can easily see which fields have been
customized and which have not. Fields that have not been
customized have a brown background. Fields that have been
customized have a white background (the background colour will change
as soon as you make a change to the field). There is also a
"Reset" button with options which allow you to reset the any or all of
the various customizations.

The labels for each item in the side panel of the Citation Window
(normally "Footnote", "Short Footnote", or "Bibliography") include, in
brackets, if the item has been customized; and if so in what way.

The Bibliography section of reports and books has been significantly
improved. Previously the Bibliography section effectively gave
details of each Source record cited in the report or book. There
was no way of customizing a bibliography entry even at the Source
record level. Now you can not only customize a bibliography
entry at the Source record level, you can even customize it at the
citation level, if you wish to. Also, instead of simply listing
Source records, the Bibliography section now looks at the complete
list of bibliography entries and effectively merges all entries which
identical. This means that 'lumpers' can have multiple
bibliography entries for a single source, if they wish to (by
associating different bibliography entries with different citations),
and 'splitters' can allow multiple Source records to share a single
bibliography entry if they wish to do that.

The area at the top of the Notes, Text from Source
and Media tabs in the Citation Window, are all now smaller.

See also Improved Options for Export of
Source and Citation information and Improvements
to Source Templates.

Addresses - can now have map locations,
pictures and notes

There is a new record type, Address, which allows
addresses to be geocoded (given a latitude and longitude) and to have
an unlimited number of pictures or other media, and notes.
Address records are normally associated with a Place record, although
they don't have to be. All event and attribute addresses are
implemented as Address records. The user interface for entering
address details is largely unchanged. When you enter an address,
auto-complete will offer options of addresses already associated with
the specified place, if there is one.

Addresses can be marked on maps. See Maps -
innovative mapping tools that let you do so much more.

Events can be marked with respect to address, places, or either
('address preferred'). See also Maps -
innovative mapping tools that let you do so much more.

New Helper dialog for address selection, allows you to select
addresses within a given place.

Smart folders for addresses allow addresses to be viewed grouped
within place

Within reports, queries and all other output, you can now combine
address and place text, with duplicate parts removed

Diagrams - numerous improvements including a
major graphics update

Major graphics update: The underlying graphics engine has been
completely reworked with new technology that features faster display
of diagrams, and improvements to their appearance. The new
technology supports 'hardware-acceleration' which means that it takes
advantage of underlying graphics hardware (GPU) to deliver optimum
performance.

Users can now create custom box presets (see Diagram
Options Dialog: Boxes Tab) and export/import presets.

New 'Effect' features for boxes (e.g. 'Glow'). You can also
control the opacity of shadows and background pictures. You can
now have no line around boxes if preferred. See Box
Features Dialog for more details.

You can now choose a preferred look for the six most important
standard diagrams, based on any standard or custom diagram (see
"Choose Preferred Look for Standard Diagrams" on the 'Chart' button
dropdown menu). The 'look' includes all the key diagram
features, such as diagram box icons and text, tree orientation and
layout, and more.

The vector format SVG, widely-used across the Internet, is now
supported for diagram box icons. Previously all default icons
were in EMF format. Now they are all SVG.

Diagram box icons can now be exported and custom diagram box icons
can be imported (see "Import/Export" on the File menu). Imported
icons are assigned the category 'Custom'.

Custom icons can be SVG, PNG, BMP, or EMF; but best results are
achieved using the SVG format, which is the preferred and recommended
format for this reason. SVG icon files can be created using free
software, such as Inkscape. Free SVG icon files are also easily
found on the Internet.

There have been improvements to fan charts. There are new
optional (and configurable) 'radial' lines fanning out from the
centre. There is also a new three-quarter size fan chart (the
new default), with an optional circle at the root. The overall
look of fan charts and layout has also improved. See Fan
Chart Dialog for more details.

Various improvements have been made to the Pedigree Chart (see Pedigree
Chart Dialog).

Dotted crossing lines now appear less often in 'All Relatives'
diagrams, and only when necessary

You now have full undo/redo on all changes to shapes in Diagram
Window (see Improved usability within the
program generally)

There are now more options for working with diagram shapes (see
Diagram Elements), including the
ability to align images (or other shapes) with respect to one another,
and to make different shapes the same height or width. There is
now also improved support for locking shapes, so that they
cannot accidentally be moved or resized.

You can now configure a diagram to make it compatible with any
Family Historian book, so that it will fit exactly on a page of a
book, or across multiple pages. This is the new "Book Layout
Compatibility" option on the Diagram menu (available when viewing a
diagram). Book compatibility can also be specified when you
create a pedigree chart (see Reports & Books -
extensive enhancements, including improved support for diagrams in
books).

Previously some diagram options could be saved and re-used, but the
policy was inconsistent and confusing. Now you can change
options for any type of diagram, and re-use them. If you make
changes, you can reset them using the 'Restore Defaults' button

There are 2 new text schemes called "Birth, Marr, Death (hide
details if Living flag set)" and "Birth, Marr, Death (hide name if
Private flag set)". The former hides all text details about a
person except their name, if the Living flag is set for them.
The latter hides all details including the person's name if the
Private flag is set. Other text schemes can be modified to copy
these examples, if required.

The Text tab and Boxes tab now each have a 'Restore Defaults'
button.

Books - extensive enhancements, including support
for scrapbooks and photo books

There is a new "Pedigree Chart (as booklet)" report. This
creates the report as a booklet. You can also now add a pedigree chart
to any book. You can revise the pedigree chart options as
required at any time (not just when adding the chart to the book).

There is much improved support for integrating diagrams with
books. You can now edit a diagram even after it has been added
to a book.

A new feature called "book layout compatibility" ensures that the
page layout of charts or diagrams is kept compatible with a given
book, so that multi-page diagrams fit perfectly into a given book,
regardless of how many pages they use. So, for example, a 5-page
diagram will take up exactly 5 book pages. This compatibility is
automatically maintained with charts and diagrams that have been added
to a book; but even with diagrams or charts that have not yet been
inserted into a book, you can adjust their page layout to ensure
compatibility with any given book.

If you want to add a small diagram, figure or map, that occupies
less than one whole page, this is also now supported.

You can now easily create a scrapbook or photo book, using images
and text that you put together yourself. The scrapbook or photo
book can be an entire book, or a section of a book. See How
to Create a Scrapbook or Photo Book.

The Windows snipping tool on the Tools
menu now allows you to quickly snip parts of a chart, diagram or
map. These can be added to a project as a Media record or
inserted directly into a scrapbook.

Book indices now index the people in all charts, including tree
diagrams, fan charts, pedigree charts etc.

If you add a report that has been generated by a plugin, to a book,
you now get one entry in the book for each entry in the report.
So if you select multiple records, you will get one chapter for
each. The heading is now taken from the heading specified for
the chapter in the book.

64 bit - Family Historian can now handle much
larger projects

Family Historian is now 64-bit. This means that it can easily
support much larger projects, diagrams, reports, and books than
previously.

Backups have been enhanced to remove previous size limitations.

Support for Non-Family Relationships

Family Historian has long supported witnesses - that is,
non-principal participants in an event, such as the best man
at a marriage or a beneficiary to a will. That support has been
extended and made even more powerful. The new functionality
makes it possible to easily record relationships of any kind.
For example, the program now has built-in support for friend
lists (a list of all of a person's friends), friendship
groups (a group of people who were all friends of one another),
and enslavement facts - each of which is a record of one or
more people who were enslaved, and optionally also the person or
persons who enslaved them.

Create your own custom relationships of any kind. These can be
one-to-one relationships (something like a marriage), one-to-many
relationships (teacher and pupils, say), or many-to-many relationships
(friendship groups or enslavement); and the parties can have the same
or different roles, as required.

To learn more, see Witnesses and How
to Record Non-Family Relationships.

Full LDS Church support

Family Historian now has extensive features to meet the needs of
members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints ("LDS
Church Support"), including support for recording church ordinances.

A new 'Enable LDS Support' option (accessible on the General
tab of Preferences) enables new functionality relating to LDS
ordinances.

The LDS Ordinances report has been updated and improved, and a new
query, also called "LDS Ordinances" has been added.

When LDS support is enabled, LDS ordinance details can now be added
and edited on the Facts tab of the
Property Box. These details included temple and ordinance
status, in addition to the usual event details (date, place, note, and
so on).

Almost all reports can now optionally include details of LDS
ordinances, if required, including narrative reports.

When LDS support is enabled, the FamilySearch
Workspace window has an additional Ordinances
Tab which displays LDS Ordinance information for the selected
person. This can be copied back to the matching record in your
Family Historian project. Click the Reserve Ordinances
button to open an appropriate web page in an external web browser for
reserving ordinances and related temple work, for the person in
question.

It is now easier than ever to create custom queries relating to LDS
ordinances. The 'Common Functions' listed in the Columns tab of
the Query Window, now includes 4 additional options relating to LDS
ordinances, for fact queries, when LDS support is enabled.

All LDS ordinance information and tasks are only available for LDS
Church members with suitable permissions in their FamilySearch
account.

See LDS Church Features for
more.

Enhancements to Reports

Reports have been significantly improved with respect to the handing
of sources, source citations and bibliographies. These various
changes are described in Sources & Citations -
extensive enhancements including free form sources, customization,
& more.

There is a new "Special Text" option on the "Formats" tab of
reports, which allows you to specify terms to use for married and
unmarried partners in relationships, as well as other similar text
details, such as the text to use when referencing a couple's
children. You can also use line and paragraph breaks with such
phrases.

As well as the already-mentioned major new narrative report, All
Relative Narrative, there is also another new narrative report,
Register Report, which uses the traditional 'register style'
layout.

Improved Expression Entry Assistant Tool

The Expression Entry Assistant tool is an improved
version of the old Data Reference Assistant tool. The
old tool only helped with entry of data references. The improved version
also helps with the entry of functions
– hence the name change. Frequently-used function calls are
grouped in a section labelled "Common Functions", which lists useful
function calls that are relevant to the context. There is also a
sub-section below labelled 'Counts' which stores a list of function
calls that can be inserted for returning a count of different things,
such as a count of a person's parent families, spouses, research
notes, etc.

No understanding of functions is required to use the function
expressions. Just select the one your require and press 'OK' to
select them. The behaviour of each function expression is
explained in a box below the list when you select the function call.

The Expression Entry Assistant tool is available in all contexts
where the old Data Reference Assistant tool had been available.
The "Common Function" section is available in all contexts in which
functions are supported.

Improved Options for Export of Source and
Citation information

Support for exporting source information has been improved.
Generic Source records use standard GEDCOM fields; so exporting
generic Source records (and source citations relating to them) in
GEDCOM format is not a problem. However, GEDCOM currently has no
built-in support for free form Source records or templated
Source records. Also, Family Historian allows all source
citations to be customized, at either the Source record level, or at
the citation level, and GEDCOM currently has no built-in support for
this either. So Family Historian offers a mechanism (called
"prioritizing compatibility") to ensure that source citations, can be
correctly transferred via GEDCOM, using standard GEDCOM fields, not
just to another copy of Family Historian but also to other genealogy
programs - even if those other genealogy programs only support basic
GEDCOM functionality, and do not support free form sources, templated
sources, or customization of source citations.

There are 6 possible choices with respect to non-generic
source-handling:

No special action

Prioritize compatibility

Copy source/citation details to first note

Copy source/citation details to new note

Prioritize compatibility & copy details to first note

Prioritize compatibility & copy details to new note

If you take any option that includes prioritizing compatibility
(that is, the 2nd, 5th and 6th), Family Historian will copy details of
footnote citations, as they would appear in reports, to generic source
and citation fields. This should ensure that any genealogy
program which supports GEDCOM sources and citations, will have the
full, correct citation details - even for sources that were originally
free form, templated, or customized. For this reason, you are
usually recommended to select an option which includes this feature.

The functionality relating to prioritizing compatibility is not
needed, and has no effect, if the GEDCOM is to be imported into a copy
of Family Historian, version 8 or later. However, even here, it
does no harm to enable it, which is why prioritizing compatibility is
the default option.

As well as, or instead of, prioritizing compatibility, Family
Historian also offers the option to copy fields from templated Source
records and citations, and/or customized source citation details, into
a note, attached to the Source record or citation. Both Source
records and citations can have multiple notes. Family
Historian supports all such notes, but some other genealogy programs
may only support one note per Source record or citation. For
this reason, you can choose between copying the details into the first
note associated with each Source record or citation (by appending the
details to the existing note, if there is one), or by copying the
details into a separate (new) note.

If your project does not contain any sources and citations based on
source templates, and does not have any free form sources or
customized source citations, these options are not applicable.

Improvements to Source Templates

Smart folders allow source templates to be grouped and presented in
meaningful ways.

Thanks to 'Auto' smart folders, source templates now add
significantly more value. This is because, within smart folders
for source records and source citations, folder groupings correlate
with source template categories, and source template fields are used
as columns in the displayed folders.

There is a new button "Adjust Field Order" in the Source
Template Definition Compare Dialog (the dialog which allows you
to compare a source template definition with its equivalent Source
Template record) which is enabled if the fields are not in the same
order, and can be used to change the order of fields in the Source
record to match that of the Source definition or vice versa.

Customizations for the Focus Window and other
improvements

You can now customize the Focus Window, by adding up to 2 additional
lines each of fully customizable text, to parent and grandparent
boxes.

You can also add an additional column to the children listing, with
a fully customizable heading and text.

The Focus Window can now display an optional FamilySearch icon for
records that are matched to the currently selected FamilySearch tree
(if any). Click on this icon to view match details in the Family
Search window.

You can now also optionally display place information for child
births and deaths.

You can now view record links for any Individual by selecting
"Record Links" on the context menu that appears when you right-click
on their record.

Improvements to the Records Window and
Record Selector Dialogs

The Records Window now supports smart folders (see Smart
Folders - an Important innovation for the genealogy world).

Record Window columns now support left, centre and right alignment
(right click on the Records Window and choose 'Configure Columns').

A new option, in Preferences
Dialog: Records Window, allows you to sort Null values
last. This is enabled by default.

You now have one-click toggle sort on columns in Record Window and
many other lists. That is, you can click a column to sort; and
then click it again to reverse the sort. Record Window columns
show the direction of the sort with a little grey triangle in the
column heading.

The first column of the Record Window is 'locked' by default, so you
can scroll sideways without losing context. This means that it
becomes practical to show far more columns in the Records Window than
was previously the case..

Text filters in Records Window have been improved and now support
wildcards (* and ?). All filtering is on text anywhere within
the field, except that you can use ^ at the start or end of a text
filter, to indicate that it must match the start or end (or both) of a
field. There is also a new filtering option if you want text
filters to always match the start of fields.

The above options are all available both in normal mode and when
displaying the contents of Smart Folders.

You can now view record links for any record by selecting "Record
Links" on the context menu that appears when you right-click on the
record (this applies not just to the Records Window but to the Focus
Window and other contexts)

You can now filter on the content of Research Notes in the Research
Notes tab.

You can now use drag-and-drop to add, move or copy columns, in the Configure Columns Dialog.

You can now press Ctrl+A to select an entire list, or
Ctrl+Shift+Home and Ctrl+Shift+End to select from a given point to the
start or end of the list.

New search tool: for searches for projects,
backup files and GEDCOM files

For searching for projects, backups and standalone GEDCOM files
(GEDCOM files that do not form part of a Family Historian
project).

The new tool can be accessed from the 'More Tasks' button on the
Project Window. It can search your entire computer, the
documents folder, or a user-specified folder.

There are menu options for restoring backups (including old-style
'zip' backup files), opening projects or GEDCOM files, and changing
the default project or default project location.

New Backup
and Restore Settings Tool

"Settings" means modified or custom fact type definitions, queries,
diagrams, reports, and text schemes, as well as record flags, language
packs, diagram box icons, accent files, plugins, program preferences
and configurations, and much more. All settings can be backed up
to a file, for easy transfer to another computer. The new tool
can be accessed from the 'More Tasks' button on the Project Window.

For advice on using Family Historian to a new PC (with settings) see
Moving Family Historian to a New PC.

If you install version 8 on a computer that already has an earlier
version installed (see Parallel Installations of
Different Versions) your settings will be automatically copied
to the new installation. This is another application of the same
technology.

Improvements to the Media Window

Individuals, families, places, sources, facts, source citations and
submitters, can all be linked to pictures and other media items.
Previously, with individuals, families, places, and sources, you could
create these links from either end. That is, you could link
either from the data item to the media item (for example, by adding
the link in the Media tab of the Property Box), or from the media item
to the data item (by clicking 'Add Frame Link' or 'Add Simple Link' in
the Media Window). With facts, source citations and submitters,
however, the link could only be created from the data item to the
media item, and not from the media item to the data item. Both
ways of creating these links are now supported. That is, if you
click 'Add Frame Link' or 'Add Simple Link' in the Media Window, you
will be able to create all of these kinds of links.

You can now also link addresses to media items, and, again, the link
can be created either from the address to the media item, or from the
media item to the address.

Easier, Quicker Data Entry, and Improved
usability across the program

Previously Family Historian supported auto-complete on many fields,
such as Place, Address, Occupation, Religion, Group/Caste and National
or Tribal Origin. Now Family Historian additionally supports a
new feature called auto-list for all of these fields and more.
Auto-list means that as you start typing, Family Historian will
display a dropdown list of values (of the relevant field type) that
match the characters you have typed so far. If you see the value
you want in the list, you can click on it, or use the arrow keys to
select it and select it by pressing Enter or the Tab key. In
tests, this made data entry significantly easier and faster.

In version 8, there is now full multilevel undo/redo on all changes
(including additions and deletions) to shapes in the
Diagram Window (see Diagrams - numerous
improvements including a major graphics update)

There is now also full multilevel undo/redo on all changes
(including additions and deletions) to shapes in the Map
Window (see Maps - innovative mapping tools that let
you do so much more).

When saving queries, charts, reports, etc, you can now see a
list of existing items of the same kind, so that you can easily avoid
existing names, and remind yourself of your preferred naming
conventions.

You now have a progress dialog with a cancel button which appears
when loading slow-to-load reports, and in other contexts.

Drag-and-drop is now more widely supported. For example, you
can used drag-and-drop to add, move and copy columns and filters in
the Query Window, and when configuring columns in the Records
Window. See Drag-and-Drop to
learn more.

As mentioned earlier with respect to books, the Windows
Snipping Tool on the Tools menu makes it easier than ever to
copy images. And there are now also more options for inserting
copied images into the program (see Web
Clipping).

In many contexts, including the Records Window, the Focus Window and
elsewhere, you can now view record links for any type of record, by
selecting "Record Links" on the context menu that appears when you
right-click on their record

Other usability improvements with respect to record lists and the
Records Window are described in Improvements
to the Records Window and Record Selector Dialogs.

Custom Fact Flags

Version 7 introduced the ability to set flags on any fact (event or
attribute). Facts could be flagged as Private,
Preferred, Tentative or Rejected.
Now in version 8 you can create your own custom fact flags.

Custom fact flags are set in the 'All' tab of the Property Box, as
follows: when viewing the relevant Individual (or Family) in the
Property Box, switch to the 'All' tab. To set a flag for a given
fact, right-click on the text of the fact field in the left-hand side
of the 'All' tab, click on 'Set Flag' in the dropdown menu that
appears, and select the required flag. If the flag does not yet
exist, click on '<New Flag>' on the same menu to create it.

Custom fact flags can be referenced in queries, smart folders,
columns, report fields, or elsewhere, like any other flag or field
item. They can also be accessed, created and set or unset by
plugins.

Improved support for high resolution monitors

Sometimes graphics features and icons could previously have appeared
to be small when displayed on high resolution monitors. Numerous
improvements have been made throughout the program to ensure that
graphics and icons are optimally sized.

Parallel installations of different versions

Users who wish to do so can now run older versions of Family
Historian alongside version 8, on the same computer. However,
care is needed with this feature. You should not edit the same project
on multiple different versions as this could lead to data loss. You
will be warned if you attempt to do so.

If you install version 8 on a computer that already has an earlier
version of Family Historian installed on it, your settings will be
copied to the new installation (see New Backup
and Restore Settings Tool for more details).

new features and improvements for
power-users

There is a new special plugin type called a "Smart Folder Plugin",
used in the context of smart folders which allows powerful flexibility
in the creation of smart folders. It uses a single entry-point:
FH_GetSmartFolderData (see documentation in the Plugin Help).

There is a new lua object in the Family Historian API: Named
List. A Named List object is used to access (but not
update) a Family Historian named list. The Named List object has
the following methods:

GetName

GetItemCount

GetItem

The new Address records are fully supported, and there is a new
value type: "address".

There are also 3 new API functions relating to named lists:

fhGetNamedListCount

fhGetNamedListByIndex

fhGetNamedList

All Family Historian plugins that use Lua libraries must now use
64-bit versions of those libraries, as Family Historian itself is now
64-bit (see 64 bit -
Family Historian can now handle much larger projects).

The FHR_Requirements title field in a plugin report is now
properly honoured (see also Enhancements to
Reports and Books).

20 new "built-in" functions (that is, functions used as expressions
within the program) have been added - see New
Functions (added in version 8) for details. Several of
these functions are used in the new Smart Folders, and some of them
are used in the new support for functions in the Expression
Entry Assistant tool.

A new parameter has been added to the fhGetFlagTag function, to
allow custom fact flags to be accessed
and created.

The Plugin Help has been extended and improved. There is a new
section "Item Pointers: Confusions and Pitfalls to Avoid", which is
recommended reading for all plugin authors. There are also new
