title: fhCreateItem(strTagOrShortcut [, ptrParent [, bReuseEmpties]])
text: functions fhCreateItem Description Creates a data item - either a record or a child item - and returns an item pointer to it. Note: If this function is called by a plugin running in the Plugin Editor/Debugger in Debug Mode, a warning message will be output to the Output pane if the function returns NULL. To create a new custom fact type, use the fhGetFactTag function with the bCreateIfNone parameter set to true. To create a new type of flag (either a record flag or a fact flag) use the fhGetFlagTag function, again with the bCreateIfNone parameter set to true. In both cases, however, once you have created the new item type (new type of fact or new type of flag), you can use fhCreateItem to create actual instances of that item type. Syntax ptrItem = fhCreateItem(strTagOrShortcut [, ptrParent [, bReuseEmpties]]) Parameters strTagOrShortcut String: Tag of Item to create, or shortcut of Item to create. Support for shortcuts was introduced in version 7.0. Currently shortcuts are only supported for metafields. For all other item types, you must use a tag. For metafields however, you cannot use a tag and must use a shortcut - see the discussion of Metafields and Shortcuts below. ptrParent Item Pointer (optional). Must be NULL or omitted if creating a record item. If creating a child item, this must point to its parent item. bReuseEmpties boolean (optional). From version 5.0.2. Default is false. If true, and if there is an 'empty' data item of the required type (no value and no child items), will return a pointer to this data item instead of creating a new one. Has no effect when creating record items or metafields. If you are creating a metafield, an empty metafield that matches the specified shortcut, will always be re-used, whether or not this flag is set. Returns ptrItem Item Pointer: for the created Item, or a NULL pointer if the create fails for any reason. Metafields and Shortcuts Metafields are a special kind of field that can be defined and created on an as-needed basis. They all have the same tag ("_FIELD"), but this tag cannot be used to create a metafield. Instead you have to use a shortcut. Family Historian metafields are used to hold the field data specified by Source Templates. These fields are created either as children of Source records, or as children of links to Source records (citations). Every metafield needs a field definition, which specifies the type of data that the metafield can hold, and other aspects of it. Family Historian metafields can have the following data types: text, name, date, place, address, repository, enumeration and URL. The field definitions are stored as fields within Source Template records. Source records have a field called 'Template' (with tag '_SRCT') which can store a link to a Source Template record. A Source record which has such a link is called a templated Source record (as opposed to a generic or free form Source record which has no such link). Before you can create a metafield for a Source record, or for a link to a Source record, the Source record itself must be linked to a Source Template record. When you create the metafield for the Source record, you must specify a metafield shortcut. The value of this shortcut must match a field definition within the linked Source Template record. If no field definition matches the metafield shortcut, or if the Source record is not linked to a Source Template record, the function will fail. A shortcut to a metafield normally looks something like this: "~TX-DOCUMENT_TITLE". The first character (a tilde) indicates that what follows is a shortcut. The next 3 characters specify the field type. The values are: Field Type 3-letter Type Prefix Text TX- Name NM- Date DT- Place PL- Address AD- Repository RP- Enumeration EN- URL UL- The remainder of the shortcut text is the code for the field definition (e.g. "DOCUMENT_TITLE" in our example) which is normally the field label, with spaces and non-alphanumeric characters replaced by an underscore. Once you have created a metafield, you can get and set its value in the usual way. For example, you can use fhGetValueAsText and fhSetValueAsText to get and set the values of Text, Name, Place and Enumeration metafields. You can use fhGetValueAsDate and fhSetValueAsDate to get and set the values of Date metafields. And you can use fhGetValueAsLink and fhSetValueAsLink to get and set the values of Repository metafields. It is possible, though not usually a good idea, to clear or delete the link from a Source record to a Source Template record after you have created metafields for the Source record or for one or more links to it. If you do this, the metafields will not be automatically deleted. They will be visible on the All tab of the Property Box, for the Source record or citation in question, as orphaned metafields. Metafields can be deleted like any other field, using the fhDeleteItem function. To learn more about metafields, see "Understanding Data References" in the main application Help (and especially the section "Data References and Metafields"). Creating Source Records of Different Types We saw in the previous section that what makes a Source record a templated Source record is that it has a link (using the _SRCT tag) to a Source Template record. Free form and generic Source records have no such link. So if you want to create a templated Source record, you need to create this link. If, for whatever reason, this link were somehow deleted, the Source record would revert to being a generic Source record. If it had metafields, it would still be a generic Source records. In that case it would be a generic Source record with orphaned metafields (see previous section). To create a free form Source record, you need to add a child item to the record item with tag "_FREE". This is a hidden tag. Users will not see it - not even in the 'All' tab of the Property Box. If a Source record has a '_FREE' tag (and doesn't have a '_SRCT' tag), it is a free form Source record. A generic Source record is simply any Source record which has no _SRCT link to a Source Template record, and no _FREE child tag. With free form sources, users can specify footnotes, short footnotes and bibliography entries. These are stored in child fields within the Source record, with tags _FOOT, _SHRT, and _BIBL respectively. These fields can contain style codes for enabling or disabling italics, bold and underline (,,,,,and ). Example Create a new Family Record and attach a Husband. ptrFam = fhCreateItem("FAM") -- now create the family record ptrLink = fhCreateItem("HUSB", ptrFam ) -- create a HUSB field in the family record fhSetValueAsLink(ptrLink, ptrDad) See Create Family Script for a full example.

title: fhDeleteItem(ptr)
text:
functions

fhDeleteItem

Description

Deletes the item - either a record item or a child item - indicated
by the item pointer. On execution the pointer will be set to Null.

Syntax

bOK = fhDeleteItem(ptr)

Parameters

ptr
Item pointer: Pointer to object to be deleted.

Returns

bOK
boolean: returns true on success and false on failure

Remarks

Deleting an item will delete all its child items and, in the case of
a record, all references to it. So, for example, deleting an
individual record will also delete all links to that record from any
family records. From version 8 onwards, deleting a place field
for a fact (event or attribute) will also cause the fact's address
field, if any, to be cleared, although the address field item will not
itself be deleted (see Special
Issues with Place and Address Fields for more on this).

In a loop that performs deletes, remember that after each call to
fhDeleteItem, the pointer passed to it as a parameter, will have a
Null value.

Example

ptrInd = fhNewItemPtr()
ptrInd:MoveToFirstRecord('INDI')
fhDeleteItem(ptrInd)
-- deletes the first Individual record in the family tree file

title: fhDisplayRichTextBox(rt[, strTitle[, hParentWnd]])
text:
functions

fhDisplayRichTextBox

Description

Displays the contents of a rich text object in a window, with a single
Close button.

There is no need to call fhUpdateDisplay before calling this function,
as there would be if you were using an IUP function to display a dialog
or message box.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

fhDisplayRichTextBox(rt[, strTitle[, hParentWnd]])

Parameters

rt
rich text: Rich Text to display
strTitle
Optional string. Title of dialog.
hParentWnd
Optional parent window handle ('light userdata'). If you are
calling the function from a dialog box, such as an IUP dialog box,
you must pass in the window handle of the dialog box - see second
example below.

Return Value

none

Remarks

Example
fhDisplayRichTextBox(fhNewRichText("An <u>important</u> point"))

require("iuplua");
iup.SetGlobal("CUSTOMQUITMESSAGE","YES");

local btn = iup.button{title="click me"};
local dlg=iup.dialog{ iup.vbox{ iup.label{title="Hello"}, btn}, title="Test Click", size="200x200"};
iup.SetAttribute(dlg, "NATIVEPARENT", fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND"));

function btn:action()
fhDisplayRichTextBox(fhNewRichText("An <u>important</u> point"), "Family Historian", dlg.HWND)
end

title: fhExhibitResponsiveness()
text:
functions

fhExhibitResponsiveness

Description

This function has only one purpose. It is used to signal to the
operating system that the current plugin (and indeed, Family Historian
itself) is still active, in order to prevent the operating system
categorising the application as "Not responding" and putting a message
to that effect on the application windows' caption bars.

Often a plugin may do some processing in a loop of some kind. If
the processing takes a long time, the operating system may wrongly
conclude that the program has stopped working. If a call to
fhExhibitResponsiveness is added within the processing loop, this will
signal to the operation system that the application is still
active. Care is needed however. In general, it is
recommended that a plugin should call fhExhibitResponsiveness as
infrequently as possible, to avoid unnecessary processing overhead.
But in order to prevent "Not responding" messages appearing, a plugin
will need to call the function at least once every 5 seconds.

In general, if a plugin needs to do some processing which is likely to
take a significant amount of time, it is recommended that plugin authors
should consider implementing a progress bar to display to the user, with
a Cancel button. Calling fhExhibitResponsiveness is not a
substitute for this.

See also fhSleep.

Minimum FH Version

7.0.7

Syntax

fhExhibitResponsiveness()

Parameters

(none)

Return Value

(none)

Example

fhExhibitResponsiveness();

title: fhFtfEncode(strPlainText)
text:
functions

fhFtfEncode

Description

Rich Text objects are encoded in eFTF syntax which contains special
commands. If you are constructing a text string, which you plan to
insert into a RichText object as rich text, you will need to use these
special commands in a string in FTF or eFTF syntax. However, it
may be that you need to add the contents of a (plain) text field to this
same text string. What if the field happens to contain some
characters which will have a special meaning in eFTF syntax? To be
quite certain that plain text will be treated as plain text, even if
added as part of a string in FTF or eFTF syntax, you should first call
fhFtfEncode on the string. This will remove all special meaning
from all special characters, if any.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

strEncoded = fhFtfEncode(strPlainText)

Parameters

strPlainText
String. The text to be encoded.

Return Value

strEncoded
The encoded text.

Example

strText = fhFtfEncode("2 * 2 < 4"); -- strText will contain "2 * 2 < 4" (the special meaning of '*' and '<' is removed)

title: fhFtfParamEncode(strPlainText)
text:
functions

fhFtfParamEncode

Description

Rich Text objects are encoded in eFTF syntax which contains special
commands, some of which take parameters. Some of these parameters may be
strings. When constructing the text for a string parameter, you
should normally enclose it in double quotes. Before doing so,
however, you should make the string 'safe' for use in this
context. To do so, a backslash must be added before various
special characters in the string - such as double quote ("), backslash
(\), less-than sign (<) or greater-than sign (>). The
function fhFtfParamEncode will do this for you and is the approved way
of ensuring that the string is safe.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

strEncoded = fhFtfParamEncode(strPlainText)

Parameters

strPlainText
String. The text to be encoded.

Return Value

strEncoded
The encoded text.

Example

strText = fhFtfParamEncode(strParam);

title: fhGetAppVersion()
text:
functions

fhGetAppVersion

Syntax

iVer1, iVer2, iVer3 = fhGetAppVersion()

Return Value

iVer2

iVer3

iVer1, iVer2, iVer3 = fhGetAppVersion()

fhMessageBox("Version number = " .. iVer1 .. "." .. iVer2 .. "." .. iVer3)

the current application version number is).

title: fhGetClipboardData(strFormat)
text:
functions

fhGetClipboardData

Description

Returns the current contents of the clipboard as a string in a
specified format.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

strText = fhGetClipboardFormat(strFormat)

Parameters

strFormat
String. Must be "HTML FORMAT" or "UNICODE TEXT".

Returns

strText
string or nil. The content of the clipboard in the specified

local sText = fhClipboardData("HTML FORMAT");

title: fhGetContextInfo(strInfoReqd)
text:
functions

fhGetContextInfo

Description

fhGetContextInfo provides access to the current Family Historian
context, which includes information on the current project folder,
project name and GEDCOM file information.

Syntax

var = fhGetContextInfo(strInfoReqd)

Parameters

strInfoReqd
string : Information required must be one of the following:

CI_PROJECT_NAME
Returns string - name of the currently open
project

CI_PROJECT_FILE
Returns string - current filename and path for
the project file

CI_GEDCOM_FILE
Returns string - current filename and path for
the GEDCOM File

CI_PROJECT_PUBLIC_FOLDER
Returns string - current project's public
folder path

CI_PROJECT_DATA_FOLDER
Returns string - current project's data folder
path

CI_PLUGIN_NAME
Returns string - current plugin name - if it
has one

CI_APP_DATA_FOLDER
Returns string - Family
Historian's data folder path. In general, it is
recommended that plugins should not use this folder at
all. It is used to store Family Historian's own
application data and changes to it are unlikely to be
safe. The option to locate this folder is only
provided because there are a very small number of cases
(such as enhanced management of plugins or custom queries)
where it can be useful for a plugin to be able to access
this folder.

If you do access this folder, please do not create any new
sub-folders within it, or store any plugin data anywhere in
it or make any changes to the contents of the files in
it. Doing so might work for a while with for some
versions of Family Historian, but might cause major problems
with later versions because of unanticipated changes to
Family Historian's own internal data formats. If in
doubt, contact Calico Pie by emailing
support@family-historian.co.uk, before accessing this
folder, to confirm that what you wish to do is safe and
won't cause problems in the future.

CI_APP_MODE
Returns string - one of the
following:

"Project Mode"

"Gedcom Mode"

"Gedcom Mode (new)"

CI_STRING_ENCODING

This parameter value is supported from version 6
onwards.

Returns a string - the current string encoding used by
the Family Historian API. This will be either 'ANSI'
or 'UTF-8'. The current string encoding used by the Family
Historian API will be ANSI if the script file itself is in
ANSI, and UTF-8 if the script itself is in UTF-8.

Family Historian expects all strings supplied to the
Family Historian API functions and methods to be encoded
used the current string encoding. Equally, all strings
returned by Family Historian functions and methods will be
encoded using the current string encoding. The only
exceptions to this are the two conversion functions fhConvertANSItoUTF8
and fhConvertUTF8toANSI
which specify the string encodings that they require and
return.

Bear in mind that with all constant strings used in the
Family Historian API (such as the text 'ANSI' and 'UTF-8'
returned by this function), you never need to know if they
are ANSI or UTF-8 because, effectively, they are always
both. All simple (unaccented) alphabetic characters, upper
and lower case, and all digits and simple punctuation
characters (quotes, full-stop, comma, brackets, hyphens,
underscore, space character and end-of-line characters,
etc) are identical in ANSI and UTF-8.

Please note: the 'current string encoding' mentioned
above applies to the Family Historian API only. Other
Lua library functions may assume different encodings.
The conversion functions mentioned above can be used to
convert strings if necessary.

CI_APP_HWND
This parameter value is supported from version 7
onwards.

Returns a light userdata value (see Lua
documentation) - the window handle of the main Family
Historian application window.

CI_PARENT_HWND
This parameter value is supported from version 7
onwards.

Returns a light userdata value (see Lua
documentation) - the window handle to use as a parent for
any dialogs you wish to display (often the same as
CI_APP_HWND, but not necessarily the same)..

CI_BOOK_CONTEXT
This parameter value is supported from version 7
onwards.

Returns a boolean value - true if the plugin is a report
plugin being run in the context of a book. False
otherwise.

CI_BOOK_ITEM_HEADING
This parameter value is supported from version 7
onwards.

Returns a string. If the plugin is a report
plugin, being run in the context of a book, the string is
the heading to use for the first top-level section in the
report. It includes the chapter number if appropriate,
and is overridable by the user. In any other context,
the string returned is empty.

Return Value

var
type varies depending on CI type - see above for details

Remarks

Where the APP_MODE is "Gedcom Mode (New)" the current Gedcom file is
unsaved and has no name and therefore CI_GEDCOM_FILE will return an
empty string.

The following example adds all the possible values for
fhGetContextInfo and then passes the results as tables to the result
window:

a = {}
a[1] = "CI_PROJECT_NAME"
a[2] = "CI_PROJECT_FILE"
a[3] = "CI_GEDCOM_FILE"
a[4] = "CI_PROJECT_PUBLIC_FOLDER"
a[5] = "CI_PROJECT_DATA_FOLDER"
a[6] = "CI_PLUGIN_NAME"
a[7] = "CI_APP_DATA_FOLDER"
a[8] = "CI_APP_MODE"
a[9] = "CI_STRING_ENCODING"

b={}

for i=1,9 do
b[i] = fhGetContextInfo(a[i])
end

fhOutputResultSetColumn("Name", "text", a, 8, 125)
fhOutputResultSetColumn("Value", "text", b, 8, 500)
fhOutputResultSetTitles("fhGetContextInfo values")
The following code is perhaps a more elegant way to achieve the same
aim:

a= {
"CI_PROJECT_NAME",
"CI_PROJECT_FILE",
"CI_GEDCOM_FILE",
"CI_PROJECT_PUBLIC_FOLDER",
"CI_PROJECT_DATA_FOLDER",
"CI_PLUGIN_NAME",
"CI_APP_DATA_FOLDER",
"CI_APP_MODE",
"CI_STRING_ENCODING"
}

b={}

for i,strCI in pairs(a) do
b[i] = fhGetContextInfo(strCI)
end

fhOutputResultSetColumn("Name", "text", a, #a, 125)
fhOutputResultSetColumn("Value", "text", b,#a, 500)
fhOutputResultSetTitles("fhGetContextInfo values")

title: fhGetCurrentPropertyBoxRecord()
text:
functions

fhGetCurrentPropertyBoxRecord

Description

Returns a pointer to the record currently displaying in the Property
Box, or a NULL pointer if no record is currently displaying in the
Property Box. Bear in mind that records of any type can be
displayed in the Property Box, so the result is not necessarily a
pointer to an Individual record.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

ptrRec = fhGetCurrentPropertyBoxRecord()

Parameters

(none)
.

Return Value

ptrRec
item pointer: New pointer to record item currently displaying in
the Property Box. Null if none.

Example

ptrRec = fhGetCurrentPropertyBoxRecord()

if (ptrRec:IsNotNull()) then
fhMessageBox(fhGetDisplayText(ptrRec)) end

title: fhGetCurrentRecordSel([strTag])
text:
functions

fhGetCurrentRecordSel

Description

Returns a table of currently selected records (from the main application), when the optional
parameter is supplied only selected records matching the parameter are returned.

Syntax

fhGetCurrentRecordSel([strTag])

Parameters

strTag
The tag of the record type required. The options are:

INDI

Individual

FAM

Family

NOTE

Note

SOUR

Source

REPO

Repository

SUBR

Submitter

SUBM

Submission

OBJE

Multimedia Object

Return Value

Record List
A table containing the selected pointer objects.

Example

tblIndi = fhGetCurrentRecordSel('INDI')
for i=1, #tblIndi do
fhMessageBox(fhGetDisplayText(tblIndi[i]))
end

Obtains the currently selected Individual records and populates a table of pointers tblIndi.
#tblIndi is the number of elements in the table. It then cycles through the records

title: fhGetDataClass(ptr)
text:
functions

fhGetDataClass

Description

Returns the data classification for the item. This function is
similar to fhGetValueType in some
ways, but there are some important differences. Only items which
actually have values, have a value type. Some items, such as records
and flags, do not store values of their own (although of course they
may have child items which do), and hence have no value type, but all
items have a data classification.

Syntax

strDataClass = fhGetDataClass(ptr)

Parameters

ptr
Item pointer

Returns

strDataClass
string: returns one of the following.

Class
Description
Value Type

(see fhGetValueType)

text
a general single-line text item
text

longtext
a text item that can extend over multiple lines
text

richtext
a text item that can extend over multiple lines and which
can contain wordprocessing features such varying fonts,
character styles (bold, italics, underline, strikeout),
paragraph styles (indent, bullets, paragraph alignment),
record links, web links, embedded source citations, tables,
and more
richtext

name
a name
text

place
a place - with place-parts comma-separated
text

address
an address or place detail, optionally with comma-separated parts
text

latlong
latitude and longitude
text

url
a web address (e.g. "https://www.family-historian.co.uk")
text

enumword
a word (or short phrase) from a fixed choice of values
text

enumlist
a comma-separated list of words (or short phrases) from a
fixed choice of values
text

word
a word (or short phrase)
text

word2
a word (or short phrase), but more tightly restricted
(e.g. brackets are not allowed)
text

wordlist
a comma-separated list of words (or short phrases)
text

rect
a set of 4 coordinate values
text

age
age data (usually in years, months or days)
age

link
a record link
link

date
a date
date

integer
a number
integer

blob
a multimedia item
blob

record
a record
(none)

flag
a flag
(none)

complex
an item which has no value of its own (and doesn't fall
into any other classification - such as record or flag).
(none)

metafield
Metafields are a special type of field that are defined
using special data definitions
(metadata). Metafields are currently only used in
Source records and source citations, to implement source
template fields. The field definitions (metadata) in
these cases are stored as fields in Source Template records.
Text, date or link, depending on the metafield. See also GetMetaFieldType.

Example

ptri = fhNewItemPtr()
ptri:MoveToFirstRecord("INDI")
ptrBirth = fhGetItemPtr(ptri,"INDI.BIRT.DATE")
fhMessageBox(fhGetDisplayText(ptrBirth) .. " Class: " .. fhGetDataClass(ptrBirth))

title: fhGetDataList(strType[, strQualifier])
text:
functions

fhGetDataList

Description

Returns a table containing a list of strings in alphabetical
order. The strings are data values used in the current project -
e.g. places, religions, etc. The function takes 2 parameters
(second is optional), specifying the data list required.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

table = fhGetDataList(strType[,
strQualifier])

Parameters

strType
String. This must be one of the following: "PLACES",
"ADDRESSES", "OCCUPATIONS", "RELIGIONS", "CASTES", "ORIGINS",
"SOURCE_TYPES"
strQualifier
String. Optional. Is ignored unless strType is
"ADDRESSES". In that case, if you supply a place name, the
table returned will be restricted to a list of addresses currently
associated with that exact place name (case-insensitive match), in
facts in the current project.

Returns

table
table containing list of strings

Example

local t = fhGetDataList("ADDRESSES", "London, England");
local sText = '';
for k, v in ipairs(t) do
sText = sText .. v .. '
';
end
fhMessageBox(sText);

title: fhGetDisplayText(ptr,[strDataReference [, strDisplayOption]])
text:
functions

fhGetDisplayText

Description

Returns a short string of text that is suitable to be used as a
representation for the item in question (in lists and elsewhere).

For example:

If the item in question is an Individual record item, it will return
the name of the person whose record it is.

If the item in question is a fact item, it will return a brief
summary of the important details.

fhGetDisplayText will always return a string, although it may be an
empty one.

See also fhGetItemText. The two
functions return very similar results when fhGetDisplayText is used with
the 'min' option; but fhGetItemText supports qualifiers (e.g. you can
extract a surname from a name) where fhGetDisplayText doesn't.

Syntax

strText = fhGetDisplayText(ptr,[strDataReference [, strDisplayOption]])

Parameters

ptr
pointer

strDataReference
string (optional): a Data Reference. If not provided the display
text for the current position of the pointer will be returned.
If the data reference contains a qualifier, this will be ignored.

strDisplayOption
string (optional): specifies more detail about the content of the
text to be returned

std
The default.

min
For many data items, the text will be returned will be the
same as for 'std'. However, there are some
differences. For attributes, the attribute value (alone)
will be returned (for 'std', the attribute label, and any date
or place information would also be included). For
places, dates, flags, and various other value types, if 'min'
is set, the value only is returned. If 'std' is set, a
label will be included. See example below.

Return Value

strText
String: Displayable value, or an empty string if no data item

Example

The code below will display the Name, followed by the Birth Fact
Information, if one exists, for the of the first individual record in
the currently opened project.

ptr = fhNewItemPtr()
ptr:MoveToFirstRecord("INDI")

-- Displays the Name of the Individual
strPointerDescription = fhGetDisplayText(ptr)
fhMessageBox(strPointerDescription)

-- Displays the Birth Information for the Individual
strPointerDescription = fhGetDisplayText(ptr,'~.BIRT')
fhMessageBox(strPointerDescription)

-- Displays the Birth Place for the Individual without the label 'Place: '
strPointerDescription = fhGetDisplayText(ptr,'~.BIRT.PLAC', 'min')
fhMessageBox(strPointerDescription)

title: fhGetFactTag(strFactName, strFactType, strRecTag, bCreateIfNone)
text:
functions

fhGetFactTag

Description

Returns the tag for a given fact (event or attribute). The fact can
be either a standard, such as 'Birth', or a custom one, such as
'Hobby'. If you set the bCreateIfNone parameter to true,
you can use this function to create a new custom fact type. If you do
this, you will then be able to use the returned tag to create facts of
that type in the current project using the fhCreateItem
function.

If bCreateIfNone is not true, this
function will return an empty string if the fact type is not found. If
bCreateIfNone is true, but the fact cannot
be created for whatever reason, the function will return an empty
string for the tag. In addition, in this case, it will return a second
string which describes the error.

Syntax

strTag, strError = fhGetFactTag(strFactName,
strFactType, strRecTag, bCreateIfNone)

Parameters

strFactName
Name of fact (event or attribute).
strFactType
string: Value

Event
Events are facts like Birth, Marriage, and Death.

Attribute
Attributes are facts like Occupation or Education.

strRecTag
string: Value

INDI
For an Individual fact

FAM
For a family fact

bCreateIfNone
boolean: true or false. Set this to true if you wish the fact tag
to be created if it doesn't already exist.
Be very careful to use the words 'true' or
'false' in lower case (without the quotes) for the boolean value.
Using upper case or mixed case, for boolean values, will probably
not be reported as an error, but will not be correctly interpreted
by Lua.

Returns

strTag
Tag returned (will be an empty string if the fact was not found or
couldn't be created).
strError

nil
Normal value if the tag string has been returned

Invalid fact name
Fact name is invalid

Create failed
Only returned when bCreateIfNone is true, and the create
failed

Not Found
Tag is not found. Only occurs when bCreateIfNone is
false.

Example

strTag = fhGetFactTag("Birth", "Event", "INDI", false)
fhMessageBox("Birth Tag: " .. strTag)
strTag, strError = fhGetFactTag(" Excommunication", "Event", "INDI", true)
if strTag ~= "" then
fhMessageBox("Tag: " .. strTag)
else
fhMessageBox("Error: " .. strError)
end

In this example, the second call to fhGetFactTag will fail because a
fact name cannot begin with a space.

title: fhGetFactTypeInfo(strTag, strType[, strFlags])
text:
functions

fhGetFactTypeInfo

Description

Returns a table of information about a specified type of fact (event
or attribute). The fact can be either a standard, such as
'Birth', or a custom one, such as 'Hobby'. The amount of
information in the table will depend on the value string you supply as
a parameter.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

tInfo = fhGetFactTypeInfo(strTag,
strType[, strFlags])

Parameters

strTag
string. A tag identifying the required fact type.
strType
string. The type of fact type required:

"INDI" = Individual fact type

"FAM" = Family fact type

strFlags
string. Optional. If not supplied (or empty) a minimum
amount of information will be returned in the table. Possible
flags are:

Flags
Meaning

(none)
A minimum amount of information will be returned in the table:

bAttribute

bHidden

all
Effectively sets all other flags to true

main

sTag

sName

sLabel

sAbbr

bStandard

templates

sTemplate (the sentence template for this fact)

sSummaryTemplate (if there is one - the template used in
the Fact tab of the Property Box)

if the 'roles' flag is also set, you will get the same
strings (if available) for each role

timeframe

sTimeFrame (if there is one)

autocreatenote

sAutoCreateNote (if there is one)

roles

If set, the table will contain a sub-table called 'roles'
which will contain details of each role. For each role,
the values returned will be:

sName

sPastTense

sTemplate (if the 'templates' flag is also set - see
'templates' above)

sSummaryTemplate (if the 'templates' flag is also set -
see 'templates' above)

Unrecognised flags are ignored. Flags are
case-insensitive. Flags can be combined in a single string by
separating them with a vertical bar. For example, if strFlags is
"main | roles", the table will contain main details, and witness roles
(if any). There is no point in combining 'all' with any other
flags, but it's not invalid to do so.

Returns

tInfo
Return type depends on the strType. It is a string for
label. For all other strType it is a boolean

Example

local t = fhGetFactTypeInfo("MARR", "FAM", "MAIN | ROLES | TEMPLATES | TIMEFRAME | AUTOCREATENOTE");
if t["bAttribute"] then
fhMessageBox("It's an attribute");
else
fhMessageBox("It's an event");
end

title: fhGetFlagTag(strFlagName, bCreateIfNone[, bFactFlag])
text:
functions

fhGetFlagTag

Description

Returns the tag for a given flag which, depending on the optional
third parameter, can be either a record flag or a fact flag. The flag
can be either a standard ('Private' or 'Living'), or a custom one. If
you set the bCreateIfNone parameter to true, you can use this function
to create a new type of flag. If you do this, you will then be able to
use the returned tag to create instances of flags of that type in the
current project.

If bCreateIfNone is not true, this function will return an empty
string if the flag type is not found. If CreateIfNone is true, but the
flag type cannot be created for whatever reason, the function will
return an empty string for the tag. In addition, in this case, it will
return a second string which describes the error.

Note: Once you have the tag for a flag (either a record
flag or a fact flag), you can then use it to set the flag for an
Individual record or for a fact (either an Individual fact or a Family
fact). "Setting a flag" just means creating a suitable child
item with the relevant tag. All such flags must be created as
children of a "Flags" item (with the tag "_FLGS"), which may or may
not already exist. If it doesn't exist, you will need to create
it. If the flag you wish to set (item you wish to create) is a record
flag, the "Flags" item will be a child of the "INDI" record
item. If the flag you wish to set is a fact flag, the
"Flags" item will be a child of the fact item. For example,
suppose you have used the fhGetFlagTag function to get or
create a custom fact flag, "Important". The tag for this will be
automatically generated as "__IMPORTANT". You can now set this
flag on any fact (event or attribute). Let us suppose that you
wish to set this fact flag on a person's Birth event. You will
need to use the fhCreateItem
function to create it as a child of the "Flags" item which has this
data reference: "INDI.BIRT._FLGS". So before you can create the
child item that represents your new "Important" flag, the flag (type)
itself must have been created if it didn't already exist, the 'Birth'
event within the relevant record must exist, and the "Flags" item
within that Birth event must also exist. Your flag (instance)
must then be created as a child of this "Flags" item. So if
"pFlags" is an item pointer that points to the "Flags" item within the
Birth event, you would use this call to create the required fact
flag instance: fhCreateChild(pFlags, "__IMPORTANT")

Minimum FH Version

Version 8 if the third parameter (bFactFlag) is used

Syntax

strTag, strError = fhGetFlagTag(strFlagName,
bCreateIfNone[, bFactFlag])

Parameters

strFlagName
Name of the flag.
bCreateIfNone
boolean: Set this to true if you wish the flag tag to be created
if it doesn't already exist.
bFactFlag
boolean: Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied.
Set this to true if the flag you want is a fact flag (standard or
custom). If not supplied, or if false, the flag will be a
record flag.

Tip: Be very careful to use the words 'true'
or false' in lower case (without the quotes) for boolean values.
Using upper case or mixed case, for boolean values, will probably
not be reported as an error, but will not be correctly interpreted
by lua.

Returns

strTag
Tag returned (empty string if the flag was not found or couldn't
be created).
strError

nil
Normal value the Tag string has been returned

Invalid flag name
Flag name is invalid

Create failed
Create failed only occurs when bCreateIfNone is
true

Not Found
Tag not found only occurs when bCreateIfNone is
false

Example

strNewFlag = 'MyNewFlag'
strTag, strError = fhGetFlagTag(strNewFlag,false)
if strTag == '' then
-- Flag Not Found
strTag, strError = fhGetFlagTag(strNewFlag,true)
if not strError == nil then
fhMessageBox('Error Creating Flag '..strError)
else
fhMessageBox('Flag Created : '..strTag)
end
end
fhMessageBox('Tag for Flag is '..strTag)

title: fhGetGedcomInfo(ptrItem)
text:
functions

fhGetGedcomInfo

Description

This function returns information about how a given data item is defined
in the GEDCOM spec - if it is. Some data items may have no direct GEDCOM equivalent.
To learn more about the data returned by this function, see the GEDCOM spec.

Syntax

bRet, iLevel, sGedcomTag, iMin, iMax, iMaxSize, iMaxConts,
iMaxConcs = fhGetGedcomInfo(ptrItem)

Parameters

ptrItem
Item Pointer: A data item

Returns

bRet
Rets true if and only if Gedcom data was found for this data item. If
this value is false, all other values should be ignored.
iLevel
The Gedcom level. Record items have level 0. 'Child' items of record
items, have level 1. Their children have level 2 - and so on.
sGedcomTag
The item's Gedcom tag.
iMin
The minimum number of items of this type, allowed in this context.
iMax
The maximum number of items of this type, allowed in this context.
iMaxSize
The maximum text length for items of this type, in this context.
iMaxConts
The maximum number of CONT continuation lines that this item may have.
iMaxConcs
The maximum number of CONC continuation lines that this item may have.

Remarks

A value of -1 returned for iMax, iMaxSize, iMaxConts or iMaxConcs means
'many' or 'no limit'. A data item that has an iMin value which is greater
than 0 is effectively mandatory.

title: fhGetIniFileValue(strFile, strSection, strKey, strValueType, varDefault)
text:
functions

fhGetIniFileValue

Description

Returns the value of a given named value (identified by a 'key') in an
Inifile. Inifiles are a standard way of storing setting
information and similar data in a text format file, in Windows.
The named values are on separate lines, grouped into sections.
Section names are on a line of their own, within square brackets.
The name for each value is called a 'key', and it is separated from the
value of the named value by an equals sign. For example, suppose a
text file contained the following text only:

[Report Options]

Header Line Depth=50

This file could be treated as an Inifile (if in an appropriate text
format) containing only one named value (50). The key for
this value is "Header Line Depth", and it belongs within the section
"Report Options".

For more information about Inifiles, see fhSetIniFileValue.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

var= fhGetIniFileValue(strFile,
strSection, strKey, strValueType, varDefault)

Parameters

strFile
String: the full file name, including path (e.g. "C:\Program
Data\Calico Pie\Family Historian\Plugins\New Report.fhr").
strSection
String: The section.
strKey
String: The key.
strValueType
String: This must be "integer", "text" or "bool", depending on the
type of the value being returned.
varDefault
Variable Type: Can be a text string, an integer or a boolean,
depending on the value of strValueType. Is the default value
to be returned if the value is not found. If a default value
is not supplied, a default value of 0 will be used for an integer, a
default value of an empty string will be used for text, and a
default value of false will be used for a boolean.

Return Value

var
The value returned as a text string, integer or boolean, depending
on the value of the strValueType parameter.

Example

strFooterRight = fhGetIniFileValue(strFile, "Report Options", "Footer - Right", "text")

title: fhGetLabelledText(ptr, strLabel)
text:
functions

fhGetLabelledText

Description

Requires version 5.0.9 or later. This function is almost
identical in function to the built-in function GetLabelledText.
It retrieves a section of text from a specified long text field (e.g.
a note or address field). The required portion of text is identified
by a short text label that is passed as a parameter to the
function. The function will search for a paragraph that begins
with the specified label. For example, if you called the
function using the label "Confirmed:", the function would search the
specified long text field for a paragraph beginning with this label..
If it found it, it would return the text that came immediately after
that label, up to the end of the paragraph. The label must not
contain any paragraph breaks within it.

See also fhSetLabelledText.

Syntax

strValue, bExists =fhGetLabelledText(ptr,
strLabel)

Parameters

ptr
item pointer

strLabel
Label to search for.

Returns

strValue
string: Text value of the item. Will be an empty string if the
label has no value or is not found.

bExists
boolean: If you need to check whether the label actually exists
or not, use this value. It will be false if and only if the label
is not found.

Remarks

The value returned will include hidden text if any.
Label-matching is case-insensitive.

Example

ptr = fhNewItemPtr()
ptr:MoveToFirstRecord('INDI')
ptrBirthNote = fhGetItemPtr(ptri,'~.BIRT.NOTE2')
fhMessageBox(fhGetLabelledText(ptrBirthNote, 'Confirmed:'))

title: fhGetPluginDataFileName([strScope[, bFolder]])
text:
functions

fhGetPluginDataFileName

Description

fhGetPluginDataFileName provides a file or folder name for
plugins to use to store settings or other data, on a per-project,
per-user, or per-machine basis. For example, the function can be
used to store the last settings used, for a specific project. If the
bFolder flag is set, the function will ensure that the full path name
returned exists, as a folder. If the bFolder flag is not set, the
function will ensure that all folders, mentioned in the path name
returned exist - creating them them if necessary - except the last part,
which the plugin can then itself create as either a file or
folder.

The plugin name is used as the last part of the string returned.
An empty string is returned if the plugin does not yet have a name, or
if an error occurs.

The function will create a "Plugin Data" folder in the project folder
automatically if one does not exist and return the name of a file or
folder to use.
Syntax

fhGetPluginDataFileName([strScope[,
bFolder]])

Parameters

strScope
Requires version 5.0.8 or later. Specifies whether the
settings or other data are to be stored on a per-project, per-user
or per-machine basis.

CURRENT_PROJECT
The default. The returned path is to a file or
folder within the folder, 'Plugin Data', in the current
project folder. The application must be in
project mode. The returned path will be:

<path to current project folder>\Plugin
Data\<plugin name>

CURRENT_USER

The returned path is to a file or folder within the
folder, 'Plugin Data' in the Family Historian application
data area for the current user. The returned path will
be:

<path to application data for current user>\Calico
Pie\Family Historian\Plugin Data\<plugin name>

LOCAL_MACHINE
The returned path is to a file or folder with the folder,
'Data' in the Plugins folder. The returned path will
be:

<path to Family Historian plugins
folder>\Data\<plugin name>

bFolder
Requires version 5.0.8 or later. boolean. False by default.
If true, the returned path is treated as a path to a folder which
will be created if it does not exist.

Return Value

strFileName
The filename / folder name which should be used for storing
settings and other data for the plugin.

Remarks

Note: If bFolder is not true, the file or folder is not automatically
created. See examples below for different methods of use:

Example
--[[
@Title: Save Settings File
@Author: Calico Pie 2011
@LastUpdated: March 2011
@Description: Example of Reading and Writing a simple settings file, it only supports simple string variables.
]]
-- functions

-- Check for File
function file_exists(name)
local f=io.open(name,"r")

if f~=nil then io.close(f) return true

else
return false
end
end
-- Split a String
function string:split(sep)

local sep, fields = sep or ":", {}
local pattern = string.format("([^%s]+)", sep)

self:gsub(pattern, function(c) fields[#fields+1] = c end)

return fields
end

-- Save Settings
function savesettings(settings,strFileName)
file,err = io.open( strFileName, "w" )

if err then
error('unable to write settings file:'..strFileName)
end

for k,v in pairs(settings) do
file:write(k..'='..v..'\n')

print(k,v)
end
file:close()
end
function loadsettings(strFileName)

if not(file_exists(strFileName)) then
-- Set Default settings
settings = {['filename']="myfile.txt",
['prompt']="true",
}

else
-- Load Settings File
tblsettings = {}
-- read the file in table 'lines'
for line in io.lines(strFileName) do

fields = line:split('=')
tblsettings[fields[1]] = fields[2]

end
end
return tblsettings
end

-- Main Script
settingfile = fhGetPluginDataFileName("CURRENT_PROJECT")

mysettings = loadsettings(settingfile)
-- Update a setting
mysettings['prompt']='no'

-- Add or update a setting
mysettings['greeting']='hello world'
-- Save Settings to file
savesettings(mysettings,settingfile)

title: fhGetQualifiedRecordId(ptr)
text:
functions

fhGetQualifiedRecordId

Description

Returns the record id of the record item as a string, with a prefix
character that indicates type. Qualified record ids are unique
across all record types, within a project.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

sRecordId = fhGetQualifiedRecordId(ptr)

Parameters

ptr
Item Pointer: pointer for which the qualified record Id is
required. If the pointer is pointing to an item which is not a
record (e.g. a child of a record) an empty string will be returned.

Remarks

Record ids in Family Historian are unique within record type. A
qualified record id adds a single letter prefix to the record id, which
indicates the record type. The correct letter prefixes (which are
always capitalised) are given by the table below:

Letter Prefix
Record Type

H

Header

F

Family

I

Individual

O

Media

N

Note

R

Repository

S

Source

U

Submitter

B

Submission

P

Place

A

Address

E

Research Note

T

Source template

Returns

sRecordId
string: The qualified record Id for the record.

Example

local ptr = fhNewItemPtr()
ptr:MoveToFirstRecord('INDI')
local sRecordId = fhGetQualifiedRecordId(ptr)
fhMessageBox(fhGetDisplayText(ptr).." [".. sRecordId .. "]")

title: fhIndGetFactList(ptr[, bIncWitnessFacts[, bIncTimelineFacts[, bTimelinePrefsOnly[, bNarrStyle[, bResolveExclusions[, bExcludePrivateFacts[, bExcludeRejectedFacts]]]]]]])
text:
functions

fhIndGetFactList

Description

Returns a list of facts associated with an Individual record.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

table = fhIndGetFactList(ptr[,
bIncWitnessFacts[, bIncTimelineFacts[, bTimelinePrefsOnly[,
bNarrStyle[, bResolveExclusions[, bExcludePrivateFacts[,
bExcludeRejectedFacts]]]]]]])

Parameters

ptr
Item pointer. Must point to an Individual record (if it points to
any other kind of item, the table returned will be empty)
bIncWitnessFacts
Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied. Set this
to true to include witnessed facts.
bIncTimelineFacts
Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied. Set this
to true to include timeline facts. These are facts about
close-relatives - such as the birth and death of parents, siblings,
children etc. Timeline facts can optionally be displayed in
the Facts tab of the Property Box.
bTimelinePrefsOnly
Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied. Is
ignored unless bIncTimelineFacts is true. Set this to true if
you want timeline facts to be limited to whatever the user specified
as their preference for timeline facts. Otherwise, the
timeline facts will be returned as if the user had ticked all
options. The only preference which does not apply is the death
date exclusion preference (see Timeline options accessible from the
Property Box). That preference is ignored in all cases by this
function.
bNarrStyle
Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied. Set this
to true if you want the returned list of facts and witness links to
be a suitable list for generating a narrative report. This
means that if a person is a witness to a fact more than once, they
will get a witness link for each occurrence.
bResolveExclusions
Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied. Is
ignored if bNarrStyle is false. Should normally be set to true
if bNarrStyle is true. If true, a fact, or an instance of a
person as a witness, will be excluded if the narrative sentence is
marked for exclusion, or if a fact node is automatically marked for
exclusion because the person's role as principal for the fact is
eclipsed by their role as a witness (see the main program help for
the Witnesses window for more on narrative sentences).
bExcludePrivateFacts
Optional. Defaults to false if not supplied. If true,
any facts which have the Private flag set will be
excluded (fact flags can be set in the Facts tab of the Property
box).
bExcludeRejectedFacts
Optional. Defaults to true if not supplied. If true, any
facts which have the Rejected flag set will be excluded
(fact flags can be set in the Facts tab of the Property box).

Return Value

table
Table contains a list of item pointers to facts and - if
bIncWitnessFacts is true - possibly also item pointers to (witness)
links to facts. If bIncTimelineFacts is false, the facts in
question may be contained in either the ptr Individual's own record
(e.g. birth or death), or in family records in which the ptr
Individual features as a spouse (e.g. marriage or divorce). If
bIncTimelineFacts is true, the facts may be belong to Individual or
Family records for the Individual's immediate family (parents,
spouses, siblings, children and grandchildren). It is up to
the caller to identify the type, meaning and record location of each
ptr in the table.

Remarks

The facts returned are in chronlogical order.

Example

local table = fhIndGetFactList(pi,true,true,false,true,true)

title: fhInitialise(iMinVer1 [, iMinVer2 [, iMinVer3, [, strSaveRequirements]])
text:
functions

fhInitialise

Description

This is a special function. It isn't necessary to call it, but if
it is called, it should be the first function called in the plugin, and
it should only be called once. It allows any plugin to specify
minimum Family Historian version requirements. And it also allows
a plugin (unless it is a read-only plugin) to require or recommend that
any unsaved changes made to the current file or project be saved, prior
to running the plugin.

It is an error to call this function after calling any function that
changes data in any way.

Syntax

bResult = fhInitialise(iMinVer1
[, iMinVer2 [, iMinVer3, [, strSaveRequirements]])

Parameters

iMinVer1
The first digit of the minimum version of Family Historian that is
required to run this plugin.

iMinVer2 (optional)
The second digit of the minimum version of Family Historian that
is required to run this plugin (defaults to zero if not supplied).
iMinVer3 (optional)
The third digit of the minimum version of Family Historian that is
required to run this plugin (defaults to zero if not supplied).
strSaveRequirements (optional)
String: Must be blank for read-only plugins (e.g. report type
plugins). For other plugins, if supplied, it must be one of
the following:

save_recommended

If there are any unsaved changes, a dialog box will tell
the user that saving changes is recommended, and ask if
he/she wishes to save now. The dialog box will have 3
buttons: Yes, No and Cancel. If the user clicks Yes,
changes will be saved, and the function will return
true. If the user clicks No, changes will not be saved
and the function will return false. If the clicks
Cancel, the function will not return, and the plugin will
terminate immediately.

save_required
If there are any unsaved changes, a dialog box will tell
the user that saving changes is required, and ask if he/she
wishes to save now. The dialog box will have 2
buttons: OK and Cancel. If the user clicks OK, changes
will be saved, and the function will return true. If the
clicks Cancel, the function will not return, and the plugin
will terminate immediately.

.

Return Value

bResult
The value returned will always be true (if the function returns at
all), unless the "save_recommended" option is used, and the user
(when prompted to save unsaved changes), clicks 'No', in which case
it will return false.

ExampleS

fhInitialise(7)
fhInitialise(7,0)
fhInitialise(7,0,0)
fhInitialise(7,0,0, "save_required")
fhInitialise(7,0,0, "save_recommended")

title: fhMessageBox(strMessage[,strMessageBoxFormat[,strMessageBoxIcon[, hParentWnd]]])
text:
functions

fhMessageBox

Description

Displays a message box with a choice of various buttons (or just an
'OK' button if not otherwise specified). Returns the button clicked on
as a text string.

There is no need to call fhUpdateDisplay before calling this function,
as there would be if you were using an IUP function to display a message
box.

Syntax

strButton = fhMessageBox(strMessage[,strMessageBoxFormat[,strMessageBoxIcon[, hParentWnd]]])

Parameters

strMessage
string: A message text to be displayed
strMessageBoxFormat
Specifies the number and type of buttons. If not supplied or an
empty string (""), defaults to "MB_OK". Options are:

MB_OK
OK Button Only

MB_ABORTRETRYIGNORE
3 Buttons Abort,Retry and Ignore

MB_OKCANCEL
2 Buttons OK and Cancel

MB_RETRYCANCEL
2 Buttons Retry and Cancel

MB_YESNO
2 Buttons Yes and No

MB_YESNOCANCEL
3 Buttons Yes, No and Cancel

strMessageBoxIcon
Specifies an icon to display with the message (the actual icons
will vary slightly depending on the version of windows installed):

MB_ICONEXCLAMATION

MB_ICONINFORMATION

MB_ICONQUESTION

MB_ICONSTOP

hParentWnd
Requires version 7 or later. Optional parent window handle
('light userdata'). If you are calling the function from a
dialog box, such as an IUP dialog box, you must pass in the window
handle of the dialog box - see second example below.

Return Value

strButton

One of the following strings will be returned, based on the
button pressed by the user:

OK

Cancel

Abort

Retry

Ignore

Yes

No

Remarks

Example
fhMessageBox("Hello World", "MB_OK", "MB_ICONEXCLAMATION")
res = fhMessageBox("Do you wish to continue?", "MB_YESNO", "MB_ICONQUESTION")
if res == "No" then
fhMessageBox("You clicked No")
elseif res == "Yes" then
fhMessageBox("You clicked Yes")
end

require("iuplua");
iup.SetGlobal("CUSTOMQUITMESSAGE","YES");

local btn = iup.button{title="click me"};
local dlg=iup.dialog{ iup.vbox{ iup.label{title="Hello"}, btn}, title="Test Click", size="200x200"};
iup.SetAttribute(dlg, "NATIVEPARENT", fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND"));

function btn:action()
local res = fhMessageBox("Hello world", "MB_OK", "", dlg.HWND)
end

iup.Popup(dlg);
iup.Destroy(dlg);

title: fhMoveItemAfter(ptrMove,ptrAfter)

ptrFam = fhNewItemPtr()

ptrChild1 = fhNewItemPtr()
ptrChild1:MoveTo(ptrFam,'~.CHIL')

title: fhOutputResultSetColumn(strColumnHeading, strColumnType, tblData, iCount[, iWidthInChar4ths[, sAlignment[, iSortPriority[, bSortAscending,strItemSortType,strVisibility[,strExpression]]]]])
text:
functions

fhOutputResultSetColumn

Description

Use this function to create a result set which the caller can view
either in the Query Window or in the Media Window, after the plugin has
completed. Plugins which don't return a result set should not call this
function at all. Those that do should call it once for each column in
the result set.

See also fhOutputResultSetTitles
and fhSetOutputDestination.

Minimum FH Version

Optional sort and alignment parameters require version 5.0.8.
The optional strExpression parameter requires version 8.

Syntax

fhOutputResultSetColumn(strColumnHeading,
strColumnType, tblData, iCount[, iWidthInChar4ths[,
sAlignment[, iSortPriority[,
bSortAscending,strItemSortType,strVisibility[,strExpression]]]]])

Parameters

strColumnHeading
string: Heading for Column
strColumnType
string: Column type must be one of the following:

text
strings

item
Item Pointer Objects

date-point
Date point Objects

integer
integers

tblData
table: contents for the column, type must match the declared
column type, or be nil. The table must be a simple indexed table.
iCount
integer: number of items in the table. For fully popuated tables
(e.g ones which contain no nil elements) you can prefix the table
name with a # to get the number of items in the table.
iWidthInChar4ths
integer: Column width in ¼ character widths (e.g. 80 = about 20
chars). Defaults to 80 if not supplied.
strAlignment
string: Column alignment:

align_left
column is left aligned

align_right
Column is right aligned

align_mid
Column is centered

iSortPriority
integer: Defaults to 0 if not supplied (0 = no sort). See remarks
below.
bSortAscending
boolean: if true (the default) sort is ascending. Otherwise it is
descending.
strItemSortType
string: Applicable only if the strColumnType is 'item'. Otherwise
ignored. [NOTE: This parameter will have no affect in versions
earlier than 5.0.8].

default
Column uses alphabetic-sorting

date
Column uses date-sorting

integer
Column uses integer-sorting

strVisibility
string: Indicates whether column is visible, or some kind of
hidden column.[NOTE: This parameter will have no affect in versions
earlier than 5.0.8].

show
Column is visible (the default)

hide
Column is hidden. Is useful if you want to sort on a
hidden column.

buddy

Column is hidden and is a 'buddy' column of the previous
column (that is, the column created in the previous call
to fhOutputResultSetColumn). A 'buddy' column can be
specified only if the previous column is not an item
column. It associates each cell of that previous column
with an item (unless NULL) to link that cell back to an
item of data.

If the user double-clicks on a data-linked cell, the
Property Box will be opened to show that item of data.
Also, the text in a data-linked cells displays in a
slightly different colour to non-data-linked cells (the
defaults are black for the former, and grey for the
latter). Ordinary item columns are data-linked
automatically. But if you want a non-item column to be
data-linked, you must define a buddy column for it. If you
want to specify a column as a buddy column, the following
must all be true:

The buddy column must be an 'item' column (see
strColumnType)

There must be a previous column

The previous column must NOT be an 'item' column

The previous column must not be hidden or a buddy
column

If any of these are not the case, it is an error and the
call will fail.

NOTE: You can have NULL values in a buddy column.
However, it is strongly recommended that if the buddy
column contains NULL for a given row, the column it is
linked to should normally also have NULL for that row
or, exceptionally, some text that indicates that the
value is NULL. Otherwise, the user is likely to believe
that they can double-click on the cell and will be
confused when nothing happens if they do so.

strExpression
string: If supplied, must be an empty string, unless strColumnType
is 'item'. When used with an 'item' column type, this
parameter can be used to provide an expression (data reference or
built-in function) which will be called with the column's data
items, to return a value derived from that data item. For
example, if the data item is a 'fact' type data item, you could
supply data items in this column which reference a fact (event or
attribute), and if the expression is '%FACT.DATE:COMPACT%', the
cells will display the date of the fact in compact format. If
the expression is '=FactValue(%FACT%)', the cells will display the
attribute value (for attributes). It is an error to enter an
invalid expression. It is not an error to enter an expression
which is valid but does not take an item pointer of the type stored
in the column. However, in that case, the cells will be blank.

Returns

none

Remarks

The first call creates the first column, the second call creates the
second column, and so on. If you create multiple columns, they do not
have to have the same number of items. The result set displayed will
have enough rows for the largest column, and columns which have fewer
values will be displayed with blank values in the rows for which they
have no value.

You can call fhOutputResultSetColumn at any point in your script, but
the normal practice is to make all calls to this function at or near
the end of the script - given that it is producing output for when the
script has completed.

When assigning object values to table variables, use the object's
'Clone' function to avoid storing the same underlying object in
multiple variables (if you do, they will all display the same value).

Sorting

If you wish, you can specify that you wish the
result set rows to be sorted for you.

Sorting only happens AFTER the plugin has completed.

Sorting rearranges the result set rows, based on values in
columns.

You can specify which column you wish to base the sort on (and
this can be a hidden column)

You can sort on more than one column (e.g. you might wish to sort
rows based on a column containing surnames, but where the surname
fields match, do a further sort based on a column which contains
given names).

You specify which columns to sort on by giving them a non-zero
value for iSortPriority. It is an error to give any two columns the
same non-zero priority.

Sort priority values do not have to be contiguous.

Low values have a higher priority than higher values. For example,
to sort on the surname column first, and then on the given names
column, you might give the surname column a priority of 1 and the
given names column a priority of 2. If you do not wish to sort on
any columns, set all their iSortPriority values to zero (or do not
specify a sort priority, as zero is the default).

The nature of the sort (alphabetic, date or integer) is normally
determined by the column contents. But if the column type is 'item'
(and bearing in mind that you can put items of any type in an 'item'
column), you must specify the sort you require, if not alphabetic,
using the strItemSortType parameter.

Example

The following script creates a result set with 10 rows and 3 columns.
Result sets can be saved in PDF, CSV or text format, copied to the
clipboard, or printed. You can select and delete any data items in any
column (one column at a time - but you can delete an entire column in
one go if you wish). You can view Properties for any data item too.
You can click on any column heading to sort on that heading (you will
be given the chance to revert to the normal sort order before printing
or saving to PDF).

ptrInd = fhNewItemPtr()
ptrInd:MoveToFirstRecord('INDI')
a = {}

ptrInd:MoveNext()
a[1] = ptrInd:Clone()
ptrInd:MoveNext()
a[2] = ptrInd:Clone()
ptrInd:MoveNext()
a[3] = ptrInd:Clone()
ptrInd:MoveNext()
a[4] = ptrInd:Clone()
a[5] = ptrInd:Clone()
a[6] = ptrInd:Clone()
a[7] = ptrInd:Clone()
a[8] = ptrInd:Clone()
a[10] = ptrInd:Clone()

b = {}
b[1] = "Apples"
b[2] = "Pears"
b[3] = "Oranges"
b[4] = "Bananas"
b[6] = "Blackcurrants"
b[9] = "NOt blank here"

c = {}
c[1] = 142
c[2] = 4
c[7] = 1600
c[5] = 1700

fhOutputResultSetColumn("Individuals", "item", a, 10, 180, "align_left", 1, true)
fhOutputResultSetColumn("Fruit", "text", b, 9, 0, "align_mid")
fhOutputResultSetColumn("Count", "integer", c, 7, 80, "align_right", 2, false)

fhOutputResultSetTitles("Display Title", "Print Title", "Print Subtitle")

fhPromptUserForDate

Description

Displays a Date Entry Assistant dialog to allow a user to enter date.
The Date Entry Assistant dialog is designed to allow a user to enter any
kind of date that Family Historian supports - including simple dates,
periods, ranges, date phrases and quarter dates.

There is no need to call fhUpdateDisplay before calling this function,
as there would be if you were using an IUP function to display a dialog
box.

Syntax

Parameters

hParentWnd

handle of the dialog box - see second example below.

Return Value

The date specified or nil if the user cancelled.

Example

dt=fhPromptUserForDate()
if dt == nil then
fhMessageBox("User cancelled")
else
fhMessageBox("Date: " .. dt:GetDisplayText())
end

require("iuplua");
iup.SetGlobal("CUSTOMQUITMESSAGE","YES");

end
end

title: fhSetConversionLossFlag(bSet)
text:
functions

fhSetConversionLossFlag

Description

Family Historian maintains internally a 'Conversion Loss' setting, or
'flag'. This flag is always set off each time that a plugin is
run. However, while the plugin is running, if the plugin at any point
calls a function or object method which implicitly or explicitly
converts text from one character encoding to another, and if any kind of
loss of information occurs during such as conversion, the Conversion
Loss flag will be set on. When the plugin completes, if the
Conversion Loss flag is set at this point, Family Historian will put out
the message: "Plugin may have failed to handle accent characters
correctly".

Internally, Family Historian stores all data in Unicode format. Suppose
that a plugin calls a function like fhGetValueAsText to retrieve
some data as text. By default, the fhGetValueAsText function
will retrieve the data in ANSI format. This means that Family
Historian has to convert the text from Unicode to ANSI. All characters
in ANSI can be represented in Unicode, but not all Unicode characters
can be represented in ANSI. Suppose then that the data being retrieved
includes one or more accent characters which cannot be represented in
ANSI. In that case, Family Historian will convert the original Unicode
text into the nearest equivalent in ANSI, and will set the Conversion
Loss flag on, if it is not already set.

As all characters in ANSI can be represented in Unicode, the Conversion
Loss flag is never set when text is converted from ANSI to Unicode. It
is only ever set when text is converted from Unicode to ANSI - and only
then if the specific text being converted has no exact ANSI equivalent.
Calling any function with a strEncoding parameter can result in the
Conversion Loss flag being set. Also, calling the function fhConvertUTF8toANSI
can also cause the Conversion Loss flag to be set.

Plugins can set or unset the Conversion Loss flag by calling the function
fhSetConversionLossFlag. Clearly this function is open to misuse. It is
perfectly legitimate to call this function to prevent users being warned
that accent characters may not have been handled correctly, if you know
that the warning is unnecessary and that any conversion 'losses' cannot
affect the correct running of your plugin, and that no possible data loss
could have occurred for your user, as a result of running your plugin -
even if the flag is set. On the other hand, it is not legitimate to call
this function to prevent users being warned that accent characters may not
have been handled correctly, if your plugin might have updated data fields
incorrectly (losing accent characters) or provided incorrect information
or behaved in any other way incorrectly, as a result of the failure to
handle accent characters correctly. In other words, this function should
not be used as a way of 'sweeping the problem under the carpet'.
Another legitimate reason why a plugin might want to set the Conversion
Loss flag off, is if the plugin itself has already warned the user about
the issue. In that case, there would be no need for the user to be
warned twice about the same thing.

Of course, the best way of ensuring that the Conversion Loss flag is
not set, is to handle accent characters in the first place. As UTF-8 is
an encoding of Unicoding, if you ensure that you always use UTF-8
encoding when setting or retrieving text data, the Conversion Loss flag
will never be set. However, you should be aware that many Lua library
functions assume that strings are in ANSI, and will not work correctly
with UTF-8 encoded strings.

See also fhIsConversionLossFlagSet.

Minimum FH Version

6

Syntax

fhSetConversionLossFlag(bSet)

Parameters

bSet
Boolean: true = set the flag on. false = set the flag off..

Returns

none

Example

sfhSetConversionLossFlag(false)

title: fhSetIniFileValue(strFile, strSection, strKey, strValueType, varValue)
text:
functions

fhSetIniFileValue

Description

Sets the value of a given named value (identified by a 'key') in an Inifile.
Inifiles are a standard way of storing setting information and similar
data in a file, in Windows. Windows Inifiles currently have to be
ANSI or Unicode (specifically UTF16-LE) only. At time of writing,
UTF8 is not supported. Be careful not to accidentally update an
ANSI file in UTF8 format when editing it using a text editor such as
Notepad. Be aware also that some text editors may wrongly identify
an ANSI file as UTF8 because it isn't always possible to distinguish
ANSI from UTF8 by the content.

If you specify a file that does not exist, when setting a value in a
call to fhSetIniFileValue, the file will be automatically created as an
ANSI Inifile. If you want to use Unicode for text values, you must
create a Unicode Inifile in UTF16-LE format before using
fhSetIniFileValue to write to it. There is an example of how to do
this below (the second), using fhSaveTextFile
to create the empty file in UTF16-LE format, if it doesn't already
exist.

As explained in String
Encoding and Unicode, plugin files and plugin text strings
can be encoded using ANSI or UTF-8. If a plugin uses ANSI
encoding, there is clearly no problem about using fhSetIniFileValue and
fhGetIniFileValue with an ANSI Inifile. Equally, if a plugin uses
UTF-8 encoding, there is no problem about using these same functions
with a UTF16-LE Inifile. Family Historian will handle all
necessary conversions for you automatically. What may perhaps be
less clear is that you can also use an ANSI Inifile with a plugin that
uses UTF8 encoding, and you can use a UTF16-LE Inifile with a plugin
that uses ANSI encoding, as long as the strings will never contain
any characters which cannot be rendered in ANSI. If you need to
use characters which cannot be rendered in ANSI, you will need to use
UTF8 string encoding (which normally means encoding the whole plugin
file as UTF8) and a Unicode (UTF16-LE) Inifile.

To learn more about Inifiles, see fhGetIniFileValue.

Minimum FH Version

7

Syntax

bOK= fhSetIniFileValue(strFile,
strSection, strKey, strValueType, varValue)

Parameters

strFile
String: the full file name, including path (e.g. "C:\Program
Data\Calico Pie\Family Historian\Plugins\New Report.fhr").
strSection
String: The section.
strKey
String: The key.
strValueType
String: This must be "integer", "text" or "bool", depending on the
type of the value being set.
varValue
Can be a text string, an integer or a boolean, depending on the
value of strValueType.

Return Value

bOK
A boolean value. A value of true means the function
succeeded. A value of false means that it failed.

Examples

local bOK = fhSetIniFileValue(strFile, "Report Options", "Footer - Right", "text", "Created by John Smith");

-- How to store Unicode in a UTF16-LE Inifile
fhfu = require("fhFileUtils")
sFile = fhGetPluginDataFileName("LOCAL_MACHINE")
if not fhfu.fileExists(sFile) then
fhSaveTextFile(sFile, "", "UTF-16LE")
end
local sTestValue = "¥ųƀđē"
fhSetIniFileValue(sFile, "My Section", "My Value", "text", sTestValue)

title: fhSetLabelledText(ptr, strLabel, strValue)
text:
functions

fhSetLabelledText

Description

Requires version 5.0.9 or later. This function sets the value
of a labelled section in a long text field, such as a note
field. It can also be used to delete the labelled section if the
'value' parameter passed in, is nil. The required portion of
text is identified by a short text label that is passed as a parameter
to the function. The function will search for a paragraph that
begins with the specified label. If the value is not nil, and if
the label is not found, a paragraph with this label and value will be
created. When entered, the value will be terminated by a
paragraph break. Neither the value nor the label supplied as
parameters may contain paragraph breaks.

See also fhGetLabelledText.

Syntax

bOK = fhSetLabelledText(ptr,
strLabel, strValue)

Parameters

ptr
item pointer
strLabel
string: label to use
strValue
string or nil: if a string, it will be the value set (which can be
an empty string). Must not contain any paragraph breaks. If nil, the
label and its current value, will be deleted, if found.

Returns

bOK
boolean: returns true on success and false on failure

Example

Label-matching is case-insensitive..

ptrInd = fhCreateItem('INDI') -- create an Individual record and ret ptr to it
ptrBirth = fhCreateItem('BIRT', ptrInd) -- create a BIRTH field within this record, and ret ptr to it
ptrNote = fhCreateItem('NOTE2', ptrBirth) -- create a NOTE field as a child of the Birth field and ret ptr to it
fhSetLabelledText(ptrNote, 'Confirmed:', 'Yes') -- set a labelled paragraph'Confirmed:' within the note

fhSetValue_Copy

Description

Copies the value of one item to another item.

Syntax

bOK = fhSetValue_Copy(ptrDst,ptrSrc)

Parameters

ptrDst
item pointer: to have its value set
ptrSrc
item pointer: containing the value to copy

Returns

bOK
boolean: returns true on success and false on failure

Remarks

This is functionally the same as using the correct GetValue function
followed by a SetValue function, but has the advantage that the type
of value is not required.

Example

The following example is taken from the christening

baptism plugin example and copies the branch to a new fact.

function CopyChildBranch(ptrSrc, ptrTargParent)
local ptrNew = fhCreateItem(fhGetTag(ptrSrc), ptrTargParent)
fhSetValue_Copy(ptrNew, ptrSrc)
CopyChildren_FromTo(ptrSrc, ptrNew)
end

title: fhShellExecute(strFileName [, strParams [, strDirectory [, strOperation [, iShowCmd]]]])
text:
functions

fhShellExecute

Description

Executes a Windows "shell" command. Is most commonly used to run an executable file, or to open a document
file using its default application.

Syntax

bOK, iErrorCode, strErrorText = fhShellExecute(strFileName

[, strParams [, strDirectory [, strOperation [, iShowCmd]]]])

Parameters

strFileName
string: the full path to the file. Remember that slashes in Lua must be doubled (e.g "C:\\My
Documents\\My Program.exe").

strParams
string: parameters. If strFileName is an executable file, strParams holds the parameters to be
passed to it. Should be empty, or not supplied, if strFileName is a document file.
strDirectory
string: specifies the default (working) directory for the action. If not supplied, the current
working directory is used.
strOperation
string: specifies the action to be performed. The set of available actions depends on the particular
file or folder. Generally, the actions available from an object's shortcut menu are available actions. The
follow actions are commonly used:

edit
Launches an editor and opens the document for editing. Will fail if strFileName is not a
document file.

explore
Explores a folder specified by strFileName.

find
Initiates a search beginning in the directory specified by strDirectory

open

Opens the item specified by strFileName. In this case, strFileName can be a file or folder.

print

Prints the file specified by strFileName. Will fail if strFileName is not a document
file.

NULL (or empty string)

The default action is used, if available. If not, the "open" action is used. If
neither action is available, the system uses the first action listed in the registry.

iShowCmd
integer: Specifies how an application is to be displayed when it is opened. If not supplied, the
value defaults to 1. The following values are defined:

0
Hides the window and activates another window

1
Activates and displays a window. If the window is minimized or maximized, Windows restores it to
its original size and position. An application should specify this flag when displaying the window for
the first time.

2

Activates the window and displays it as a minimized window.

3

Activates the window and displays it as a maximized window.

4

Displays a window in its most recent size and position. The active window remains active.

5

Activates the window and displays it in its current size and position.

6
Minimizes the specified window and activates the next top-level window in the Z order.

7

Displays the window as a minimized window. The active window remains active.

8

Displays the window in its current state. The active window remains active.

9
Activates and displays the window. If the window is minimized or maximized, Windows restores it to
its original size and position. An application should specify this flag when restoring a minimized
window.

Return ValueS

bOK
boolean: rets true on success and false on failure
iErrorCode
integer: will be nil if the call succeeded. If it fails will return an error code between 0 and
32, some of the more common ones are listed below.

Return Code
MS Name
Description

2
ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND

The specified file was not found.

3
ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND

The specified path was not found.

11
ERROR_BAD_FORMAT

The .exe file is invalid (non-Win32 .exe or error in .exe image).

5
SE_ERR_ACCESSDENIED

The operating system denied access to the specified file.

27
SE_ERR_ASSOCINCOMPLETE

The file name association is incomplete or invalid.

32
SE_ERR_DLLNOTFOUND

The specified DLL was not found.

31
SE_ERR_NOASSOC

There is no application associated with the given file name extension. This error will also be returned
if you attempt to print a file that is not printable.

8
SE_ERR_OOM

There was not enough memory to complete the operation.

26
SE_ERR_SHARE

A sharing violation occurred.

strErrorText
string: will be nil if the call succeeded. If it fails, will contain a textual description of the
error. May be less specific than the iErrorCode. For some unusual error codes strErrorText may
just contain the text "An error has occurred".

title: fhSleep(iWaitInMillisecs[, iPumpInMillisecs])
text:
functions

fhSleep

Description

Use with caution as misuse could cause deadlock. Suspends the
execution of the current thread until the time-out interval elapses.

See also fhExhibitResponsiveness.
Syntax

fhSleep(iWaitInMillisecs[, iPumpInMillisecs])

Parameters

iWaitInMillisecs
integer: the time-out interval in milliseconds. A value of
zero is permitted, and causes the thread to relinquish the remainder
of its time slice to any other thread that is ready to run. If
there are no other threads ready to run, the function returns
immediately, and the thread continues execution. If you wish
to specify a value larger than 1000 milliseconds, you are
recommended to set an iPumpInMillisecs value - see next.

iPumpInMillisecs (optional)

integer: Defaults to zero if not supplied. If greater than
zero, Family Historian will 'pump' messages to windows every
iPumpInMillisecs milliseconds until the full timeout interval has
elapsed (these 'messages' are system communications between the
operating system and the application and are not visible to the user
in any way). For example, it would not be a good idea to cause
Family Historian to simply sleep for 30 seconds. This might
cause problems with the system, and Windows might diagnose that
Family Historian was "not responding" and prompt the user to close
it. If, however, Family Historian 'pumps' messages regularly
during this 30 second period, it should not cause problems and
Windows is likely to consider that the application remains in a
healthy state. Normally, iPumpInMillisecs will be smaller than
iWaitInMillisecs. For example, if iWaitInMillisecs was 10,000,
it might be reasonable to set iPumpInMillisecs to 1,000 (say).
If however iPumpInMillisecs is equal to, or larger than
iWaitInMillisecs, the application will simply wait for the timeout
interval to elapse, and then pump messages before returning.
Be aware that allowing Family Historian to pump messages, may itself
have consequences that you may need to guard against. If you
are displaying a window or form, it might mean that the user could
close it, causing your plugin to crash. If this is an issue,
you may need to consider disabling any windows or forms you have
open, before your call to fhSleep, and then re-enabling them
afterwards. Note: If you are making multiple calls to fhSleep
in a loop, you may need to set a value for iPumpInMillisecs, even if
in each call to fhSleep the value for iWaitInMillisecs is low.

Return Value

none

Example

fhSleep(500)

title: Item Pointers: Confusions and Pitfalls to Avoid
breadcrumb: Item Pointers: Confusions and Pitfalls to Avoid
text:
The Family Historian API
