This entry-point is called to render date information into text
appropriately.

Syntax

strRenderedDateText = FH_GetDateText(strFormat,
date, strQualifier)

Parameters

strFormat
String. The date format required. Possible values are
"SENTENCE" or "PREDICATE". The former is used if the date will
occur in the context of a narrative sentence.

date
A Family Historian Date
object.

strQualifier
String. Will be an empty string if there is no
qualifier. If supplied, possible values are "MONTH_NAME",
"LONG", "COMPACT","ABBREV", "ABBREV2", "ABBREV3", "ABBREV4",
"XDATE1", "XDATE2", "XDATETYPE". See the main application help
for an explanation of the meaning of these qualifiers (search for
"date formats" in the Help).

Returns

strRenderedDateText
String. The rendered date text. Return nil if unable to render a
particular date value.

Example

function FH_GetDateText(sFormat, date, sQualifier)
local sText;
local bSentence = false;
if sFormat == "SENTENCE" then
bSentence = true;
end
if date:GetType() == "Simple" then
if bSentence then
sText = GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "le ", "en ");
else
sText = GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1());
end
elseif date:GetType() == "Period" then
if date:GetSubtype() == "From" then
if bSentence then
sText = "à partir " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "du ", "de ");
else
sText = "à partir " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "du ", "de ");
end
elseif date:GetSubtype() == "To" then
sText = "jusqu'" .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "au ", "en ");
elseif date:GetSubtype() == "From-To" then
sText = GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "du ", "de ") .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt2(), " au ", " à ");
end
elseif date:GetType() == "Range" then
if date:GetSubtype() == "After" then
if bSentence then
sText = "après " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "le ", "");
else
sText = "après " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1());
end
elseif date:GetSubtype() == "Before" then
if bSentence then
sText = "avant " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "le ", "");
else
sText = "avant " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1());
end
elseif date:GetSubtype() == "Between" then
if bSentence then
sText = "entre " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1(), "le ", "") .. " et " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt2(), "le ", "");
else
sText = "entre " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt1()) .. " et " .. GetDatePtText(date:GetDatePt2());
end
end
elseif date:GetType() == "Phrase" then
sText = '"' .. date:GetPhrase() .. '"';
end
return sText;
end

title: FH_GetFamilyText (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetFamilyText (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called to provide a description of a family,
identified by the parents, in the output language. This will
normally be a translation of a phrase like "The family of Ian Munro
and Charlotte Carrington" or "...of Ian Munro and Charlotte
Carrington".

Syntax

strRenderedFamilyText = FH_GetFamilyText(bHusband,
strHusband, bWife, strWife, bStartOf)

Parameters

bHusband
Boolean. True if a reference to the husband (or first
partner) should be included

strHusband
String. The name of the husband or first partner. If
bHusband is true, but this string is empty, use instead a string
which means "(no name)" (written like that, in brackets).

bWife
Boolean. True if a reference to the wife (or second partner)
should be included

strWife

String. The name of the wife or second partner. If
bWife is true, but this string is empty, use instead a string which
means "(no name)" (written like that, in brackets).

bStartOf
Boolean. If true, this means that the the text returned
should begin with the equivalent in the output language, of the word
'of' preceded by 3 dots. For example: "...of Ian Munro and
Charlotte Carrington" (avoids unnecessary repetition of "the
family"). If bStartOf is false, start the text returned with
the phrase "The family of " (no dots this time) - for example, "The
family of Ian Munro and Charlotte Carrington".

Returns

strRenderedAgeText
String. The rendered age text. If both bHusband and bWife are
false, return the text "(unknown parents)" translated into the
output language (written like that, in brackets).

Example

function FH_GetFamilyText(bHusband, sHusband, bWife, sWife, bStartOf)
local sText;
if sHusband == '' then
sHusband = '(sans nom)';
end
if sWife == '' then
sWife = '(sans nom)';
end
if bStartOf then
sText = "...de "
else
sText = "La famille de "
end
if bHusband and bWife then
sText = sText .. sHusband .. " et " .. sWife;
elseif bHusband then
sText = sText .. sHusband;
elseif bWife then
sText = sText .. sWife;
else
sText = "(parents inconnus)";
end
return sText;
end

title: FH_GetLifeDatesText (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetLifeDatesText (entry-point)

Description

In various reports, especially narrative reports, a person's life
dates are often given in brackets after their name - for
example,"Susan Dowling (1925-2008)". If still alive, or if no
death date is recorded, their life dates might be written like this
"(1925- )". If their birth date is not known, their life dates
might be written as "( -2008)". More complex variants are
possible, if birth and/or death dates are not known, but other useful
dates are - such as baptism, christening, burial or cremation. Another
consideration is if some of the relevant dates are approximate, or
specified as a range. When supplying life dates, a plugin
author can choose to make them as complex or a simple as they wish.

Syntax

strRenderedLifeDatesText = FH_GetLifeDatesText(StartDate,
strStartDateType, EndDate, strEndDateType, bFemale, bSimplify,
bForceHyphen)

Parameters

StartDate
A Family Historian Date
object or nil if no start date.

strStartDateType
String. Possible values are "ESTIMATED", "BIRTH", "BAPTISM",
"CHRISTENING" or the empty string.

EndDate
A Family Historian Date
object or nil if no end date.

strEndDateType
String. Possible values are "ESTIMATED", "DEATH", "BURIAL",
"CREMATION" or the empty string.

bFemale
Boolean. True if the person in question is female. It
is possible that this could affect the generated text in some
languages.

bSimplify
Boolean. This parameter is currently always false. In
the future, users may be given an option to simplify life dates in
reports, in which case, the chosen option will be reflected in this
parameter. Meanwhile, a plugin author can nevertheless choose
to simplify all life date text, if they wish to.

bForceHyphen
Boolean. If true, and if both dates are nil, " - " should be
returned as life dates. Otherwise, nil can be returned in that
case.

Returns

strRenderedDateText
String. The rendered date text. Return nil if unable to render a
particular date value.

Example

function FH_GetLifeDatesText(date1, sType1, date2, sType2, bFemale, bSimplify, bForceHyphen)
local sDate1;
local sDate2;
local sDateText;
local bUseCirca = false;
if (date1 ~= nil and sType1 ~= "BIRTH") or (date2 ~= nil and sType2 ~= "DEATH") then
bUseCirca = true;
end
if not bUseCirca and date1 ~= nil and not HasDefiniteYear(date1) then
bUseCirca = true;
end
if not bUseCirca and date2 ~= nil and not HasDefiniteYear(date2) then
bUseCirca = true;
end
if date1 ~= nil then
local datept = date1:GetDatePt1();
if not datept:IsNull() then
sDate1 = string.format("%04d", datept:GetYear());
end
end
if date2 ~= nil then
local datept = date2:GetDatePt2();
if datept:IsNull() then
datept = date2:GetDatePt1();
end
if not datept:IsNull() then
sDate2 = string.format("%04d", datept:GetYear());
end
end
-- now put it all together
if date1 == nil and date2 == nil then
if bForceHyphen then
sDateText = " - ";
end
else
sDateText = "";
if bUseCirca then
sDateText = "ca ";
end
if sDate1 ~= nil and sDate1 ~= "" then
sDateText = sDateText .. sDate1;
elseif sDateText == "" then
sDateText = " "; -- "( -1987)" looks better than "(-1987)" (but don't want "(ca -1987))
end
sDateText = sDateText .. "-";
if sDate2 ~= nil and sDate2 ~= "" then
sDateText = sDateText .. sDate2;
else
sDateText = sDateText .. " "; -- "(1987- )" looks better than "(1987-)"
end
end
return sDateText;
end

title: FH_GetMiscellaneousText (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetMiscellaneousText (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called to translate items of text such as report
names, titles, headings, field labels, and various text parts.
Another way of putting it is that it is used to translate text which
isn't date, place or age information, and isn't a value (such as an
attribute value) that has been entered into the project - all of which
are handled separately. The default implementation of this
function does a lookup in a table called g_trans_misc, which is stored
in a separate file ("lang_trans_misc.fh_lua") in the language pack
folder. The user can add and edit items in this table using
tools in the Language Pack window, without needing to access the
plugin directly, and without needing to understand Lua. By
default, Family Historian will mark report text with a distinctive
colour, if this function returns nil (i.e. fails to find a translation
for the text). This way, the user can work out how to correct
the problem if there are missing entries in the 'Miscellaneous' lookup
table.

Syntax

strTranslation = FH_GetMiscellaneousText(strText,
tContext)

Parameters

strText
String. Text to translate.

tContext
Table or nil if not supplied (so test that it is not nil before
using it). If supplied, holds some or all of the following
contextual information:

bDate
boolean. True if the context is date text

bPlace
boolean. True if the context
is place text

bVowel
boolean. True if the string to be translated is
associated with another string which begins with a vowel

bPlural
boolean. True if the context is plural. This does
not necessarily mean that the word to be translated is
plural. For example, if the word to be translated was 'he'
and the context was plural, you should not return a translation
of 'they'. Such a context might occur if 'he' was being
used like this: "he and Mary Jones were married in 1982".
In some languages, the translation of 'he' would be different in
a context like that, where the subject is not the sole subject
term.

bFemale
boolean. True if the context is such that a female
version of the translation is required.

If the relevant value is not applicable, the value will not have
been set - i.e. will be nil. See the example below for an
illustration of how to test these values.

Returns

strTranslation
String. The translated text. Return nil if none.

Example

function FH_GetMiscellaneousText(sText, tContext)
if tContext then
if tContext["bPlural"] then
return g_trans_misc["~PLURAL:" .. sText];
elseif tContext["bPlace"] then
if tContext["bVowel"] then
return g_trans_misc["~PLACE_VOWEL:" .. sText];
else
return g_trans_misc["~PLACE:" .. sText];
end
elseif tContext["bFemale"] then
local sTrans = g_trans_misc["~FEMALE:" .. sText];
if sTrans then
return sTrans;
end
end
end
return g_trans_misc[sText];
end

title: FH_GetNthItemAsText (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetNthItemAsText (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called primarily to translate headings like
"First Generation", "Second Generation" and so on, which are found in
the Ancestors by Generation and Descendants by
Generation reports.

Syntax

strTranslation = FH_GetNthItemAsText(iNumber,
strItem)

Parameters

iNumber
Integer. The number to be translated into adjectival form.

strItem
String. The noun that the number goes with. At
present, this is always likely to be the word 'generation'.
However, other nouns may be used in the future.

Returns

strTranslation
String. The translated text or nil if none. For example, if
the number was 7 and strItem was "Generation", the translated text
should be a translation of "Seventh Generation" or "7th
Generation". The default implementation of this function uses
words up 10, and digits thereafter (in adjectival form, for the
language concerned).

Example

function FH_GetNthItemAsText(iNumber, strItem) -- an implementation in a French-language plugin
local sText;
local sItemL = FH_GetMiscellaneousText(sItem);
local bFemale = false;
if sItemL == nil then
sItemL = sItem;
end
if sItemL == "Génération" then
bFemale = true;
end
if iValue <= 0 then
sText = "0";
elseif iValue == 1 then
if bFemale then
sText = "Première";
else
sText = "Premier";
end
elseif iValue <= 10 then
sText = g_Nths[iValue];
else
sText = iValue .. "ème";
end
if sItemL then
sText = sText .. ' ' .. sItemL;
else
sText = sText .. ' ' .. sItem;
end
return sText;
end

title: FH_GetPersonText (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetPersonText (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called as a helper function, to help Family
Historian to generate text that will refer to a person or persons,
when processing certain codes in sentence templates, with narrative
reports. The relevant codes are: {individual},
{individual/him/her}, {individual's}, {him/her}, {his/her},
{spouse/her/him}, {couple}, {principal}, {principals}, {role name},
{role=____}, {role(single)=____}, {role(plural)=____}, {other=____},
{other(single)=____} and {other(plural)=____} (the last 6 are codes
which all take a list of role names as, effectively,
parameters). To learn more about these codes, see the main
application Help for the program (e.g. search for "Sentence Template
Codes" in the Help, or click on Fact Types on the Tools
menu, edit any fact type, click the Help button, and
follow the links in the "Sentence Template" section). Any of the
listed codes can be attached to other items of text, by placing the
additional text before the code or after it, or both, within angle
brackets: e.g. "<{individual's} hobby>". This additional
text is referred to here as the wrapper, and is written as a
single item of text, with the angle brackets removed, and the position
of the code marked by "%s". So the wrapper for
"<{individual's} hobby>", for example, would be "%s hobby".

The job of the FH_GetPersonText entry-point function is potentially
two-fold:

if there is a wrapper (and there may or may not be one), it may
need to be translated. Usually however, no translation should
be required because the wrapper should normally already be in the
output language (this is because the language pack should provide
translated sentence templates called 'language variants'). But
even in that case, the wrapper may need to be modified to
fit the context (more on this below).

if the bPronounReqd parameter is set to true, the function must
return the appropriate pronoun for the context

When Family Historian processes the sentence templates containing the
codes, it will replace some of the codes with names, and some with
pronouns; and in some cases, it will replace the same code with either
a name or with a pronoun, depending on the context. If a name is
to be used, Family Historian will generate that. It is not the
job of this function to generate any names. But as we have seen,
it is the job of the function to generate a pronoun if the
bPronounReqd parameter is set to true.

Lua allows functions to return more than one value. This
function returns two: the first is the updated wrapper (or nil if
there is no wrapper, or if it does not need to be updated). The
second is the pronoun required (or nil if no pronoun is required).

The following example illustrates how this works. Imagine that
you have added "Hobby" as a new fact type - an Individual
attribute. You create a sentence template for this fact type
that looks like this (say):

{individual's} hobby was {value}

Let us suppose that you have a French language pack. You create
a language variant sentence template for this language pack that looks
like this:

<{individual's} passe-temps> était
{value}

Notice that the word 'passe-temps' now occurs within an angle-bracket
expression. This was done so that the wrapper "%s passe-temps"
will be passed to FH_GetPersonText. We will see why shortly.

If Family Historian were rendering this in English, it might,
depending on the context, become either "John Smith's hobby was
gardening" or "his hobby was gardening" (or possibly even "John's
hobby was gardening"). Each sentence can be achieved by simple
code substitution into the wrapper "%s hobby" with the appropriate
name or pronoun (possessive versions). That does not work in
French, however. In French, the equivalent texts would be "Le
passe-temps de John Smith était jardinage" or "Son passe-temps était
jardinage". The first effectively requires the wrapper to be "Le
passe-temps de %s". The second requires the wrapper to be "%s
passe-temps" - i.e. completely different wrappers. Also, if the
person's name began with a vowel, it would be slightly different
again. If the person was called "Alain Dupont" instead of "John
Smith", the sentence would be "Le passe-temps d'Alain Dupont était
jardinage". In this case, we need a third wrapper: "Le
passe-temps d'%s", which is similar but not identical to "Le
passe-temps de %s".

There are numerous ways that a plugin could handle this kind of
problem. The default implementation of this function checks the
Miscellaneous lookup table for a version of the wrapper which requires
a pronoun or is designed for names beginning with a vowel, and it
substitutes that for the passed-in wrapper, if found.

Syntax

strTranslation = FH_GetPersonText(strWrapper,
bLangVar, bPronounReqd, tContext)

Parameters

strWrapper
String. The wrapper. May be an empty string if there
is no wrapper (in which case ignore it and return nil as the first
return value). If not empty, it will always contain "%s"
somewhere within it. The modified wrapper must also contain
"%s" somewhere within it too. If it doesn't, it will be
ignored. Notice also that any other percentage signs used in
the returned wrapper (if any), must be doubled. The doubled
percentage signs will converted back to a single percentage sign
when output.
bLangVar
This is set to true if the wrapper forms part of (was
extracted from) a language variant sentence template. If bLangVar is
not true, this could be because no language variant has been
supplied for this fact type. It could also be because the
sentence was overridden by the user, in the Sentence field of the
Fact tab of the Property Box.
bPronounReqd
Set to true if a pronoun is required (see discussion above).
The pronoun must be returned as a string in the second return value.
tContext
Table that provides the following contextual information:

sCase
String. The grammatical case of the context. The
options are:

SUBJECTIVE

OBJECTIVE

POSSESSIVE

These are the modern terms for "Nominative", "Accusative" and
"Genitive", which may be more familiar to some.

sName
String. Optional. If
supplied, is the name that will be inserted. Is most
likely to be of use for debugging purposes.

bMale
Boolean. True if the person to be referred to is
male. This may affect the pronoun (if required) in some
languages.

bFemale
Boolean. True if the person to be referred to is
female. This may affect the pronoun (if required) in some
languages.

sPerson
String. Optional. If supplied and if it contains
the text "PLURAL" it means that, if a pronoun is required, it
should be a plural pronoun (equivalent of 'they' or 'them').

bVowel
Boolean. True if the name that will be substituted
begins with a vowel.

With all booleans, if the relevant value is not applicable, the
value will not have been set - i.e. will be nil. See the
example below for an illustration of how to test these values.

Returns

strWrapper
String. The modified (and possibly translated) wrapper. Or
nil if there is no wrapper, or no modification or translation is
required.

strPronoun
String. The required pronoun in the output language, or nil if the
bPronounReqd parameter was false.

Example

function FH_GetPersontext(sText, tContext)
if sWrapper ~= "" then -- sWrapper can be an empty string, in which case this function shld return nil for the wrapper translation
if tContext.sCase == "POSSESSIVE" then
if bPronounReqd then
sTransWrapper = g_trans_misc["~PRONOUN:" .. sWrapper];
if g_trans_misc["~FEMALE:" .. sWrapper] then
bFemaleNoun = true;
end
elseif tContext.bVowel then
sTransWrapper = g_trans_misc["~VOWEL:" .. sWrapper];
end
elseif tContext.sCase == "OBJECTIVE" then
if bPronounReqd then
sTransWrapper = g_trans_misc["~PRONOUN_OBJECTIVE:" .. sWrapper];
end
elseif not bLangVar then
sTransWrapper = g_trans_misc[sWrapper];
end
end
if bPronounReqd then
if tContext.sPerson == "PLURAL" then
if tContext.sCase == "SUBJECTIVE" then
if tContext.bFemale then
sPronoun = "elles";
else
sPronoun = "ils";
end
else
sPronoun = "leur";
end
else
if tContext.sCase == "OBJECTIVE" then
if sTransWrapper then
sPronoun = "l'";
elseif tContext.bFemale then
sPronoun = "elle";
else
sPronoun = "lui";
end
elseif tContext.sCase == "POSSESSIVE" then
if bFemaleNoun then
sPronoun = "sa";
else
sPronoun = "son";
end
else
if tContext.bFemale then
sPronoun = "elle";
else
sPronoun = "il";
end
end
end
end

return sTransWrapper, sPronoun;
end

title: FH_GetPlaceText (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetPlaceText (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called to translate place names - if they need to
be translated - and sometimes also to render them appropriately, with
the correct preposition.

Syntax

strRenderedPlaceText, bHandledContext = FH_GetPlaceText(strPlaceText,
bShortForm, sPreposition, sContext)

Parameters

strPlaceText
String. Place text. This can consist of several
comma-separated parts - e.g. Greenwich, London, England. The
plugin function should split the place into parts, translate
whichever parts need to be translated, and re-assemble them.

bShortFrom
Boolean. True if in context, Family Historian thinks that a
shortened form of the place name would be appropriate (which
typically will happen if it's a repeated reference to the same
place). This might be implemented by excluding all but the
first place part. It is up to the plugin function to decide
how much information to include. This parameter can be ignored
altogether if a plugin does not wish to support this feature.

sPreposition
String or nil. Possible values are "IN", "FROM", "TO" or nil
if there is no preposition. A language pack does not have to
condition its behaviour on the value of sPreposition. It may
make miore sense, for a given language, to condition processing for
prepositions based on either the place type, or the value of
the sContext string, or both..

sContext
String or nil. Is always nil unless this function is called in a
context which uses a context string. Currently there are two
kinds of context string:

(1) if the function is being called in the context of a sentence in
a narrative report and an angle bracket expression (like "<in
{place}>") is used, the angle bracket expression (without the
angle brackets) will be passed as the context string. In that
case, the function will be called to translate, or render, the place
text, where a place-related sentence template code is used. There
are 3 place-related sentence template codes: {place}, {_place} and
{_place2}. The first is used with an implied 'IN' preposition. The
other two have no implied preposition are normally used in the
context of an angle-bracket expression, such as "from
<{_place}>" or "<to {_place2}>" ("{_place2}" is the
second place code, used in the context of the Emigration or
Immigration fact types). If an angle-bracket expression is
used with a place-related code, the contents of the angle-bracket
expression will be passed in the sContext value (without the angle
brackets).

(2) A second kind of context string occurs if the function is being
called in the context of a call to the built-in function =FactText()
(widely-used in diagrams), the context string will be the format
string of that function. These format strings always being
"E_" (for an event) or "A_" (for an attribute). A typical
format string for a birth fact, for example, might be "E_Born: _ in
". If you want to always specify prepositions in your
language, pack, you should not specify one for text templates.

By checking the context string, and by also checking the place type
(possibly using the kind of techniques used in Calico Pie's French
language pack, for example), you should be able to product
appropriate prepositions for any context.

Returns

strRenderedPlaceText
String. The rendered, and possibly translated (or partially
translated) text - including preposition if appropriate. Return nil
if none.

bHandledContext
Boolean. Defaults to false if not supplied. Return true if
sContext is not nil and you have handled the context in the
strRenderedPlaceText returned. Otherwise return false (or do
not return a second return value). For example, if the
sContext is "de {place}" (a sentence template context) and you have
returned "d'Angleterre" (i.e. handling the preposition), you don't
want Family Historian to insert another "de " in front of it, giving
"de d'Angleterre". To prevent that, return true as the second
return value. Note: bHandledContext currently only affects
processing with respect to sentence-generation (e.g. for narrative
reports). It has no effect on the behaviour of the FactText
function, widely-used in diagrams.

Example

-- This example is taken from Calico Pie's French Language pack
-- See the plugin for that language pack for the full context
function FH_GetPlaceText(sPlaceText, bShortForm, sPreposition, sContext)
local sTemp;
local sTrans;
local sFirstPlacePart;
local sFirstChar;

if not sPreposition then
sPreposition = "";
end

local bHandledContext = false;

if sContext then
if sContext:sub(1,3) == "de " then
sPreposition = "FROM";
bHandledContext = true;
elseif sContext:sub(1,3) == "en " then
sPreposition = "TO";
bHandledContext = true;
end
end

local tParts = stringx.split(sPlaceText, ','); -- split comma-separated place text into a table of parts
sPlaceText = nil;

for i = 1, #tParts do
sTemp = tParts[i];
sTemp = stringx.strip(sTemp);

if sTemp ~= "" then
if g_bOutputMatchesProjLang then -- don't translate place names if same-language-rendering
sTrans = sTemp;
else
sTrans = g_trans_place[sTemp];
if sTrans then
sFirstChar = sTrans:sub(1,1);
if sFirstChar == g_Flag_NonCountry or sFirstChar == g_Flag_PluralCountry then -- strip off first char if it's a flag
sTrans = sTrans:sub(2);
end
end
if not sTrans or sTrans == "" then
sTrans = sTemp;
end
end

if sPlaceText then
sPlaceText = sPlaceText .. ", ";
else
sPlaceText = '';
end

sPlaceText = sPlaceText .. sTrans;

if not sFirstPlacePart then
sFirstPlacePart = sTrans;
end
end
end

if not sPlaceText then
sPlaceText = "";
end

if not sFirstPlacePart then
sFirstPlacePart = "";
end

sFirstPlacePart = sFirstPlacePart:lower(); -- force lower-case for case-insensitive checks...

if sPreposition == "IN" then
if g_countries[sFirstPlacePart] then -- country test
if g_countries_plural[sFirstPlacePart] then -- plural country test
sPlaceText = "aux " .. sPlaceText;
elseif TreatAsFemalePlace(sFirstPlacePart) then
sPlaceText = "en " .. sPlaceText;
else
sPlaceText = "au " .. sPlaceText;
end
else
sPlaceText = "à " .. sPlaceText;
end
elseif sPreposition == "TO" then
if g_countries[sFirstPlacePart] then -- country test
if g_countries_plural[sFirstPlacePart] then -- plural country test
sPlaceText = "aux " .. sPlaceText;
elseif TreatAsFemalePlace(sFirstPlacePart) then
sPlaceText = "en " .. sPlaceText;
else
sPlaceText = "au " .. sPlaceText;
end
else
sPlaceText = "à " .. sPlaceText;
end
elseif sPreposition == "FROM" then
if g_countries[sFirstPlacePart] then -- country test
if g_countries_plural[sFirstPlacePart] then -- plural country test
sPlaceText = "des " .. sPlaceText;
elseif fhBeginsWithVowel(sFirstPlacePart) then
sPlaceText = "d'" .. sPlaceText;
elseif TreatAsFemalePlace(sFirstPlacePart) then
sPlaceText = "de " .. sPlaceText;
else
sPlaceText = "du " .. sPlaceText;
end
else
if fhBeginsWithVowel(sFirstPlacePart) then
sPlaceText = "d'" .. sPlaceText;
else
sPlaceText = "de " .. sPlaceText;
end
end
end

return sPlaceText, bHandledContext;
end

title: FH_GetSentenceTemplateWrapper (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_GetSentenceTemplateWrapper (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is used when processing sentence templates for
narrative reports. It allows a language pack plugin to translate
or possibly modify the wrapper associated with a code value
in a sentence template. Wrappers are discussed in the
page for FH_GetPersonText.
They are text within a sentence template, that is wrapped around, or
attached to, a code, using an angle bracket expression. For
example, a sentence template might contain a section of text like
"<at {address}>". The text within the angle brackets
(excluding the code) is referred to here as the wrapper, and
is written as a single item of text, with the angle brackets removed,
and the position of the code marked by "%s". So the wrapper for
"<at {address}>", for example, would be "at %s".

Syntax

strRenderedFamilyText = FH_GetSentenceTemplateWrapper(strOriginal,
strWrapper, strInsert, bLangVar)

Parameters

strOriginal
String. The original angle bracket expression, with code
included.

strWrapper
String. The wrapper to be translated. it will always
contain "%s" somewhere within it. The modified wrapper must
also contain "%s" somewhere within it too. If it doesn't, it
will be ignored. Notice also that any other percentage signs
used in the returned wrapper (if any), must be doubled. The
doubled percentage signs will converted back to a single percentage
sign when output.

strInsert
String. The string that will be substituted into the
wrapper. The plugin can check this value in case it affects
the translation of the wrapper.

bLangVar

Boolean. True if wrapper comes from a language variant on a
fact definition. This value will be false if either no
language variant sentence template has been provided, or if the user
tweaked the sentence in the Sentence field of the Fact tab of the
Property Box.

Returns

strTranslatedWrapper
String. The translated wrapper, or nil if none.

Example

function FH_GetSentenceTemplateWrapper(sOriginal, sWrapper, sInsert, bLangVar)
local sTrans;
if not bLangVar and not g_bOutputMatchesProjLang then
sTrans = g_trans_misc[sWrapper];
end
return sTrans; -- rets nil if no translation
end

title: FH_LangPackBegin (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_LangPackBegin (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called before any other entry points in a
language plugin. It takes a single parameter which indicates
whether the output language matches the project language. A
language plugin may choose to run a little differently depending on
whether this is the case or not. For example, a plugin might
choose to do no place or attribute value lookups, if the project
language matches the output language, on the basis that if the
languages already match, there should be no need for further
translation. To make this possible, a plugin can assign the
value of the parameter to a global variable, which can be tested later
in other entry-points.

Syntax

FH_LangPackBegin(bOutputMatchesProjLang)

Parameters

bOutputMatchesProjLang
Boolean. True if the project language matches the output
language. The project language is set in the Header record (to
access the Header record, the user clicks on the View menu,
then Special Records, and then Header Record).

Returns

(none)

Example

g_bOutputMatchesProjLang = false; -- global variable, set outside all functions

function FH_LangPackBegin(bOutputMatchesProjLang)
g_bOutputMatchesProjLang = bOutputMatchesProjLang;
end

title: FH_LangPackEnd (entry-point)
text:
Language Plugins

FH_LangPackEnd (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called when report creation is completed, just
before the plugin is closed and just before the report is
displayed. If the report has been accumulating debugging
information (e.g. in a global variable), this is an opportunity to
display it. The entry-point function takes no parameters and has
no return value.

Syntax

FH_LangPackEnd()

Parameters

(none)

Returns

(none)

Example

function FH_LangPackEnd()
-- put out debugging message here if needed
end

title: Language Plugins
text:
Special Plugin Types

Language Plugins

The language of Family Historian (the program language) is
English, but the program is designed to be used with projects where the
content can be in other languages, and also to produce reports and other
output, in other languages. The project language is the
language that field values and notes are entered in. The report
or output language is the language displayed in reports and
books, and other output. If we say that a project language is, say,
Norwegian, this does not mean that within the program itself, dates will
show in Norwegian, or that other details will necessarily be given in
Norwegian. It just means that if text is entered (a note, for
example) the text is in Norwegian, and sentences are overridden, these
overridden sentences are also in Norwegian. If there is a date
phrase, the text of the date phrase is in Norwegian. Equally,
if a person was a farmer, the value entered in the Occupation field would
be the Norwegian word for 'farmer', and not the English word.

Family Historian is designed to produce good results if you wish to work
with a non-English content language and produce non-English output.
But in order to do so, you must have a language pack for the language you
wish to use. Each language pack is specific to a particular
language. Language packs potentially serve two functions:

If the project language is not English, a language pack can be used
to help render output (for reports and books) in that same language.

A language pack can also be used to translate content from one
language into another. For example, if the content language is
Norwegian, you can produce a report in Russian - if you have a
suitable Russian language pack.

It should be possible to get good results in rendering output in a
language other than English, if the report language matches the project
language. If the report language does not match the project language
(if, say, you are translating from Norwegian into Russian), the results
are likely to be less good. In particular, any text that is entered
in Norwegian (such as notes or sentence overrides) will not be
translated. Nevertheless, even in this case, the results should be
useful if not perfect.

How to Create a Language Plugin

Whereas source-driven data entry plugins and report plugins are created in
the normal way in the Plugin window, language plugins are not.
Instead, a language plugin is created for you automatically when you
create a language pack - by clicking the New
button on the Language Packs window (accessible from the Tools menu).
The newly-created language plugin will not be listed in the Plugin
window. If you wish to edit it, you do by selecting the appropriate
language pack and clicking the Plugin button,
in the Language Packs window.

Language Plugins Are "Read-Only"

Like smart folder plugins and report plugins (and unlike source-driven
data entry plugins and ordinary plugins) language plugins are read-only.
They can read values from records and fields, but they cannot add,
update or delete records and fields. This does not mean that they
cannot be used to update anything. Like any plugin, they could in
principle update or delete files on your computer, for example.
The label just means specifically that they cannot be used to update
your project data (your project records and the fields contained within
them). More specifically it means that you cannot call any of
these functions from a language plugin:

fhSetValue... functions (i.e. any functions with names beginning
"fhSetValue..." - such as fhSetValueAsInteger)

fhMoveItem... functions (there are only two: fhMoveItemAfter and
fhMoveItemBefore)

fhCreateItem

fhDeleteItem

For the avoidance of doubt, a read-only plugin can call any method on
any object. Some of these methods will update the values of
objects, but they don't change project data, and hence are OK. You
can also call fhCallBuiltInFunction. None of the built-in
functions update program data. And you can call functions like
fhSetIniFileValue. These change file values, but again, they do
not change project data. To repeat, the only functions you cannot
call in a read-only plugin are the functions listed above. If you
call any of these functions from a read-only plugin, you will get an
error.

The only other restriction on read-only plugins is that if you call
fhInitialise in a read-only plugin (which you can do), the fourth
parameter must be blank. That is to say, you cannot specify save
requirements for read-only plugins.

Running Language PLugins

Users do not choose to run language plugins as such. Instead what
happens is that they associate a report with a language pack, and the
language pack is run automatically for them, when they open the
report. The language pack is only used while the report is being
created. By the time the report is open and can be viewed in the
Report Window by the user, the language plugin's job has been completed,
and it will have been closed by Family Historian. If the user
changes report options, Family Historian will re-open the language
plugin and will run it once again, to re-generate report contents.

There are 2 ways that a user can associate a language pack with a
report. They can either explicitly select the report language in
the Language tab of report options; or they can select a default output
language in the International tab of Preferences. If they choose
this latter option, all reports will be associated with the default
language pack, unless the user explicitly chooses otherwise for a given
report.

Combining Language PLugins with report plugins

Even reports that have been created using a report plugin, can be
associated with a language plugin. The 2 plugins will be run at
the same time to generate the report, although neither has any awareness
of the other.

title: FH_GetMiscSectionContent (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_GetMiscSectionContent (entry-point)

Description

Required if and only if you have implemented the FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired
entry-point in your report plugin, and returned a number greater than
0, in which case that will be the number of times this function will
be called when generating or refreshing the report.
Miscellaneous sections can be useful whether or not you also have
ordinary 'record' sections. If you do have record sections
(specified in FH_GetRecordSectionContent), you can still add
'miscellaneous' sections to the end of the report - such as sections
providing information about the places or occupations used in the
earlier record sections of the report. But you can also create a
report which doesn't require any record selection and doesn't have any
record sections - as would be the case in a report about your project
as a whole, say. In that case, you might require just one 'misc'
section. In all cases, you specify the contents of 'misc'
sections in your implementation of FH_GetMiscSectionContent.

Syntax

FH_GetMiscSectionContent(snTop,
index[, reclist])

Parameters

snTop
A top-level Section
object. Call the member functions of the section object
to give it a heading, pictures, body text, and child sections, as
required by your report. Child sections can themselves have
child sections, and so on indefinitely. Both headers and body
text are specified using Rich
Text objects which can be built up in parts, as required.
index
Integer. If you requested just one miscellaneous section,
this will have index 1. If you requested, 3, they will have
indices 1, 2 and 3 in turn.
reclist
Table containing item pointers (records) or nil. Is
only not nil if you set "record_collection" to true in
FH_Requirements. If so, reclist will contain the records that
the user chose for the report.

Returns

none

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to specify miscellaneous section contents
function FH_GetMiscSectionContent(snTop, index)

rtHeading = fhNewRichText();
rtHeading:SetText("A Miscellaneous Section");

rtBody = fhNewRichText();
rtBody:SetText("Hello World!");

snTop:SetHeading(rtHeading);
snTop:SetBodyText(rtBody);

end

title: FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired (entry-point)

Description

If you wish to have top-level sections of your report which are not
about a record that has been selected by the user, these are called
'miscellaneous' sections. Implement FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired
and return the number of miscellaneous sections you require. The
actual content of each miscellaneous section must be generated by
implementing another entry-point: FH_GetMiscSectionContent.

Syntax

iNum = FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired()

Parameters

none

Returns

iNum
The number of miscellaneous sections required.

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to specify the number of miscellaneous sections required
function FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired()
return 1;
end

title: FH_GetRecordSectionContent (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_GetRecordSectionContent (entry-point)

Description

Required if you specified a record type in FH_Requirements,
or if you did not implement FH_Requirements at all (in which the
'Individual' record type is presumed by default). When you
specify a record type, the default startup dialog will allow the user
to choose one or more records of that type, and this function will be
called once for each record selected, when generating or refreshing
the report.

Syntax

FH_GetRecordSectionContent(snTop,
rec, index, count)

Parameters

snTop
A top-level Section
object. Call the member functions of the section object
to give it a heading, pictures, body text, and child sections, as
required by your report. Child sections can themselves have
child sections, and so on indefinitely. Both headers and body
text are specified using Rich
Text objects which can be built up in parts, as required.
rec
An item pointer object. The record to generate section
content for.
index
Integer. The index number of the record being processed. If
the user selected 3 records, the function will be called 3 times
when the report is generated or refreshed - once for each record
selected - with index values 1, 2, and 3, respectively. This
is particularly useful for initialising any global variables you may
wish to maintain. For example, if you are maintain a list of
place records referenced, you can empty the list when index =
1. You can also test when the last record is called, which
will be when index is equal to count (see next).

count
Integer. The number of records selected by the user.
If the user selected 3 records, the function will be called 3 times
when the report is generated or refreshed - and count will be 3 in
each case.

Returns

none

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to specify record section contents
function FH_GetRecordSectionContent(snTop, rec, index, count)

rtHeading = fhNewRichText();
rtHeading:SetText(fhIndGetName(rec, true));

rtBody = fhNewRichText();
GenerateTableItems(rec, rtBody)

snTop:SetHeading(rtHeading);
AddPictures(snTop, rec);
snTop:SetBodyText(rtBody);

tb_factlist = fhIndGetFactList(rec, true, true, false);

GenerateSectionEventsAndAttrs(rec, snTop, tb_factlist);

end

title: FH_PromptUserOptions (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_PromptUserOptions (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is rarely needed or used. If possible, you
should avoid using it. If you wish to allow the user to choose
options, you will normally specify these using the 'options' value in
FH_Requirements. In that case,
these options will then be accessible to the user in the Main (first)
tab of the ordinary Report Options dialog. You can specify
numerous options of all kinds using this technique. All such
options are saved to the 'Plugin' section of the Report Options file.
You get the path to this file by calling
fhGetContextInfo("CI_REPORT_OPTIONS_FILE"), and you can access the
values using the fhGetIniFileValue function.

If you have requirements that for whatever reason cannot be handled
in that way, the alternative is to implement your own user-defined
report options dialog. This is what FH_PromptUserOptions allows
you to do. If you choose to do this, you should still be sure to
save all of the options the user chooses in the usual Report Options
file. You can also use fhGetIniFileValue and fhSetIniFileValue
to get and set option values. Your options dialog will be called if
the user clicks the More Options link on the default
startup dialog (if there is one), or if the user clicks on the Options
button in the Report Window. Your plugin should then prompt the
user to choose the options they require, perhaps using an IUP
dialog. Your dialog should also provide some way for the user to
access the default report options dialog (via a button or link or menu
command, say). This is because the default report options dialog
provides numerous options relating to page layout and possibly other
things, which your options dialog will not handle, but which the user
will still need to be able to access. If the user clicks the relevant
button or link, you should call
fnShowDefaultRptOptionsDlg to display the default report
options dialog. fnShowDefaultRptOptionsDlg is
FH_Startup's only parameter. It is an unusual kind of
parameter. Most parameters are text, booleans, numbers, or some
kind of object. fnShowDefaultRptOptionsDlg is a function (or
if you prefer, you can think of it as a link to a function).
More specifically, it is a function which takes one parameter and does
not return anything. The parameter it takes is a window
handle. This must be supplied. It should be either the
window handle of your own options dialog (if still visible at this
point), or failing that, the 'parent window' handle returned by
fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND"). Iup dialogs have a read-only
attribute HWND which is the window handle (as a light userdata
object).

Allocating a Parent Window Handle

If special care is not taken, your options dialog could easily
disappear behind the main Family Historian application window. To
ensure that this does not happen, when you display your report options
dialog, you must ensure that your dialog is made a child of an
appropriate parent window in the main application. To do this
call fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND") to retrieve the parent window
handle, and use iup.SetAttribute to allocate it to your dialog.
The code snippet below shows how this is done. It might appear
that there are other ways of doing this which are equivalent and
should work equally well. However, this is the only
way of doing it with main application handles that we have found which
works, so we recommend that you stick closely to it.

require("iuplua")
....
dlg = iup.dialog{btn; title="Test dialog"};

iup.SetAttribute(dlg, "NATIVEPARENT", fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND")); -- Set the parent window handle

dlg:show()
iup.MainLoop()
dlg:destroy()

Syntax

bOK = FH_PromptUserOptions(fnShowDefaultRptOptsDlg)

Parameters

fnShowDefaultRptOptsDlg
A function object. The function takes one parameter (a
window handle, passed as a light userdata object), and returns
nothing. Call this function to display the default Report
Options dialog. If hwnd is the
required window handle, call it like this:

fnShowRptOptsDlg(hwnd)

Returns

bOK
boolean. Return true if the user made changes to the options
file and false if they cancelled. If you return true, the report
will be rebuilt.

Example

local OptionsFile = fhGetContextInfo("CI_REPORT_OPTIONS_FILE");

....

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to display your own options dialog
function FH_PromptUserOptions(fnShowDefaultRptOptsDlg)

-- options should be retrieved from, and stored to, the report options file (see above)
local opt = {};
opt.title = fhGetIniFileValue(OptionsFile, "Plugin", "title", "text", "");
opt.alt_title = fhGetIniFileValue(OptionsFile, "Plugin", "alt_title", "text", "");

-- add your own options dialog here.

....

-- hwnd is the handle of your options dialog if still visible (or allocate it to fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND") if your options dialog is not visible)

fnShowDefaultRptOptsDlg(hwnd); -- normally you would only call this function if the user clicked to view standard report options

return true
end

title: FH_Requirements (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_Requirements (entry-point)

Description

Add an instance of this function to a report plugin to specify the
requirements of the plugin. If your report plugin does not have
an FH_Requirements function, the plugin will use the default startup
dialog with an Individual record selector. If the user opens the
Report Options dialog in that case, the only tab showing will be the
Page Layout tab.

Syntax

tblRequirements = FH_Requirements()

Parameters

none

Returns

tblRequirements
table: requirements of your plugin. All values are
optional, and have defaults which apply if the value is not
supplied. The table below gives the possible values you can
set:

startup
String. Defaults to "default" if not supplied.
Possible values are:

default = the default startup dialog is displayed

plugin = the startup dialog is implemented by the report
plugin in a FH_Startup
function.

options = the Report Options dialog is displayed as the
startup dialog

none = there is no startup dialog. The report just
opens.

record_type
String.

Many reports require the user to select one or more
records. If you want your report to work like this,
specify the 'record_type' here. Defaults to "INDI" if
not supplied. The field specifies the tag of the record type
required. For example, set record type to "INDI" for
Individual records or "FAM" for Family records. The full
list of available record tags are:

INDI = Individuals

FAM = famiilies

SOUR = sources

NOTE = note records

_PLAC = place records (don't omit the leading
underscore!)

OBJE = media records

SUBM = submitter

SUBN = submission

REPO = repository

If you are using the default startup dialog (i.e. you have
not provide an implementation of FH_Startup), the user will
be prompted to select records of the required type.
Also, once the report has opened, the user will be able to
change the record selection by clicking 'Records' on the
Report Window.

If your report does not require a record selection, set
record_type to an empty string.

Reports that require a record selection are called
'record-driven reports'.

record_collection
Boolean. By default, in record-driven reports
(see previous section), it is assumed that you want to produce
one top-level section for each record that the user
selects. To support this, Family Historian will call
your implementation of FH_GetRecordSectionContent once for
each record that the user selects. Sometimes however
that's not what you want. Sometimes you may want to
produce a report that is about a collection of records that
the user selected, taken as a whole. In that case set
'record_collection' to true (the default, if not supplied, is
false). If this setting is true, Family Historian will
not call FH_GetRecordSectionContent. Instead your
implementation of FH_GetMiscSectionContent will be called once
for each miscellaneous section that your report requests
(using your implementation of the FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired
function), and the last parameter, 'reclist', will be a table
containing a list of the selected records.

records_min
Integer. The minimum number of records the user
may select. Defaults to 1 if not supplied. Ignored if the
report does not require record selection (see 'record_type'
above).

records_max
Integer. The maximum number of records the user
may select. Defaults to -1 (no limit) if not supplied. Ignored
if the report does not require record selection (see
'record_type' above).

title
String. The title to use for this report when it is included
in a book. Defaults to the plugin name if not supplied.
May contain an expression, such as "%INDI.NAME:ADORNED_FULL%
(=LifeDates2())". If it does contain an expression, this
must be appropriate for the record type (see 'record_type'
above) of the report.

generations
Boolean. Defaults to false if not supplied. If
you specify true for this value (note: no quotes around it!)
the user will be prompted to specify the number of generations
in the default startup dialog (if not overridden), and in the
Report Options dialog main page. They will be able to
choose a number or "All".

generations_default
String. Only applicable if you set generations equal
to true. Defaults to "3" if not supplied. Specifies the
default number of generations as a string. The reason that as
string is needed rather than a number is that you can specify
"all" if you wish. The value specified here will be the
initial value for generations in your report, and the value
that appears if the user clicks 'Restore Defaults' in Report
Options.

options
String. Specifies the
report-specifiic options required by your report.

When your report is displayed, the user will be able to choose
(depending on the 'tabs' setting below) many of the standard
options, normally available in Report Options. But you
may also wish to specify your own options, in addition to
these. There are two ways to do that. If you really need
to, you can provide your own user options dialog and allow the
user to choose options there. See FH_PromptUserOptions
for more on this. That is not the normal, nor the
recommended way of doing it. If at all possible, the
preferred option is to specify the options you require in a
text string here.

The text string allows you to specify as many distinct report
options as you like using 'controls'. Each control can
be:

an ordinary edit box, prefixed by a label

an edit box that will only accept numbers, prefixed by a
label

a check box. Checkboxes do not have a separate
label.

a dropdown list of items to select from, prefixed by a
label.

an edit box with a dropdown list of suggested values,
prefixed by a label.

In addition, you can also add plain text (e.g. as additional
headings). Plain text is implemented by the static
control type.

For each non-static control, you need to specify 5
parts. Static controls have only 4 parts. The
parts are:

a name (for static controls only the name can be left
blank - i.e. a static control can begin like this:
"~|...")

a label

the control type: edit, integer, dropdownlist,
dropdownedit, checkbox, static. For dropdownlists
and dropdownedits, the dropdown item list is specified in
brackets after the control type name, using a semicolon to
separate items. e.g.
"dropdownlist(Ancestors;Descendants;All Relatives)"

the default value (non-static controls only! For
non-static controls, it can be blank but cannot be
excluded altogether as it is for static controls)

spacing

The specification of each control starts with a tilde
character (~). Values are separated by a vertical
bar. You can have as many control as you like on each
line. It is recommended to leave at least one space
between control specifications, for improved
readability. Terminate the last item (spacing) with a
newline character (\n) if the control is the last on its
line. Use the escape character (\) in front of any
vertical bar that is part of the text and should not be
treated as a separator.

The spacing part - for all controls except checkboxes and
statics - is in the format:

a:b(c)

... where a is the width of the label in
horizontal dialog units, b is the width of
the interactive part of the control in horizontal dialog
units, and c is the width of the gap after
the control, in horizontal dialog units. Horizontal
dialog units are approximately one-quarter of the average
character width, of dialog text, using the dialog's current
font.

The last part "(c)" is optional. You should leave it out
if the control is the last on the current line.

Checkboxes and statics do not have a separate label, so for
them the format for spacing is:

a(c)

... where a is the width of the checkbox or static in
horizontal dialog units and c is the (optional) gap after it.

You can also leave vertical line gaps by inserting additional
new line characters.

As well as the example below, see plugin report samples for
more examples of how to specify report options.

tabs
String. Tabs required in
report options as a comma-separated list. Options are:

pictures

sources

index

format

privacy

language

The Page Layout tab is always displayed (unless the report has
been added to a book, in which case it will be displayed as
part of book options). Also, there is no need to specify
the main options tab (indeed you can't). If you have set
generations to true, and/or if you have provided
options in an options string, there will be a main tab with
these, in Report Options. If not, there won't be.

Note: Regardless of what you specify here, the sources, index,
privacy and language tabs will not display as options for your
report if you add the report to a book, and click on the
'Settings' button, when editing book details, to view the
report options. This is because sources, index, privacy
and language are handled as part of book options, in a book
context. The Format tab will display even in a book
context, but shows reduced information. The font and
heading style parts are configured within book options.

fonts

String. Comma-separated list of font types that the
user should be able to configure in the Format tab of the
Report Options dialog (i.e. the font types that are applicable
to your report). The labels to use for each font
category are those specified for the Style command
in eFtf Syntax.
For example, the string "secdata,seclabel" would mean that
your report needs the "Section Data" and "Section Label" font
types to be configurable by the user in Report Options.

This command has no effect on fonts which are explicitly
specified by font name (e.g. using the Font command
in Ftf Syntax).
It only affects those fonts that the user can configure in the
Format tab of Report Options. The use of some of these
fonts (index heading, caption etc) are obvious. The
applicability of others is less obvious. Some of them
are the default fonts used in sections at various heading
levels. A top-level section has heading level 1.
If it has child sections, they have heading level 2.
Their children have heading level 3. These sections can
in turn have child sections, and so on indefinitely, but they
will all be treated as heading level 3. The default font
types used in the various sections are as follows:

A heading level 1 section will use "Heading Level 1" for
its heading (by default), and will use "Section Data" by
default for body text.

A heading level 2 section will use "Heading Level 2" for
its heading (by default), and will use "Section Data" by
default for body text.

A heading level 3 section will use "Heading Level 3" for
its heading (by default), and will use "Subsection Data"
by default for body text.

If your report includes a table with style "auto", the first
column of the table will have the "Section Label" font by
default, and all other columns will use the "Section Data"
font by default. For more information, see eFtf
Syntax.

Font types can also be explicitly selected using the eFTF
Syntax Style command (see eFtf
Syntax)

picture_categories

String. Comma-separated list of labels to use for
picture categories in the Pictures tab of Report Options.

In the pictures tab of report options, a report can have up to
5 different categories of picture. Having different
categories allows the user considerable flexibility in choice
of size and location for pictures of each category. When
designing your report, you can use these 5 categories in any
way you like. If you do not specify a value for
"picture_categories", 5 categories of picture will be listed
in the Pictures tab of report options, and the default labels
will be used. These are: "Individual", "Spouse Family",
"Spouse", "Children" and "Other". The
"picture_categories" setting allows you to specify the number
of categories you require and the labels to use for
them. You supply the labels in a comma-separated list
(e.g. "Person,Parent,Grandparent"). The number of items
in the list determines the number of categories shown to the
user, up to a maximum of 5.

heading_levels

Integer (1-3). Determines the number of "Hdg Style"
lines displayed in the Format tab of Report Options.

column_indents

Integer (0-4). Determines the number of column indent
values shown to the user in the Page Layout tab of Report
Options. This will only be applicable if your report has
one or more tables that use the ConfigColWidths flag
(see eFtf Syntax).
The values specified by the user are not the width of the
columns, but the indentation of each column (including the
first) from the left margin.

column_gap

Boolean. If you specified a column_indents value greater
than 1, column_gap is treated as true automatically. If
column_gap is set to true, the 'Gap' field in the 'Column
Indents' section of the Page Layout tab of Diagram Options, is
displayed to the user. This gap field is used in any
table that has the ConfigColWidths flag.
It is also used if even if the ConfigColWidths flag
is not set, if the ConfigColGap flag is
specified (see eFtf
Syntax).

para_indent

Boolean. Set this to true if your report uses any
para-indents (see eFtf
Syntax). This will cause the "Para. Indent" setting
to be visible in the Page Layout tab of Report Options,
allowing the user to specify the width of para-indents.

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to specify its requirements
function FH_Requirements()
local t = {};

-- default startup options
t.record_type = "INDI"; -- ignored if FH_Startup is overridden. Specifies the record type of the record selector
t.generations = false; -- ignored if FH_Startup is overridden. Do you want the default startup dlg to prompt for no. of gens?

-- report options dialog requirements
t.options = "~title|Title:|edit||32:60(20) ~alt_title|Alt. Title:|edit||32:60\n" ..
"~count|Number:|integer|6|32:28\n" ..
"\n" ..
"\n" ..
"~|MORE STUFF!|static|50\n" ..
"~fruit|Fruit:|dropdownlist(Apples;Oranges;Bananas;Cherries)|Apples|50:49\n" ..
"~country|Country:|dropdownedit(America;France;Germany;UK)|Germany|50:49\n" ..
"~notes|Include Notes|checkbox|true|70(20) ~places|Include Places|checkbox|false|70(20) ~occups|Include Occupations|checkbox|false|80\n" ..
"~rels|Relatives:|dropdownlist(Ancestors;Descendants;All Relatives)|Ancestors|41:70";
t.tabs = "sources,index,pictures,format"; -- report options tabs required (may not show in rpt opts when report is part of a book)
t.fonts = "hdg1,hdg2,hdg3,secdata,seclabel,sublabel"; -- fonts shown in format tab of report options
t.picture_categories = "Individuals"; -- max 5 labels for picture categories in pictures tab. Defaults (all 5) if not supplied
t.heading_levels = 3; -- affects no. of heading levels shown in format tab of report options
t.column_indents = 4; -- no. of column indent value required in layout tab of rpt opts
t.para_indent = true; -- para indent value required in layout tab of rpt opts

return t;
end

title: FH_Reset (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_Reset (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is called during first-run processing or if the user
clicks the Restore Defaults button on any tab of the Report Options
dialog. First-run processing only occurs the first time a report
plugin is run on a new PC. Reports options are kept in a file
that has the same name as the plugin, but with a .fhr suffix.
When the plugin runs, Family Historian will check to see if an
equivalent .fhr file exists. If it doesn't, Family Historian
will execute first-run processing. This means creating a new
.fhr file by copying a standard .fhr file and calling FH_Reset in the
report plugin, to give the plugin a chance to set default values, and
to do any one-time initialisation that may need to be done.

If you wish to force first-run processing to be repeated, it is only
necessary to delete the .fhr file for the plugin. It is kept in
the same folder as the plugin itself.

Syntax

bOK = FH_Reset( strTab)

Parameters

strTab
This parameter will be nil if the function is being called during
first-run processing. If called when the user clicks the
Restore Defaults button with Report Options, it will give the name
of the tab which the user was wishing to reset.

Returns

bOK
Return value has no effect if the entry-point was called during
first-run processing. If called during Restore
Defaults, a return value of true means that the report must
be rebuilt.

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to handle first-run processing and to implement 'restore-defaults' functionality
local OptionsFile = fhGetContextInfo("CI_REPORT_OPTIONS_FILE");

function FH_Reset(strTab)
if not Tab or Tab == "pictures" then
fhSetIniFileValue(OptionsFile, "Report Options", "Pic Opts Individuals", "text", "[RL,M]");
return true; -- only return true if you actually change OptionsFile in some way. Will cause a refresh.
end

return false
end

title: FH_Startup (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_Startup (entry-point)

Description

This entry-point is rarely needed or used. Implement this
function if you wish to replace the default startup dialog - that is,
the dialog that appears each time the report is run. You must also
specify "plugin" as the value for 'startup' in FH_Requirements.

If you prompt the user with options, you are strongly recommended to
store the values chosen in the report options file, in a section named
"Plugin" (this is where by default, plugin-specific options are
stored). If possible, your dialog should also provide some way for
the user to access the default report options dialog (via a button or
link or menu command, say). This is because the default report
options dialog provides numerous options relating to page layout and
possibly other things, which your options dialog will not handle, but
which the user will still need to be able to access. If the user clicks
the relevant button or link, you should call
fnShowDefaultRptOptionsDlg to display the default report options
dialog. fnShowDefaultRptOptionsDlg is FH_Startup's only
parameter. It is an unusual kind of parameter. Most
parameters are text, booleans, numbers, or some kind of object.
fnShowDefaultRptOptionsDlg is a function (or if you prefer,
you can think of it as a link to a function). More specifically,
it is a function which takes one parameter and does not return
anything. The parameter it takes is a window handle. This
must be supplied. It should be either the window handle of your
own options dialog (if still visible at this point), or failing that,
the 'parent window' handle returned by
fhGetContextInfo("CI_PARENT_HWND"). Iup dialogs have a read-only
attribute HWND which is the window handle (as a light userdata
object).

Syntax

bOK = FH_Startup(fnShowDefaultRptOptsDlg)

Parameters

fnShowDefaultRptOptsDlg
A function object. Call this function to display the default
Report Options dialog. The function takes one parameters and
returns no value. Call it like this:

fnShowRptOptsDlg()

Returns

bOK

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to replace the default start up dialog
function FH_Startup(strReportOptsFile, fnShowRptOptsDlg)

-- add your own start up dialog here.

fnShowRptOptsDlg() -- normally you would only call this function if the user clicked to view standard report options

end

title: FH_ValidateUserOption (entry-point)
text:
Report Plugins

FH_ValidateUserOption (entry-point)

Description

If you wish to provide validation for any options you specified in
the options string in FH_Requirements,
this is how you do it. Implement an FH_ValidationUserOption
function in your plugin and check each option in turn. Return
nil or an empty string to indicate that an option is OK. If you
return a non-empty string, this means that the option is not valid,
and the error message string you returned will be displayed.

Syntax

strErrorMessage = FH_ValidateUserOption(strOptionName,
strOptionValue)

Parameters

strOptionName
The name of the report option (as specified in the options string
in FH_Requirements).
strOptionValue
The value for the option in question that you are validating,
expressed as a text string. Boolean values are "1" for true
and "0" for false.

Returns

strErrorMessage
string. Return an empty string if the option is valid or an
error message if it isn't.

Example

-- Add this entry-point function to your report plugin to validate options supplied in FH_Requirements
function FH_ValidateUserOption(strOptionName, strOptionValue)

if strOptionName == "title" and strOptionValue == "" then
return "Title is mandatory - please supply.";
end

return "";

end

title: Report Plugins
text:
Special Plugin Types

Report Plugins

A report plugin is a special kind of plugin that generates a report that
is displayed in the Report Window. You have always been able to
create reports using a plugin, but creating a "Report Plugin" has numerous
advantages. Here are some:

You can get a professional-looking result with relatively little
work.

Sophisticated display features are easy to use - such as bold,
italics, strike-out, underline, indent, bullets, body-indents, fonts
(or all kinds and sizes), text colours and highlight colours, text
alignment and more.

Many of the key features of reports are taken care of for you
automatically, so you don't have to worry about them - such as
margins, page size and orientation, page numbering, page display
options (scrolling, zooming, etc) and most aspects of page layout.

With little effort from you, your users can have considerable
control over page layout, and report options.

With little effort from you, your report can support advanced
features such as pictures, source citations and an index - all of
which can be configurable for the user.

All reports you create in this way can be saved in PDF format or in
word-processing format, and can be re-used by the user in generated
web-sites, or in books.

The report will be displayed in a way that is familiar to the user
(the Report Window), so users will have nothing to learn when viewing
it. From the user's point-of-view, a report generated by a
plugin should be indistinguishable from a report created directly by
Family Historian.

Report Plugins are very flexible so you should be able to adapt the
model quite easily to get the results you want.

How to Create a Report Plugin

At a minimum, a report plugin must have a header and the header must
include a line "@Type: report". Also, it must contain a function
that provides report content - such as FH_GetRecordSectionContent.
The following is an example of a very minimalistic report plugin. If
you run it (not under the debugger!), it will prompt you to
choose one or more Individual records and will then output a report which
has the name of each selected person as heading, and the text "Hello
World" in the body of the report, for each selected person

--[[
@Type: report
]]

function FH_GetRecordSectionContent(snTop, rec, index, count)

rtHeading = fhNewRichText();
rtHeading:SetText(fhFtfEncode(fhIndGetName(rec, true)));
snTop:SetHeading(rtHeading);
rtBody = fhNewRichText();
rtBody:SetText("Hello World");
snTop:SetBodyText(rtBody);
end

The example given above is a very minimal report. Normally, you will
want to create a much more extensive report. There are 6 stages in
generating a report. These are, in order:

Requirements (FH_Requirements will
be called if available)

First-Run Processing (FH_Reset will be
called if it is the first time this report has been run)

Startup (FH_Startup will be called if
you are providing your own replacement startup dialog - as specified
in FH_Requirements)

Content Generation for Record Sections (FH_GetRecordSectionContent
will be called for each selected record - if the report has a record
type defined in FH_Requirements)

Miscellaneous Section Requirements (checks the number of
Miscellaneous sections required by calling FH_GetMiscSectionsRequired,
if it exists)

Content Generation for Miscellaneous Sections (FH_GetMiscSectionContent
will be called for each miscellaneous section required, as specified
in 5.)

Any report can be refreshed at any time. If so, steps 4 to 6. will
be repeated.

In addition to these stages, a user can choose to view Report Options,
either during the startup dialog, or at any time when viewing the
report. If they change report options, the report will be refreshed
with the new options. It is possible to override the Report Options
dialog (see FH_PromptUserOptions)
but this is not usually necessary and is not recommended. A much
better option is to specify any options required in FH_Requirements.
You can also validate options by providing an FH_ValidateUserOption
function.

Context Information

The function fhGetContextInfo
is used to get contextual information in plugins. There are a number
of values for this function that are particularly of interest for authors
of report plugins. These are given in the table below (note this is
not a complete set of values that can be passed to fhGetContextInfo):

CI_PARENT_HWND
Parent window handle. If you
display a dialog (e.g. if you implement a custom report options
dialog using IUP), you should always set its parent window handle
to this value, to ensure that the dialog does not disappear behind
the Family Historian main window.

CI_REPORT_OPTIONS_FILE
String. Very important and used
all the time in plugin reports. Report options are stored in
the Report Options File. You can get the location of this
file at any time by calling fhGetContextInfo("CI_REPORT_OPTIONS_FILE").
Then use the functions fhGetIniFileValue
and fhSetIniFileValue
to get and set the option values. Plugin-specific options
should be stored in the "Plugin" section. You can call
CI_REPORT_OPTIONS_FILE outside any function, and store the result
in a variable at that level. This variable with then be
available to all functions within your plugin.

CI_BOOK_CONTEXT
Boolean. Returns true if, and only if, the plugin is a
report plugin and the report forms part of a book.
Occasionally useful.

CI_BOOK_ITEM_HEADING

String. Important. Call this function to get the
heading for the first section of your report. In a book
context, this may be a chapter heading, and may require a chapter
number. Will return an empty string if not in a book
context. In that case, generate the section name in the
ordinary way. Note: This function will use the title
setting, specified in FH_Requirements, when generating the
appropriate title. Do not call it before FH_Requirements has
been called.

Report Plugins Are "Read-Only"

Like smart folder plugins and language plugins (and unlike
source-driven data entry plugins and ordinary plugins) report plugins
are read-only. This does not mean that they cannot be
used to update anything. Like any plugin, they could in
principle update or delete files on your computer, for example.
The label just
means specifically that they cannot be used to update your project data
(your project records and the fields contained within them). More
specifically it means that you cannot call any of these functions:

fhSetValue... functions (i.e. any functions with names beginning
"fhSetValue..." - such as fhSetValueAsInteger)

fhMoveItem... functions (there are only two: fhMoveItemAfter and
fhMoveItemBefore)

fhCreateItem

fhDeleteItem

For the avoidance of doubt, a read-only plugin can call any method on
any object. Some of these methods will update the state of
objects, but they don't change project data, and hence are OK. You
can also call fhCallBuiltInFunction. None of the built-in
functions update program data. And you can call functions like
fhSetIniFileValue. These change file values, but again, they do
not change project data. To repeat, the only functions you cannot
call in a read-only plugin are the functions listed above. If you
call any of these functions from a read-only plugin, you will get an
error.

The only other restriction on read-only plugins is that if you call
fhInitialise in a read-only plugin (which you can do), the fourth
parameter must be blank. That is to say, you cannot specify save
requirements for read-only plugins.

Running Report PLugins

As well as running report plugins from the Plugins window, report
plugins are also automatically listed under 'Custom Reports' on the
Publish menu, and under 'All Reports' on the Publishing Tools
Finder. Depending on the Keywords specified for the Plugin, they
may also be listed in other sections of the Publishing Tools Finder (see
next).

Keywords

All plugins can have keywords. If you give your report plugin one or
more of the following keywords, it will result in the plugin being
listed as a custom report in an appropriate section of the Publishing
Tools Finder:

Keyword
Section of Publishing Tools Finder

Individual
Individual Reports

Family
Family Reports

Relationships

Relationship Reports

Places

Places & Address Reports

Addresses

Places & Address Reports

Occupations

Occupation Reports

Religions

Religion Reports

Facts

Fact & Event Reports

Events

Fact & Event Reports

Sources

Source Reports

Citations

Source Reports

Media

Picture/Multimedia Reports

List of Individuals

Lists of Individuals

Named Lists

Named Lists

Plugin Header Type

We saw earlier that at a minimum, a report plugin must have a header
and the header must include a line "@Type: report". If your plugin
handles a particular record type (this is specified in FH_Requirements),
you can also mention the record type supported. So, instead of
just specifying "report" you could also specify the report type as
"Individual Report", "Family Report", "Source Report" and so on.
This can affect where your report is listed. For example, your
report will not be listed as a possible 'Primary Page Type' report in
step 3 of the website wizard unless you have specified its type as
either "Individual Report" or "Family Report". To be specified as
a possible 'Secondary Page Type' report, it would have to be specified
as an "Indivdual Report".

Other Points

You are recommended to look at the sample report plugin, downloadable from
the Plugin Store. This is designed to show many of the features of
plugins and is a good example of what can be done.

When you design your reports, you may want to include source citations and
support an index. To do this, just add source citations and index
markers using the appropriate commands in eFTF
Syntax. Do not include a separate section for Sources or for
an Index. If the user chooses to view sources or an index in report
options, a suitable source section and/or index section, will be generated
automatically from the source citation and index markers you have inserted
into the main sections.

Debugging report plugins is a little trickier than debugging ordinary
plugins, because the debugger will not call the entry-point functions
unless you add special debugging code of your own, to get it to do
so. It is recommended to look at the Sample Report Plugin for an
example of how this can be done.

Tip: When designing your report, it is likely to be
helpful to look at how other reports are designed. To view how any
given report is designed, open the report in the Report Window, then
right-click on it while holding the Shift key down. Click on the
menu option that appears: 'View Report Dump'.

title: FH_GetSmartFolderData (entry-point)
text:
Smart Folder Plugins

FH_GetSmartFolderData (entry-point)

Description

This is the only entry-point used by smart folder plugins. It
takes a single parameter, a table of data items as input. The
type of data item depends on the the folder set type that the smart
folder belongs to. The function returns a table, in a specified
